author: Dan DiMaggio
title: Book Review: A Model for U.S.-Mexico Cross-Border Solidarity
content:
Labor law reform in Mexico has opened up a major opportunity for workers fighting for genuine, independent unions. What can U.S. unions do to support our brothers and sisters there? And how can we build cross-border campaigns to confront our common employers?


Unions asking these questions will find valuable ideas in the e-book

International Solidarity in Action: The Relationship Between the United Electrical Workers (UE) and Frente Auténtico del Trabajo (FAT)

, available for free download

here

.


Author Robin Alexander, retired director of international affairs for UE, led her union’s partnership with the FAT, which began in 1992, during the campaign to oppose the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).


UE members were seeing their employers cut manufacturing jobs in the U.S. and shift production to Mexico. “The UE leadership became convinced that the union needed to find a labor organization it could work with in Mexico,” Alexander writes, “and also that it was essential to connect international work more directly with UE members and with organizing.”


In a meeting in Mexico to discuss the campaign against NAFTA, the UE found the FAT—the only Mexican labor organization to oppose NAFTA.


Here was a union that had a lot in common with the left-led UE: fiercely independent, with radical roots and leadership. The FAT had long stood out against Mexico's state-dominated unions and fought for workers’ right to form genuine, independent unions.


Both unions were concerned about the growing number of jobs that corporations had moved to assembly plants near Mexico’s northern border with the United States, where unions were either nonexistent or a tool of the government’s development strategy of low wages and long hours.


“The UE,” Alexander writes, “was interested in seeing the plants organized by a union that would serve as a partner and ally in Mexico and believed that it could provide solidarity, including some leverage, where it continued to represent workers employed by those companies in the U.S… The FAT was eager to organize the plants that were moving across the border, but lacked the resources to do so.”


LIKE-MINDED UNIONS


Thus kicked off a partnership that has now lasted 30 years. The book contains several case studies of how the UE and the FAT worked together to back each other’s campaigns against employers such as General Electric and Echlin (a transnational auto parts maker later bought by Dana).


For U.S. unionists unfamiliar with the obstacles that Mexican workers are facing as they struggle to oust protection unions and replace them with genuine unions, these sections will be particularly valuable.


At Echlin, for example, workers attempting to confront dangerous exposure to asbestos and solvents and form a democratic union were met with a barrage of tactics often deployed by employers, official unions, and Mexican labor boards.


For instance, workers were refused a copy of their own collective bargaining agreement. The company fired dozens of independent union supporters, and stalled the union election by claiming the independent metal workers union did not have the proper paperwork to represent auto parts workers.


Worse, it allowed the official union to deploy 170 thugs, “some wielding metal rods, clubs, and guns,” into the plant on the eve of the election. And workers were forced to vote out loud in front of the company, official union, and labor board officials.


TWO-WAY SOLIDARITY


The UE supported the FAT’s organizing by filing complaints under NAFTA’s labor side agreement (NAALC), as well as by providing funds, pressuring shareholders, and organizing speaking tours to draw attention to workers’ rights in Mexico.


The relationship went both ways, with the FAT providing important material support to UE’s organizing efforts and fight for labor law reforms in the United States. During a UE organizing drive at a Milwaukee foundry, the FAT provided a Mexican organizer—an activist who had been fired from a GE plant in Ciudad Juarez—to help campaign among a predominantly Mexican immigrant workforce. The organizer spread the word that the UE was not like the official unions in Mexico which so many had had bad experiences with.


The FAT has also helped draw attention to the severe limitations on labor rights in states like North Carolina—home of UE Local 150, the North Carolina Public Service Workers Union—where many public sector workers are banned from collective bargaining …

title: Hitting the mark: “Grand Theft Capital”, by Fred Magdoff and John Bellamy Foster
content:
REVIEWS


Red Pepper

 picks: “

Botany, welfare, friendships, work and housing.

David Matthews

 picks six of the best new books for leftists

“


“Capitalism has been stagnating for decades, characterized by sluggish growth. Yet the wealthy continue to grow richer while the rest of us face declining wages and eroding living standards. Focusing on the United States yet deeply relevant to Britain and other capitalist countries, Magdoff and Bellamy Foster make clear that in a climate of economic decline, big business has deliberately and strategically targeted workers as a primary source of wealth extraction. Their conclusion is a call for mass action, from below…”


People’s Voice

(Canada):

“Succinct and accessible, this economic primer hits the mark for working people today”

, by Stéphane Doucet


“Magdoff and Foster have truly hit the mark with this short book…Interesting figures include the precipitous drop of work stoppages involving over 1000 workers, from over 330 per year in 1975 to less than 20 since the 2010’s; the corporate tax rate being more than halved since 1950; the CEO-to-worker pay ratio being multiplied by more than 10 times in 60 years; labour’s share of GDP dropping more than 10 percent since the 1960’s; and private sector workers with defined-benefit pensions dropping for 60 percent to 10 percent of the workforce. All these are very broad, clear, decisive and very powerful figures. The book provides many more, along with the necessary context…”

Read more

…


Counterpunch

: “

Why Working People Got the Blues

“, by Ron Jacobs


“The lack of affordability is the curse of the working class, whether its individual members are working or not. Politicians talk about it and some might even propose legislation to moderate it, but the cost of almost everything keeps going up more than wages and retirement benefits. The domination of the economy by monopolies and cartels–many of which are invested in the business of war and resource extraction–and by politicians at their service means the bills they rack up are going to be paid by us. When the ruling class tells us they can’t afford to continue providing social services, they’re lying. It’s not that they can’t, it’s that their priorities lie elsewhere, with consistently higher profits being near or at the forefront.”

author: Erica Chenoweth
title: Will historic protests against ICE shape the midterms?
content:
This article

Will historic protests against ICE shape the midterms?

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


Tomorrow’s midterm elections are widely viewed as a referendum on Trump’s second presidency.

Prior studies

 have found strong associations between protest and U.S. election outcomes, including the

2010

 and

2018

 midterm elections. Protests can influence popular

opinion

 on policy issues, boost turnout among eligible voters, and shape how candidates

set policy priorities

.


At the Crowd Counting Consortium, or CCC, we have tallied an

extraordinary number of protests

 since Donald Trump’s second inauguration in January 2025. The majority of protests in Trump’s second term so far have named democracy or the presidency itself as a primary claim — think the nationwide Hands Off and No Kings protests in 2025 and 2026. 


But among protests focused on more specific policy domains, one key theme stands out. The administration’s anti-immigration policies and expansive, violent crackdown on immigrants have generated active, grassroots support

networks

 in neighborhoods across the country and fueled a wave of protests in support of immigrants’ rights. During Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis and St. Paul, protests took place in over 30 percent of counties containing 80 percent of the nation’s population. March 2026 may have been the month with the highest number of pro-immigrant protests in U.S. history. A significant proportion of these protests occurred in counties that Trump won in 2024. 


Trends in immigration-related protests since January 20, 2017


Of course, the current wave of protest builds on a longer-term foundation of pro-immigrant demonstrations. Since the CCC started collecting data on protest in the United States in 2017, we’ve seen that protests against the federal government’s immigration policies have been a constant feature of the protest landscape across all three presidential administrations — Trump 1, Biden and Trump 2 (see Table 1). 


Table 1: Immigration protest events as a share of all left/liberal protests


Little more than a week after Trump’s first inauguration in January 2017, numerous protests took place around the country in response to his Jan. 27 signing of Executive Order 13769, sometimes called the “Muslim Ban,” which restricted citizens of seven majority-Muslim countries from entering the U.S. On Jan. 28 and 29, mass protests occurred in and around airports, where immigrant rights groups and community members assembled to ensure the safe arrival of citizens of those countries who were in transit when the executive order went into effect. Protests against the executive order continued in February 2017 under the slogan “No Ban No Wall.” The Trump administration ultimately revised the executive order to a narrower version that the U.S. Supreme Court upheld as lawful; multiple protests followed on June 26, 2018. 


But the biggest jumps in protest participation came on coordinated, nationwide days of action related to the administration’s immigration policies. The first, on June 30, 2018, was a national day of action declaring that “Families Belong Together.” These protests demanded an end to the administration’s “child separation policy” — the practice of separating migrant children from parents and caretakers upon arrival at the U.S.-Mexico border — which was in effect under the Obama administration but escalated under Trump. This protest campaign was highly effective: The pressure placed on the administration led the White House to end the policy through an

executive order

, though loopholes remained.


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


On Jan. 19, 2019, the third annual Women’s March on Washington represented an additional increase in coordinated nationwide protests in which immigrants’ rights were a core issue. And July 12, 2019 saw the

Lights for Liberty

 day of action, which attempted to pressure elected officials (particularly in the newly Democratic Congress) to close detention centers and adopt more humane immigration policies. Ultimately, congressional Democrats introduced legislation in 2021 to reunite immigrant children with their families. In sum, the first Trump administration saw an impressive range of protests on behalf of immigrants’ rights, some of which had powerful impacts. 


Overall, the Biden administration saw a decline in such protests, with about 60 percent fewer than …

author: Hilde Marie Rekstad
title: The Process: Helen Wesnes Fights for Her Rights
content:
Editor’s Note: This piece was originally published on our affiliate site,

Mad in Norway

.


Helen Wesnes took control of her own case from the beginning and has already won several victories in the legal system. She does this for all those who lose their lives in psychiatry. Photo: private


H


elen Wesnes was 19 when she sought help from the health care system. It cost her 15 years, followed by a 12-year legal process. She has already won millions in damages and is ready for the next round. Now she explains how she built her case.


Few people know that in Norway there is a society within a society, full of paradoxes and with no known way out. This is the Norway offered to psychiatric patients once they fall under the Mental Health Care Act. “Someone must have slandered Josef K., for one morning, without having done anything wrong, he was arrested,” writes Franz Kafka in his world-famous

The Trial

, and what follows is a nightmare about the individual’s powerlessness against the arbitrariness of bureaucracy. Josef K. and Helen W. don’t have a great deal in common, since she walked out alive and victorious. Otherwise, the process was much the same.


“The media are failing their mission when they don’t raise this case to a systemic level. The practice itself is the problem, not whatever diagnosis the patient may have.”


Helen Wesnes speaks out about her 15 years of confinement, and the legal process that followed


I have invited Helen Wesnes to a conversation in which she shares reflections on the 15 years she was locked up in psychiatry, cut off from both physical and emotional contact with other people. This was the consequence of seeking medical help after a collapse brought on by a critical life event. Her story is an almost unbelievable process, and so is the battle Helen is now fighting in the Norwegian legal system. It is a battle she is fighting for everyone who loses their lives to psychiatry. She holds hard-won experience of what health care should have been, but isn’t, for those who need it most.


There has been limited media interest in covering the legal process Helen Wesnes has pursued for 12 years, and which is still ongoing. This despite the fact that it is historic for a psychiatric patient in Norway to be awarded damages for human rights violations. The articles that have been written have focused on the fact that she was misdiagnosed. Helen says the media are failing their mission when they don’t raise this case to a systemic level. The practice itself is the problem, not whatever diagnosis the patient may have.


Helen has unique expertise in how to prevail against the system once mistakes have been made. She has acquired these skills through what has so far been a more than twelve-year war against state bodies, along with insight into what goes on behind closed doors. In this in-depth interview you can read about a Norway that very few people know exists. She is now asking for deeper understanding from the media and others. “They tend to focus on how terrible it is that I was misdiagnosed, back when trauma was interpreted as schizophrenia. They don’t ask the fundamental question: Should any human being be treated like this?”


Above the entrance to Reinsvoll hospital, the sign reads “Emergency care.” When Helen needed two weeks of rest after a crisis, the consequence was 15 years of confinement and inhumane treatment. Photo: Helen Wesnes


There are events in this story that reveal eugenics thinking, and this is Norway in the 2000s. The sum of what she has been subjected to can also be understood as misogyny. The mechanisms meant to detect and correct problems in the many locked wards in our country have proven to fail. Helen herself says she believes she got out at the last minute, when medical tests showed alarming values.


What began as a patient injury case in 2015 has become an insane process in which the State is doing everything to crush a patient, where the hospital had admitted its mistakes even before the case began. This shameful story should have been compensated many years ago. Instead, the state has dared to appeal.


A brief outline of the Norwegian system


Patients subjected to compulsory treatment must turn to the Control Commission to complain, or to the County Governor (Statsforvalteren) if the complaint is unsuccessful. Once treatment has ended, patients can claim compensation from NPE (the Norwegian System of Patient Injury Compensation). If the claim is rejected …

title: S. E. Parker - Krieg und Frieden
content:

Mehr Kontakt Material Sticker, Plakate, etc.

Während der letzten zwei Jahrzehnte haben wir uns so daran gewöhnt in einer Welt des Krieges oder der Bedrohung durch einen Krieg zu leben, daß wir begonnen haben, eine solche Situation beinah als normal zu betrachten. In einer Atmosphäre dauernder Krisen, Kriege und heißer Vorfälle hat ein aktiver Widerstand gegen den Krieg eine deutliche Neigung schwach zu werden, sogar bedeutungslos zu sein, obschon es scheint, daß der Kessel auf dem Punkte ist, jederzeit überzukochen. Bis heute hat er es noch nicht getan, mag er uns auch dann und wann bange machen, wenn sein Deckel klappert.

Als eine Folge dieser “Normalität” der Krisen verlieren Warnungen gegen die Gefahr des Krieges, seine Übel und gänzliche Unverantwortlichkeit, ihre Dringlichkeit und werden ein Teil der täglichen Klischees. Es ist wahr, daß Explosionen der A- und H-Bomben hysterische Wellen und Spannungen auslösen, aber nachdem die Versammlungen gehalten wurden, die Bittschriften unterzeichnet, die Wissenschaftler sich gezankt haben, glätten sich diese Wellen wieder. Sogar auf der Höhe einer solchen Panik fühlt man, daß hier etwas fehlt. Die Phrasen vom Frieden und von den Übeln des Krieges scheinen unwirklich, abgenutzt und verblaßt zu sein durch andauernden Gebrauch und andauernden Verrat. Man muß an die Versammlungen vor dem ersten Weltkriege denken, mit ihren Beschlüssen von internationaler Solidarität: man erinnert sich der Debatten und Demonstrationen zwischen 1918 und 1939, und der Gelübde, das Kämpfen abzulehnen. Und dann erinnert man sich, wie alles praktisch zwecklos war, die Massen gehorsam die Uniformen anzogen und wie sie sich gegenseitig abschlachteten auf Befehl ihrer Herrscher: mit Beifall begrüßt von vielen derjenigen, die vorher so laut nach Frieden schrien.

Auf diese Weise gefangen in einer für den Krieg gerüsteten Welt, zwischen der falschen Hoffnung, daß der Krieg abgewandt oder auf unbestimmte Zeit verschoben werden kann und dem niederdrückenden Wissen von den Mißerfolgen aller Anstrengungen für den Frieden wird man oft in die Verzweiflung gestürzt.

Was können wir, die Anarchisten, darauf antworten?

Wie wir es sehen, kann das Problem des Krieges nicht isoliert von den anderen sozialen Fragen betrachtet werden. Die Wurzeln des Krieges liegen in der heutigen sozialen Anordnung. Der Krieg ist heute notwendig für die kapitalistische Ökonomie. Ohne Krieg oder der Vorbereitung für einen Krieg würde es dem Kapitalismus unmöglich sein, die erzeugten Waren unterzubringen und die Vollbeschäftigung für seine Lohnsklaven aufrechzuerhalten oder die unheilvollen Preisstürze und Krisen abzuwenden, die vor 1939 charakterzeigend für seine Existenz waren. Es gibt keine Märkte mehr zu erobern, keine neuen Quellen von Rohmaterial, die nicht direkt oder indirekt unter der Kontrolle irgendeiner Macht stünden; die kapitalistischen Nationen sind in Verlegenheit. Einziger Weg aus dieser Verlegenheit ist der Krieg. Durch einen Krieg kann der “Überschuß” an Waren untergebracht werden und brauchbare Quellen für Material und “Reichtum” werden gewonnen. Das heißt nicht, daß die einzelnen Kapitalisten ihre Zeit damit verbringen, Kriege anzuzetteln oder wissentlich darauf hoffen, aber Krieg ist dem Mechanismus der Profit-Ökonomie angeboren und dem Staate der dieses unterstützt. Sogar wenn der Staat aufhörte, das ausführende Organ einer herrschenden Klasse zu sein und der politische und wirtschaftliche Herr der Gesellschaft wird, so kann er doch nicht die Notwendigkeit eines Krieges vermeiden als das letzte Instrument im Kampfe um die Weltherrschaft.

Natürlich gibt es viele, besonders unter den Pazifisten, die im Grunde mit dieser Analyse einverstanden sind, aber die anführen, daß der Krieg das größte Übel unserer Zeit sei und darum mit allen Mitteln versucht werden müsse, einen Krieg zu verhindern. Deshalb ihre Verteidigungen der Zusammenkünft von Staatsmännern mit den Versuchen durch Verhandlungen die A- und H-Bomben zu ächten, Unterstützung der UNO und Forderung einer Weltregierung. Gewiß, auf den ersten Blick scheinen solche Vorschläge viel praktischer zu sein denn die Haltung der “Puritaner”, die den Krieg als eine Folge des Staats- und Eigentums-Systems ansehen und seine Abschaffung als untrennbar von der Abschaffung dieser Systeme. VAMOS A IR. QUIÉRANLO O NO, VAMOS A IR Denuncia del GOBIERNO COMÚN DE LOS 12 CARACOLES ZAPATISTAS

Compañeras, compañeros y compañeroas: Hermanoas, hermanas y hermanos:

En julio de este año, anunciamos nuestra intención de viajar a la Ciudad de México para encontrarnos con grupos, colectivas, y familias sin grupo, de Familiares Buscadoras. No para asambleas, no para crear nuevas redes o coordinadoras, sino para escuchar, grupo por grupo, familia por familia, sus historias y las historias de sus ausentes. Y también, si lo aceptan, darles un abrazo que mandan las comunidades zapatistas.

Nombramos a la Ciudad de México como sede central para evitarles, a los familiares con ausencias, el desgaste y gasto que hubiera significado venir hasta territorio zapatista.

Desde entonces, el gobierno federal, el estatal de Chiapas y distintos gobiernos municipales han realizado una serie de acciones que no sólo violan los derechos humanos (no sólo de zapatistas, también de partidistas y sin partido), también contradicen el discurso de paz, felicidad y bienestar que predican allá arriba.

Les damos los detalles, pero antes les informamos que no son sino provocaciones para obligarnos a suspender el viaje de finales de este mes, la estancia en la Ciudad de México en el mes de diciembre y primera semana de enero del 2027, y las visitas que están por concretarse a Oaxaca, Veracruz, Puebla, Jalisco y Querétaro en esas fechas.

Entonces allá arriba, a nivel federal, estatal y municipal, tienen que entender que vamos a ir (puede ser que alguien de los nuestros ya está allá) a la Ciudad de México, vamos a reunirnos con las familias buscadoras que quieran y puedan en la Ciudad de México, en Veracruz, en Puebla, en Jalisco, en Oaxaca y en Querétaro; vamos a escuchar la historia de su dolor; les vamos a abrazar; vamos a guardar su palabra en nuestras morraletas; vamos a traer de regreso sus historias y las vamos a guardar para que no las manchen el olvido y la indiferencia.

Cualquier provocación va a ser respondida con fuerza y movilización. Tienen que decidir si aceptan ese hecho y se conforman con que cumpliremos nuestra palabra. O pueden seguir con sus torpezas (en las que está todo el gabinete federal, estatal y las presidencias municipales) y darle otro carácter a nuestra iniciativa. No vamos a hacer bulla, pero podemos hacerlo.

1.- En el ejido La Culebra, municipio oficial de Ocosingo (gobernado por el Partido Verde Ecologista de México), siguen hostigando, amenazando y encarcelando a familias bases de apoyo. Quienes provocan ahí son miembros del Cártel de Mario Delgado, secretario de educación pública federal. El sicario principal es Eusebio Cruz Ruiz, que se presenta como maestro y que dice recibir órdenes directas de Mario Delgado.

Ahora han dado un paso más al prohibir a todos que acudan a la tienda cooperativa de los compas so pena de cárcel. Y, también, que cualquier poblador de ese ejido o de comunidades cercanas, que se atienda en la clínica del común (atiende a zapatistas, a partidistas y a sin partido), será encarcelado y multado. Quien no obedezca, es tomado preso.

Además de que prohíben el libre tránsito, el libre comercio y el acceso a la salud, meten “respetuosamente” a la cárcel y multan a quien no les obedece, no sólo en el ejido, sino en todas las comunidades de alrededor.

title: “Vatandaşın hakkı olan 615 milyon doları BYD’den tahsil edin”
content:
Yeni Parti Zonguldak Milletvekili Deniz Yavuzyılmaz, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, BYD’ye sağlanan yatırım teşviklerini ve vergi muafiyetlerini gündeme taşıdı.

BYD’ye sağlanan vergi muafiyetleri nedeniyle kamunun 615 milyon doların üzerinde kayba uğradığını iddia eden Yavuzyılmaz, “AKP’nin, Çinli otomotiv devi BYD’ye 615 milyon dolar vergi kıyağı yaptığını tespit ettik! Peki nasıl? 5 Temmuz 2024’te; Ticaret Bakanlığı, BYD’ye yapacağı kıyaklara giden yolun taşlarını döşemeye başlıyor. Yatırım teşvik belgesi kapsamında yapılan ithalatı ek gümrük vergilerinden muaf tutuyor. Üç gün sonra 8 Temmuz 2024’te; BYD ile Sanayi ve Teknoloji Bakanlığı arasında, 1 milyar dolarlık yatırım taahhüdü üzerinden bir ‘yatırım anlaşması’ imzalanıyor. Ancak süreç boyunca: BYD ile imzalanan yatırım anlaşmasının detayları kamuoyundan gizleniyor” dedi.

BYD’ye verilen teşvik belgesinin sır gibi saklandığını söyleyen Yavuzyılmaz, “10 Haziran 2026’da; BYD, Türkiye’de yapmayı taahhüt ettiği Manisa yatırımı için takvim bulunmadığını ve projeyi askıya aldığını açıklıyor. Peki BYD, yatırım anlaşmanın imzalandığı Temmuz 2024’ten, yatırımı askıya aldığı Haziran 2026’ya kadar ne yaptı? İmtiyazlı şekilde, devasa vergi indirimi avantajlarıyla Türkiye’de tam 59.168 adet araç sattı. AKP eliyle, otomotiv sektöründeki adil rekabet ortamı paramparça edildi. Sonuç: Vergi kaybı tutarı 615 milyon dolar! Güncel kurla yaklaşık 30 milyar lira! Nasıl hesapladım? Ticaret Bakanlığı’nın BYD’ye sağladığı vergisiz ithalat hakkı kapsamında; Araç başı gümrük öncesi fiyat ortalama 11.500 dolar alındığında; Gümrük vergisi, ek vergi muafiyeti ve bu muafiyetlerin ÖTV ile KDV matrahlarına zincirleme etkisi hesaplandığında toplam vergi kaybı 615 milyon doları aşıyor” ifadelerini kullandı.

Sanayi ve Teknoloji Bakanı Mehmet Fatih Kacır’a çağrıda bulunan Yavuzyılmaz, “Ya BYD’nin taahhüt ettiği fabrikayı derhal kurdurun ya da teşvik belgesini iptal edip sağlanan tüm destekleri derhal geri alın. Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat’a: Çin menşeili araç vergilerinden BYD’yi muaf tutan düzenlemeleri hemen yürürlükten kaldırın. Zamanaşımı süresi dolmadan, devletin ve vatandaşın hakkı olan 615 milyon doları faiziyle birlikte BYD’den tahsil edin” dedi.

title: Varto-Karlıova'da JES direnişi: Bilirkişi keşfine yüzlerce köylü katıldı
content:
Muş'un Varto/Gimgim ve Bingöl'ün Karlıova/Kanireş ilçeleri arasındaki köylerde planlanan jeotermal enerji santrali projesine karşı açılan davada, Bingöl İdare Mahkemesi'nin görevlendirdiği bilirkişi heyeti 2 Kasım Pazartesi günü proje alanında inceleme yaptı. Keşif, aylardır projeye karşı çıkan köylülerin ve ekoloji örgütlerinin katılımıyla gerçekleştirildi.


Heyet, sondaj kuyularının açılması planlanan Licik, Çermî ve Şorik köylerinde incelemelerde bulunduktan sonra Varto'nun Xwarik (Çalıdere) köyüne geçti. Buradaki keşfi yüzlerce köylü izledi.


Xwarik'te yüzlerce kişi keşif heyetini bekledi


Xwarik'te keşif heyetini bekleyen köylüler/Fotoğraf: MA


Bilirkişi heyeti Karlıova'daki incelemelerini sürdürürken Varto'nun Xwarik köyünde farklı kentlerden gelen ekoloji savunucuları, siyasi parti ve demokratik kitle örgütü temsilcileri, “Varto yeşildir yeşil kalacak” ve “Direne direne kazanacağız” sloganlarıyla projeyi protesto etti.


DEM Parti Muş Milletvekili Sümeyye Boz, köylülerin yalnızca doğal çevrelerini değil, geçim kaynaklarını ve geleceklerini savunduklarını söyledi. Jeotermal projenin suya, toprağa ve hayvancılığa zarar vereceğini savunan Boz, halkın rızası olmadan verilen izinlere karşı çıktı.


“Biz burada geçim kaynaklarımızı da yaşam kaynaklarımızı da geleceğimizi de savunuyoruz” diyen Boz, köylülerin taleplerinin dikkate alınmasını istedi ve “Zafer Varto halkının olacak” dedi.


DEM Parti İzmir Milletvekili İbrahim Akın ise enerji yatırımlarının çevresel sonuçlarıyla hükümetlerin iklim politikaları arasındaki çelişkiye dikkat çekti. Akın, COP31 hazırlıklarına değinerek iklim değişikliğiyle mücadele iddiasında bulunan yönetimlerin bir yandan ekolojik yıkıma yol açabilecek projelere izin vermesini eleştirdi.


Akın, bu politikaları “sahte yeşil politikalar” olarak nitelendirerek yaşam alanlarını koruma mücadelesinin sürdürülmesi gerektiğini söyledi.


Varto Belediye Eşbaşkanları Gıyasettin Aydemir ve Gülbahar Kaya da köylülerin mücadelesini desteklediklerini belirterek ilçenin doğal varlıklarını korumakta kararlı olduklarını açıkladı.


İncelemelere DEM Parti milletvekilleri İbrahim Akın ve Sümeyye Boz'un yanı sıra baro temsilcileri, avukatlar ve ekoloji örgütleri de katıldı.


180 günü aşan çadır nöbetinden bilirkişi keşfine


ABD merkezli IGNIS H2 Enerji Üretim AŞ'nin geliştirmek istediği projeye karşı köylüler nisanda Bingöl İdare Mahkemesi'nde dava açtı. Varto'nun Xwarik köyünde 3 Mayıs'ta başlatılan çadır nöbeti ise 180 günü geride bıraktı.


Muş'un Xwarik köylüleri mera savunmasında: JES projesine direnişin 180. günü


31 Ekim 2026


Köylüler, jeotermal sondajların yeraltı su kaynaklarını, tarım alanlarını, meraları ve hayvancılığa dayanan geçim kaynaklarını olumsuz etkilemesinden kaygılı. Bölgenin aktif fay hatları üzerindeki konumu da itirazların başlıca gerekçeleri arasında.


Bingöl İdare Mahkemesi, 21 Temmuz'daki ara kararıyla bilirkişilere 13 ayrı başlıkta soru yönelterek keşif yapılmasını istedi. İlk olarak 8 Ekim'de yapılması planlanan keşif, heyette yeterli uzmanlığa sahip bir jeofizik mühendisi bulunması talebiyle yapılan itirazın ardından 2 Kasım'a ertelendi.


Avukatlardan fay hattı ve eksik rapor uyarısı


Keşfin ardından açıklama yapan davanın avukatı Barış Yıldırım, bölgedeki fay hatlarına dikkat çekerek projenin hayata geçirilmesinin yaşam hakkı açısından ciddi riskler doğuracağını savundu.


Yıldırım, şirketin proje için ilgili kurumlardan alınması gereken raporları tamamlamadığını ileri sürdü. Türkiye'nin taraf olduğu uluslararası sözleşmelerin de dikkate alınması gerektiğini belirtti.


Muş Barosu Başkanı Kadir Karaçelik, köylülerin aylardır sürdürdüğü mücadeleye destek vererek şöyle konuştu:


“Umut ediyorum ki mantıklı bir şekilde değerlendirilir yasal organlar tarafından. Gimgim halkının yaşam çığlığına ses verilir.”


Van Barosundan avukat Rojhat Özgökçe de hukuki sürecin yanı sıra köylülerin mücadelesinin önemine dikkat çekti:


“Bir şeyler dönüşecekse, sizin direnişiniz sayesinde dönüşecektir.”


DEM Parti Muş Milletvekili Sümeyye Boz ise mahkemelerin halkın yaşam hakkını gözeten bir karar vermesini umduklarını belirterek mücadeleyi sürdüreceklerini söyledi.


Davanın konusu çevresel değerlendirme kararları


Davanın esasını jeotermal kaynak arama faaliyetlerine ilişkin çevresel değerlendirme kararlarının hukuka uygun olup olmadığı oluşturuyor.

title: « GenZ de merde »
content:
23 OCTOBRE 2026


À la télévision


un monsieur a dit


que Trappes


était la capitale européenne du djihad


À Trappes


il y a des écoles


des maisons


des arrêts de bus


un jardin d'enfants


et une petite fille de douze ans


Dans le jardin d'enfants


il y a des jeux pour les enfants


des bancs pour les parents


et des enfants qui jouent


pendant que les parents


les regardent jouer


Vendredi matin


un autre monsieur


est arrivé en voiture


Les enfants jouaient


les parents regardaient


Pan


pan


pan


JE SAIS


Il faut trouver du travail maintenant.


T'as peut-être pas choisi la bonne voie.


Je connais des jeunes, ils ont pas tous le même discours.


Si t'es déprimé, oublie pas de prendre tes médicaments.


Je te dis ça pour t'aider.


COMPLAINTE DU PROGRÈS


ça va être la complainte du progrès si tu m'demandes


est-ce un film de Tati ou un film de Godard ?


j'suis pas bien sûre


un gloubi-boulga des deux peut-être


deux ou trois choses que je sais de l'époque moderne


c'est qu'on n'a pas fini de faire la pute


et que Godard qui se croit très malin


n'avait rien vu


c'est du vrai sang pas du rouge


parce que


à ce stade


par où commencer


c'est la post-post-post-modernité


prostitution au carré


aliénation au cube


milliard de possibilité pour se faire *******


pas de possibilité quand on peut pas payer


l'argent ne fait pas le bonheur


attend de voir ce que la misère te fera (proverbe italien)


on y est


la vraie vie n'est pas sur Mars


et ça repart


NE TRAVAILLEZ JAMAIS


Dès qu'un lycée est bloqué


qu'un bâtiment est occupé


que des travailleurs font grève


il y a toujours quelqu'un


dans les commentaires


pour écrire


Allez travailler !


bande de feignasses !


On travaille depuis qu'on est petits


On travaille à l'école


on travaille au collège


on travaille au lycée


on travaille pour passer le bac


on travaille pour avoir un diplôme


on travaille pour en avoir un autre


on travaille pour payer son loyer


on travaille pour manger


on travaille pour avoir le droit de continuer à travailler


Et quand on n'a plus de travail


on travaille à en chercher


Les jeunes ne veulent plus travailler


ils préfèrent rester chez eux


à ne rien faire


ils n'ont plus le goût de l'effort


Ils se lèvent à cinq heures


pour bloquer leur lycée


ils fabriquent des pancartes


ils tiennent des assemblées


ils prennent les transports


ils marchent toute la journée


week-end compris


Et il y a toujours quelqu'un dans


les commentaires


pour écrire


Allez travailler !


LE MOUVEMENT S'ESSOUFLE


Une vieille dame de quatre-vingt-sept ans a refusé de quitter son appartement


Elle y vivait depuis soixante et onze ans


La police est venue la chercher


Elle s'appelait Maricarmen


Elle avait résisté à quatre tentatives d'expulsion


Cette fois, ils ont réussi


Elle est morte deux semaines plus tard


À Jakarta, un livreur à moto est mort écrasé par un véhicule de police


À Katmandou, les manifestations contre la corruption ont fait tomber le gouvernement


À Tirana, des étudiants mettent le feu au ministère de l'Éducation


Les flamants roses défendent leur lagune contre le gendre de Trump


En Kanaky, on refuse que Paris décide qui a le droit de voter


En Martinique, on manifeste contre le prix de la nourriture


Au Maroc, Gen Z 212 réclame écoles, hôpitaux, dignité


Au Pérou, on descend dans la rue contre une réforme des retraites


À Rio aussi, on descend


Un drapeau de pirate apparaît au-dessus d'une foule


Puis d'une autre


Chapeaux de paille, Spider-Man & Under Armor


À Hong Kong, des parapluies contre les lacrymos


Des lasers pour aveugler les caméras


Les robocops avancent


Ça charge, ça court, ça revient


Des pavés volent


Les robocops reculent


Les journalistes demandent si on condamne les violences


Gen Z de merde !


Terroristes !


Agents étrangers !


Parasites !


En Inde, on fonde le Parti des cafards


Pas la même langue ? Who cares ?


Dans les cortèges français, on chante en italien


À Berlin et à Turin, ça scande « Tout le monde déteste la police »


Génération Tasty Crousty polyglotte


Six seven six seven


Les ministres annoncent que le mouvement s'essouffle


On nous disait enfermés dans nos écrans


Voilà qu'on nous reproche d'être dehors


QUITTER L'ÉPOQUE CONTEMPORAINE


On a appris l'Antiquité


On a appris le Moyen Âge


On a appris l'époque moderne


L'époque contemporaine


On va vous apprendre comment elle finit …

author: Unknown
title: Trino Vercellese: un caso simbolo del tandem data center, nucleare e bolla speculativa
content:
Riportiamo parte degli interventi della serata informativa organizzata da


Legambiente del Vercellese e della Valsesia – gruppo di Trino


il 16 ottobre 2026 a Trino alla quale abbiamo partecipato, in modo da fissare alcuni concetti chiave nell’approcciarsi a questo terreno. 


I PARTE Domanda energetica fuori dalla realtà 


1.1 Dal reattore al Data Center 


Ad aprire l’incontro è stato Fausto Cognasso, già membro del

comitato TriNO

 contro l’installazione del Deposito nucleare nazionale nella pianura risicola vercellese. Il suo intervento è servito a confrontare la narrativa istituzionale sul

Cavour Hyperscale Campus

 (CHC) con i rischi reali per il territorio legati alla realizzazione del progetto.


Del CHC si parla infatti solo in termini entusiastici. 400 MW di potenza di calcolo, 4 miliardi di euro di investimento, importanti ricadute occupazionali: un rilancio economico a tutto campo. Ma né dentro né fuori dalle sale comunali si è ancora avuto un vero confronto politico sul progetto.


Il silenzio ufficiale lascia al momento sospese questioni decisive per la valutazione del CHC da parte del territorio. Ad esempio, il

campus

 potrà affidarsi a fonti rinnovabili per le sue esigenze energetiche? O si dovrà piuttosto ricorrere al nucleare, come ha lasciato intendere l’assessore all’Ambiente della Regione Piemonte Marnati? C’è il rischio che i costi di adeguamento della rete elettrica alla proliferazione di data center in Lombardia e Piemonte vengano scaricati sui cittadini attraverso un aumento in bolletta? L’insediamento di un data center potrebbe dare luogo o esasperare fenomeni di isole di calore? E se, come dovrebbe avvenire nel caso del CHC a Trino, i

server

 non saranno raffreddati ad acqua, si userà allora un liquido refrigerante a base di PFAS? I rischi legati a questi “inquinanti eterni” sono stati opportunamente valutati?


Colmare il vuoto d’informazione


In merito a questa ondata di data center che si sta abbattendo sul nord Italia, l’opacità rilevata anche a Trino in merito al progetto del CHC è la regola: comitati, associazioni, stampa indipendente e cittadini si stanno mobilitando per “coprire il deficit di informazione e democrazia”.


Ad esempio, il nesso tra crescita della produzione di PFAS e accelerazione sui data center per le necessità dell’intelligenza artificiale è un fatto assodato. In un

report

 pubblicato dalla ONG svedese ChemSec viene illustrato come dai piani industriali dei primi dieci grandi produttori mondiali di PFAS emerga l’intento di espandere la produzione dei composti in risposta alla crescita esponenziale del settore

tech

. Come abbiamo accennato, nel caso dei data center i PFAS entrano in gioco per il raffreddamento in quanto necessari ai liquidi refrigeranti alternativi all’uso di acqua o aria fredda. Queste moderne tecnologie di raffreddamento dipendenti dai PFAS vengono tipicamente impiegate negli

hyperscaler

 come il CHC. Il colosso francese dei materiali Arkema, ad esempio, ha inaugurato in Kentucky uno stabilimento da circa 60 milioni di dollari per la produzione del gas HFO R1233Z, refrigerante di largo impiego e utilizzato anche nei data center per il raffreddamento dei server.


Quanto alle ricadute occupazionali, resta da capire se artigiani e imprese locali abbiano effettivamente le competenze per lavorare a una struttura come il CHC. Nel caso della centrale Galileo Ferraris, ad esempio, gran parte dell’imprenditoria locale dovette accontentarsi di subappalti marginali.


Sul piano amministrativo il coinvolgimento del territorio è completamente assente. La dichiarazione di interesse strategico nazionale approvata recentemente dal Consiglio dei Ministri per il CHC comporta la nomina di un Commissario straordinario di governo, incaricato di garantire la “tempestiva realizzazione dell’investimento”. L’iter ordinario, che pur essendo più laborioso offre maggiori tutele per il territorio e le comunità che lo abitano, qui dovrebbe lasciare il posto a un’autorizzazione unica, pensata per accelerare i tempi e offrire certezze a chi muove i capitali. Come in altri casi di grandi opere imposte dall’alto, il rischio è che la pianificazione urbanistica locale ne esca subordinata a interessi di mercato e politica di palazzo. Tanto più grave risulterebbe in questo quadro l’assenza di dibattito pubblico fin dalle fasi preliminari del progetto.


La concentrazione di data center, di vecchie centrali atomiche non ancora dismesse e depositi nucleari su aree …

author: PETA-Team
title: PETA Vegan Award 2027 – jetzt bewerben für den Bereich Food
content:
Immer mehr Menschen entscheiden sich für eine

vegane Lebens-

 und

Ernährungsweise

. Zudem greifen auch vermehrt Menschen auf vegane Alternativen zurück, die sich

vegetarisch

,

pescetarisch

 oder omnivor ernähren. Um der wachsenden Nachfrage in dieser Branche gerecht zu werden, bieten mittlerweile zahlreiche Marken und Unternehmen vegane Produkte an.


Um diese bemerkenswerte Entwicklung hin zu mehr Tierschutz durch ein zunehmendes veganes Produktangebot in der Ernährungsindustrie zu würdigen, verleihen wir von PETA Deutschland jährlich den

PETA Vegan Award im Bereich Food

.


Der PETA Vegan Award im Bereich Food


Mit unserer jährlichen Auszeichnung werden tierfreundliche vegane Lebensmittel wie Alternativen zu verschiedensten Milch-, Eier- und Fleischprodukten sowie Snacks und Fertiggerichte prämiert.Wir zeichnen zudem Produktreihen, Sortimente und Supermärkte für ihren Beitrag aus, eine vegane Ernährung in der Gesellschaft zu etablieren.


Der PETA Vegan Award ermöglicht den Gewinnern eine deutschlandweite, reichweitenstarke Plattform, um ihre herausragenden Produkte zu präsentieren, die vegan und tierfreundlich sind.


„Mit dem PETA Vegan Award im Bereich Food 2027 wollen wir zeigen,, dass tierfreie Innovationen nicht nur die Zukunft der Ernährung prägen, sondern auch Spaß machen, inspirieren und positive Veränderungen für Tiere, Menschen und unseren Planeten bewirken können. Jetzt ist die Zeit, eure Ideen sichtbar zu machen!“

Tobias Schalyo, Senior Corporate Engagement Manager bei PETA Deutschland


In den vergangenen Jahren wurden bereits Unternehmen und Marken wie LIDL mit der Eigenmarke VEMONDO, die Fleischalternativen von GREEN MOUNTAIN, Fischalternativen von UNFISHED, der Haferblock von THE VEGAN COW als Butteralternative und MAGNUM für sein veganes Angebot an Eis mit der heißbegehrten Auszeichnung gewürdigt.


		Jetzt bewerben


In diesen Kategorien werden Awards vergeben


Für den PETA Vegan Award 2027 im Bereich Food gibt es zwölf klar definierte Hauptkategorien. Pro Kategorie wird grundsätzlich maximal ein Award vergeben. So schaffen wir mehr Exklusivität der eingereichten Produkte.


Die Kategorien umfassen:


Beste vegane Innovation


Beste vegane Fleisch- oder Wurstalternative


Beste vegane Fisch- oder Meeresfrüchtealternative


Beste vegane Käsealternative


Beste vegane Milch- oder Joghurtalternative


Bestes veganes Frühstücksprodukt oder bester Aufstrich


Bestes veganes Convenience-Produkt


Bester veganer herzhafter Snack


Beste vegane Süßigkeit oder bestes Dessert


Beste vegane Sauce, bester Dip oder beste Würze


Bestes veganes Getränk


Bestes veganes Protein- oder Functional-Food-Produkt


Zusätzlich können bis zu zwei jährlich wechselnde Kategorien hinzukommen, sofern ausreichend qualifizierte Einreichungen vorliegen.


Unser Auswahl- und Bewertungsverfahren


Sie möchten ein Produkt für den PETA Vegan Award einreichen? Dann füllen Sie zunächst unser

Bewerbungsformular

 aus. Voraussetzung für die Teilnahme ist, dass das Produkt vollständig vegan ist und die Teilnahmebedingungen erfüllt.


Die eingereichten Produkte werden anschließend anhand dieser einheitlichen Bewertungsmatrix von unserer Jury beurteilt:


Geschmack, Textur und sensorische Qualität:

 30 %


Innovationsgrad:

 20 %


Potenzial, tierische Produkte zu ersetzen:

 20 %


Alltagstauglichkeit und Marktzugang:

 15 %


Nachhaltigkeit:

 10 %


Transparente und glaubwürdige Kommunikation:

 5 %

title: Συγκέντρωση – πορεία για την αποτροπή έξωσης σε ζευγάρι ηλικιωμένων, Δευτέρα 2/11, στις 18.00, οδός Καππαδοκίας 64, Κάτω Τούμπα
content:
“Από το πρωί σήμερα, Δευτέρα 2/11, πραγματοποιείται συγκέντρωση από δεκάδες αλληλέγγυους/ες για την αποτροπή έξωσης ηλικιωμένου ζευγαριού με προβλήματα υγείας (ο ένας εκ των οποίων καρκινοπαθής) που επιβιώνουν με μια μικρή σύνταξη.


Το σπίτι κατασχέθηκε λόγω αδυναμίας αποπληρωμής δανείου που αφορά άλλη οικεία συγγενικού προσώπου και αποκτήθηκε από τον νέο ιδιοκτήτη (εταιρία Real Estate) με πολυ μικρό ποσό, ενώ τώρα ετοιμάζεται να το βγάλει στο σφυρί για καθαρό κέρδος.


Οι νέοι ιδιοκτήτες/διαχειριστές του σπιτιού φάνηκαν ανένδοτοι στα αιτήματα αναβολής της έξωσης και επιμένουν στην αλλαγή της κλειδαριάς σήμερα. Κλήθηκε δικαστική επιμελήτρια η οποία μάλιστα προσπάθησε να εισέλθει στον χώρο.


Μοναδική ασπίδα προστασίας για τη κατοικία του ηλικιωμένου ζευγαριού μέχρι στιγμής αποτελεί ο συγκεντρωμένος αλληλέγγυος κόσμος: Δεκάδες γείτονες, εργαζόμενοι/ες, συνδικάτα, μέλη πολιτικών οργανώσεων και η Ένωση Ενοικιαστ(ρι)ών Θεσσαλονίκης έχουν σπεύσει από τις 8 το πρωί έξω από το σπίτι.


Στις 18:00 καλείται πορεία γειτονιάς με αφετηρία το σπίτι στην οδό Καππαδοκίας 64 στην Κάτω Τούμπα.”


Καλέσματα:


Ένωση Ενοικιαστών/τριών Θεσσαλονίκης


ΝΑ ΣΤΑΜΑΤΗΣΕΙ Η ΕΞΩΣΗ ΣΤΗΝ ΚΑΤΩ ΤΟΥΜΠΑ – ΚΑΛΕΣΜΑ ΣΕ ΠΟΡΕΙΑ ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗΣ!


Η Ένωση Ενοικιαστ(ρι)ών Θεσσαλονίκης καλεί σε πορεία αλληλεγγύης για την υπεράσπιση της κατοικίας του ηλικιωμένου ζευγαριού, 77 και 75 ετών, που απειλείται με έξωση από fund, παρά τις εκκρεμείς δικαστικές προσφυγές.


Δεν θα επιτρέψουμε να πεταχτούν στον δρόμο δύο ηλικιωμένοι άνθρωποι για τα κέρδη των funds!


Καλούμε τη γειτονιά, τα σωματεία, τις συλλογικότητες και κάθε άνθρωπο να σταθεί στο πλευρό τους!


Σήμερα, Δευτέρα 2/11, στις 18:00


Καππαδοκίας 64, Κάτω Τούμπα


ΑΠΑΙΤΟΥΜΕ:


– Να σταματήσει τώρα η έξωση του ηλικιωμένου ζευγαριού στην Κάτω Τούμπα.


– Να κατοχυρωθεί η προστασία της πρώτης κατοικίας απέναντι σε τράπεζες, funds και servicers.


– Να μπει τέλος στις εξώσεις και τους πλειστηριασμούς που αφήνουν ανθρώπους χωρίς σπίτι.


– Καμία οικογένεια χωρίς σπίτι! Προσιτή, ασφαλής και αξιοπρεπής κατοικία για όλες και όλους.


Η ΣΤΕΓΗ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΜΑ, ΟΧΙ ΕΜΠΟΡΕΥΜΑ!


ΚΑΝΕΝΑΣ ΜΟΝΟΣ, ΚΑΜΙΑ ΜΟΝΗ!


Αυτόνομη Θύρα 10 – Ηρακλής


Σήμερα από τις 08:00 στην οδό Καππαδοκίας 64 στην κάτω Τούμπα, διαδραματιζεται ακόμα ένα περιστατικό στην Ελλάδα 2.0 για το οποίο θα έπρεπε να ντρεπομαστε όλοι που το επιτρέπουμε.


Ένας παππούς καρκινοπαθης με άνοια, 77 και μια γιαγιά 73 χρόνων πετιούνται έξω από το σπίτι τους γιατί έκαναν το έγκλημα να υπογράψουν ως τριτεγγυητες σε ένα δάνειο.


Οι δύο αυτοί άνθρωποι τυγχάνει να είναι ο παππούς και η γιαγιά δύο αδερφών μας και πλέον είναι παππούδες όλων μας!


Καλούμε όλο τον κόσμο του Ηρακλή να σπεύσει στο σημείο ώστε να εμποδίσουμε την όποια αρνητική εξέλιξη.


Στο μέλλον θα ντρεπομαστε που επιτρέψαμε να συμβαίνουν τέτοια περιστατικά στους χρόνους μας!


Διαρκής Αγώνας για την ταξική απελευθέρωση


Κάλεσμα σε πορεία γειτονιάς για την υπεράσπιση της λαϊκής κατοικίας στις 18:00, στο σπίτι του ηλικιωμένου ζευγαριού, Καππαδοκίας 64 | Η έξωση πάγωσε προς το παρόν με την κινητοποίηση και την αλληλεγγύη του λαού


Η μαζική συγκέντρωση από τα εργατικά σωματεία, την γειτονιά, τον αλληλέγγυο κόσμο αλλά και από οργανώσεις, κατάφεραν να αποτρέψουν προς το παρόν την έξωση. Χωρίς καμία εμπιστοσύνη στους δικαστικούς επιμελητές, τα funds, τα παντός τύπου κοράκια και την αστυνομία που επιτελεί τον ρόλο του μπράβου τους, παραμένουμε σε επαγρύπνηση και στήνουμε λαϊκό τοίχος προστασίας ενάντια στις εξώσεις. Η μία δικαστική επιμελήτρια, η οποία ήταν θρασύτατη, έφυγε μετά τις πιέσεις του κόσμου. Η άλλη παρέμεινε στο τέλος του δρόμου με τους μπάτσους. Στη συγκέντρωση παραμένει κόσμος και αλλάζει με βάρδιες. Παραμένουμε στο σημείο και καλούμε σε πορεία στις 18.00.


 Κατά τη διάρκεια της συγκέντρωσης μοιράστηκαν πόρτα-πόρτα ανακοινώσεις στην γειτονιά και μόνο μέσα σε 20 λεπτά βρέθηκαν άλλες 4 περιπτώσεις που τα σπίτια του λαού απειλούνται με πλειστηριασμούς. Υπενθυμίζουμε πως το ζευγάρι των ηλικιωμένων είναι πολιτικοί πρόσφυγες από την Τσεχοσλοβακια και ο 77 χρόνος είναι καρκινοπαθής υπό θεραπεία. Το fund μέσα στην λύσσα του στρέφεται κατά δύο κατοικιών: τόσο του σπιτιού του ζευγαριού όσο και εκείνο των παιδιών τους, επειδή ο πατέρας ήταν εγγυητής των δανείων.


 Οι πλειστηριασμοί και οι εξώσεις λαϊκών οικογενειών από την πρώτη τους κατοικία αποτελούν μια ακόμα πλευρά της συνολικής επίθεσης που δέχεται η εργατική τάξη και ο λαός. Την ώρα που οι μισθοί και οι συντάξεις δεν φτάνουν ούτε για τις στοιχειώδεις …

author: ROAPE
title: Africa on the map, but still off the table
content:
On 4 September 2026, the United Nations General Assembly adopted a non-binding resolution that might initially appear to belong to the relatively technical world of cartography. The resolution, “Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World’s Regions, Particularly Africa,” was introduced by Togo on behalf of the African Group and adopted by 164 countries, with one country voting against and six abstaining.


In presenting the resolution, Togo’s Foreign Minister Robert Dussey argued that maps are not merely technical tools: their repeated use in schools, the media and digital platforms shapes how people understand and visualise the world. The African Group argued that the Mercator projection, designed for specific purposes—especially maritime navigation—had become a general-purpose image of the world that visually minimises Africa and other regions near the Equator.


The delegation framed the initiative around scientific and educational accuracy, cognitive justice, historical memory and the equal dignity of peoples. It also stressed what the resolution would not do: condemn the Mercator projection, impose a single map for every use, alter borders or take a position on territorial claims. Instead, it encouraged the use of projections such as Equal Earth when comparing the relative areas of continents, alongside better teaching about the strengths and limitations of different projections.


The resolution encourages the use of equal-area map projections, including Equal Earth, particularly when the relative size of regions matters. It also highlights the implications of existing representations for geographical and cartographic literacy. Importantly, however, it does not replace the Mercator projection, redraw international borders or alter the legal status of any territory. So why does a map matter? And why now?


These questions are more significant than the technical debate over which projection should be used. The UN resolution opens a much larger question about who has historically possessed the authority to represent the world, whose knowledge becomes universal knowledge, and what happens when previously marginalised actors begin to challenge that authority.


Mercator Map versus Equal Earth (wikicommons)


The map is not the territory—but it shapes how the territory is imagined


Gerardus Mercator’s famous projection was first published in 1569. It was developed primarily as a tool for maritime navigation, as its preservation of angles and constant compass bearings made it particularly useful for sailors plotting routes across oceans. The projection was never intended to provide an accurate comparison of the relative size of continents. Its distortion, however, has had a long afterlife.


Because the Mercator projection increasingly enlarges landmasses as they move away from the Equator, Greenland can appear comparable in size to Africa, despite Africa being approximately fourteen times larger.There is therefore an important distinction to make. Mercator was not invented as a deliberate attempt to make Africa smaller. Its original purpose was navigational. The political question emerges from what happened afterwards: how a projection designed for a particular technical purpose became normalised as a general image of the world.


A cartographic choice made for navigation became, through repetition, an educational and cultural convention. Maps entered classrooms, atlases, newspapers, television graphics, websites and digital platforms. In doing so, they did more than provide geographical information. They participated in producing a particular visual imagination of the world. This is where cartography becomes political. Can a two-dimensional map ever be neutral?


From geographical distortion to cognitive hierarchy


The significance of the new

UN resolution

 therefore lies less in replacing one map with another than in recognising that representation itself has consequences. The resolution’s language is striking. It connects cartographic representation to education, perception and collective understanding, framing the correction of historical distortions as a matter of equitable representation. The UN Office of the Special Adviser on Africa has presented the initiative as an African-led effort to challenge the symbolic minimisation of the continent. But the tension remains.


If representation contributes to how societies imagine the world …

author: Doha Ali
title: There are no apolitical girls in war
content:
“Doha, come sit with us. We need to talk to you.”

I was 15 years old, had just finished high school, and was getting ready to start university in Sudan. My mother knocked on my bedroom door and asked me to come into the living room. My parents were waiting for me.

“We need you to understand something important,” my father began. “When you go to university, don’t talk about politics.”

I remember asking the only question that made sense to me. “What is politics?”

My father paused for a moment before answering. “Politics is the art of what is possible,” he said. “It’s how people pursue what they believe can be achieved.”

I stared at him, trying to make sense of words that felt much too big for a 15-year-old. Before he could explain any further, my mother interrupted him.

“No,” she said quickly. “Politics is what old people talk about.”

She looked directly at me. “You shouldn’t talk about it. Bad things can happen if you do.”

That was the lesson I understood.

Politics was dangerous.

Looking back, I realize that my parents were not trying to teach me politics. They were trying to teach me how to survive.

The conversation was not unique to me. My older brother had already had it. So had my sister. When I arrived at university, I discovered that almost all of my friends had grown up with some version of the same warning.

We learned where not to stand on campus. We learned to walk past the “political corners” without slowing down. We learned that curiosity could be mistaken for affiliation, and that sometimes the safest opinion was no opinion at all.

I became very good at being what I thought was an apolitical girl.

Even when I began working in human rights and activism, I carefully separated my work from politics. I spoke about dignity, equality, and justice, while convincing myself that these belonged to a different conversation altogether.

Looking back now, I smile at the contradiction.

What are human rights in a country where people are taught not to have opinions?

The 2019 revolution unsettled the belief I held all my life about avoiding politics.

Suddenly, politics escaped our living room.

For the first time in my life, I witnessed people debating it in cafés, on buses, in university hallways, and in the streets. Conversations that had once been whispered became public. My political realization was clearly shaped: politics does not belong to politicians; it belongs to all of us, and we can shape it together.

The streets became classrooms. Neighborhoods became places of organizing. Around me, people argued, dreamed, volunteered, fed each other, protected each other, and imagined a country that felt possible.

For the first time, I felt as though I had permission to talk politics without immediately looking over my shoulder.

But permission is not the same as understanding.

People often say that understanding the past helps us understand the future. Yet Sudan’s history felt less like a straight line than a circle: military rule, uprisings, coups, moments of hope, and promises that always seemed to collapse back into the familiar.

But the revolution changed something deeper than the government. It changed what those outside of institutional power believed they were capable of. I had never thought of myself as a political actor, but suddenly questions of how my neighborhood was organized, protected, and cared for felt like questions I could participate in answering. We were not simply demanding that someone else build a different Sudan; we were beginning to practice it ourselves.

Later, I came across the “Revolutionary Charter for Establishing People’s Power.” What stayed with me was not simply the language of a political document, but the idea behind it: that the people who had filled the streets could also become the people who shaped what came next.

Looking back, I wonder if that was what frightened those in power most: not simply that people were demanding change, but that they had discovered their own power to organize without waiting for permission — to build networks, provide care, protect their neighborhoods, and imagine political alternatives from below.

And perhaps this is what makes popular movements so threatening to systems built on concentrated power.

You can suppress a protest.

You can arrest a leader.

You can overthrow a government.

But what happens when people have already discovered that they have power together?

Then came the coup of 2021.

But the coup did not erase what …

author: Carine Kaneza Nantulya
title: Kenya’s 2027 Election: Time to Address the Warning Signs
content:
On August 16, 2026, hundreds of people armed with machetes, guns, and sticks

attacked

 a convoy carrying opposition politicians and supporters of the Linda Mwananchi movement in Homa Bay county, western Kenya. The attackers killed at least three people and beat and robbed journalists covering the violence. Witnesses said police officers were present but failed to contain the attacks. The incident was among

a series of violent attacks targeting civil society events and opposition gatherings

 in the months leading up to Kenya’s August 10, 2027, general elections. At least six people have reportedly been killed and dozens injured in these attacks, raising serious concerns about the safety of political participation as the campaign season gathers pace.


I returned to Nairobi, Kenya’s capital, where my colleagues and I have been speaking with people from different walks of life to understand how they view the political and human rights environment ahead of the 2027 elections for president and the National Assembly. President William Ruto is expected to seek a second term, while opposition parties and candidates have already begun mobilizing supporters at rallies across the country.


One conversation, with a 28-year-old woman, stayed with me.


“I will not vote in next year’s elections.”


Her words were clear and definitive. I asked her why.


“It is always the same. Our votes do not change anything.”


Another young woman sitting nearby offered a different perspective. We need to look beyond elections, she said, and ask what elections are supposed to achieve: ensuring that every vote counts, that people can participate freely, and that everyone—including women—can participate without fear.


Our conversations revealed a growing sense of anxiety about the elections, and a troubling lack of confidence that the institutions responsible for protecting people’s rights will be able to prevent violence and ensure accountability.


First, there is a palpable fear that the 2027 elections could be violent. Several people we met—including civil society actors, opposition members, grassroots organizers, and youth mobilizers—pointed

to recent violence at political rallies

 as early warning signs.


The violence in Homa Bay was repeatedly described as a turning point. For many, it signaled a deterioration in the political environment and raised concerns about what could lie ahead as campaigning intensifies.


Then there are the so-called “goons”—gangs, allegedly

mobilized or paid

 by politicians to disrupt political rallies, intimidate opponents, and engage in violence. I repeatedly asked interlocutors how best to describe this phenomenon.


Some drew parallels with the

Mungiki,

 an ethnic-based militia and criminal gang that has historically been mobilized for political violence and was entangled in Kenya’s electoral cycles. Opposition and civil society members described young people being mobilized or allegedly paid to disrupt rallies, intimidate political opponents, and influence political gatherings. Some alleged links to senior officials but provided no evidence. The consistency with which these allegations were raised points to a serious concern: the blurring of the lines between political violence, organized criminality, and the government security apparatus, underscoring the need for independent, impartial, and transparent investigations.


At the heart of these concerns is impunity. The

lack of accountability for past abuses

 has left many questioning whether state institutions will protect them or hold those responsible for the abuse accountable.


Some people we met questioned the role of the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights. Young people expressed doubts about the effectiveness of its statements and said it should do more. When we raised these concerns with commissioners, they cited constraints including inadequate funding and other significant capacity and resource limitations.


People also raised concerns about the

independence and effectiveness

 of other institutions responsible for protecting rights and ensuring electoral integrity, including the judiciary, the electoral commission and the Independent Policing Oversight Authority.


A young Gen Z leader described the contradiction between increased youth political engagement and growing fear. Despite young people mobilizing through protests and registering to vote, she told us: “We are all scared

.”

author: Abahlali_3
title: We mourn the loss of Des D’sa
content:
30 October 2026 Abahlali baseMjondolo press statement

We mourn the loss of Des D’Sa, father, uncle, grandfather, and a comrade to many

The death of Desmond D’Sa has plunged many people on the left in Durban and beyond, across numerous organisations, into shock and despair. Siyakhala ngo Des.

Comrade Des was a stalwart in the struggle against apartheid and was a well-known organiser who formed the South Durban Community Environmental Alliance (SDCEA), an environmental organisation that raised the concerns of families living in the oil- and gas-affected areas of Wentworth and the Bluff.

His activism and the fight against injustices did not end with environmental issues and it definitely did not end in Wentworth and the Bluff. Comrade Des fought against all forms of oppression and injustice, including gangsterism and the mining companies in rural areas, and supported everyone from fisherfolk to migrants and poor people, whether living in flats, hostels or shacks. He did not back down when struggle became dangerous. Comrade Des spoke fluent isiZulu and engaged everyone with the same respect.

He joined the first march against ANC councillor Yacoob Baig organised from Kennedy Road in 2005, which became part of the process towards the formation of our movement. He stood with our movement from the beginning, and was one of the few who never wavered in his support even when we were under severe attack and isolated.

Comrade Des was one of the founders of the Right to Know Campaign that fought fought against secrecy while promoting the right to information. He was also one of the founders of The Durban Coalition, which was first formed in response to the devastating floods of 2022. The Coalition, which unites community organisations across the city in a united front, is thriving today and is an important formation in the city.

We will miss Comrade Des so much. He was always on the side of the people. He was always so warm and kind. We always laughed when he was around.

We wish to thank his family for him. And wish to express our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and comrades.

It is so sad and devastating that you have left us. Till we meet again.

Hamba kahle Comrade Des D’Sa. Ubuyiqhawe.

author: Anele Mbi
title: Buffalo City’s broken houses and decades of empty promises
content:
A housing rectification project in Braelyn Extension 10 in Buffalo City Municipality (BCM) has left residents frustrated with the municipality’s failure to address severe structural faults.


Serious defects in the RD houses include cracked walls and roofs, leaking roofs, and inadequate foundations. Braelyn residents say they have repeatedly complained to the municipality, which has promised to rebuild the houses since 2004, but has taken no action until today, except for a laydown yard constructed by the sitting, ANC ward councillor, Mendi Wetsetse.


The stalled housing project intersects with service-delivery defects across the ward, including unpaved and potholed roads, poor refuse collection, and electricity shortages brought about by the growing Inkandla informal settlement.


Recently, President Cyril Ramaphosa authorised the Special Investigating Unit (SIU) to probe allegations of extensive corruption and maladministration of major BCM tenders.


According to Braelyn residents, talks about rectifying Braelyn Ext 10 RDP houses began before 2010. The then ward councillor, Thabo Myira, who served as a councillor between 2005 and 2010, confirmed the claim.


Media reports also indicate that in 2009, the then minister of human settlements, Tokyo Sexwale promised people living in faulty RDP houses in East London that their houses would be rebuilt. Today, councillor Wetsetse, who is campaigning for a third term in the upcoming local government election, promised to rectify the situation.


Housing defects


Ntombizanele Mabala, an 80-year-old pensioner, said since residents arrived in Braelyn in 1997, they have complained to councillors and the municipality about the poor condition of their houses, but their pleas were ignored. “These are not houses but hokkies. We have children and a family of six. Rain comes in from every direction – through the roof, the walls and underneath – because these houses have no foundations,” she said. “The councillor promised that the housing rectification process would begin before 4 November, but there are still no signs of work apart from a laydown-yard fence erected two years ago.”


Another pensioner, Nothembile Mqhayi, whose house was built below ground level, said her house floods when it rains. She showed

Elitsha

 a hole she had made at the bottom of a wall to let water that entered the house drain out.


The Mqhayi family had to make a hole in the wall to drain out water when the house floods.


Ziyanda Mpakantsho (42), who recently joined an EPWP project and earns R3,000 a month, said rectification is urgently needed because she lives with a sick and disabled person. “I grew up hearing that the cracks in the walls would be repaired, but many years have passed. These Braelyn houses have no proper foundations, so water leaks in when it rains. The houses have not been rectified because the money is being squandered,” she said.


Zama Thutha (70) said the government had not fixed the RDP houses because it was corrupt and unaccountable to voters. “Even the EPWP jobs created recently will end after the elections. Our system of government is capitalism, which puts profit before the needs of ordinary people,” he said.


Recurring delays and more promises


Responses from both the BCM and the Eastern Cape department of human settlements (DHS) are not only conflicting but also suggest the rectification process remains a false hope for Braelyn residents. When asked whether the municipality or its ward councillor has made any promises of rectification, the municipality said the provincial government is responsible for the rectification process.


“The Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality wishes to clarify that it does not currently run a municipal housing rectification programme; this falls outside local government funding allocations. What we can say is that the laydown yard established on-site remains a site-securing measure for future development once capital is allocated.”


The laydown yard is overgrown

.


The provincial DHS said that, despite the constitutional principle of cooperative governance that compels the various spheres of government to share information and support each other, implementation requires compliance with the necessary technical, administrative, planning, and budgetary processes. The department has not denied the fact that rectification has been recognised for several years.

title: From Mombasa to Yaoundé, the vision and the demand is for reparative justice
content:
Through WoMin’s work alongside African women organising against extractivism, against the drivers of the climate crisis and its impacts, the destruction of the commons through false solutions, unjust energy transitions (and generally a world order that serves a minority over the global majority), we have been asking: what is the full range of impacts and costs in the face of environmental and climate impacts? Who and whose work absorbs these impacts and costs? And what would repair mean from the perspective of women, their communities and the ecosystems they care for and are cared for at the frontline of the climate crisis, where centuries of continued systems of accumulation by dispossession and destruction meet?


Our experience shows us that reparations cannot simply be another form of compensation. They must confront the very systems producing the harm – extractivism, odious and illegitimate debt, colonial legacies, patriarchy, racism, and corporate power promoting more false solutions whose aim is not climate justice but profit. Reparations must indeed offer us all a real chance to build Pan African feminist futures that centre care, including the restoration of the commons, and the conditions that make life possible.


Connecting the “c-words” – colonialism to climate reparations


The recent

African Symposium on Climate Reparations

 in Mombasa, Kenya, started on that same note: “there is no “c-word” that we cannot bring into conversations on climate reparations”, argued a comrade in his opening remarks. And indeed, the current

climate disorder

1

 is a historical process, and Colonialism (the c-word that in other climate justice spaces some shy away from) is part and parcel of it. As is, we argue at WoMin, capitalism. What is more, not only do climate reparations need to address colonialism and neocolonialism, but also the solution to the climate crisis will not be found within capitalism. Or as Audre Lorde put it, “… the master’s tools will never dismantle the master’s house. They may allow us temporarily to beat him at his own game, but they will never enable us to bring about genuine change.”


Not only we need our own tools, but also a broad alliance, as broad, yet united in principles and analysis, as broad and urgent is the task ahead. And the symposium offered an important space to bring together many working for reparations across the continent and in the diaspora, in conversations navigated along four main tracks: rights of nature and ecosystems stewardship; finance, debt and tax justice; law and human rights; and lived realities from frontline communities.


And the timing matters. We are entering the Decade of Justice and Reparations for Africans and People of African Descent, while the debt crisis in Africa continues to exponentially grow and deepen climate vulnerability, false climate solutions continue to expand, further threatening the commons millions of Africans depend upon for their everyday subsistence, and the African Court considers an Advisory Opinion on States’ obligations in the climate crisis.


As powerful expressed in an

open letter

 which emerged from the symposium, a Pan African position and action plan for climate reparations is urgent, but it cannot be constructed only through states, legal and financial tools. Those at the frontlines absorbing the costs of extractivism, ecological destruction and climate disruption have to shape what counts as harm, what constitutes repair, and what must stop. And importantly, we need to organise at all levels the collective power to make repair possible.


African women united for climate justice and reparations


This was the task of the 4th

Women’s Climate Assembly

 (WCA) in Yaoundé, Cameroon, held in early October under the theme, “Our lands, our voices: African women united for climate justice and reparations!”. The Assembly convened over 75 women community leaders, activists, feminist organisations, civil society groups and allies from twelve countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Guinea-Conakry, Liberia, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Zambia.


Oh ancestors, watch over Africa and let everything return to Africa! If we are coveted today, if there are wars, it is because our ancestors bequeathed this land to us. They did not abuse its riches. They used them sustainably. So we ask our ancestors to guide us during this Assembly, so that peace and food …

author: Mada Masr
title: Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure
content:
Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was fined LE3 million by the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, which convicted her on charges of managing an unlicensed website, issuing an order for the website’s closure. Attalah was taken into custody after the issue of the ruling.


Tuesday’s session at the ninth circuit of the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, presided over by judge Mohamed Mubarak, was temporarily suspended for deliberations after Attalah’s defense counsel requested time to review the case file.


After the court returned from deliberations, the judge ordered the courtroom cleared of everyone except Attalah and her defense counsel, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights’ executive director Hossam Bahgat, who was also present, told Mada Masr. The room then filled with plainclothes officers and guards, with a National Security Agency officer in attendance, he added.


The presiding judge and a Supreme State Security Prosecution representative returned to the session and the judge announced that the court has decided to stand by its rejection of all the procedural arguments presented by the defense, including requests to bring in any documentation or hear any witnesses.


The judge then asked the defense team to present its plea. The counsel insisted that it would not submit a plea as long as its requests were unanswered by the court.


The judge then abruptly asked for a lawyer unknown to any member of the defense counsel to be brought in, “in a move that astonished all those present,” said Bahgat, and announced that the court decided to appoint a lawyer for Attalah.


At that point, all members of the defense counsel cried out to reject the court’s appointment of a lawyer when the eight chosen lawyers were present. Attalah herself spoke to say she did not accept the court-appointed lawyer acting on her behalf, an objection the judge refused to have recorded in the session’s minutes.


“In an even more shocking move,” said Bahgat, the judge himself began to log down the requests of the court-appointed lawyer, without the lawyer having said a word. The judge then read out the conviction amid shouts and protests from the defense counsel.


The judge sentenced Attalah to the maximum possible penalty: a LE3 million fine, the closure of Mada Masr’s website and the confiscation of its property.


Security personnel then surrounded Attalah, lifted her off the ground and took her out of the courtroom, where she remains in custody in the courthouse.

Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure

 first appeared on

Mada Masr
