author: AfricanFeminism
title: Morocco’s First Woman Prime Minister and the Terms of Freedom
content:
Something changes when a woman occupies an office men have treated as their natural inheritance. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri’s

appointment

 on 29 September 2026 makes that change visible in Morocco. For women whose competence is routinely scrutinised, the pleasure is neither naïve nor trivial.


But the woman forming a government and the woman labouring in the fields, raising children without pay and denied an equal share of her inheritance encounter power differently. Representation changes who governs; emancipation changes what all women have the power to do. That distinction shifts our attention from PM Mansouri’s gender to the politics of the centre-right

 Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM

)

, which she leads. Will its programme redistribute the resources and rights on which women’s freedom depends?


The history beneath the headline


Calling women’s leadership foreign to Morocco requires forgetting its history. Historian Osire Glacier

documents

 women’s authority long before the contemporary premiership. Kenza al Awrabiya, the Amazigh mother of Idris II, helped secure the Idrisid dynasty, founded in the late eighth century in what is now Morocco. Zaynab al Nafzawiyya influenced eleventh-century Almoravid politics around Aghmat, near Marrakech. Sayyida al Hurra governed Tétouan, a city in northern Morocco, during the sixteenth century. Khnata bint Bakkar intervened in eighteenth-century dynastic politics.


Across the region,

Dihya

 is remembered as an Amazigh queen who led resistance to the Arab conquest in the Aurès, in present-day Algeria, during the late seventh century. Tuareg oral tradition remembers

Tin Hinan

 as a queen and founding ancestress of noble lineages in the Ahaggar, in present-day southern Algeria.


These histories expose how male authority is made to appear natural. Fatima Mernissi’s

The Forgotten Queens of Islam


challenges that selective memory. Colonialism also reorganised authority: French Protectorate administrators

reshaped

 customary courts around imperial priorities. What survives as tradition can carry the history of political intervention. 


Religious interpretation can give exclusion another claim to permanence. Islamist and other conservative opponents invoke this

hadith

 against women’s political authority:


«لَنْ يُفْلِحَ قَوْمٌ وَلَّوْا أَمْرَهُمُ امْرَأَةً»


Usually translated as saying that a people governed by a woman will not prosper, it becomes a prohibition irrespective of her competence. Asma Lamrabet, a

Moroccan Islamic feminist thinker

, questions turning a

narration linked

 to Persia’s dynastic succession into a universal ban. She reads it against the Qur’anic Queen of Sheba, whose judgement demonstrates capable leadership. Her argument contests male authority’s claim to divine necessity.


PAM’s promises and its record


Women have long contested how authority is distributed within the family. Fatima Sadiqi

documents

the Union de l’Action Féminine’s 1992 million-signature campaign to reform the Moudawana, Morocco’s family code. The 2004 reform abolished wives’ duty of obedience but retained unequal inheritance and exceptions to the marriage age of eighteen. Proposals announced in December 2024 left fundamental equality demands unresolved. In October 2025, more than sixty civil society organisations and public figures

joined to call for comprehensive reform

. Rights in Morocco have advanced through organised demands, not the gender of an officeholder.


PAM, a centre-right party founded in 2008,

advocates

 social modernisation and positions itself against the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD). It entered government in 2021 alongside the National Rally of Independents and conservative nationalist Istiqlal. Opposition to Islamist conservatism, however, does not itself entail reforming the laws and economic conditions that subordinate women.


PAM’s

2026 programme

 promises improved widow pensions, childcare, safe transport, a women’s enterprise fund and labour inspection. The commitments leave inheritance equality, abortion reform and decriminalisation of consensual same sex relations unaddressed. Mansouri called for

banning child marriage

 without exceptions in 2024, yet PAM’s electoral programme

omits that commitment

. Employment can support independence, but a wage does not cancel criminalisation or unequal property rights. The programme leaves those constraints intact.


Even PAM’s narrow promise to increase …

author: ROAPE
title: The sports commercializers are in town
content:
Two recent stories from Kenya reflect the rapid growth, rising ambitions, and increasing commercialization and professionalization of East Africa’s sports sector.


In the first, Helios Sports and Entertainment Group, a private equity firm focused on the continent, teamed up with Zaria Group, fronted by former NBA executive

Masai Ujiri

, to build a $294 million sports and entertainment hub in Nairobi. Then, Oscar-winning actress Lupita Nyong’o

announced

 she was investing in Nairobi City Thunder, which plays in the Basketball Africa League (BAL).


A few days later, reports said Nyong’o’s investment in Nairobi City Thunder may kickstart further investment in the BAL and sports in Kenya. This was followed by

more bullish coverage

 of

further investment

. What do we make of all this? What analytical language and tools do we have to observe and account for these significant on-ground events and dynamics?


One thing is clear: sports and commerce in East Africa are forming ever closer ties in countries such as Kenya and Uganda, across sectors, from rugby, boxing, basketball, and football to athletics, golf, badminton, and motocross, and, lately, e-sports. Major companies, often foreign, attach their brand assets to

competitions

,

leagues

, events, teams, and

sports


champions

, with a wide range of promotional messages, causes, and sector representation (banking, insurance, telecommunications,

betting

 and real estate, food and beverages, and tires).


The media in these two countries run numerous pieces every month about sports sponsorship partnerships that are signed, announced,

renewed

, and upgraded (for example, in financial commitment). Weekends in Kampala and Nairobi during sports season are packed with competitions and events (including community and charity events), and the media again

reports

 on them, naming the sponsors prominently.


TV live coverage is increasing; viewers can join in for free or pay a fee (for example, to follow

boxing

 in Kampala or

rugby

 in Nairobi). Ugandan newspapers Daily Monitor and New Vision, or sports news website

Kawowo Sports

, for example, are full of articles, week after week, with headlines, pictures and stories about sport aspirations, achievement, triumphs, records, trophies, medals and rewards,

players’

 pride,

moves

 and

signings

, or various aspects of

fandom

. Thus, there is not just sports buzz (including participation among viewers/fans) but also commercial and media (including social media) interest.


Political

, including diplomatic, buzz also exists, with the governments of

Kenya

 and

Uganda

 regularly joining initiatives and events in varying roles and capacities, including supporting the hosting of major sports 

events

, national teams and champions competing at international events, and so on. Officially launching sports events and welcoming home athletes from competition elsewhere also get solid

media


coverage

, with officials, sponsors, national flags, and fans joining in. Representatives of international sports federations; prominent, popular, or small but growing international sports competitions; or well-known global sports leagues, clubs, and personalities visit their counterparts to talk, inspect, plan,

announce

, and so on.


Relatedly, both countries are also undertaking significant 

venue 

construction 

and repair. This is related especially to football (the upcoming AFCON 2027, hosted with Tanzania) but also to other sports (such as paddle), or other formats and purposes, such as

multi-function

 sports facilities for rent for leisure or competitive activity (non-professional competitions, for example), or sports venues in the

education

 sector for schoolchildren and students’ recreational and competitive activities.

Hamz

 Stadium in downtown Kampala is one

example

.


Significantly, the facilities upgrade and sport events, participation, commerce, and fandom buzz are also evident in viewing venues: the entertainment

bars

 and

clubs

 (even a

cinema

 venue) that

broadcast

 sports events, especially football (from the EPL to the World Cup and AFCON), some of them almost throughout the entire week; say, from Tuesday in EPL-heavy weeks; or the

venues

 (clubs, bars, shopping malls) that host live sports such as

boxing

 (professional and

celebrity

 fights) or

martial arts

.


These trends, dynamics, and transformations are part of the wider

African Sports Economy

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: St’át’imc Chiefs Council challenges Ottawa’s pipeline plans in court
content:
A group of First Nations in British Columbia announced they have filed a federal court application for a judicial review of the federal government’s decision to fast-track the proposed Pacific Link oil pipeline between Alberta and BC as a “project of national interest.” In a press conference held in Richmond B.C. this morning, members of the St’át’imc Chiefs Council — representing eleven Nations of the St’át’imc people (also known as Lilloee) —decried what they called a lack of consultation and stressed the need for the courts to slow the developmental process.

Chief Bonnie Adolph of the Sekw’el’was (Cayoose Creek) First Nation began by outlining threats to the salmon upon which her people rely. She said that when her community wrote to the Major Projects Office asking to be consulted about listing the project under the Build Canada Act, they were told since their land was not on the proposed pipeline route, the Crown would not consult with them.

“When we told the Major Projects Office their narrow geographic approach failed to account for downstream, interconnected and cumulative environmental risks to our inherent St’át’imc title and rights,” Adolph said, “We were told that we could send comments like any member of the public, but not as a First Nation whom the Crown had a legal [duty] to consult. This is not lawful, this is not constitutional, this is not consistent with the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous People.”

The salmon central to the lives of St’át’imc people are all over the waters threatened by an oil spill from the pipeline, said Chief Travis Peters from N’Quatqua (Anderson Lake) First Nation.

“The salmon we rely upon travel the Fraser Estuary and the Fraser River twice,” he explained. “Once, as juveniles heading out to the ocean, and [again] as adults returning home to spawn. There are salmon in the river system almost all year. The idea of the construction of new crude oil infrastructure in the heart of the Fraser River Estuary on unstable soil is terrifying.

“What happens if there’s an earthquake? What happens if the pipeline leaks? What happens if the tankers run aground?”

Peters noted that 100 First Nations signed the 2010 Save the Fraser Declaration, but “if anything, the health of the Fraser River salmon has only worsened since 2010. The cumulative impacts of climate change and development have become more severe.”

Chief Justin Kane from Ts’kw’aylaxw First Nation (formerly Pavilion Indian Band), who is also Chair for the St’át’imc Chiefs Council, said the Chiefs Council filed for a judicial review because the federal court failed to meet its constitutional duties to St’át’imc.

“We know this project could have serious, potentially catastrophic risks for our fishing rights and way of life,” he told media. “Salmon is part of who we are. It’s part of our identity. And we have the right to understand what those risks are and to be immediately consulted about whether they are actually working.”

The federal government forced the Chiefs’ hands, Kane said, by insisting that the only question is how — and not if — the project will go ahead.

“If this decision is not challenged in court,” Kane argued, “it sets a dangerous precedent all Canadians should be concerned about. It is foolhardy for the government to try to push through a project at breakneck speed without proper assessment and consultation. Canada is attempting to circumvent its own laws, and ours.”

He said Ottawa has said it would consult with First Nations later, despite the fact that the project is moving ahead.

“Because the Pacific Link is listed under the Building Canada Act,” he said, “the Act says it must be granted a conditional document that is deemed to be all environmental approvals for the project. How can the future of consultation be meaningful if the decision is already made?”

Hugh Braker is a member of Tseshaht First Nation on Vancouver Island as well as of the First Nations Summit Political Executive.

In his statement to media, Braker noted that Mark Carney has said repeatedly that taking action to protect against climate change is “a moral duty.”

“Those were his words,” Braker said. “And what’s he doing about it? He’s building a pipeline. Probably the worst thing he could do. Our prime minister wears a coat of hypocrisy. And he has to realize that. He has to realize that things like life expectancy are going down because of climate change.”

author: Jake Johnson
title: Mamdani Threatens Trump Admin With Legal Action Over ICE’s Use of Parking Lots
content:
Agents’ use of city parking lots to stage raids amounted to “unlawful commandeering” of public property, he asserted.

Agents’ use of city parking lots to stage raids amounted to “unlawful commandeering” of public property, he asserted.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday threatened the Trump administration with legal action over federal immigration agents’ use of city parking lots to stage raids, which the Democratic elected official said amounted to “unlawful commandeering” of public property.

“This use of city property in furtherance of federal immigration enforcement is unauthorized and is therefore illegal, endangers city residents, and sows fear among those who seek to access city property,” Mamdani wrote in a letter addressed to U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) acting director, David Venturella.

Mamdani’s letter notes that ICE agents have “reportedly parked their vehicles and conducted meetings in several city-owned, unstaffed parking lots” — including ones near a park and a city-run preschool.

“ICE has not secured any authorization from the city to use these lots for immigration enforcement. To be clear: the city does not authorize ICE using its property in this manner,” Mamdani wrote. “Parking lots connected to city parks are reserved for the safe use and enjoyment of New Yorkers and visitors who wish to use our parks. Use of these lots for other purposes, including ICE’s reported use of these lots, amounts to unauthorized activity on City property. Accordingly, you must immediately issue guidance to your agents prohibiting them from using any City lots to stage or conduct enforcement operations.”

Mamdani’s letter comes weeks after a plainclothes ICE agent shot a Dominican immigrant in the Bronx while his 5-year-old son was in the car, infuriating community members and intensifying pressure on the mayor to do everything in his power to remove the rogue agency from New York City.

“We know that ICE is rotten to its core,” Mamdani said after the shooting. The mayor has called on President Donald Trump to end all ICE operations in New York City and has demanded abolition of the agency, saying it is “making a mockery of what law and order is supposed to be.”

In mid-October, Mamdani and more than 100 other elected New York officials called on private parking lot owners to bar ICE agents from using their property.

“In solidarity with immigrant New Yorkers and in our shared commitment to the city we love, we ask that you do not rent, lend, or otherwise make your property available to ICE as a staging area for its enforcement operations,” reads the October 16 letter. “Make it known to ICE that it is not authorized to use your garages and lots.”

author: Kiara Green
title: What Rights Are at Stake in the Supreme Court’s 2026-27 Term?
content:
The US Supreme Court reconvened on October 5 for its 2026-27 term which concludes in June of 2027. Cases involving the rights of immigrants, rules governing elections, LGBTQIA rights, and more, stand at the forefront this term. The Court’s decisions could have significant consequences for how federal and state laws protect individual rights.

The Court begins this term with a 6–3 conservative majority. Three of the nine justices, Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett, were nominated by President Donald Trump. Recent decisions, including the overturning of Dobbs and rulings affecting the enforcement of the Voting Rights Act, have already reshaped the legal landscape. This term, the justices will consider additional disputes over voting regulations and the rights of young people.

Among these cases is Republican National Committee v. Mi Familia Vota, which is scheduled to be heard on December 8. The Court will decide whether Arizona can require proof of citizenship to register to vote and if the National Voter Registration Act prohibits Arizona from canceling the registrations of non-citizens within 90 days of a federal election.

Despite the lack of evidence of noncitizen voting, concerns about voter eligibility have led to policies that can create additional hurdles for eligible voters in Arizona, especially indigenous people. Arizona is home to one of the largest Indigenous reservations in the US, but was one of the last states to allow Indigenous people to vote.

Indigenous votes play a vital role in deciding the outcome of state and federal elections. In 2020, Indigenous voters from the Hopi and Navajo reservation cast nearly 60,000 votes.

The Supreme Court’s decision could affect how Arizona and other states administer voter registration and verify citizenship. It will also determine how federal law limits states’ authority to change voter registration records close to an election.

The Court will also hear International Partners for Ethical Care, Inc. v. Ferguson on December 7. The Administration has vilified the queer community spewing anti-trans and homophobic rhetoric in the name of religious freedom. The decision of this case will impact the livelihood of queer adolescents that struggle with their gender identity.

The case is challenging a Washington State law on whether runaway minors can seek access to gender-affirming care without parental permission. Ending gender-affirming care has been a top priority for the Trump administration pushing for hospitals to discriminate against patients based on gender orientation and identity. This pressure has led at least six hospitals to agree to refuse gender-affirming hormones and surgery for transgender young people and agreed to make payments to the federal government.

As the term continues, the Court’s decisions will shape how federal protections and state laws apply to voting access, family rights and LGBTQIA+ communities. Oral arguments will offer insight into the justices’ questions, but final rulings are expected later in the term.

The Supreme Court’s work affects people across the country, often in ways that reach beyond the specific parties involved in a case. As the midterm elections approach on November 3, make a plan to vote, bring friends, spread the word. For nonpartisan voter registration information, election dates and voting resources, visit Vote411.org/feminist.

author: Victoria Valenzuela
title: Incarcerated Los Angeles Youth Fought for the Right to Hug Their Parents — and Won
content:
This story was co-published with


Truthout

.


Mercedes Maradiaga sat across from her 19-year-old son in the Los Padrinos Juvenile Hall in Los Angeles in complete devastation. Her son had at that point been incarcerated at the prison for two years and she had visited him every weekend. But that day in September 2024 was especially hard because it was their first visit since he had been beaten by officers earlier that week in a space in the jail where there were no cameras. The guards had jumped on and kicked him, and he needed surgery for a torn ACL. All she wanted was to give him a hug and reassure him that she was there. However, because of the no-contact visit policies at Los Padrinos, she was unable to give him that comfort.


Even during birthdays and holidays, they weren’t allowed to embrace. The boy endured the jail’s horrible living conditions — including rat infestations and flooded toilets — but couldn’t hug his mom for a moment of escape.


“I couldn’t even let him know I’m here just with the little hug,” Maradiaga said. “It would have meant everything to him. It was sad, and I did that for four years.”


Los Padrinos had

reopened a year earlier

 in 2023, after being shut down in 2019 due to conditions that violated the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) standards, including abuses by staff. Six officers were criminally charged with

assault and child abuse

 for using pepper spray on several teenage girls. Reports

also cited a decreasing youth population

 as a factor for closure, yet staff

claimed to feel “outnumbered.”

 When Los Padrinos closed, youth were shuffled to another facility called Central Juvenile Hall — and then in 2023, that facility was closed down due to similar issues. Los Padrinos reopened, and just months later, the abuses restarted. In 2025,

30 officers were criminally charged

 by the California Attorney General with child endangerment and abuse, conspiracy, and battery for encouraging “gladiator fights” that pit youth against each other.


Olivia Shields, a justice transformation policy coordinator at Urban Peace Institute, described the constant closing and reopening of BSCC facilities as a “cycle of noncompliance.” Shields said the Los Angeles County Probation Department has ultimately failed with these maneuvers to address the core issue: unmet youth needs — which won’t be addressed through incarceration but through coordinated care in the form of individualized, robust support systems and resources.


“Rather than decarcerate these populations of young people and find community-based alternatives or step-downs for as many of them as possible, they basically shift the youth around from facility to facility to avoid noncompliance,” Shields said.


Long before the closing of Los Padrinos in 2019, the facility had a bad reputation among Angelenos. Maradiaga recalled hearing disturbing stories about the facility in the ’80s when she was a kid.


“I think it needs to be shut down,” Maradiaga said. “I think that there needs to be a better way for the youth. I don’t think locking them away from their family is the answer.”


The Appeal in Your Inbox


Subscribe to our newsletters for regular updates, analysis and context straight to your email.


          Sign Up


Barred From Basic Human Contact


When Ilana Parach, executive director and co-founder of

Hoops 4 Justice

, went inside Los Padrinos with a basketball and mentorship program, she quickly learned about what youth were facing inside. She felt it was important to give them a platform to express their needs directly, so she pivoted to working with them on legislation.


“They made a list of specific programs they wanted — resources for their families, reentry support,” Parach said. “At the bottom of that list, they wrote, ‘We want to hug our moms.’”


Incarcerated youth directly told her that one parent who hugged her son during a visit on his birthday then had her visit terminated and future visits suspended for two weeks. She said another youth was incarcerated for three years and had no choice but to watch his mother cry during the visits because she couldn’t hug him.


Contact visitation policies vary across California and are often left at the discretion of correctional officers. Parach said youth and staff both told her that Los Padrinos stopped allowing contact visits after the pandemic. Parach said that during meetings of the board of supervisors, she heard officers citing staffing shortages …

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: PWHL team leads hockey camp for female players in Iqaluit
content:
Forty-seven girls in Iqaluit trained with a professional women’s hockey team over the weekend.


From right, players Sophia Mearns, Mary Suvega, Olivia Sulurayok and Hazel Kilukishak, in the back, await their turn to get back onto the ice between drills at a Nunavut Ukpiit Hockey Association camp. (Photo by Lilli Akpaleeapik)


The Nunavut Ukpiit Hockey Association hosted the camp Friday to Sunday at the Arctic Winter Games Arena in collaboration with the Toronto Sceptres, a Professional Women’s Hockey League team.


Professional players Emma Woods, Raygan Kirk and Brooke Disher arrived in Iqaluit Friday with Kate Germain, their strength and conditioning coach, to lead the event.


This was Woods’ second time visiting the territory for a hockey camp.


“It’s just been great to work with all the girls,” said Woods, a forward for the Sceptres.


“You can just see they pay attention to everything we say, and you can see they’re learning throughout the weekend. Honestly it’s been such a treat coming up and working with this group.”


The players and coach led workouts at Aqsarniit Middle School, on-ice drills and scrimmages.


Creating a hockey camp for young girls was a big priority for association president Jesse Mike, who grew up in Iqaluit.


She remembers convincing a friend to join her on the ice at 11 years old so she wouldn’t be the only girl playing hockey with adults. Not only did Mike grow up with few other girls in the sport, she said, but there was also never a time in her career where she had an Inuk coach.


“Now these girls have no idea what it’s like to live in a world where hockey isn’t for them,” she said in an interview. “They can aspire to have a career that involves hockey and that’s a big part of why it’s important for us to have Inuit women as coaches, so that they can see themselves as coaches.”


The Nunavut Ukpiit Hockey Association hopes to continue programs similar to this throughout the year, Mike said.

author: Nick Manley
title: Kiri Radikal, Radikalisme, Hierarki, Kapitalisme, dan Pemerintahan
content:
Oleh:

Nick Manley

. Teks aslinya berjudul “

Radical Leftism, Radicalism, Hierarchy, Capitalism, and Government

”. Diterjemahkan ke dalam Bahasa Indonesia oleh Taratsa


Akademisi kiri, Corey Robin, baru-baru ini

menulis

tentang apa yang ia pandang sebagai karakter radikal CIO (Congress of Industrial Organizations) pada masa awal pembentukannya. Ia mengutip David Montgomery yang menjelaskan bahwa dalam konvensi tahunannya, CIO menyerukan:


Kelanjutan pengendalian pemerintah atas harga dan alokasi bahan-bahan produksi; “pengembangan energi atom untuk kepentingan sipil di bawah naungan Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa”; penyediaan perumahan oleh pemerintah untuk mengatasi kegagalan pasar dalam memenuhi kebutuhan mendesak para pekerja; serta perluasan jaminan sosial agar mencakup seluruh pekerja pertanian, pekerja rumah tangga, dan pekerja maritim, termasuk perlindungan kesehatan.


Tidak ada yang benar-benar radikal dari tuntutan-tuntutan tersebut. Pemerintahan merupakan institusi yang sudah sangat tua, begitu pula hierarki yang melekat di dalamnya. Penggunaan kekuatan agresif, kekerasan, pemaksaan, dan tekanan untuk memaksakan kehendaknya juga bukan hal baru dalam sejarah manusia. Kaum kiri non-anarkis atau non-libertarian sering kali tampak ingin mengganti hierarki kapitalisme korporat dengan hierarki pemerintahan. Inilah konsekuensi dari perencanaan terpusat atas harga dan alokasi sumber daya produktif. Pemerintah monopolistik yang mengendalikan produksi maupun harga tentu dapat dikategorikan sebagai perencana terpusat yang hierarkis dan bertumpu pada kekerasan.


Sebaliknya, anarkisme pasar libertarian kiri mengupayakan tatanan sosial yang horizontal, tempat hierarki diratakan semaksimal mungkin – bahkan dihilangkan sama sekali jika memungkinkan. Mewujudkan berbagai tuntutan di atas melalui pemerintahan justru membutuhkan struktur hierarki yang kuat. Bagaimanapun, pemerintahan adalah institusi kuno yang sejak awal lekat dengan kekuasaan dan kekerasan. Sulit untuk menemukan unsur radikal, setidaknya dalam hal sarana, pada beberapa tuntutan tersebut, apalagi jika keseluruhannya dilihat secara utuh.


Kiri radikal semestinya berangkat dari penolakan terhadap struktur kekuasaan hierarkis yang mengandalkan pemaksaan secara agresif, di mana pun struktur semacam itu berada. Bukan sekadar berusaha mengurangi watak koersif dan agresif dari institusi-institusi tersebut. Banyak kelompok kiri non-anarkis atau non-libertarian telah memberikan kontribusi yang patut diapresiasi dalam membatasi kekuasaan represif pemerintah. Namun, solusi yang benar-benar radikal adalah menghapuskan pemerintahan itu sendiri. Sebab, penggunaan segala bentuk pemaksaan agresif merupakan salah satu akar utama persoalan yang melekat pada institusi tersebut.


Tidak mengherankan jika struktur kekuasaan lain yang hierarkis dan bertumpu pada pemaksaan secara agresif, seperti kapitalisme, memiliki hubungan yang begitu erat dengan pemerintahan. Sejarah panjang pemberian berbagai fasilitas dan keuntungan oleh negara kepada korporasi (corporate welfare) menjadi salah satu buktinya. Namun, poin utama yang perlu ditekankan di sini adalah bahwa memperjuangkan penghapusan pemerintahan tidak berarti harus membebaskan kapitalisme dari kritik atau memberinya pembenaran begitu saja. Sebaliknya, penghapusan pemerintahan justru dapat menjadi bagian penting dari upaya membongkar kedua struktur kekuasaan yang menindas dan bertumpu pada pemaksaan tersebut. Mari kita mulai!

https://c4ss.org/dukung-c4ss.

author: By Dan Feidt, Unicorn Riot
title: Deep Dive: Minnesota 15 Case Reveals Range of Pervasive Surveillance
content:
St. Paul, MN – Looking closely at court filings around the “Minnesota 15” prosecution has revealed vast patterns of surveillance by federal agents, in Minnesota and beyond. We took a closer look at the summer’s largest set of filings, 30 main exhibits and several subsequent ones, to map out just how undercover operations,

facial recognition

, pole cameras, and other tactics played out. The project gives a sharp illustration of the cutting edge of America’s modern, lavishly funded surveillance state.


We did an in-depth

webinar-style recording

 going through all of

these defense exhibits

. Covering hundreds of pages of evidence, it’s around 100 minutes long. While it is an almost overwhelming level of detail, it is worth checking out to get a glimpse at both the breadth and the depth of how this campaign worked.


Watch the full report on

Vimeo

 or

YouTube

.


The prosecution of the Minnesota 15

(United States v. Sant, et al)

 has been playing out through the summer — one of the more high-profile politicized court cases Minnesota has seen in years. Unicorn Riot has

interviewed many defendants

 about their experiences getting raided.


ICE in Minnesota: 2025-2026


Federal prosecutor Brian W. Lynch, who

marched masked at the January 6 riot in Washington, DC,

 was integral to the Minnesota grand jury presentation of “The Conspiracy,” a foundational component of the Minnesota 15 prosecution.


Kieran F. Knutson, the president of Communication Workers of America Local 7250, told Unicorn Riot that the surveillance which targeted his union’s finances was part of an effort to “map out the resistance to ICE”:


“In my opinion the federal investigations should be seen as both an attack on and an effort to map out the resistance to ICE in Minnesota including the trade unions.


The Feds have a broad understanding of the different facets of the resistance and they have used these investigations as a means to map out the specific organizations, influential organizers, and networks of solidarity and collaborative activity.


The release of documents shows that this is not limited to investigating incidents involving ICE agents and protesters but is expansive to include unions and community groups that sponsored and organized the January 23rd Day of Truth & Freedom with No Work, No School, and No Shopping, including their finances.


This investigation started concurrent with the launching of Operation Metro Surge revealing its purpose as a counter-insurgency operation to, in the words of Commander Greg Bovino, ‘pacify this place’.


The unions – as a part of the active resistance to the illegal and deadly ICE operation – are an important target for the Federal government.”


Kieran F. Knutson, President CWA Local 7250


Federal Reserve wire transfer systems searched for CWA union, Sunrise Movement, and other data between January 1, 2023 and March 29, 2026.


Anti-Left Campaign Centered on Minnesota


Ali Winston in Wired pointed out that

ICE is running one of the largest anti-left surveillance campaigns in U.S. history

, and Minnesota is at the heart of it. By his count, 115 ICE-HSI agents were involved in the Minnesota 15 case, including several high-profile agents from other states. He also found a

spinoff surveillance campaign in Chicago

 in April 2026.


As Winston noted, Unicorn Riot’s previous

exposure of the confidential ICE-HSI Undercover Operations Handbook

 helps decode the concepts around their operation.


Attorneys for the Minnesota 15 filed documents showing that Operation Keyhole was a “certified undercover” (CUC) operation. On September 9, this forced

Minnesota U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen to disclose Keyhole has been in effect since late 2008

. “77 separate criminal investigations” were approved under Keyhole.


As of June 2026, five investigations including Whipple Shield were being supplied under Keyhole, according to Rosen. The point of including Operation Whipple Shield and Puppet Master in Keyhole was to enable “the use of CUC Keyhole funds to provide investigative support, such as funding the deployment of personnel and the acquisition of necessary equipment,” according to Rosen.

title: In the Crosshairs of the Far-Right Advance : An Update on Anti-Fascists and Anarchists in Greece
content:
Anarchist graffiti from Athens, Greece (2026)


The anarchist movement in Greece faces a new wave of repression. Urged on by the US and its obsession with combatting “far-left extremism,” the Greek state has targeted anti-authoritarians with new legal charges and attacked demonstrations, while fascists carry out street attacks and plot their return to the halls of power. Amidst a landscape of ongoing austerity, terrorism designations, lethal prisons, and ferocious wildfires, anarchists nonetheless continue to forge a combative culture of revolutionary solidarity.


In this article, we present an interview with an anarchist comrade in Athens assessing the current situation among anarchists and anti-fascists in Greece, along with analysis of the US’s role in advancing state repression and fantasies of Western supremacy.


The US and Greece: A Right-Wing Alliance to Defend “The West”


Earlier this month, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a speech at the Pnyx in Athens. With the historic Acropolis and the Parthenon—that ancient symbol of Western democracy, constructed with slave labor—in the background, he delivered a warning message to Greece’s political and business elite.


“The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world or resigns itself to a future of atrophy and servitude and decline,” Rubio cautioned. “We will either choose to act now or lose the choice to act at all.” Lamenting how “nationalism became a dirty word,” he called for renewed militarism, praised Christian faith and martyrdom, and announced a new counterterrorism information-sharing program between the two countries. His statements were calculated to reinforce the colonial legacy of Western dominance over the rest of the world, while urging the worst of Greek society to imitate America’s current political trajectory.


US Secretary of State Marco Rubio constructs an elaborate photo op for his defense of nationalism, militarism, and “the West” (October 7, 2026).


The speech came in the wake of a conference Rubio convened in July that aimed to coordinate intensified repression against “far-left extremism.” The following month, the US government imposed a “global terrorist” designation on the Italy-based

Autistici/Inventati (A/I) tech collective

, which operated the free publishing platform NoBlogs.org.


Greece’s right-wing politicians and business leaders benefiting from the country’s endless austerity measures are heeding Rubio’s call to preserve the hubris of the so-called West. Meanwhile, governments are collaborating to escalate repression against any truly revolutionary movements that challenge the world’s current status quo.


Greece’s strategic importance to Western powers is rooted in its symbolic status as the birthplace of “Western Civilization,” as well as its strategic location in the world today. The country offers the US access to four military sites, including a dedicated Navy base in Crete’s Souda Bay. Those with a longer memory have not forgotten how the US supplied napalm to Greece’s fascist forces, who worked with the Nazis during World War II and later with the British and US in a Cold War anti-communist alliance. Fascists dropped American napalm on Greek partisan resistance fighters during the civil war from 1946 to 1949, scorching bodies and charring forests, leaving the countryside scarred to this day.


More recently, the Greek people were pummeled by the 2008 global economic crisis, brought on in part by Wall Street firms such as Goldman Sachs that raked in immense profits while destabilizing the world’s economy and immiserating millions. The US then contributed to the austerity measures imposed on Greece in 2010 by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), leading to years of ferocious resistance to neoliberal capitalism and government complicity.


Today, Greece’s current New Democracy regime upholds

the legacy of the brutal military junta

Despite its nationalist rhetoric, the government continues to lick the boots of the US, crushing opposition in the streets and enforcing a never-ending precarity on the majority of Greece’s increasingly exhausted and numb population.

author: Dionne Phillips, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Utilizing beadwork, an artist encounters her mother’s history in the child ‘welfare’ record
content:
A closeup of Krystle Silverfox’s beadwork over her mother’s Sixties Scoop files, as shown in the display ‘Apprehension.’ Submitted image (cropped)


Krystle Silverfox uses straight lines of colourful beads to cover names, places and events recorded in her mother’s Sixties Scoop files. On the art pieces, printed headlines and handwritten notes remain with information relevant to the family’s journey in the child welfare system.


Apprehension,

 a body of work by Silverfox of Selkirk First Nation (Wolf Clan), is a multimedia display of her family’s archival documents and records. 


With colourful beads redacting personal information on the documents, Silverfox’s artwork represents a reclamation of traditions severed by countless Indigenous families during the Sixties Scoop.


Apprehension

 is on display at the 27th edition of Art Toronto from Oct. 29 to Nov. 1 at the Metro Toronto Convention Centre in downtown Tkarón:to. Pieces from

Apprehension,

 along with other artwork by Silverfox, are also set to be on view from Oct. 30 until Jan. 17, 2027 at the Two Rivers Gallery in “Prince George.”


A protection of family history


The Sixties Scoop term refers to the widespread removal of Indigenous children from their families and communities by child “welfare” authorities, who forced them into foster care or for adoption, often with non-Indigenous families. The Sixties Scoop Indigenous Society of Alberta describes removals – that separated children from their languages, cultures and communities – beginning in the mid-1950s and continuing through the 1980s.


“Canada’s” national Sixties Scoop class litigation, reached in 2017 and approved by the courts in 2018, aimed to provide eligible survivors with compensation to “support healing, wellness, education, language, culture and commemoration.” 


To apply for compensation under the settlement, Silverfox’s mother, a Sixties Scoop Survivor, submitted a freedom of information request to receive her records.


Her mother then gifted Silverfox about 280 pages of documents including health records, court documents and apprehension and social worker records.


A piece by Krystle Silverfox that’s part of an exhibition ‘Apprehension,’ now on display in Toronto. Submitted image


Silverfox worked for more than a year with the documents and tells IndigiNews that the redacted information includes people’s names, places and events recorded in her family’s files. What she covers varies from page to page. 


While she was working on the exhibition, she recalls taking time for herself and going for walks or discussing the findings with family members if they wanted to, but has “been giving this project a lot of space,” as the physical redaction has been very impactful.    


She said the documents are difficult to go through because the material is “reflecting this difficult family history.”


“That’s why it’s called

Apprehension

 because I have this apprehension towards working with this as a material,” Silverfox said.


She added that the documents she worked with included “actual apprehension records,” creating a layered creation journey.


For Silverfox, the beadwork acted as protection for her family’s history.


“But then I also think about the beadwork as a symbol of care. So taking care of these really difficult moments and protecting my family through the beadwork.”


Beading on paper


Silverfox has been beading since she was a child and now uses her beadwork to create these three-dimensional pieces in

Apprehension

 and previous artworks which also utilize other materials such as blankets, pennies and more. 


Silverfox says the works in

Apprehension

 are among her most demanding pieces. 


“It’s very challenging, to be honest. This is probably the most difficult project I’ve undertaken yet,” she said.


Silverfox has created other artwork with beads on images, including some of her

Distant Relatives

 collection, which featured multicoloured flowers and their leaves over images such as neon signs and landscapes from her travels. 


“I’m more used to beading curves than I am to bead straight lines, so it’s been really challenging,” she said about the creation of her new art pieces.


She notes that the works in

Apprehension

 were “more delicate” as they feature straight lines of beads purposefully covering personal information. 


While Silverfox had created beaded works in

Distant Relatives

,

Apprehension

author: Valerie Anne
title: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Season 2 Trailer Has Sapphic Sex and Sad Exes
content:
Season one of The Hunting Wives was a wild ride, and I have a feeling season two is going to be even wilder. The full trailer dropped and it has me clapping and kicking my feet at the sapphic chaos about to descend upon us.

The trailer opens with Sophie’s husband asking if Sophie is “still dreaming about her” (“her” being Margo) and a few flashing scenes implies that yes, yes she is.

Other things we see flash by: a glam cowgirl photo shoot, Margo being manipulative to all kinds of people, and Callie being a sad ex and using a photo of Margo as target practice.

This show also knows exactly what it is and is leaning into it. For example, the song playing is Nancy Sinatra’s “Bang Bang”, which is the perfect backdrop for this trailer full of guns and sex and chaos. And the tagline for the season is “someone is going down,” which the narrator says while the visuals cut between a dead body and also a more…explicit interpretation of the phrase.

Based on how season one ended, I can’t wait to find out how Sophie ends up back in Margo’s bed (and her bubble bath!), and luckily we only have one month left to wait.

Check out the whole trailer here:

+ Bravo’s latest reality series looks like it’s channeling…The Hunting Wives in real life? Small Town Trouble: Texas, according to the trailer, features some women who are not-so-secretly hooking up with other women

+ Cara Delevingne once went on a bad date to a lesbian sex party that involved kitten heels

+ Actress Mary Beth Barone talks about Marissa and Alex from The O.C. being her bisexual awakening, her new comedy special, and the return of Overcompensating

+ Holland Taylor reflects on her time on Two and a Half Men, saying she didn’t re-sign her contract because they weren’t paying her enough—to which I say, good for her!

+ Chappell Roan’s fundraiser for LGBTQ+ youth, the Super Graphic Spectacular, featured artists like Fantasia Royale Gaga and MUNA

author: CMI Argentina
title: Despidos masivos en IOSFA: más de mil trabajadores de todo el país quedan en la calle
content:
La liquidación y el desmantelamiento del Instituto de Obra Social de las Fuerzas Armadas y de Seguridad (IOSFA) avanzan con consecuencias devastadoras para sus trabajadores y sus familias, denunciaron desde la Asociación de Trabajadores del Estado.


En el marco de la lucha nacional que el gremio está desarrollando en defensa de las funciones de la Obra Social de las Fuerzas Armadas y del Personal Civil (IOSFA/OSFA), en el marco de la cual

realizó una Jornada Nacional el último jueves

, la Seccional Rosario de ATE denunció hoy que el gobierno cierra la estructura de la obra social en Rosario, lo que afecta directamente a 60 estatales. En la ciudad de Santa Fe, capital provincial, otros 25 trabajadores enfrentan la pérdida de sus puestos laborales.


Esta situación se enmarca en un proceso que alcanza a más de 1.000 trabajadores de IOSFA en todo el país, muchos de ellos con décadas de antigüedad, que hoy quedan sin trabajo y sin reconocimiento por toda una vida de servicio a la institución.


Durante años, estos trabajadores fueron contratados mediante contratos sucesivos y renovaciones consecutivas que no les reconocían estabilidad laboral, pese a que en la práctica sostenían tareas permanentes y esenciales para el funcionamiento de la obra social. Hoy, esa modalidad de contratación se convierte en el argumento para desvincularlos, desconociendo décadas de trabajo y compromiso, denunciaron desde el gremio


Para ATE, no se trata solamente de una reorganización administrativa. Son miles de familias las que pierden su sustento. Son trabajadores que sostuvieron IOSFA durante años y que ahora enfrentan la incertidumbre y la desprotección.


Por eso el Sindicato exige respuestas, respeto por los derechos laborales y soluciones concretas para todos los trabajadores afectados.


La entrada

Despidos masivos en IOSFA: más de mil trabajadores de todo el país quedan en la calle

 se publicó primero en

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

.

author: anred
title: Nuevo intento para habilitar la megaminería en la meseta chubutense
content:
En un contexto de incremento de solicitudes de permisos de exploraciones de uranio en la Meseta de Chubut, con un gobierno provincial que ofrece nuestra cuenca uranífera al mundo, esta vez la iniciativa la habilitar la minería pareciera estar impulsada a través de la localidad de Paso de Indios. Los embates mineros aparecieron una y otra vez, el resultado fue el mismo: el rechazo social a la actividad. En ésta oportunidad, vecinos de Paso de Indios enviaron nota al gobernador Ignacio Torres con copia al presidente de la Legislatura de Chubut solicitando la reactivación del debate vinculado al desarrollo de la actividad minera en su localidad y en la Meseta Central. Sin embargo, el debate ya se hizo y se ratificó con la movilización popular en contra de la megaminería de diciembre de 2021, durante el denominado Chubutazo, que tiró por tierra la Ley que la habilitaba.

Por No a la Mina.


Decía un vecino de Esquel: “los embates mineros no se van a terminar, se repetirán como en ciclos porque las empresas mineras tienen tiempo y dinero”.


Una historia con varios capítulos y un mismo resultado


El

Plebiscito de Esquel

 del 23 de marzo de 2003, cuando

más del 81%

 de los vecinos le

dijo NO al Emprendimiento Minero Cordón Esquel

, tuvo como consecuencia la sanción de la

ex Ley Nº5001 (hoy, XVII Nº68)

 que

prohíbe la minería a “cielo abierto” y la utilización de cianuro

, siempre las empresas y los gobiernos han tratado de revertirlo utilizando diferentes estrategias que hasta hoy no han funcionado. La ausencia de licencia social se ha evidenciado en diferentes oportunidades a lo largo de éstos 23 años.


Transcurridos 5 años, en el

año 2008

, el entonces

Ministro Coordinador de Gabinete del gobierno de Das Neves,


Norberto Yahuar

, afirmaba:

“nosotros estamos avanzando con el desarrollo de lo que denominamos Meseta Central, … no solamente con el proyecto Navidad, sino estudios sobre las posibilidades de explotación del uranio, en la zona de Cerro Solo, en la zona de Paso de Indios”.

Ante la resistencia de las poblaciones cordilleranas a la minería metalífera a gran escala, la estrategia oficial consistía en virar la atención a proyectos en territorios que afectarían a comunidades de la Meseta Central de Chubut, una región más vulnerable e históricamente abandonada por los sucesivos gobiernos provinciales.


“Vamos a entrar por la Meseta” – Norberto Yahuar


La resistencia no surgió por generación espontánea sino fue producto de un trabajo colectivo e ininterrumpido de educación popular basado en información científica y la difusión de las experiencias de los impactos negativos de esta actividad extractiva exportadora sobre las comunidades afectadas a nivel mundial. La ecuación era siempre la misma, empresas ricas con pueblos empobrecidos.


Así fue que la conclusión que sacamos fue:


“La megaminería es sinónimo de SAQUEO y CONTAMINACIÓN” – Asamblea No a la Mina Esquel


La concientización sobre los riesgos de la actividad se extendió siguiendo el curso de nuestro Río Chubut que nace en la Cordillera, atraviesa la Meseta y desemboca en la Costa.


Ese fue el motivo por lo que en

junio del 2008

, en la

Embajada de Canadá

 el gobernador

Mario Das Neves

 decía a los empresarios interesados en la explotación de la mina de plata conocida como

Proyecto Navidad

:


“Hay que tener cuidado porque la gente está informada” – Mario Das Neves  


El proceso de información y difusión de los vecinos demoró casi 10 años hasta lograr la

conformación de la Unión de Asambleas de Comunidades Chubutenses (UACCh)

 que se oponen a la megaminería.


En

junio del 2012

 durante la gobernación de

Martín Buzzi

 se intenta aprobar sin éxito el

Marco Regulatorio Minero

 que tempranamente genera el rechazo de las

Asambleas Patagónicas

 manifestando:

“Cualquiera sea el marco regulatorio en cuestión, exigimos la prohibición de la minería a cielo abierto, por lixiviación o flotación, y la utilización de cianuros, ácido sulfúrico, xantatos y cualquier otro reactivo tóxico, peligroso o susceptible de serlo, que se use en la actividad extractiva.” 

Cabe recordar, el ataque violento que sufrieron los integrantes de las asambleas que se oponían a la sanción de esta norma en las inmediaciones del Legislatura de Chubut por parte de un grupo perteneciente a la

UOCRA. 


Ante la necesidad de contar con una Ley más protectora que la 5001, la

 UACCh

 decide utilizar una herramienta de democracia semidirecta presentando un …

title: O som das conchas ameaçadas
content:
Fui convidada para um casamento no território Rikbaktsa, na região de Brasnorte, Mato Grosso. A noiva não usaria véu, grinalda ou vestido branco, e o noivo não vestiria terno. O enlace, no entanto, seria cercado de ritos, vestes de fibra e comidas tradicionais, como a xixá e o mingau.


A cerimônia gira em torno de uma peça muito importante: o colar tutãra. A tradição dita que a madrinha use o adorno, guiando os noivos até a casa onde a celebração será realizada. O trajeto é feito à noite ou de madrugada, enquanto o som das conchas anuncia o matrimônio para o restante da aldeia.


O colar tutãra, sagrado para os indígenas Rikbaktsa, pode ser visto nas costas das mulheres


Na prática, porém, não cheguei a presenciar a união. Realizar o casamento tradicional tornou-se um desafio para a comunidade, que hoje esbarra na dificuldade de encontrar as conchas que formam a joia. Retirada exclusivamente das águas do rio Arinos, a matéria-prima do tutãra é esculpida no formato do peixe cará, que, segundo o professor Juarez Paimy, é o peixe-mãe na mitologia Rikbaktsa e o grande símbolo da origem do seu povo.


Conheci os detalhes sobre o casamento pelos relatos das comunicadoras Carol Rikbaktatsa e Lilian Rikbaktatsa, na Aldeia Cajueiro, durante o encerramento da Festa da Chuva. As duas tiveram um papel muito importante, registrando cada momento da festividade, que se estende por seis meses, até a sua finalização. Carol fez o acompanhamento contínuo captando fotos, vídeos e atuando na produção, enquanto Lilian cuidou da mobilização, também registrando o evento em imagens.


O colar existe graças ao rio Arinos (chamado de tutãra Itsik), único local onde o molusco que produz a concha é encontrado em jornadas de coleta que, segundo Lilian, chegam a exigir mais de dois dias de viagem. A integridade desse ecossistema, contudo, enfrenta a ameaça de grandes projetos de infraestrutura.


Conchas para montar o colar tutãra vem de um tipo de molusco encontrado no rio Arinos


Um deles foi a previsão de instalação da Usina Hidrelétrica Castanheira no rio Arinos e na bacia do rio Juruena — o Juruena corre para o norte após receber o Arinos, se juntando ao Teles Pires para formar o Tapajós. A gravidade das ameaças do projeto foi detalhada no estudo “Saber, Fazer, Existir: O Povo Rikbaktsa, o Tutãra e o Rio Tutãra Itsik”, elaborado pela antropóloga Adriana Athila para a Operação Amazônia Nativa (OPAN). A pesquisa foi encomendada em meio às discussões sobre os impactos da Hidrelétrica. Conforme aponta boletim da OPAN, o empreendimento em questão, agora arquivado, figurava entre 185 projetos com potencial de instalação na bacia do rio Juruena.


Estudo apontou 185 projetos que poderiam ser instalados no rio Juruena, onde vivem os Rikbaktsa


A antropóloga alerta que o Estudo e Relatório de Impacto Ambiental (EIA/RIMA) apresenta lacunas graves, omitindo avaliações sobre a dinâmica dos peixes, da água e do meio biótico. Esse descaso ameaça diretamente a reprodução do molusco Paxyodon syrmatophorus, que produz das conchas usadas no colar tutãra, prevendo-se o seu desaparecimento definitivo na área de coleta imemorial Rikbaktsa.


O estudo de Adriana Athila demonstra que o tutãra, uma das obras de arte plumária e eclética mais elaboradas das Américas, depende de uma complexa interconexão estruturada de comunidades e povos tradicionais. Diante disso, a antropóloga afirma que “nada disso é passível nem de restituição, nem de mitigação”, pois os recursos destruídos pela UHE Castanheira seriam consumidos de forma irreversível.


São as mulheres que portam o colar sagrado, além de serem quem puxa as danças, cantos e lideram os trabalhos


Um colar que simboliza a força das mulheres e da história indígena


A última grande festa havia sido realizada há seis anos, na aldeia Laranjal, no território Erikpatsa, embora tenha ocorrido uma outra celebração mais recente, em 2024, na aldeia Pé de Mutum, na Terra Indígena Japuíra. O grande diferencial de agora é a memória: não se tem registro visual dessas edições passadas, mas a deste ano estará documentada graças ao trabalho das comunicadoras em cada etapa do evento.


Esse esforço de registrar cada momento ganha ainda mais sentido diante da importância da festa para o povo. Sobre a importância de vivenciar e documentar essa extensa celebração, Carol destaca:


“A festa cultural é importante para nós porque valoriza a nossa cultura, mantém vivo o que a gente já vinha fazendo ao longo do tempo e fortalece a …

author: Nahuel Lag
title: El suelo como espejo de la relación entre humanidad y naturaleza
content:
Por Patricia Fernández y Lourdes Gil Cardeza*


Somos muchas las personas, organizaciones e instituciones que reconocemos estar atravesando una crisis civilizatoria muy profunda. Hay tantísima evidencia que muestra cómo estamos sobrepasando los límites físicos que permiten nuestra existencia en el planeta Tierra. Hay un área específica de la economía que lo estudia: la economía ecológica. El estilo de vida que impone la sociedad occidental implica calentamiento global, una creciente y continua contaminación de suelos y aguas, y el constante despojo de tierras a pueblos indígenas y campesinos debido al avance del modelo económico, que pone en jaque a los procesos biológicos de la vida que han ido coevolucionando desde hace, al menos, 460 millones de años, cuando empezó a desarrollarse la vida fuera del agua.


El suelo es un espejo de los vínculos que lo conforman. Es la resultante de la convivencia evolutiva entre la roca madre, el clima y los seres vivos. En otras palabras, el suelo es parte de los procesos del planeta Tierra, el suelo es vida, el suelo está vivo. Tanto su color oscuro característico como ese olorcito que percibimos corresponden a la materia orgánica (componente fértil y vital del suelo), compuesta por los organismos vivos que lo habitan y por lo muerto en vía de descomposición que nutren de manera espiralada a los organismos y las plantas de las que nos alimentamos. El estilo de vida occidental pone en riesgo esa vitalidad.


El tipo de agricultura que domina al planeta no es un simple conjunto de técnicas para producir alimentos (y muchas veces commodities): es la materialización de una lógica de poder que entrelaza colonialismo, patriarcado y capitalismo. Así lo evidencian las voces críticas de pensadoras que ayer y hoy señalan cómo el avance sobre la tierra y la naturaleza es un reflejo de la misma lógica de dominación ejercida sobre los cuerpos de las mujeres y los territorios. Llegar a comprender la crisis o la degradación del suelo hoy, exige, en principio, desentrañar esta trama histórica y epistemológica que ha convertido a la naturaleza en un objeto de explotación ilimitada. 


Creemos que hacer el intento por desarmar esta trama (o trampa), es condición necesaria en el proceso de deconstrucción que elegimos, como dijo

Audre Lorde

, para transformar la ira en un proceso creativo. Con este texto buscamos traer a la actualidad, y a latinoamérica en particular, a Eve Balfour, una mujer de la aristocracia inglesa quien, con mucha claridad y simpleza, se atrevió a abordar temas invisibilizados en Europa y sus continentes colonizados, al publicar su libro

El Suelo Vivo

 (

The Living Soil

) en 1943. 


Foto: Matías sarlo - Minga


Esta tesis describe de manera sencilla los vínculos entre la salud humana y el cultivo de nuestros alimentos y pone la lupa en el suelo jerarquizando su rol como promotor de la salud toda. En palabras de Eve:

“La evidencia acumulada sobre la interrelación entre la vitalidad del suelo y la salud de las plantas, los animales y el ser humano es de tal importancia y de tan profundas implicancias que ya es hora de que el público en general tenga la oportunidad de estudiar y formarse su propio juicio al respecto”

.


La matriz del despojo


La crítica al modelo agrícola industrial debe partir de la constatación de que su origen no es meramente técnico, sino profundamente político. La antropóloga maya-kaqchikel

Aura Cumes

 sostiene que el patriarcado colonial llega desde Europa y se reconfigura en América para ejercer el sometimiento sobre las mujeres, las poblaciones indígenas y afrodescendientes convirtiéndolas en sujetos despojables y así validar la extracción del territorio y del cuerpo-territorio. Este proceso de dominación tuvo un pilar fundamental: la disociación del hombre respecto de la naturaleza, a la cual se feminizó para legitimar su conquista. "A partir de ello —explica Cumes— se atribuye la potestad de descubrirla, penetrarla, torturarla y convertirla en mercancía." 


Esta visión no es casual, sino que se fundamenta tanto en los textos bíblicos que otorgan al hombre el "señorío" sobre la creación como en el discurso científico que adoptó estos postulados como base de su conocimiento. En esta trama (o trampa), el capitalismo manifiesta la continuidad de las mismas lógicas que motorizaron al colonialismo al implementar la sustitución de ecosistemas enteros por una "biota mixta" europea (trigo, ganado vacuno, cerdos, malezas, microorganismos, personas) …

author: Rizomatica
title: Documental sobre el estallido social dirigido por María Teresa Larraín llega a la UCT el 5 de noviembre
content:
Cuerpos en Crisis sigue a cinco activistas durante el estallido social de 2019 y el proceso constituyente de 2021-2022 en Chile. La función es de entrada liberada y contará con un conversatorio abierto a la comunidad.


El jueves 5 de noviembre, a las 17:00 hrs, se presentará en Temuco Cuerpos en Crisis, el nuevo documental de la cineasta chileno-canadiense María Teresa Larraín. La actividad, de entrada liberada, se realizará en el Auditorio H2 del Campus San Francisco de la Universidad Católica de Temuco y es organizada por el Observatorio Ciudadano, con el patrocinio del Departamento de Sociología, Ciencia Política y Administración Pública de la UCT.


Tras la exhibición habrá un conversatorio con la directora y con la abogada y ex convencional constituyente mapuche Rosa Catrileo, moderado por Mabel Cobos, codirectora del Observatorio Ciudadano.


La película registra el estallido social de 2019 y el proceso constituyente a través de cinco activistas de los movimientos de la discapacidad, migrantes, diversidades sexo-genéricas y personas privadas de libertad. También participan integrantes de la Convención Constitucional, entre ellos tres mujeres indígenas, y personas que filmaron las calles con imágenes que nunca llegaron a la prensa oficial.


Larraín, ciega y residente en Toronto, dejó Chile tras el golpe de Estado de 1973. Comenzó a perder la vista durante el montaje de un documental anterior. Su primer largometraje independiente fue El Juicio de Pascual Pichun (2007), que retrata la historia de dos familias, la del lonko Pascual Pichun y la del terrateniente Agustín Figueroa, en lo que se conoció como uno de los juicios más emblemáticos de la historia de Chile. Su obra posterior incluye Niña Sombra (2016), sobre los vendedores ambulantes ciegos de la Alameda.


“Esta película es mi respuesta. Un homenaje a quienes perdieron la vida defendiendo un proceso transformador que me marcó para siempre”, afirma la directora.


Estrenada en 2025, Cuerpos en Crisis obtuvo el Premio a Mejor Film de la Diáspora en el Toronto International Nollywood Film Festival 2025, donde además fue nominada a Mejor Documental de Canadá, y fue nominada a Mejor Documental de Derechos Humanos en el Montreal Independent Film Festival 2026.


Tras su paso por Toronto y México, la película recorre Chile antes de su lanzamiento oficial en Sala K de Santiago el 27 de noviembre. En la región, además de Temuco, se exhibirá el 6 de noviembre en Saavedra (Ruka y Huerto Llelliuken, con integrantes de la comunidad mapuche KOLWE) y el 7 en Curarrehue (Aldea Intercultural Trawupeyüm).

author: Administrador
title: Preparativos Zapatistas para el Encuentro Abrazo con familias Buscadoras. Parte 3: CUIDAR, PROTEGER, GUARDAR
content:
Música: Meme del Real, «El mundo en que nací» Imágenes, edición y producción: Terci@s Compas Zapatistas

Compañeras Familias Buscadoras:

Les saluda el Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés, coordinador general de la Gira por la Vida – Capítulo México.

Pues les comento que seguimos preparándonos para el viaje que haremos para conocerlas, y escuchar y aprender de sus dolores y resistencia. Y para guardar su palabra en nuestros corazones y en nuestra memoria. Esperamos, de veras, aprender mucho de ustedes.

Acá donde estamos concentrados, de repente llueve mucho y hace frío. Está bien para quienes vienen en tierras frías, pero los de tierra caliente, pues sufren un poco porque no están hallados. A la lluvia todos estamos bien hallados, porque de por sí acá en las montañas del sureste mexicano llueve mucho. Montaña adentro, en las lomas y la selva, llueve hasta cuando no llueve.

Unas con frío, otras con calor, las comunidades zapatistas han mandado a prepararse a delegadas, delegados y 3 delegadoas. Hasta ahora 1530 según la cuenta. Tal vez baja la cantidad por enfermedades o asuntos familiares. Por ejemplo, una compañera se sintió mal, la atendieron y salió en el ultrasonido que trae cría en su panza. Tuvo que regresar, por razón de que estén bien ella y su pichito. Pero rápido, un compañero que le sabe a eso de los tacos (de hacerlos, no de comerlos; porque de comerlos todos, todas y todoas estamos muy bien entrenados), rápido dijo que él entra de relevo. Y sí lo aprobaron las comandantas y comandantes porque de por sí escucha las pláticas que se dan para prepararnos bien.

Aquí en el video les mostramos unas de nuestras preparaciones.

Sea toda la delegación completa, sea en las partes en que nos organizamos, nos preparamos para marchas si es que hay o para mítines que les dicen. En esas marchas, si es que se hacen, nuestra principal preocupación no es el rollo que digamos, sino cuidar, guardar y proteger a las familias buscadoras. O sea que no vamos a la bulla, a echar relajo, sino a escuchar su palabra. Y pues tenemos que ver de cuidarlas porque en su corazón tienen palabras fuertes, duras, que enseñan y orientan en la lucha por la vida.

Y sabemos que aprenderemos porque llevamos nuestra libreta y nuestro lapicero. Y hasta computadoras y tabletas y celulares. Y van compañeras que les decimos “Tercias Compas” que le saben a eso de la cámara, la grabación, la edición y la transmisión de los encuentros. Pero lo más importante es que llevamos la cabeza, el corazón y las tripas con ganas de aprender.

Ahí pueden ver, en el video, que se ponen unas compañeras con sus pichitos como si fueran familias buscadoras marchando por verdad y justicia, y luego nuestra delegación o parte de nuestra delegación, camina a su lado y luego las envuelve en un como escudo.

Y hasta el Comando Palomitas practica de hacer el escudo que cuida, protege y guarda.

De por sí así nos enseñaron nuestros anteriores, que nos dijeron que somos guardianes y guardianas de la tierra, la madre más primera.

Como ven en las imágenes, con tanto lodo que se hace en las prácticas pues ya casi no es que marchamos, sino que como que nos deslizamos. Como patinando pues. Y luego pasa pues que la chancla se quedó atorada, o el tenis, y no se puede parar porque atrás viene la bola, el bulto de compas. Y entonces pues ni modos, hay que esperar a que termina la práctica para ir a buscar en el lodo, dónde es que quedó la chancla o el tenis. Y pues mientras andamos como chuchito renco.

Compañeras familias buscadoras:

No vamos a pasear. Vamos a abrazarlas si quieren, y si no, pues también vamos para oír su palabra.

Lo sabemos que hay gente que está mal hablando de la gira. Dividen, quieren decir quién sí y quién no puede reunirse con nosotros, o sea que quieren dejar fuera a otros grupos porque no se llevan, y cosas así. Ahí después, otro día, el Capitán Marcos les va a decir de eso hasta con nombres.

Por ahora sólo queremos mandarles nuestros respetos y cariño.

Desde las montañas del Sureste Mexicano. Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés. México, octubre del 2026.

author: CMI Argentina
title: El martirio de Nancy
content:
A Nancy Godoy el estado la dejó sola. Horas a caballo para llegar a su escuela, en medio de la nada, en el territorio de una estancia, que tenía dentro una escuela para sus peones. Llegó por primera vez y era una ruina. Lo denunció con detalles. La ignoraron. No llegó a cobrar un sueldo desde agosto. Apareció asesinada. Toda su lucha debió conocerse antes.


Por Silvana Melo


Nancy Godoy tenía ocho alumnos en una escuela pública dentro de una estancia. Es decir, en un territorio privado. Para llegar tenía que recorrer decenas de kilómetros de caminos rurales correntinos hasta ese punto de poder donde la alcanzaban hasta el paraje en el que un caballo la trasladaría durante tres horas para llegar a la escuela. Cruzando bañados, riachos y soledades escampadas que se volvían de una hostilidad imprevisible en caso de lluvias.


Tenía 52 años cuando ese 15 de agosto llegó a la escuela N° 626 del paraje El Malezal, en Esquina, Corrientes, para hacerse cargo de una suplencia. Era una casita desgastada, destruida, como si por ella hubiera pasado no sólo el tiempo, sino la desidia estatal y el desprecio privado.


Después de hacerse un panorama general de aquello a lo que se enfrentaba –suciedad extrema, ausencia de años de cualquier autoridad, falta de registros de todo tipo, situación sanitaria peligrosa, imposibilidad de habitar para ella, que debía quedarse la semana entera- el 15 de agosto escribió una carta manuscrita para enviar al ministerio de Educación de Corrientes. Y denunció cada detalle. Envió un expediente y sostuvo que la escuela estaba totalmente abandonada, sin agua, con inodoros llenos de tierra y ratas, que tuvo que acudir a una madre y a la baqueana que la acompañaba en el último tramo de su trayecto, María Rosa Leguizamón. En su casa tuvo que dormir las tres primeras noches porque la escuela era inhabitable. Esa misma mujer quedó involucrada después en la investigación por el crimen.


Decía que el techo se le caería encima, que las ventanas estaban rotas, que la humedad se comía el edificio, que las ratas y los murciélagos se habían apropiado de la casa, que el olor de sus heces era insoportable, que no había muebles suficientes, que los libros se habían mojado. Ella era docente, cocinera, portera y directora. Y era la responsable del edificio.


La carta que escribió Nancy a las autoridades educativas


Y la dejaron sola.


El estado la dejó sola. En medio de la nada, dentro de una estancia, en las manos de un propietario que hacía y deshacía, que tenía dentro de su propiedad una escuela para sus peones. Y ella debería comportarse como su maestra, directora, portera y cocinera. Con un sueldo pagado por el estado que la dejaba a la buena de dios. Sola de toda soledad.


Su denuncia fue ignorada por las autoridades educativas, sólo sostenida después de su desaparición por la comunidad de Esquina, sus docentes y su familia.


Pero esta lucha de ella debió conocerse antes de la tragedia.


No después. Cuando alguien la asesinó por el motivo que sea. Por ser mujer. Por ser maestra rural. Por tener coraje. Por denunciar.


Nancy se pasaba los días en esa escuela que tuvo que rehacer con sus manos y el fin de semana volvía con su familia. Sin señal de celular, sin comunicación de ningún tipo, su familia sabía que seguía viva cuando regresaba su sonrisa destruida por el cansancio. Pero aquel fin de semana no volvió. Y todo comenzó a volverse sombrío.


La dejaron sola. Tres horas a caballo y sin señal.


Apareció asesinada.


A metros del aula que había sabido reparar con sus manos, en la tapera del capataz, había ropa quemada.


Hay un estado que manda una trabajadora sola. A educar. Precarizada. A caballo. Sin señal de ningún tipo. Sin procurarle un transporte oficial. A que llegue como pueda. A una escuela en ruinas. Dentro de una propiedad de un estanciero. Ese estado cajonea su denuncia. Investiga su desaparición. Y la encuentra cuando fue asesinada.


En el territorio de la estancia El Curupí. En una escuela pública dentro de una zona privada.


El espacio Docentes Autoconvocados Corrientes – Sector 2019 aseguró que Nancy Godoy fue asesinada sin llegar a cobrar un solo sueldo a pesar de trabajar desde agosto.


A pesar del sacrificio para llegar. A pesar del desastre que encontró y del que nadie se hizo cargo. A pesar de que el docente que hacía años que no iba a la escuela seguía cobrando su salario.


Y ella fue asesinada por ser maestra en una escuela pública y tener que afrontar una realidad …

author: anred
title: La inminencia de una guerra de exterminio contra Irán
content:
La reanudación de la guerra contra Irán, por parte de Trump y Netanyahu, es probablemente una de las más anunciadas en la historia reciente. El primero viene advirtiendo que se encuentra totalmente preparada para después del martes próximo, cuando hayan pasado las elecciones de medio término en Estados Unidos. En cuanto al segundo, ha asegurado su posición como gobierno provisional por un tiempo no definido luego de que su coalición alcanzara el primer lugar en las elecciones recientes en Israel y el partido del primer ministro fuera el más votado de ella, aunque sin obtener los escaños suficientes para formar un nuevo gobierno. “Netanyahu puede lanzar una nueva campaña de bombardeos con Estados Unidos”, asegura el Financial Times, “mientras sirve como primer ministro provisional…” (29/10). “Netanyahu”, prosigue el diario, “había dado instrucciones a sus militares para preparar un campaña de bombardeos para el 10 de octubre, que tuvo que levantar por carecer del visto bueno de Trump”. De acuerdo a informaciones obtenidas por el diario, Gadi Eisenkot, un exjefe del ejército sionista, que encabezó la lista opositora que quedó detrás de Netanyahu, no pondría objeciones si fuera debidamente informado por los servicios de Seguridad de Israel. “Ahora, los jefes del Mossad y del Shin Bet son leales a Netanyahu”. La población israelí apoya en su mayoría una reanudación de la guerra.

Por

Jorge Altamira (Política Obrera).


Por otro lado, “los negociadores de Qatar han vuelto a Teherán en un último esfuerzo de mediación (…) para prevenir una intensa nueva ronda de guerra” (30/10). Trump exige que Irán transfiera al exterior el uranio enriquecido que guarda en sus centros de investigación, que no pudieron ser destruidos por los bombardeos en profundidad realizados por Estados Unidos el año pasado. Rusia se ha ofrecido para receptarlo, sin obtener el acuerdo de Trump. Mientras tanto, la flota norteamericana sigue ocupando los puertos de Irán y bloqueando las exportaciones de petróleo iraníes, y protege militarmente a las naves que transitan el Estrecho de Ormuz sin autorización de Irán. El gobierno y la Guardia Revolucionaria de Irán han respondido con ataques selectivos, en un esfuerzo por salvar a una tregua de hecho de su completo derrumbe. Con relación al stock nuclear, Irán aceptaría una reanudación de las inspecciones de la Agencia Internacional de Energía si Trump levanta el bloqueo a sus puertos, elimina las sanciones a su comercio internacional y retorna al estado iraní unos 25.000 millones de dólares secuestrados por Estados Unidos; es un reclamo que se ha ganado contra una guerra no provocada. La respuesta ha sido el despliegue en el Mediterráneo y en las mediaciones del Golfo Pérsico de varios portaviones norteamericanos, incluyendo un número de tropas disponibles para un desembarco. Dado el fracaso manifiesto del intento de imponer un cambio de régimen, a la venezolana u otra, el diseño sería una guerra que deje sin estructuras civiles a Irán, para asegurar una ulterior ocupación militar. Para esto debería producirse un aniquilamiento sin precedentes en el caso de un país de 90 millones de habitantes.


El gobierno de Irán ha respondido que se encuentra preparado para enfrentar una reanudación de la guerra y ha amenazado con una destrucción de activos norteamericanos en la región y fuera de ella, en la que ha incluido a los cables subterráneos y a los centros de datos de las compañías de Inteligencia Artificial, que en este momento han sido reducidas a la categoría de “basura” (Anthropic) en la calificación de las agencias de riesgo. Trump ha buscado cuidar sus espaldas suspendiendo las sanciones económicas contra Rusia para contrarrestar el aumento del precio del diesel y, probablemente, obtener el apoyo político de Putin, no solamente en la guerra europea; ha invitado a Putin a la reunión de presidentes del G-20 en Florida, en diciembre próximo. La reanudación de la guerra de Trump y Netanyahu contra Irán excede las fronteras del Medio Oriente; es también un medio para imponer sus objetivos a las potencias rivales y en especial a la Unión Europea. Trump y su agencia MAGA se encuentran promoviendo alianzas políticas con los fascismos históricos de Europa para forjar una ‘Internacional’ de ultraderecha bajo comando del imperialismo norteamericano.
