El Rapto. Observatorio del sonambulismo contemporáneo

 que en enero de 2012 dedicamos al 15M y su inaudita floración en la Puerta del Sol.


Quince años después el espectáculo consumista y turístico se enseñoreaba impúdicamente de lo que volvió a ser la más desoladora plaza dura, la gentrificación y la infame avaricia de los fondos buitre limpiaron las calles de vecinas y compañeros mientras que los cadáveres andantes del turismo de masas ocupaban el lugar de los espíritus errantes de la deriva, se recrudecía el aislamiento y la misantropía, y el orden volvió a reinar en Madrid como si nunca hubiera pasado nada.


Ciudad-mercancía aséptica e irreconocible, calles genéticamente modificadas, mutiladas y desinfectadas que, al parecer y así nos decían, volvían a ser suyas como en los viejos tiempos del fascio y el cilicio.


Y aunque sabíamos que volveríamos, y por eso nos empeñábamos en seguir invocando a la Ballena Blanca de la ciudad insurrecta, no acertábamos a imaginar cuándo y cómo.


Es que "la ciudad muere de vejez, o accidentalmente, o por suicido, incluso asesinada, pero nunca conserva su vida como una sola vida", observaba Eugenio Castro con la lucidez visionaria del que sabe porque ve y siente: y la ciudad muere “para revivir de sus muertes sucesivas”: y se reencuentra consigo misma y con sus habitantes enamorados en los lugares donde la poesía fue: porque “los hechos de la libertad que han acontecido en determinados momentos de la historia, se han depositado en el tiempo y en el espacio, y son latentemente revitalizados al ser frecuentados por los individuos en sus luchas personales y colectivas mediante un nuevo acontecer”.


Así Madrid rediviva.


Y así… 


 


                                                        

II


Y así una nueva ola de rebelión recorre España, una rebelión contra el capital pero también contra el Estado, o contra la complicidad y cohabitación miserable de capital y Estado. Consiga o no sus objetivos, sea con o sin esperanza, la rebelión ya ha cumplido su principal tarea: cuestionar y romper los límites de la dominación y abrir el horizonte de lo posible.


Lo posible: lo imposible: lo que no está escrito: lo que no nos permite escribir, pensar, soñar, desear: lo que a veces tememos escribir, pensar, soñar, desear: por hipocresía, por oportunismo, por cobardía: eso es el realismo: disfrazarse con los colores del ambiente: todo y cualquier realismo: realismo capitalista, realismo racionalizado, realismo de la prosa lógica y del manual de instrucciones técnicas y expertas, realismo de la costumbre caducada y el hábito mortuorio y la experiencia fosilizada: nuestro enemigo.


Y así el distanciamiento social se cuartea y la promiscuidad del roce y del encuentro resurge y se acaricia, las pasiones ardientes anulan a las tristes, y la divina sorpresa de la disponibilidad y la potencia del Único con la Comuna se insinúa en el horizonte utópico señalando el umbral de la otra parte donde todo se tendrá que poner en cuestión tarde o temprano …

author: ACG
title: Labour and the budget: same old same old (with a side of pickles)
content:
When Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey presented his budget on Wednesday October 28

th

 he said: “This is a Budget for the working people of Britain. For British businesses, big and small.”  Well, no. It offered little to working people, and plenty to businesses, to the military and to the defence industry.


We were offered the pittance of 86p a week off of electricity bills. In addition, there will be a £100 one-off winter fuel payment for 20 million households in council tax bands A to D. This will almost immediately be wiped out by a predicted rise by £276 in January, to just under £2,000 a year. Another forecast from the EDF energy company, predicted that it might rise higher than this.


Healey introduced a £2 cap on single bus fares in England from January 2027. But, for example, many workers and students in London cannot afford to live in inner London and must make long journeys by bus to get to work and study, because they cannot afford the rail and tube fares.


He also announced the end of gas standing charges, which will save a mere £45 a year, and then only for 60% of households. Healey had already announced that an extra £432 million would be spent on a programme to get rough sleepers in England off the streets. Unpaid carers would no longer lose all of their Carer’s Allowance if they earnt more than 1p over the £204 allowed and instead there would be a tapered payment.


On the other hand, Healey reassured the boss class by stating that he was committed to “prevent regulation from holding back investment by removing regulation and tariffs worth £800m to business.” The banks feared that the corporation tax surcharge would be raised by as much as 8 per cent. In fact, Healey only raised it by six per cent, and smarmed the banks by saying,” I celebrate and am grateful for the role you play”. In fact, this surcharge will only last for 15 months from January. As a result, share prices of the main UK banks increased, after the budget announcement.


The Financial Times, the bosses’ voice, enthusiastically noted that Healey and Burnham wanted to reassure business and the banks.


He promised an increase of £10 billion on economic and military support for Ukraine, in addition to the £25 billion already committed by previous Tory and Labour administrations. He would also make cuts in the budgets of various government departments by 1%to further fund defence spending. As a result, the Warm Homes Plan, would suffer a £1 billion cut. He promised a maximum amount of private investment in defence, including through public private partnerships.


Labour had promised to end discriminatory age bands and to increase the minimum wage for 18- to 20-year-olds to be the same as those over 21 years old. Healey broke this promise with the 18 to 20 years olds earning nearly £2 an hour less. scrapping “discriminatory” age bands, and to increasing the minimum wages for 18- to 20-year-olds so young workers are paid the same as those over 21. Healey broke this promise—18- to 20-year-olds will still earn nearly £2 an hour less. The rate for both age levels will rise by 3.9% but this will be cancelled out by rising inflation.


Labour will use these young workers as a cheap labour force, and is already pushing an unpaid work experience scheme at Sainsbury’s.


Labour is preparing for further attacks on welfare, and Healey promised, “As the Prime Minister and I have both said, we will bring down the welfare bill.” They are eying up attacking the Personal Independence Payment, the major disability benefit. All of this is in the pipeline.


Healey did not remove the Triple Lock on pensions, and this will not happen before the 2030 election, but made the menacing statement that Labour would adjust the Triple Lock after that.


All in all, the budget was low key, with a series of minor announcements. In addition to the above, there was the removal of import tax on some 100 products, meaning cheaper prices for things like, baked beans, gherkins, garlic and marmalade. This was derided widely in the media, as this would save around £21 a year, or £1.75 a month! Parental pay would be extended, so that 150,000 parents will receive two weeks of support of up to £194 a week. Again, this will be wiped out by rising inflation.


So, no real challenge to big business and a massive increase in defence spending, with looming attacks on pensioners, young workers and the disabled. But we never expected anything else from the Burnham …

author: Unknown
title: Iain Mckay - Michael Bakunin, Anarchist & Syndicalist
content:
Author

: Iain Mckay

Title

: Michael Bakunin, Anarchist & Syndicalist

Date

: 2026, Fall

Notes

: Publication information is available online at

https://syndicalist.us/

Source

: Scanned from Anarcho-Syndicalist Review #95, Fall, 2026, page 40


 This year marks the 150th anniversary of the death of Michael Bakunin (May 30, 1814, to July 1, 1876). While best known for his struggle against Marx in the (First) International and his correct prediction that the so-called workers' state would generate a new ruling class, there is much more to Bakunin than that. He wrote on a wide range of subjects which activists today will find of interest—the nature of a social revolution, union organizing, nationalism and national liberation, atheism, the need for a specific anarchist organization, amongst others.


 It is important to stress that the conflict within the International was not a personal one. Bakunin championed a tendency that had existed within the International since the start, one which could be termed (to use a later word) syndicalist—that argued for struggle on the economic terrain and favored federalist socio-economic organization which prefigured the socialist world desired. This inevitably brought the federalist wing of the International into conflict with Marx who favored political action (electioneering) and centralized political organization (parties). Bakunin championed this tendency (which was supported by the majority of the International) and became its best-known advocate.


 As is clear from the writings included in this issue, Bakunin advocated syndicalist tactics and specific anarchist organization. However, this is often ignored by commentators upon him and anarchism. Instead, Bakunin's constructive ideas are replaced with suggestions that he was an advocate of pan-destruction and terrorism. Suffice to say, comparing hostile accounts of Bakunin to anarchist ones and the reader would not be condemned if they concluded that there were about two different people with the same name.


 Often this criticism is based on works for which any actual evidence of Bakunin's authorship is lacking or, at best, limited, superficial or dubious. These date from his short association—and infatuation—with the Russian Nihilist Sergei Nechaev and many of the commentators seem blissfully unaware of any research conducted since Marx and Engels first made the assertion, research which shows that Bakunin had no role in the infamous works written during that short period and that Nechaev was their author. This explains why their content is so at odds with Bakunin's other writings, whether public or private.


 Bakunin's advocacy of syndicalism can be seen from his public writings, his letters to comrades and his posthumously published works. Thus we see him argue for economic organization and struggle, reject electioneering and correctly predict it would lead to reformism, see the general strike as a means of commencing the social revolution (although not rejecting the need for insurrection) and a host of other ideas which are associated with the later syndicalism which is all too often claimed to be different to revolutionary anarchism or a new development produced by the failure of "propaganda by the deed" (again, wrongly all too often proclaimed the anarchist tactic).


 Yet we find Bakunin arguing that the "International, by thus placing the proletariat outside the politics of states and the bourgeois world, constitutes a new world, the world of proletarian solidarity across all countries. This world is that of the future... it is the organisation of international solidarity for the economic struggle of labor against capital." Likewise, he indicated that the organs formed to fight capitalism (unions, councils) would be what replaced it:


 This completely practical, completely vital study of social science undertaken and constantly pursued by the workers themselves, both in their respective trade sections and in these trades councils, will necessarily lead and has already led to a large extent to produce in them this unanimous and fully considered conviction, demonstrable both in theory and in practice, that the serious, final, complete emancipation of the workers is possible only on one condition, and that this condition is the appropriation of capital, that is to say the raw materials and all the instruments of labor, including land, by the workers collectively....The economic question considered in this extent …

title: Tuncay Yılmaz: We want to build a united front of resistance in Europe - Part Two
content:
ANF spoke to Tuncay Yılmaz, founding co-chair of the Socialist Refoundation Party (SYKP), about the outcomes of the Cologne meeting, the need for a common struggle, the situation of left-wing and democratic forces in the face of the rising far right in Europe, and the roadmap for the proposed alliance.


The first part of this interview can be read

here

. 


On 17 October, 25 organisations from different political traditions came together in Cologne. Similar attempts to build alliances have been made in Europe before. Why has the need to establish a common platform for struggle emerged again today? What distinguishes this meeting from previous initiatives?


Organisations from different political traditions and social groups in Europe have come together at various times. Previously, there was the European Assembly for Peace and Democracy (ABDEM). We then extended the organisation of the Peoples' Democratic Congress (HDK) in Turkey to Europe, establishing a broad organisation under the name HDK Europe. This organisation later became the European Democratic Forces Union (ADGB) and continued its activities under that name. Most recently, ahead of the NATO summit, a joint initiative called PANEV was established against imperialist aggression, wars and NATO.


All these initiatives emerged from efforts to find ways for the forces of democracy, peace, equality and freedom to become better organised in Europe and pursue more effective political action against the enormous aggressive power confronting us.


The alliances we established at different times sometimes lost their effectiveness, both because of changes in the objective conditions in which they were formed and, to speak frankly, because of our own shortcomings. This is a reality, and we are aware of it. Indeed, this was one of the issues on the agenda of our meeting. We want to learn from our previous experiences.


However, the mistakes we made in the past or the changes we have experienced should not prevent us from bringing democratic forces together again and carrying out a common struggle. And indeed, they are not preventing us. One of the main motivations that brought us together at this meeting was the growing hostility towards migrants in the European countries where we live, the rise of the right, fascist movements coming to power and increasing state violence. The fact that laws targeting asylum seekers have reached almost inhumane proportions is also deeply concerning to all of us. We want to build a united front of resistance against all of this.


At the same time, however, all our attention, thoughts and concerns are focused on developments in Turkey. Looking at Turkey, we see a totalitarian regime being built step by step. Everyone who opposes it becomes a target. Presidential candidates are arrested. Selahattin Demirtaş has been imprisoned for years, as has Figen Yüksekdağ. Ekrem İmamoğlu was subsequently arrested. The Republican People's Party (CHP), which prides itself on being the founding party of the state, is also under serious pressure. Attempts are being made to divide the party, and many of its representatives have been arrested.


Alongside all this, a negotiation process has begun. It has not yet reached the stage of a peace process. However, this negotiation process has the potential to generate a collective strength capable of pushing back attacks on democracy through the positive developments it could bring to the country's political life. Despite this, we see that the political authorities are acting with appalling arbitrariness in this process as well.


To speak frankly, this process has been made possible by the determination and goodwill of Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. After all, decisions were taken to lay down arms and dissolve the organisation. These decisions represent a profound transformation in the movement's historical existence.


Despite this, the state continues to display an extremely indifferent and unserious attitude towards taking steps on these issues, potentially jeopardising the process. Its actions could allow the anti-democratic practices it maintains throughout the country to continue in different forms in this area as well. We can all see that, for months, instead of implementing the legal arrangements brought onto Parliament's agenda with broad support, the authorities have merely continued saying, "We want this as well, and we want that too."


Frankly, they are acting entirely with …

author: paradox-a
title: Die falsche Welt des Gute-Laune-Faschismus
content:
Zum Posterboy des Gute-Laune-Faschismus wurde Ulrich Siegmund gekürt, der AfD-Ministerpräsident in spe aus Sachsen-Anhalt. Die AfD fuhr hier mit 43,8% ihr bislang bestes Ergebnis ein. Je strukturschwächer, gottverlassener und migrationsärmer die Gegenden sind, desto stärker ist der Zuspruch zum nationalistischen Autoritarismus. So bereisen die ewig grinsenden Rattenfänger das Land und punkten unter Deutschen, die die Überwindung ihrer eigenen bürgerlichen Existenz herbeisehnen und hoffen dies auf dem Weg der Zerstörung der liberalen Demokratie zu erreichen.


Der Wohlfühl-Faschismus ist ein Phänomen, das vor zwanzigdreißig Jahren noch völlig unvorstellbar gewesen wäre. Und in zweidrei Jahrzehnten werden wir uns ebenfalls fragen, was in dieser Phase eigentlich passiert ist. Wer sie verstehen will, muss sich dazu nicht nur die Wahlkampf-Strategien der AfD anschauen, sondern auch kultur- und medienwissenschaftlich vorgehen. So ist es kein Zufall, das seit Anfang des Jahres 2026 massenhaft KI-generierte Songs bei Youtube erscheinen. Aufgrund ihrer hohen Klickzahlen landen diese wiederum durch die Algorithmen sehr schnell in der Vorschlagleiste.


Die extrem rechte Propaganda-Maschinerie bedient sich somit nahezu perfekt abgestimmt der Mittel, die der Plattform-Kapitalismus entwickelt hat. Und sie greift auf eine künstlich-sentimentale Popkultur zurück, die unterm Strich meistens schon sehr schlicht und beschränkt war. Ob volkstümelnd wie Heino, oder neu-deutsch-hart wie Rammstein, sülzig wie Julia Juls, Runa&Rebellin oder pop-rockig wie Weimar, Sleipnir und andere – Vorbilder für die extrem rechte Computermusik gibt es genug…


Sicher könnte man auch dagegen halten und sagen, dass die Generierung von Musik und Video-Material durch technische Sprechapparate von allen möglichen Leute mit kommerziellen Absichten, um Aufmerksamkeit zu erhalten oder einfach nur aus Langeweile generiert wird. Und das stimmt auch. Bedenkt man, wie durchproduziert und geglättet kommerziell erfolgreiche Musik heute ist, scheint der Schritt zur sogenannten KI klein zu sein. Dennoch gibt es eine spezielle Affinität von faschistischem Denken zur offensichtlich künstlichen Kultur, die den Anschein von menschlicher Kreativität verlässt und damit post-human ist. Laut Jason Stanley wird damit auf die Herstellung von „Unwirklichkeit“ abgezielt.


Um ein paar Beispiele von viralen KI-generierten Songs und „Künstler“ zu nennen, sind da beispielsweise:


– „Spätestens HIER wacht jeder auf! Der Sound des Wandels“ („Aufbruch Deutschland“, 501.537 Aufrufe)


– „Steh auf, wenn du Deutscher bist | Stolz auf Heimat und Kultur“ („Ottilie“, 339.081 Aufrufe)


– „Was ist aus unserem Land geworden? | Ein Lied über den Verlust der Heimat“ („Fenja“, 338.697 Aufrufe)


– „Dorfmarie – So war es, so soll es wieder sein“ („Dorfmarie“, 160.534 Aufrufe)


– „DIE WACHT AM RHEIN (LIVE) | Rock-Version eines historischen Gedichts“ („Julia im Exil“; 113.198 Aufrufe)


– „Kein schöner Land… WO DIE EICHEN STEH’N“ („Freya“; 18.974 Aufrufe)


– „Thüringen Ein Land Eine Geschichte Ein Herz“ („Der Heimatklang“, 4334 Aufrufe)


– „Heimweh nach Deutschland“ („Liv Eisen“, 2067 Aufrufe)


Die Titel verraten schon das Wesentliche. Wenn man die Textzeilen hört oder liest, wird deutlich, dass die immer gleichen Narrative, endlos wiederholt werden. Stets geht es um den Verlust einer imaginären „Heimat“ oder glorreichen „Nation“, um eine angebliche „Überfremdung“, anknüpfend an den Verschwörungsmythos eines „großen Austauschs“. Der Gute-Laune-Faschismus lebt in der ewigen Wiederholung von Mustern immer gleicher Opfer-Inszenierungen, dem Streicheln narzisstischer Kränkungen, sowie der Vorstellung einer zukünftigen Größe, die nur durch die Erniedrigung der ausgemachten Feinde erreicht werden kann. All dies sind Produkte einer staatlich-kapitalistischen Gesellschaftsform, die mit Patriarchat, Rassismus und Naturbeherrschung verknüpft ist. Zusammengefasst ist die Computer-produzierte Lyrik in ihrem billigen Abklatsch armselig – und faschistisch.


Dabei darf man nicht vergessen, dass auch der historische Nationalismus keine naturwüchsige Volksbewegung war, sondern ein Elitenprojekt, das eine Nation und eine darin angeblich ursprünglich vorhandene Kultur verordnete, anerzog und drillte.


Hört man die künstlich erzeugten Lieder und ihre Texte an, greifen Form und Inhalt ineinander. Bekanntlich ist den Fans derartiger wohlfühlfaschistischer Erzeugnisse vollkommen egal, ob sie ein KI-generiertes Lied …

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Rosa Amorim: "Hablar de reforma agraria en Brasil es hablar de un proyecto de dignidad de vida"
content:
“Com a barriga vazia não consigo dormir,

E com o bucho mais cheio, comecei a pensar.

Que eu me organizando posso desorganizar

Que eu desorganizando posso me organizar

Que eu me organizando posso desorganizar”.

Da lama ao caos, Nação Zumbi - Chico Science


“Con la panza vacía no puedo dormir,

Con el buche más lleno, empecé a pensar.

Que desorganizándome puedo organizar

Que organizando me puedo desorganizar

Que desorganizándome puedo organizar”


Por Mariángeles Guerrero y Carla Perelló

Desde Brasil


Rosa Amorim es la primera mujer del Movimiento de los Trabajadores Rurales sin Tierra (MST) en ser electa diputada nacional en Brasil. Es negra, lesbiana, oriunda de Pernambuco, nordeste del país, y tiene 29 años. Integra el Partido de los Trabajadores (PT). Durante la pandemia, mientras gobernaba Jair Bolsonaro, fue una de las impulsoras de la red de cocinas solidarias que enfrentaron el hambre en los barrios populares de las ciudades. La reelección de Lula da Silva significa una victoria popular y una esperanza, pero la conformación de un Congreso con mayoría de la extrema derecha plantea sus propios desafíos. En ese escenario, sostiene que la “lucha parlamentaria” será vital. “Queremos que Brasil deje de ser uno de los países que más venenos y agrotóxicos consume”, afirma.


Hija de la lucha por la reforma agraria, Amorim creció en las filas del MST y también fue dirigente estudiantil. Desde sus orígenes, el movimiento campesino mantuvo su autonomía aunque apoyó candidaturas del PT. Pero, en 2022, tras el retroceso en materia de derechos que significó el gobierno de Jair Bolsonario, presentó sus propios candidatos. Ese año, ella fue electa diputada del estado de Pernambuco.

El pasado 5 de octubre fue electa diputada nacional; una de lxs 38 legisladorxs LGBT+ que obtuvieron un escaño y una de los cuatro integrantes del MST que estarán en el Congreso brasileño

.


En el histórico proceso electoral que consolidó a Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva como presidente por los próximos cuatro años, Amorim fue una de las jóvenes que acompañó la campaña para revertir la derrota que el PT obtuvo en la primera vuelta.

Llevará las banderas de la reforma agraria y la soberanía alimentaria al Poder Legislativo. Allí el agronegocio presiona, de la mano de la bancada ruralista, para obtener beneficios y seguir extendiendo la frontera agropecuaria

, causando deforestación y contaminación.


En contraste, el MST lleva cuatro décadas de lucha por la tierra para la producción de alimentos sanos.

“Alimentamos al pueblo porque con comida en la panza podemos tener mentes pensantes y con mentes pensantes podemos organizarnos”

, sostuvo en entrevista con Tierra Viva, haciendo honor a la histórica banda nordestina Nação Zumbi liderada por Chico Science.


Foto: Prensa PT


Las cocinas solidarias, que define como “una tecnología social para organizar al pueblo”, se convirtieron en política pública en 2023, durante el gobierno de Da Silva. Su objetivo es vincular el campo con la ciudad, llevando alimentos sanos a espacios comunitarios de los barrios populares. En esos ámbitos se brinda un plato de comida pero también escucha, alfabetización, contención y cuidados. Para la diputada, comer es el primer paso para cuestionar por qué existe el hambre y la pobreza.


—¿En qué situación está hoy la soberanía alimentaria en Brasil?

—Hablar del hambre no es solamente hablar de si el pueblo come por la mañana, por la tarde y por la noche. Es más profundo. Combatir el hambre también significa hablar de la calidad de lo que se come. Y para eso vamos a tener que librar una lucha muy grande. Ya la estamos librando, pero va a ser todavía mayor: la lucha contra el agronegocio, contra el modelo de producción vigente que hace que las personas se enfermen por lo que consumen todos los días. Queremos que Brasil deje de ser uno de los países que más venenos y agrotóxicos consume. Y esto tiene una relación directa con la lucha parlamentaria. Vamos a tener que librar una enorme disputa contra el agronegocio en el Congreso para reducir la cantidad de agrotóxicos que se autorizan en Brasil. También vamos a tener que poner en la agenda la ampliación de las tierras cultivables destinadas a la agricultura familiar y campesina.

Llego al Congreso Nacional para conformar y construir la bancada de la tierra, de la agricultura familiar y de la agricultura campesina. Queremos debatir cómo combatir el hambre y qué estamos consumiendo en Brasil.

Tenemos que debatir la …

author: rezgar2
title: The Brazilian Victory: Left Unity and Digital Autonomy
content:
Rezgar Akrawi : Lula's victory offers an experience worth studying and learning from. It demonstrates the possibility of cooperation among left-wing forces despite their differences, while recognizing the other factors that contributed to the result.


The left does not need to erase its diversity in order to unite. It needs to turn that diversity into an organized and effective force, strengthen its independence across all five pillars, and pursue the struggle for freedom, equality, and social justice while developing democratic, humanist socialist alternatives to capitalism.


Author


Rezgar Akrawi


رزكار عقراوي


    Submitted by

rezgar2

 on October 29, 2026


Rezgar Akrawi


The leftist leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic victory in Brazil’s presidential election on October 25, 2026. The result came amid intense political and social polarization and the growing influence of the far right in Brazil and across Latin America, backed by the American far right led by Donald Trump.


The significance of this electoral victory extends beyond Lula securing a fourth term. It also lies in the political and organizational experience that helped make it possible, above all the ability of diverse left-wing and progressive forces, with different programs and ideological outlooks, to forge a broad electoral alliance around common ground in confronting the far right.


A Broad Left-Wing and Progressive Alliance Despite Differences


Lula contested the election with the support of the ‘Brazil Ready for More’ alliance, comprising seven left-wing and progressive parties organized into two party federations and two separate parties. The ‘Brazil of Hope’ federation brought together Lula’s Workers’ Party, the Communist Party of Brazil, and the Green Party. The second federation united the Socialism and Liberty Party, which includes socialist and radical-left currents, with the Sustainability Network. The Brazilian Socialist Party and the Democratic Labour Party also joined the alliance, alongside supportive social movements and trade unions. Lula ran with Geraldo Alckmin of the Brazilian Socialist Party as his vice-presidential candidate.


The importance of this alliance lies in its ability to bring together communists, socialists, the radical left, social democrats, and Greens despite their disagreements over capitalism, the role of the state, and the limits of social reform. These forces agreed on common electoral objectives while preserving their identities and organizational autonomy.


This is one of the most important lessons of the Brazilian experience. Left unity does not require ideological or organizational uniformity. It means being able to work together on common ground while respecting pluralism and differences.

 Disagreements over Lula’s economic and social policies will naturally persist, including among the forces that supported him at the ballot box.


Unity Does Not Mean Abandoning Criticism or Autonomy


The Brazilian experience raises an important question for left-wing forces around the world. Why do ideological and organizational differences become barriers to cooperation, despite so much common ground, even when these forces face shared political and class challenges?


Pluralism among communists, social democrats, the radical left, environmentalist and feminist currents, and independent leftists can be a source of strength and intellectual and political richness, provided it is managed democratically and constructively, without monopolization, exclusion, or claims to possess the absolute truth.

 Unity does not require abandoning criticism or offering unconditional acceptance of the policies of governments led by left-wing and progressive alliances.


Confronting Capitalism and the Far Right Requires a Broad Social Front


The victory demonstrated the importance of connecting the defense of democracy, rights, and freedoms with the economic and social demands of working classes and poor and marginalized communities.


Lula drew broad support from lower-income groups and proposed expanding social assistance, improving living conditions, and defending democratic institutions.


Confronting capitalism and the far right therefore cannot be confined to elections and party alliances. It requires sustained mass organizations in workplaces, neighborhoods, universities, trade unions, and social movements, together with policies that tackle class inequality and improve the lives of the majority …

author: Mary Stuart
title: How the Far-Right Uses Climate Disasters to Build Political Power
content:
Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s

End Times Fascism and the Fight for the Living World

 is critical reading for anyone seeking to understand and push back against the far-right coalitions wielding considerable state and corporate power around the world.


Klein and Taylor posit that today’s fascists believe that end times have arrived, and have made it their mission to profit from cascading global crises, while hunkering down and protecting themselves as the world burns around them.


The book details three factions of end times fascists, united by their shared apocalypticism. The religious fundamentalists believe end times are upon us, but they will be saved by their messiah. The Silicon Valley technologists are building technologies they say could be world-ending, that in the meantime are killing jobs, consuming vast resources, and polluting communities. The ethno-nationalists espouse conspiratorial ideas about cultural replacement and treat immigration as an existential threat.


DeSmog Canada editor/reporter Mary Stuart spoke with Astra Taylor about how climate change fits into end times fascism, the importance of AI data centre fights, and how we can understand Canadian Prime Minister Carney’s neoliberal moves in response to U.S. President Donald Trump.


Taylor is a writer, documentarian, and activist. She co-founded the

Debt Collective

, a membership-based union for debtors, and is the author of several books, including

The Age of Insecurity

 and

Democracy May Not Exist But We’ll Miss It When It is Gone

.


This interview was conducted by phone and has been edited for length and clarity.


Mary Stuart:

 

I


want to start by


asking how your book can help us understand some recent elections. Jair Bolsonaro’s son Flávio won the first round of voting in Brazil’s election and


nearly


became president. The far-right AfD recently won in Saxony-Anhalt.


How do these wins fit into your analysis of end times fascism?


Astra Taylor:

 One phenomena we describe in End Times Fascism relevant here is the role of Pentecostal religious communities in turning out the vote. To paraphrase reporting from Brazil, a voter said “my heart’s with Lula, but my pastor told me to vote for Flávio”.


The incredibly difficult conditions that we’re living under created fertile terrain for prophecy and religion, for kinds of pentecostalism, a faith that is focused on prosperity, individual advancement and banking on the idea that life is suffering here on earth, but you will be rewarded in the afterlife.


There’s also interference from Tech oligarchs. We don’t know the half of it at this moment, but the way the platform [Meta] refused to run ads for Lula’s party and beyond is certainly a factor. And the Trump regime [is playing a role] as well.


AfD is a similar. Naomi and I wrote a piece in the

Financial Times

 and we open with the images that went viral this summer of the Danube River drying, and Nazi warships emerging. Hundreds of Nazi warships sank during WWII, and as the river receded, this paraphernalia was coming out of the mud. We thought it was a powerful metaphor for today. What’s really striking is the riverbed— the fact that it’s drying because of climate change. Our point is that fascism always emerges from crises. And we cannot separate the ecological and economic crises people are facing.


People are really struggling with affordability. People are feeling that they don’t have a future. And actually quite strikingly, rates of immigration are quite low, right? So [Saxony-Anhalt is] one of the places with the least immigration, but [the AfD] step in and say “the problem is the immigrants, it’s not a larger economic system.” This is a classic fascist move that we describe throughout the book.


MS:


What role do climate change and climate denial play in end times fascism?


AT:

 Naomi and I are insistent that the planet is a player in our politics. Fascism always surges in moments of crisis.


We are in a world that is being roiled by disasters and shocks. We’ve reached a point where the consequences [of climate change] are undeniable. You cannot deny a heat dome when you’re inside it. You cannot deny a hurricane when it’s blowing the roof off your house. Of course, you can still deny why the storm is coming. You can embrace a Marjorie Taylor Greene perspective and say that it’s due to space lasers or you can say “the climate has always changed, this is nothing new, we don’t know if it’s human causing it.” …

author: nodes of resistance
title: Rechenzentren, „KI“ und Strategien für emanzipatorischen Widerstand
content:
Im Vorfeld der bundesweiten Konferenz zur Vernetzung von Widerstand gegen „KI“ und Rechenzentren. am 7.11.26 in Berlin veröffentlichen wir folgendes Diskussionspapier


Es regt sich Widerstand gegen Rechenzentren und das, wofür sie stehen. Damit dieser Widerstand möglichst weit trägt, halten wir eine Diskussion zu drei Themen für wichtig:


1) Der enge Zusammenhang von Rechenzentren und „KI“


2) Gemeinsam kämpfen für Klima- und soziale Gerechtigkeit, gegen Faschismus und Militarisierung


3) Wirksamer Widerstand durch Vielfalt und Unberechenbarkeit


1) Der enge Zusammenhang von Rechenzentren und „KI“


Der massive Ausbau von Rechenzentren und der Hype um „KI“ hängen unmittelbar zusammen. Denn: Der Hype um „KI“ mobilisiert die finanziellen Ressourcen und die politisch einstimmige Unterstützung für einen in Geschwindigkeit und Umfang beispiellosen Ausbau materieller Infrastruktur. Der Zusammenhang umfasst die technische, ökonomische und politische Dimension.


• Der technische Zusammenhang: Rechenzentren sind gewissermaßen die Fabriken von „KI“. Während es schon länger Rechenzentren gibt (seit dem Aufkommen von „Cloud“ als zentral verwaltete Rechenkapazitäten), macht „KI“ noch viel mehr und größere Rechenzentren erforderlich: Manche Rechenzentren dienen primär dem Training von „KI“-Modellen (diese brauchen besonders teure Halbleiter-Chips und liegen oft eher ländlich), andere primär der Inferenz, also dem Errechnen von „KI“-Outputs basierend auf trainierten Modellen (diese liegen meist möglichst nah an Internetknotenpunkten, oft urban). Rechenzentren liegen am Ende einer komplexen globalen Lieferkette: Besonders deutlich ist die erhöhte Nachfrage nach seltenen Erden und Metallen sowie nach Wasser und (fossiler) Energie, die an vielen Stellen dieser Lieferkette benötigt werden: Bei der Herstellung der Lithografiemaschinen, die wiederum nötig sind, um Chips zu produzieren zu können, die wiederum nötig sind, um ein Rechenzentrum zu betreiben. Die Infrastruktur rund um Rechenzentren und „KI“ ist seit einigen Jahren in erheblichem Aufbau und schließt zunehmend auch Endgeräte ein, deren Funktionieren an eine kontinuierliche Anbindung nicht nur an Internetkonnektivität, sondern auch an „KI“ und Cloud gebunden ist (von Heimgeräten über industrielle Produktion hin zu Kampfjets).


• Der finanzielle Zusammenhang: Der Finanzierung von Rechenzentren liegt ein quasi-religiöser Glaube an die Unausweichlichkeit und die Spekulation auf zukünftige Profitabilität von „KI“ zugrunde. „KI“-Unternehmen fahren jährlich Milliardenverluste ein, weil ihre Ausgaben in Form von Kosten von Rechenkapazitäten, Energie und Löhnen über den Einnahmen liegen. Rechenzentren sind dabei der Knotenpunkt für finanzielle Risiken: Die Chipherstellung ist (bisher) profitabel (siehe Bilanzen von Nvidia, TSMC, SK Hynix), das gleiche gilt für die Bereitstellung von Rechenkapazitäten als Dienstleistung, die vor allem die drei Hyperscaler-Unternehmen Amazon, Microsoft und Google anbieten. Rechenzentren sitzen zwischen der Chipherstellung und der Bereitstellung von Rechenkapazitäten und werden häufig nur angemietet von denjenigen, die dann wiederum Rechenleistung nutzen oder verkaufen. Rechenzentren sind extrem kapitalintensiv (bis zu mehreren Milliarden Euro pro Rechenzentrum) und hochspekulativ, sodass auch Menschen aus der Rechenzentrumsbranche (anonym/vertraulich) sagen: „Wer das Risiko versteht, wird nicht investieren.“ Das Risiko (also die Wahrscheinlichkeit von Verlusten) ergibt sich u.a. aus einer kurzen Lebensdauer von Chips (je nach Quelle ein, zwei oder max. sieben Jahre), der langfristigen Finanzierung von Rechenzentrumsbau (oft 15-20 Jahre), einer hohen Unsicherheit über die Verfügbarkeit und den Preis von Chips, Energie und Wasser und einer ebenfalls hohen Unsicherheit über die Nachfrage nach „KI“-Rechenkapazitäten. Diese Risiken werden aktuell immer neu verschachtelt durch komplexe Zirkelkäufe zwischen „KI“-Unternehmen, Chipherstellern und Rechenzentrumsbetreibern, was selbst Finanzanalyst*innen kritisch bewerten. Bereits seit mehreren Jahren attestieren u.a. Analyst*innen von Goldman Sachs das Vorliegen einer „Blase“.


• Der politische Zusammenhang: Die vermeintliche Unausweichlichkeit von „KI“ wird politisch verknüpft mit einem Wettbewerb um geopolitische Vorherrschaft (v.a. zwischen USA und China), einem Streben nach „Souveränität“ (z.B. durch Chipherstellung und Rechenzentren in Europa) und dem (Un-)Heilsversprechen immer mächtigerer …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Anarquistas pela anarquia sobre as eleições no Brasil/ Anarquistas por la anarquía sobre las elecciones en Brasil
content:
Enviado a La Zarzamora/ *Traducción al español al final.

Contra o fascismo todas as ações são úteis! Encontra teu lugar na luta. Revolte-se!

São os dizeres de um cartaz que apareceu nas ruas de Porto Alegre em 2019, e que são dizeres vigentes, antes de 2019, depois de 2019, nestes dias e que serão vigente ainda muito depois.

Nestes tempos em que o apelo anti fascista tende a afunilar-se no voto diante de um contexto em que o resultado das eleições no Brasil podem consolidar o neo fascismo a nível continental, nos é importante compartilhar um olhar anárquico que nos possibilite sair do pânico e construir antagonismos aos fascismos atuais, apesar de que nada seja tão simples assim. Para isso inicialmente vamos a entender que enquanto anárquicos e anarquistas, fazemos parte de coletividades, redes, e grupos dentro da sociedade que não compartilham nossa posição política, para depois apontar e precisar que nossas posições políticas não são sinônimos de pertencimentos ou identidades.

Cientes de que habitamos territórios felizmente diversos e com pessoas que tem maior ou menor apego à autonomia e a auto determinação, pensarmos nos diferentes lugares de luta contra o fascismo, consiste precisamente em aceitarmos dentro dessa diversidade, mutuamente, o que quer dizer horizontalmente, longe das tentativas uniformizadoras. Então podemos respeitar e entender que os cidadãos votantes “lutem” por não ter um presidente fascista, mediante o voto. Ao final é uma vergonha andar pelo mundo com a imposição majoritária de governantes misóginos, racistas, e aquele longo etc que bem sabemos sobre as famílias com tendência monarquista e miliciana. E mais profundamente, é respeitável o ódio que sentem por um personagem desse naipe. Quando trata-se de pessoas que não compartilham o local ácrata de luta contra o sistema, seu lugar na “luta” é nas urnas e é entendível.

Agora quando falamos de pessoas que escolhem a anarquia como posição política, e seus locais de luta é que nos debruçamos com um debate que a cada eleição nos faz perder companheiros e que a cada eleição nos joga diante de acusações de supostos purismos, falta de tática, falta de solidariedade, indiferença e outro longo etc. No entanto, o que no fundo incomoda a cada eleição é o fato de que os mesmos anarquistas chamem a fazer campanha por um candidato e façam apelo ao chamado “voto tático”.

Independentemente dos argumentos, isso incomoda não apenas quem escuta esses apelos e decide que sendo anarquista não tem como votar, mas acredito que incomoda também a quem vai na campanha, faz o apelo e tem que pensar, argumentar, escrever, fazer vídeo ou responder que apesar de… segue sendo anarquista. É nessa mesma justificativa que pode ser percebido que votar não forma parte do repertório das práticas anarquistas.

Ao nos perguntarmos sobre nosso lugar na luta contra o fascismo o que evidencia que somos anarquistas? Qual é a diferença com os demais? O apelo ao voto anarquista já nos indica que somos reconhecidos por não votar. Então pedem-nos, diante do desespero, o favor de abdicar de uma de nossas práticas e isso não é pouca coisa.

Um dos nossos fundamentos, enquanto anárquicos e anarquistas, é o rechaço ao Estado. Odiamos ele porque enxergamos nele a cristalização de todos os processos opressivos, mas mesmo odiando o Estado ele nos afeta, e as pautas que possam resultar do circo dos horrores que foi eleito, vão nos afetar com politicas que procuram devolver forças para o patriarcado, ao militarismo, ao extrativismo, a moralidade religiosa, ao conservadorismo. De fato é por isso que odiamos o Estado, porque ele nos afeta, porque nos impõe.

Para além desse fundamento, o que do anarquismo fez com que nosso coração batesse e escolhêssemos esse caminho? Se há algo que fazemos sem nenhuma obrigação é ser parte das agitações e movimentos anarquistas, então sendo uma escolha tão livre, o que dessa proposta nos tocou o coração?

A autonomia, a autogestão, a horizontalidade, o apoio mútuo, a solidariedade, são práticas anarquistas que também são fundamentais e que, inegavelmente, são também incompatíveis com a existência dos Estados, porque cada Estado pretende anular essas práticas. Se sustenta no discurso de que as pessoas não sobreviveríamos sem o Estado, apesar de que catástrofes já demonstraram a efetividade da organização horizontal, apesar de que a história social e coletiva tem se desenvolvido majoritariamente sem Estado se pensamos nela historicamente e fora do eurocentrismo …

author: Unknown
title: 29 women killed in Southern Kurdistan in ten months
content:
In the first ten months of 2026, at least 29 women were victims of femicide in Southern Kurdistan. Another 29 women died under suspicious circumstances, according to a recent analysis by the Roj News agency. Three women were killed in October alone.


On October 15, a 20-year-old woman was killed by her brother, who was eight years older than her, in the Domîz subdistrict of Sêmêlê district near Duhok. Five days later, on October 20, 30-year-old Kîjan Burhan was murdered by her father, who shot her three times, in Sulaymaniyah.


The third case was reported on October 29 in the village of Şêx Turab near Hewlêr (Erbil), where the body of a murdered woman was discovered. Four suspects were arrested, and police in Hewlêr launched an investigation.


Women’s organizations have long criticized domestic violence as one of the most serious social problems in Southern Kurdistan. They are calling for effective prevention and intervention measures aimed at preventing violence, protecting victims, and bringing about lasting changes in violent patterns of behavior.

author: Sara Fayyazi
title: Making Women’s History Part of the Curriculum
content:
Two teachers from Sacred Heart Preparatory School in California, Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams, have proposed an Advanced Placement U.S. Women’s History course in response to the issue of students not learning about women’s history. The courses would allow studying women’s experiences and contributions in greater depth. Establishing this course would create a better understanding of American history as it includes the diverse experiences of women and would help students connect the historical struggles for equality to gender issues today.

Women have contributed to shaping the nation’s politics, economy, and social movements, yet their participation is often overlooked by traditional history classes. From fighting for the right to vote, challenging discrimination, and advocating for female autonomy, women have had a significant role in building the foundation of the United States today.

One of the main arguments for WAPUSH is that women’s experiences are not explored in the classroom. In the article Educational Activism: Creating an AP U.S. Women’s History Course, Serene Williams, Kristen Kelly, and Clara Robinson explain that topics such as women’s suffrage and reproductive rights receive limited attention in the current AP U.S. History curriculum. The women’s suffrage movement involved decades of organizing, political campaigning, and resistance. However, teachers may not introduce this topic to students or have enough time to examine its strategies and leaders in detail. A dedicated course would allow students to study these movements more thoroughly and understand how women helped shape American democracy.

Women’s history is much broader than the fight for voting rights. The proposed WAPUSH curriculum includes women’s labor, politics, religion, culture, war, and violence against women. It also examines how race, class, sexuality, religion, and other identities shaped women’s experiences. This approach is important because women throughout the years have never shared one universal experience. Indigenous women, Black women, Immigrant women, etc., have faced different opportunities and forms of discrimination. Studying these differences would help students develop a greater understanding of American history and that America was not built on just our founding fathers, but by women who paved the path for opportunity and development through blood, sweat, and tears.

An AP course would also help students recognize the connection between historical events and current issues. The debate over reproductive rights and other feminist struggles today cannot be fully understood without examining the laws and political movements that shaped access to contraceptives, abortion, and female economic support. Studying topics from the suffrage movement to the Equal Rights Amendment can help students understand the political equality that has developed through activism and engage in feminist discussion. Learning this history would give students the context needed to evaluate debates instead of viewing them as different events.

Establishing this course would show that women’s history is worthy of advanced academic study. The WAPUSH campaign began in 2022, and according to its website, the campaign gathered more than 4,000 petition signatures and received encouragement from College Board leadership as it worked toward launching this course. Its proposal has also received university support, while the campaign continues seeking letters from high schools willing to offer the course. This continued support brings women closer to bringing light to women’s history and giving women a space in school systems and curricula. This petition is one step closer every day to its goal to educate and inform people all across America of women’s contributions.

An AP U.S. Women’s History course would make education more comprehensive, inform students even more about the history of the U.S., and connect past struggles to present issues. Women have influenced American politics, economics, culture, and social movements, yet their experiences are not always given sufficient attention in existing courses. By offering students an opportunity to examine these experiences, the College Board could help create a more inclusive and accurate understanding of the nation’s past. Women’s history is not separate from American history but instead an essential part of it.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Remembering Legendary Farmworker Organizer and Activist Dolores Huerta
content:
Huerta wasn’t just an organizer — she also loved life, says journalist Maria Hinojosa.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Immigrant rights and labor icon Dolores Huerta died Wednesday at the age of 96. Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America, working with Cesar Chavez. From 1965 to 1970, the union organized the historic Delano grape strike, which ended in major gains for farmworkers’ labor rights.

In the years that followed, Huerta became heavily involved in the women’s liberation and immigrant rights movements and became a major supporter of the Democratic Party. In March, The New York Times published an investigation into Cesar Chavez’s history of sexual abuse of women and girls in the farmworkers’ movement, prompting Huerta to reveal that she, too, had been raped by Chavez. Huerta said the assaults led to the births of two of her children.

Dolores Huerta appeared on Democracy Now! many times over the years. We remember her legacy with Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Maria Hinojosa, who says, “Dolores was not only a labor organizer, a civil rights organizer, a feminist, committed, always optimistic about the possibilities of this country, but she loved life, and I want people to remember that.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman.

The legendary labor organizer, feminist and civil rights activist Dolores Huerta has died at the age of 96. She was co-founder of the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America. She worked with Cesar Chavez at both groups. The United Farm Workers grew out of a merger between the National Farm Workers Association and the Filipino-led Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee.

Dolores Huerta coined the phrase ”¡Sí se puede!,” “Yes, we can!” It became a rallying cry for farmworkers, a lasting slogan for social justice movements.

title: The Cornell Case and the Left's Betrayal of Itself
content:
Here's an article about the feminist reaction to the "Cornell 7" case that has been in the news recently (October 2026). A version of it was published in "Compact." (The hyperlinks have been deleted, unfortunately.) The general point is that contemporary feminism has become an albatross for the left, and is also contributing to destructive social and cultural trends.

In the 1960s, feminists demanded that women and men have legal equality, that women be treated as mature adults who are free to make their own choices be it with regard to sex or their careers, that patriarchal paternalism be dismantled. In the 2020s, feminists demand that women be constantly protected against men, that patriarchal paternalism be resurrected, that women be legally treated as not responsible for decisions they’ve made because, in certain contexts, only men have agency. And men, they argue, are inveterate misogynists, abusers, and rapists, so the agency they manifest is almost invariably malign.

The reaction to the “Cornell 7” case is the latest example. A remarkable wave of hysteria has swept liberal and left culture, from mass media and social media to university campuses. Misandry is drenching the discourse; mobs are going after anyone who questions the dominant narrative; the guilt of the accused is automatically assumed, because the accused are men and men are by definition guilty. Is it any wonder that millions of men in recent years have turned away from the left—which seems to hate them—and fallen into the clutches of the far-right and the “manosphere”?

Consider what has transpired. Far from condemning the wildly irresponsible comments of public figures like Governor Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James, which treat as established fact accusations made in a civil lawsuit, leftists themselves, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Zohran Mamdani, have talked as though the case has already been decided. This is despite the highly ambiguous evidence that has been presented, much of which tends to exonerate the alleged perpetrators of the “gang-rape.” Not only is presumption of innocence thrown out the window; it is obvious that even if the accused end up being found innocent, most liberals and leftists will remain sure of their guilt.

Lynch mobs have been out for blood. A few weeks ago, it was easy to find thousands of people “liking” public demands to kill the accused. Even innocent bystanders were victimized. The campaign of overwhelming harassment to which the journalist Michael Tracey has been subjected for questioning the “guilty until proven innocent” narrative led to his father receiving “thousands of nonstop crazed texts/calls/voicemails” threatening him with brutal violence. The current owners of Tracey’s childhood home were “inundated” with “crazed threats,” and received suspicious packages at their house. Friends and family of the accused men were harassed by thousands. So was the family of an innocent man who happens to have the same name as one of the accused.

Since liberals and leftists are refusing to stand up for decency and the rule of law, it is left to conservatives to do so—which enables them to claim the moral high ground against “lunatic” leftists and thereby score political points. It turns out that many conservatives take women more seriously as (potentially) responsible adults and moral agents than most leftists do.

Feminist moral panics may seem well-intentioned in that they’re allegedly motivated by concern for the safety of women, but these episodes illustrate the extent to which the (so-called) “left” has been corrupted and co-opted by neoliberal dynamics, particularly in the era of social media. The atomized, polarized, siloed, anti-intellectual, narcissistic soundbite culture of social media—itself a reflection of capitalist tendencies—has helped produce a liberal-left that dehumanizes others, reflexively assumes the worst of men, exploits controversies for social media clout, and contributes to the very social breakdown that leftists rightly attack neoliberalism for engendering. After all, a feminism that teaches women to hate and fear men, and to view themselves as being on a higher moral plane, doesn’t exactly promote healthy relationships. It exacerbates gender wars and culture wars, thus, again, gifting the right wing with talking points and grievances to rally around.

author: Tam Saavedra
title: The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality are Here!
content:
Ver versión en español


The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality Just Changed the Game for Disability Rights—Here’s What You Need to Know 


Big news for women with disabilities and all feminist disabled advocates, allies, and organizations worldwide!

 


During its 35th Session in August 2026, the

UN Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

 (UN CRPD)

 officially adopted the historic

Guidelines on Identifying and Addressing Intersectional Discrimination Against Girls, Adolescents, Women, and Older Women with Disabilities

.

 


This milestone represents a monumental step forward for disability rights. For the first time, States have explicit, actionable guidance to support their obligations at the intersection of gender and disability.

 


Read the official CRPD Guidelines here

 


What Are the CRPD Guidelines on Intersectional Discrimination?


The Guidelines serve as an authoritative framework developed by the UN


CRPD Committee to help States better prevent, monitor, and address intersectional discrimination.

 


Throughout years of UN CRPD country review processes, the Committee identified a persistent, critical gap:

the specific rights of women with disabilities and the complex, intersectional discrimination they experience are rarely understood or adequately addressed by governments.

 


As the UN CRPD celebrates its 20th anniversary, these Guidelines were issued to bridge that gap—ensuring the convention is implemented to benefit

all

 women, girls, and gender-diverse people with disabilities across their lifespans.

 


Why Are These Guidelines a Game


–

Changer?

 


International documents rarely explicitly focus on the detailed, lived experiences and rights of women with disabilities. These Guidelines clearly name and elaborate on the systemic barriers

 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities face daily across the globe, including:

 


Sexual & Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR):

 Addressing and preventing enforced sterilization, forced contraception, lack of accessible healthcare, restrictions on abortion, and lack of perinatal, menstrual, and menopause care.

 


Gender-Based & Disability-Based Violence:

 Exposing institutional violence, digital/online abuse, and the widespread lack of support services for victims.

 


Caregiving Recognition:

 Validating women with disabilities as active caregivers and mothers, rather than only recipients of care.

 


Economic & Educational Exclusion:

 Highlighting barriers in the labor market, economic and exclusion from education during puberty.

 


Crisis & Climate Response:

 Tackling compounded exclusion during environmental disasters, climate emergencies, and humanitarian relief efforts.

 


…just to name a few.

 


7 Key Breakthroughs in the Framing of the Guidelines 

 


What makes this document uniquely transformative is its progressive, structural approach:

 


Explicit Inclusion of Gender Diversity:

 The Guidelines explicitly encompass the rights of transgender, intersex, non-binary, and other gender-diverse people with disabilities and ask for gender diversity – inclusive interpretation of all obligations described.

 


Recognition of Historical Root Causes:

 The Committee explicitly addresses the legacy and ongoing impacts of

colonialism and enslavement

, establishing that States benefiting from these historical systems bear a particular responsibility to remedy their ongoing effects.

 


An Open Catalogue of Diversity:

 The text recognizes that women with disabilities belong to multi-marginalized communities—including Indigenous, Black, Dalit, Adivasi, refugee, asylum-seeking, religious minority, and pastoralist groups or people living in informal settings, among others —while leaving space for all intersecting identities.

 


Structural & Preventive Approach:

 Moving beyond a strictly punitive, reactive model, the Guidelines demand the dismantling of systemic oppression (such as ableism, audism, racism, and patriarchy) through early intervention, education, and public policy reform. 

 


Decriminalization

 is also a disability issue:

The guidelines recognize impacts of criminalization of abortion, homosexuality, gender identity and expression as well as

restricting marriage or consensual relationships as an important intersectional disability rights issue.

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Nunavik school board to pilot sex-education program
content:
Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, Nunavik’s school board, will test a sexuality education program in Kuujjuaq and Umiujaq in November.


The pilot program was developed with the Nunavik Regional Board of Health and Social Services and is intended to help children understand personal boundaries and how to stay safe in sexual situations, said Sarah Aloupa, president of Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, in an interview.


“It’s important for parents to take this very seriously. This program is for the students’ well being,” she said.


Aloupa said the initiative responds to a need raised by Nunavik residents and parents. The school board’s council of commissioners heard a presentation from the health board about the proposed program in June.


The program will cover students from kindergarten to Grade 11, with information packages for different age groups.


Aloupa declined to share the teaching material.


The pilot is scheduled to run Nov. 2 to 6 at Jaanimmarik School and Pitakallak School in Kuujjuaq and Nov. 16 to 20 at Kiluutaq School in Umiujaq. The schools were chosen in part because they were ready to take part and have staff with relevant experience, said Jade Duchesneau-Bernier, spokesperson for the school board.


During those weeks, staff will participate in training and parents can review material and ask questions at evening information sessions.


Their feedback will help shape the final program. While the board has not yet clarified how parents can do so, they can opt their children out, Aloupa said.


Information about the sessions is being sent to parents through school letters and posted on Facebook.


Aloupa pointed to sexual abuse cases in the region as part of the broader need for education on the subject.


In February 2025, Nicolas Cyr, a physical education teacher at Jaanimmarik School, was

charged

 with sexual assault of a minor, sexual interference of a minor and assault.


The pilot is intended to help the Nunavik school board and the region’s health board assess the program before considering whether to expand it to the other 18 schools Kativik Ilisarniliriniq operates, Aloupa said.


The organizations have not yet set a timeline for a region-wide rollout.

title: Leonard Leo-Linked VA Bishop Pushes Congregants to Vote for Regressive Agenda
content:
Moves by the Trump administration may be emboldening churches to jump into state proposition fights.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

On November 3, Virginians will vote on two ballot initiatives that have become the center of a well-resourced campaign led by Catholic Bishop Michael Burbidge.

This campaign is urging congregants to vote “no” on two ballot measures. Ballot Question 1 would affirm abortion access as a constitutional right in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Ballot Question 2 would repeal a 2006 same-sex marriage ban that defines marriage as between one man and one woman. Burbidge, who leads Virginia’s Arlington Diocese, which says it has 432,000 registered parishioners, is using his position to call on Catholic parishioners to vote against abortion access and marriage equality for all Virginians and to urge others to do the same.

This campaign has deployed the resources of the church, including church bulletins and guest speakers to preach against the ballot initiatives. The Archdiocese of Arlington itself hosts the CatholicsVoteNo.com website, which states that the church is “not partisan” while condemning the supposed “many evils and unintended consequences” of the initiatives, and even assailing surrogacy.

That website also features a “pledge to vote no,” and details how followers can get involved in opposing the ballot measures, from hosting registration drives to reaching out to their specific pastor for directions on community outreach. Burbidge’s identified goal is to convince the nearly 700,000 confirmed Catholics across the state to vote “no” on these amendments, a figure that could be decisive in making the initiatives fail.

For decades, the IRS forbade places of worship from endorsing or opposing political candidates as tax-exempt organizations. However, Donald Trump’s IRS has recently engaged in efforts to roll back what’s known as the “Johnson Amendment,” a tax provision that has been in place for more than 70 years that bars tax-exempt nonprofits from endorsing or opposing political candidates. That move was struck down in the courts, but it is currently under appeal in the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. In the meantime, the IRS has issued new guidance on the Johnson Amendment, seemingly giving tax-exempt places of worship enough legal wiggle room to engage in political campaigning directly to parishioners without jeopardizing their status. Beyond that, there is no legal bar on nonprofits engaging on public policy issues, including on referenda, as with the documented role of the Mormon Church in opposing marriage equality via Proposition 8 in California in 2008.

If Virginia is any indication, the Trump administration’s efforts to lift limits on churches directly backing political candidates may be emboldening churches that may have previously stayed out of state proposition fights to jump in strongly, using the hierarchy and wide reach of a religious institution to tell adherents how to vote. For years, Catholic Church leadership in the U.S. has wrestled with controversy and pressure to deny holy communion to believers in public office who vote to protect access to abortion. This includes Burbidge, who used his post to uphold a ban from a San Francisco archbishop denying Speaker Nancy Pelosi communion in the Arlington diocese because of her support as a representative for abortion access and, in 2022, he publicly called on Joe Biden to “repent” for his support of abortion health care.

In this coming election in Virginia, as a leader within the Catholic Church, Bishop Burbidge is using the resources contributed by his congregation to call on parishioners to vote in support of his anti-LGBTQ, anti-abortion agenda. Meanwhile, the majority of Catholics in the U.S. support marriage equality and access to abortion health care.

Burbidge has close ties to Leonard Leo and his more than $1 billion network of groups, which includes the Marble Freedom Trust and Rule of Law Trust. Leo’s network helped capture the U.S. Supreme Court that overturned Roe v. Wade and now is being marshaled to capture other key democratic institutions, from state courts, to the media, to the entertainment industry, to push Leo’s regressive agenda. title: [“In a world that constantly shames us for our bodies, genders, or sexualities, we can trick…
content:
gatheringbones

:

[“In a world that constantly shames us for our bodies, genders, or sexualities, we can trick ourselves into thinking that we are “taking control” and that achieving a certain body ideal is liberation. It is far from that.

For those of us who face multiple forms of oppression, developing eating disorders is not simply wanting our bodies to meet the impossible aesthetic ideal associated with people in dominant culture. Queer and trans people don’t develop disordered eating simply because we want to assimilate to cisgender, heteronormative culture. Of course, appearances can be and often are part of the picture. But when we attribute eating disorders solely to the desire for our bodies to look a certain way, the conversation stops. And we miss out on opportunities for crucial conversations about the connections between eating disorders, trauma, and survival.

Eating disorders help us to survive trauma and oppression.

 For queer and trans folks, the way we both conceptualize and heal from eating disorders must account for the ways we are harmed by systems of power. Eating disorders help us to cope with everyday microaggressions and macroaggressions. They help us to get by in the face of food insecurity. They can keep us safe in a world in which being read as queer or trans can mean life or death.

For many people, disordered eating or behaviours are attempts at shape control, which are attempts to blend in and not become a target. For many of us, eating disorder “treatment” that aims to strip us of the very armour that has allowed us to stay alive, can actually cause more harm if there isn’t an adequate substitute or systemic change to help us to safely exist in the world. Treatment cannot simply be aimed at challenging our “distorted thoughts” or symptom reduction or cheerleading body positivity. Treatment approaches that aim at skills training (e.g., dialectical behaviour therapy) and challenging unhelpful thought patterns that fuel an eating disorder (e.g., cognitive behavioural therapy) are often crucial, but they are not enough for a true sense of feeling safe and at home in one’s body.

Most mainstream treatment approaches perpetuate white supremacist, capitalist systems of harm. Fat people are told that they are holding on to their fat as protection and that if they worked through their trauma, the weight would fall away. Thin people are told they need to restore their weight but they are not to go beyond an established “upper limit.” When we demonize “emotional eating,” there is an inherent assumption that the individual can get to a calm, neutral state at all times when their body needs or wants to be fed. Sometimes “emotional eating” is harm reduction.

Our disorders and symptoms, the things that we feel shame about, were once what helped us to get through the night. We might still be in survival mode. Or, we might have a hard time recognizing that we no longer need to be in survival mode. But before we move on, we might have to pay respect and allow ourselves to grieve how we have been called to protect ourselves in ways that are simultaneously brilliant and destructive.”]

sand c. chang, from dreaming bigger: body liberation and weight inclusivity in health care, from The Care We Dream Of: Liberatory & Transformative Justice Approaches to LGBTQ+ Health, edited by Zena Sharman, 2021
