author: Unknown
title: ISIG: At least 678 migrants died on their workplace in six years
content:
Data compiled from reports by ISIG (Health and Safety Labour Observatory) show that migrant and refugee workers accounted for 4.8 percent of the 14,110 workers killed in workplace accidents between 2020 and the first nine months of 2026. Four workers were killed and another was injured when a tornado struck Antalya during the night of 26 October. Antalya Governor Hulusi Şahin said that the tornado had torn apart two containers housing workers employed at a residential construction site.


A judicial investigation was launched following the deaths of the four workers. Four people, including the construction contractor and site manager, were detained as part of the investigation.


Three of the workers were refugees


The workers who lost their lives were identified as Aycan Kılınç, Muhammed El Omar, Isa Elnevvah and Muhammed El Zeyn. The fact that three of the workers were Syrian brought renewed attention to the deaths of migrant and refugee workers in workplace accidents in Turkey in recent years.


Annual reports by ISIG provide information on deaths among migrant and refugee workers. According to ISIG reports, at least 678 migrant and refugee workers were killed in workplace accidents between 2020 and September 2026. The Observatory's annual reports show that a total of 12,374 workers were killed in workplace accidents between 2020 and 2025.


ISIG compiles its records through media monitoring and reports from workers, families, trade unions and other local sources. The actual number of deaths may be higher because of unregistered employment and difficulties in identifying workplace fatalities.


Highest number recorded in 2023


ISIG reports recorded 101 deaths among migrant and refugee workers in 2020, 94 in 2021, 90 in 2022, 106 in 2023, 94 in 2024 and 91 in 2025. The highest figure during this six-year period, both in absolute numbers and as a proportion of total workplace deaths, was recorded in 2023. Of the 1,932 workers killed that year, 106 were migrants or refugees. Migrant workers accounted for 5.49 per cent of recorded workplace deaths.


First nine months: 102 deaths


According to the latest ISIG report published as of 28 October 2026, at least 1,736 workers were killed in workplace accidents between January and September. The number of migrant worker deaths reported in the monthly reports for the same period reached 102.


Syrian and Afghan workers


Of the 94 migrant and refugee workers who died in 2024, 49 were Syrian and 13 were Afghan. Workers from these two countries accounted for approximately two-thirds of recorded migrant worker deaths that year.


In 2025, of the 91 migrant workers who lost their lives, 33 were Syrian, 12 Afghan, nine workers from Turkmenistan, eight Iranian and seven Egyptian.


Figures on the distribution of deaths by sector in 2023 also show that fatalities were concentrated in agriculture, construction and industry. That year, 22 percent of migrant and refugee worker deaths occurred in agriculture, 14 percent in construction and a combined 34 percent across various industrial sectors.


Twenty-two deaths in the earthquake region


Construction sites in the earthquake-affected region are another area where migrant workers have lost their lives. According to ISIG's compilation covering the period from 6 February 2023 to 6 February 2026, at least 296 workers were killed on construction sites across the 11 provinces affected by the earthquakes. At least 22 of those who died were migrant workers.


Eight of these workers were Syrian, six Iranian, three Egyptian and two Algerian, while one worker each was from Afghanistan, Iraq and Pakistan. ISIG drew attention to subcontracting arrangements, long working hours, employment without insurance and occupational health and safety conditions at construction sites in the region.


Deaths missing from official records


ISIG compiles its data through media monitoring and information received from workers, families, trade unions and local sources. The organisation said that it was sometimes unable to obtain even the identities of migrant workers and that the deaths of workers employed without registration could be concealed. For this reason, ISIG emphasises that the figures it publishes represent the minimum number of deaths recorded.

author: Mag
title: Die „Systemschmarotzer“ – nun auch in der Flüchtlingsarbeit
content:
Dossier


„

Das Wohltätigkeits- und Sozialarbeitsgeschäft ist in Deutschland gut aufgeteilt zwischen den großen, Parteien und Religionsgemeinschaften zugehörigen Organisationen. So ist die Diakonie federführend bei der Wohnungslosenhilfe, Caritas und auch Rotes Kreuz weisen Erfahrungen in der Flüchtlingsarbeit vor, die AWO und die „Parität“ beackert das Thema „Armut“ usw.. Kein Berufszweig ist in den letzten 15 Jahren so stark gewachsen wie das gesamte Feld der „Sozialen Arbeit“. Kein Wunder, „Sozialarbeit und Polizei statt Sozialstaat“ heißt das Motto. Unter dem Titel „

Katzenjammer der Systemschmarotzer

“

 habe ich diese Geschäftemacherei schon vor Jahren beschrieben. Mit der großen Zahl der neuen Geflüchteten in diesem Jahr ergeben sich für genannte zusätzliche Geschäftsfelder (…) Einige dieser Organisationen arbeiten in hohem Maße mit eigenen „Ehrenamtlichen“. In der Flüchtlingsbetreuung kommen sie damit aber nicht aus, für bezahlte Stellen will die öffentliche Hand ungern Geld locker machen. Letztlich sind die staatlichen Stellen hier die „Systemschmarotzer“: Sie wälzen ihre Pflichtaufgaben ab auf freiwillig Helfende, die teils jetzt schon seit Monaten über die Erschöpfungsgrenze hinaus ackern. (…) Berichte von Problemen zwischen autoritäres Handeln gewohnten Organisationen und freiwillig Helfenden sind aus der ganzen Republik zu vernehmen.

“

Kommentar von Norbert Herrmann vom 26. November 2015

. Siehe dazu die Lektüre-Empfehlungen und weitere Informationen:


Geschäftsmodell Asyl: Millionen für Flüge, Ärzte und Konzerne – viele Unternehmen verdienen an Abschiebungen und der Versorgung Geflüchteter


„Fluggesellschaften, Reisebüros, Ärzte und Betreiber von Unterkünften: Eine neuer Report zeigt, wie viele Unternehmen an Abschiebungen und der Versorgung Geflüchteter verdienen. Öffentliche Gelder fließen in Millionenhöhe an private Dienstleister. Wie viel Gewinn sie damit machen, bleibt häufig im Dunkeln.


Ein Mensch, fünf Bundesbeamte, ein eigens gechartertes Flugzeug. Am 2. Mai 2025 startete vom Flughafen Köln/Bonn eine Maschine in die Republik Kongo. An Bord: eine Person, die abgeschoben wurde, und ihre fünf Begleiter. Die Kosten allein für das Flugzeug: 215.785 Euro. Weitere Ausgaben, etwa für Personal, sind darin nicht enthalten. Die Zahlen stammen aus einer

Antwort der Bundesregierung


 auf eine parlamentarische Anfrage. Ein außergewöhnlich teurer Einzelfall. Doch er wirft eine grundsätzliche Frage auf: Wer verdient eigentlich an Deutschlands Abschiebungen? Dieser Frage ist Journalist*in Bo Wehrheim für das Projekt „Abschiebungsreporting NRW“ in einer am Dienstag veröffentlichten

Recherche


 nachgegangen. Das Ergebnis: Rund um Abschiebungen hat sich ein weit verzweigter Markt privater Dienstleistungen entwickelt. Fluggesellschaften, Reisebüros, medizinische Dienstleister und Technologieunternehmen erhalten staatliche Aufträge. Und das Geschäft reicht weit über den Flughafen hinaus. (…) In Nordrhein-Westfalen organisiert die Zentralstelle für Flugabschiebungen in Bielefeld entsprechende Maßnahmen. Für die Buchung von Flügen setzt sie auch auf private Reisebüros. In einem Fall betrug der ausgewiesene

Auftragswert 454.780 Euro


 für zunächst zwei Jahre mit Verlängerungsoptionen. Organisiert werden sollten unter anderem Flüge für abzuschiebende Menschen sowie für Begleitpersonal und medizinische Fachkräfte. An der eigentlichen Beförderung verdienen Fluggesellschaften. Der Report nennt zahlreiche Charteranbieter. Sie stellen Flugzeuge samt Besatzung bereit. Während einzelne Menschen auf regulären Linienflügen abgeschoben werden können, mieten Behörden für Sammelabschiebungen ganze Maschinen. Das kostet. Nach einer

Recherche von FragDenStaat


 gab Deutschland im ersten Halbjahr 2025 fast 15 Millionen Euro allein für die Miete von Charterflugzeugen aus. Ein Jahr zuvor waren es für denselben Zeitraum rund 12,7 Millionen Euro. Dabei bleibt es nicht. Dolmetscher, medizinische Begleitung, Bodenpersonal und Bundespolizisten verursachen weitere Kosten. Allein die Sicherheitsbegleitung bei Abschiebungen kostete den Bund im gesamten Jahr 2025 nach

Regierungsangaben


 mehr als 10 Millionen Euro. Wie teuer eine Abschiebung insgesamt ausfällt, lässt sich dennoch nicht immer nachvollziehen. Kosten verteilen sich auf unterschiedliche Behörden und Haushalte. Ein Teil der Flüge wird außerdem von der EU-Grenzschutzagentur Frontex finanziert oder mitfinanziert. Die Geldflüsse waren auch bei der Recherche schwer …

author: FMF Staff
title: Deporting Afghans to the Taliban by Way of Pakistan Is a Betrayal That Gets the United States Nothing
content:
The Trump administration is reportedly preparing to put more than 150 Afghans on a flight to Pakistan, where they would then be transferred across the border into Taliban-ruled Afghanistan. AfghanEvac, a coalition advocating for Afghan allies, says some of those facing removal are the brothers and sons of men who served alongside U.S. forces. The first flight could leave as early as Monday, just one day before Election Day in the United States.

Because the United States cannot deport people directly to Afghanistan, it lacks official diplomatic relations with the Taliban regime; the plan routes them through Pakistan. Call it what it is: a deportation to the Taliban with a layover. Officials reportedly told The New York Times that the removal is, in effect, to Afghanistan, and detainees have been told the same. Pakistan’s role is to carry out the handoff.

What the layover adds is risk. Afghans would be moved through a third country and beyond any oversight, and placed in the hands of authorities who have no obligation to protect them. From there, they could be pushed across the border to a regime they fled and one that would seek to harm them. These are the people who escaped Taliban rule after August 15, 2021.

Pakistan is not safe for Afghans. Since 2023, the Pakistani government has expelled over 2.4 million Afghan refugees back to Afghanistan as relations with the Taliban have deteriorated. Earlier this year, Pakistani officials ordered law enforcement agencies nationwide to arrest Afghans without valid visas. This is part of a years-long campaign of forced returns that has sent millions of Afghans back to a country where many face homelessness and unemployment. Many of those Afghan refugees were born and raised in Pakistan.

The Taliban’s “amnesty” is empty words. It is not a guarantee of safety.

On its first day back in power in August 2021, the Taliban announced a general amnesty for Afghans who worked with Western-backed forces and the former republic government of Afghanistan. That promise was never kept. The United Nations has documented reports of extrajudicial killings, arbitrary detentions, and other abuses. The families of former U.S. partners have particular reason to fear for their safety.

The policy to return Afghans to Afghanistan also lends credibility to the Taliban.

When the United States sends people into Taliban-controlled Afghanistan, even through a middleman, it implies that returning is safe. It suggests that the United States is willing to rely on the assurances of a regime that has repeatedly broken its promises and violated fundamental rights. Deporting Afghans in this way serves the Taliban’s desire to be treated as a legitimate government and to establish normal relations with the Trump administration.

The Trump administration advanced a similar narrative last year in May, when it ended temporary protections for Afghans, claiming that “Afghanistan has had an improved security situation” despite clear evidence to the contrary.

Cooperating, even indirectly, with a regime that has barred half the population of Afghanistan – girls and women – from education and public life, and has violated every international and national law gains the United States nothing in return. It is neither smart nor logical. It would not serve the U.S. now or in the future. It adds to the humiliation of how the U.S. withdrew from Afghanistan and handed the country back to the Taliban, a terrorist group it fought for 20 years.

The United States gains nothing from this policy. It loses far more.

The cost of this policy lands on American credibility. The United States asked Afghans to translate, guard, drive, gather intelligence, cook, clean, implement the many projects, and fight beside its forces, and promised to stand by them. Abandoning those allies, or their families, breaks that promise and abandons its obligation to protect people who are in harm’s way because they supported the U.S. mission.

The damage goes beyond Afghanistan. Future partners in any other conflict will remember how the United States treated those who stood with it. This is not border security. These individuals have already undergone vetting. It does not make Americans safer. It uses federal resources to send people toward danger, and abandons those who trusted the United States.

63% of Americans do not want Afghans to be deported.

A bipartisan national poll by AfghanEvac and HIAS, designed and run by Lake Research Partners and The …

author: Unknown
title: Eskişehir’de göçmen ve mülteci işçiler güvencesizliğe mahkûm ediliyor
content:
Berivan Özkara [email protected]

Eskişehir’de tarımdan hayvancılığa, sanayiden otomotiv atölyelerine, ev içi bakım işlerinden farklı hizmet alanlarına kadar pek çok sektörde göçmen ve mülteci işçiler çalışıyor. Düşük ücret, sigortasız çalışma, ödenmeyen alacaklar, işten çıkarılma ya da sınır dışı edilme korkusu, göçmen ve mülteci işçilerin karşı karşıya kaldığı başlıca sorunlar arasında. Patronlar, göçmenlerin güvencesiz koşullarını emek maliyetini azaltmanın bir aracı olarak kullanıyor. Avukat Şahap Arpacı ile Eskişehir’deki örnekler üzerinden göçmen ve mülteci işçilerin çalışma koşullarını, yaşadıkları hak ihlallerini ve bu tablonun işçi sınıfının bütünü açısından ne anlama geldiğini konuştuk.

Eskişehir’de mülteci işçilerin yoğun olarak çalıştığı alanların başında tarım ve hayvancılık geliyor. Özellikle kırsal bölgelerde mevsimlik işlerde çalışan Afgan ve Suriyeli işçiler, ağır çalışma koşullarına ve düşük ücretlere rağmen geçimlerini sağlamaya çalışıyor. Alpu, Beylikova, İnönü, Mihalıççık ve Seyitgazi çevresindeki tarımsal üretimde mülteci emeğinin yaygın biçimde kullanıldığını belirten Şahap Arpacı, “Eskişehir’in köylerinde tarımla uğraşacak bir genç nüfus kalmadığı için bu bölümü Afganlar ve Suriyeliler doldurdu. Şu anda patates sökeceksek, domates toplayacaksak, pancar sökeceksek Eskişehir köylerinde bu işi büyük oranda Afganlar ve Suriyeliler yapıyor” diyor.

Bu işlerde çalışan mülteci işçiler, yerli işçilere kıyasla çok daha düşük ücretlerle çalıştırılabiliyor. Arpacı, kayıt dışılığın iş kazası ve hastalık durumlarında da işçileri savunmasız bıraktığını vurguluyor: “Herhangi bir iş kazası geçirmeleri halinde, bu tarlada da olabilir fabrikada da olabilir, hastaneye, adliyeye gidip hukuki anlamda başvurabilecek bir mekanizmadan da yoksunlar.”

Eskişehir’de mülteci işçilerin çalıştığı bir diğer alan sanayi. Avukat Şahap Arpacı, Teksan ve Baksan Sanayi Sitelerinde, otomotiv tamirhanelerinde, boya ve mobilya sektöründe çalışan Iraklı ve Suriyeli işçiler bulunduğunu; organize sanayi bölgesinde ana fabrikalara üretim yapan yan sanayi işletmelerinde de mülteci emeğinin kullanıldığını anlattı.

Bu alanlarda da kayıt dışılık, düşük ücret ve güvencesizlik öne çıkıyor. Göçmen ve mülteci işçilerin çalışma izinlerinin ya da sigorta kayıtlarının bulunmaması, ücret alacaklarını kanıtlamalarını da zorlaştırıyor. Arpacı, işçilerin aylarca ücret alamadığı durumlarla karşılaştıklarını belirterek, kayıt dışı çalışmanın hukuki süreçlerde yarattığı güçlüğü şöyle anlatıyor:

“En büyük sorunlardan bir tanesi, çok düşük ücretlere çalışmış olmalarına rağmen maaşlarını zamanında alamamaları. Sigorta girişleri yok, çalışma izinleri yok. Hangi hukuki yolla alamadığı üç aylık maaşı alacak? Avukat tutsa, iş mahkemesine, ara bulucuya başvuracak olsa bunu kanıtlayamayacağız. İş mahkemeleri SGK girişine ve çalışma izinlerine bakıyor.”

Patron ücreti eksik ödendiğinde ya da ödemeyi geciktirdiğinde işçi işten çıkarılma tehdidiyle karşılaşabiliyor. Mülteci ve göçmen işçiler bakımından bu baskıya, sınır dışı edilme korkusu da ekleniyor. İşçilerin çalışma ve oturma durumlarına ilişkin belirsizlikler, patronların elini güçlendirirken işçinin emeğinin karşılığını istemesini dahi zorlaştırıyor. Böylece ücretin ödenmemesi yalnızca iş yeri içinde yaşanan bir sorun olarak kalmıyor; işçinin ülkede kalma ve yaşamını sürdürme kaygısıyla birleşerek daha ağır bir baskıya dönüşüyor.

Arpacı’nın aktardığı Filistinli bir işçinin yaşadıkları, bu baskının nasıl işlediğini gösteriyor. Boya ve kimyasallarla çalıştığı iş yerinde işçinin fazla mesai ve diğer ücret alacaklarıyla birlikte 200 bin liranın üzerinde alacağı olduğunu belirten Arpacı, bu alacağın tahsili için hukuki sürecin başlatılmak istendiğini ancak patronun diğer işçileri tehdit ederek tanıklığı engellediğini anlattı:

“Şahit var; kendisi gibi Iraklı, Filistinli birçok işçi var, aynı problemleri yaşıyorlar. Ama hepsi bırakın şahitlik yapmayı, korktukları için müvekkilimizin telefonlarına çıkmamaya başladı. İşveren, ‘Sizi deport ederim, sizi göç idaresine şikayet ederim’ diyerek işçileri korkutuyor. Göç idaresinde tanıdıkları olduğunu söylüyor. Böyle bir şey olmasa bile ‘Göç idaresi müdürü benim akrabam, orada çalışan memur benim amcamın oğlu’ diyerek işçi üzerinde idari, işveren kaynaklı ve sosyal bir baskı kuruyor.” Arpacı, işçinin alacağının sonunda çok daha düşük bir tutar üzerinden anlaşmaya bağlandığını dile getirdi: “Biz en son 200 küsur bin liralık alacaktan vazgeçtik. Ara bulucuda 80 bin …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Migrant Rights Remain Unheard Ahead of Election
content:
THE KUAI KUAI STRIKE that came to an end earlier this month involved migrant workers being led across picket lines by labor brokers. Migrant workers were instructed to say on video that they were willing to work, unlike striking Kuai Kuai workers.

The strike by workers at iconic snack Kuai Kuai’s Zhongli factory came to an end after five days earlier this month. Kuai Kuai is an iconic snack best known for a superstition that keeping bags of it near machinery keeps them running smoothly. Kuai Kuai operates one factory in Taoyuan, but 130 out of 155 union members voted in favor of a strike after the company decided to relocate to Hsinchu.

The two sites are 39 kilometers from each other, meaning that the move is untenable for many workers. Workers were only informed of the land scale on September 1st. The factory has operated in Zhongli since 1968, and 1/3rd of workers at Kuai Kuai have worked there for more than thirty years, despite the fact that their wages are near minimum wage.

Workers have accused the San-Ti Group that owns Kuai Kuai of perhaps having only acquired the company with an eye on selling its land to Advanced Semiconductor Engineering Inc. Originally, Kuai Kuai workers were only offered a 5% pay increase and verbal assurances that they would be relocated to the new factory. It is to be seen if acquiring land to sell it to technology companies is a tactic increasingly adopted in corporate acquisitions going forward.

The incident of labor brokers bringing migrant workers across the picket line then highlights when migrant workers are pitted against domestic Taiwanese workers by their employers. In particular, one notes that this may become an increasingly common feature of protests going forward, in which employers aim to leverage splits between blue-collar migrant workers and domestic workers.

Indeed, this would sometimes be taking advantage of periodic waves of backlash against migrant workers.

Migrant worker groups recently demonstrated outside of the Ministry of Health and Welfare earlier this month, calling for being allowed to exercise their rights to maternity leave, as well as having days off. Instead of having work shifts, sometimes migrant workers are expected to work around the clock, sometimes even needing to hire other migrant workers to fill in.

On the same day, employers’ groups demonstrated outside of the Ministry of Labor, criticizing the government for not taking enough action about workers who have absconded from the job, what is framed as too long of a wait between replacing caregivers, and when migrant workers are pregnant and cannot work. Though this was framed as defending the interests of people with disabilities who require caregivers, the attempt is also to weaken migrant rights, so that they are less able to defend their labor rights, and are not made to work around the clock–as if they were robots, rather than human beings.

title: ‘Icepick’ Leak Exposes Thousands of Homeland Security Personnel, Groups and More
content:
Washington, DC — There’s been yet another major security breach among federal agencies. The Department of Homeland Security’s ‘single sign-on’ (SSO) login system was reportedly subverted by a hacker going by “Department of Peace” (DoP), which has revealed thousands upon thousands of federal employee records. Around one-fifth of Homeland Security’s personnel have been exposed. Offices and locations are identified in great detail, from Canadian airports to agents in U.S. embassies around the world. Groups assigned within the SSO system, going back at least to 2011, are also exposed, showing the names of globe-spanning activities, and management personnel handling undercover operations.


Thousands of personnel records include supervisors and subordinates, which enabled generating gigantic organizational charts automatically across these agencies. Combine this with the groups (some officials tagged in dozens) and one can easily browse around the highest levels of activities, including thousands of groups dealing with surveillance, special operations, finance, social media, and much, much more. author: Wini Omer
title: It’s not the refugees, it’s the austerity measures!
content:
A Sudanese journalist, with whom I worked for two years at the same newspaper, told me when I contacted him to check on his situation after the last wave of attacks against refugees in Libya: “We are trapped in our homes. We can’t leave. I didn’t send my kids to school since the beginning of this wave of violence. The situation is difficult beyond imagination.”

The Sudanese who left Sudan seeking refuge in Libya, amid very violent clashes that started in April 2023 and continue to this moment, are facing violence, danger, and hatred in what was supposed to be a safe refuge. But this reality is not exclusive to Sudanese refugees, and the violence is indifferent to other nationalities who are fleeing conflicts, war, and instability at home: Ethiopians, Eritreans, and refugees from the Central African Republic.

In Libya, African refugees faced waves of violence, the latest in June this year. Despite competing for power, Libya’s rival authorities in the east and west have united in stoking anti-migrant rhetoric and launching a violent campaign of mass detention and expulsions against migrants and refugees, as a recent

Human Rights Watch report

 has indicated.

In Egypt, a

crackdown campaign

 led by security forces, accompanied by social media hate speech against Sudanese and Syrian refugees, intensified on the ground, blaming them for the rise in living costs, mainly rents, groceries, and basic life needs. As a result of systematic brutality, between January and June 2026,

12 Sudanese passed away in Egyptian detention centers

 and police cells, including a child of 17. Refugees processed for deportation are forced to sign voluntary return declarations.

Sudan hosts one of the largest refugee and asylum-seeker populations in Africa, mainly South Sudanese, Ethiopians, and Eritreans, who currently face detention and

forced deportation

 from the capital, Khartoum, to refugee camps close to the borders with their countries of origin, after the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) regained control of the capital. This step was taken following a growing political rhetoric that profiled them as criminals and blamed them for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) controlling Khartoum. Accordingly, they were deported to refugee camps in White Nile State, Al-Gadarif State, and Kassala State, camps that lack all basic human needs and restrict freedom of movement and the right to work. Many South Sudanese mothers were deported while their children were not allowed to accompany them, leaving them in limbo.

Such rhetoric, mainly produced and shared by pro-SAF individuals and platforms, provides the military establishment with a popular cover to reproduce its symbolic authority. It is also used by some actors within the army as a tool to bolster its legitimacy against the Rapid Support Forces, portraying it as the guardian of national sovereignty and the representative of the “authentic Sudanese” against the “foreign threat.” This reflects a deeper attempt to regain control over the state and society at a moment of total collapse of political and legal frameworks.

For many of these refugees, especially the Eritreans, returning is not an option, considering the human rights situation in Eritrea. But according to media reports, both Eritrea and Sudan are

complicit in the repatriation of civilians from Sudan

 back to Eritrea.

Whether it is the systematic violence against Sudanese refugees on the continent, or the deliberate violence against African refugees in Sudan, these incidents reflect one broader reality in which violence is used and reproduced either by state actors or by the citizens of the host countries to whom the refugees sought safety within the African continent. This reality raises a critical question about how to understand such incidents, the politics behind them, and why we are seeing them now.

Shifting the blame

Have the refugees led to the economic crises in Egypt, Libya, or Tunisia? Or are these crises a direct result of the state’s social and economic policies?

In Egypt, the last ten years have witnessed a high level of dependence on debt; Egypt has become one of the IMF’s largest borrowers, while social expenditure, including social protection, health, and education, has shrunk, accompanied by political oppression. Those debts have been invested in projects lacking a developmental dimension, such as

the new administrative capital

 project, which is expected to cost up to $300 billion by the time it’s finalized …

author: Amina Khan
title: EU transforms Frontex into a high-tech deportation command centre
content:
Yesterday, 27 October 2026, the European Commission tabled a new Regulation for Frontex, the EU’s border agency, expanding its powers and refocusing its mandate on deportations, preventing arrivals, and surveillance beyond EU territories and into social media. This would effectively turn Frontex into the EU’s deportation agency, equivalent of ICE in the United States.

At the centre of this reform is a budget that would almost double to nearly €12 billion for 2028–2034, leading to a massive expansion of the EU security and surveillance industrial complex. Frontex will test and deploy new technology to repress migrants, funnelling billions of taxpayer money to surveillance, security and defence contractors. EU’s hostile border security regime has for years produced systemic and massive human rights violations of migrants, refugees and racialised people, and those who stand in solidarity with them. This proposal will accelerate that.

Frontex as an ICE-style deportation enforcement agency

The proposal operationalises the recently adopted Deportations Regulation and deepens Frontex’s position as the central actor of a Europe-wide deportation machine. This will make the agency responsible for collecting and analysing data from Member States in order to “predict” deportation needs, and allocating resources to them. Frontex will now have a “Deportation Coordination Centre” that is expected to act at all stages of the deportation procedure, from detecting and identifying people that may be expulsed, booking or arranging flights and escorts, to monitoring their “reintegration” in the destination country.

Alarmingly, it expands Frontex’s powers to deport outside of the EU’s borders. Based on a simple status agreement, Frontex will be able to deport people from one third country to another, with the aim of preventing people from even reaching the EU. This will likely mean sharing sensitive data with third countries and countries of origin, where individuals may be at risk of persecution or harm.

The Frontex mandate reform comes in a package with a proposal to digitalise the management of deportation cases. The border control agency is given a key role in the harmonised technical design of EU and national digital systems, to exchange data on deportations, including sensitive data transfers to third countries (biometric data, travel documents and history, grounds for deportation, health data, etc.), and automate certain steps of the procedure, such as adding deportation orders in the Schengen Information System (SIS) to detect people.

Increased data processing and content policing

With this reform, Frontex’s practice of “debriefing interviews” is codified, particularly during the screening procedure introduced by the Migration Pact. The agency conducts these covert “voluntary” interrogations of people immediately after they disembark or cross the border. During these interviews, the agency extracts data from migrants deemed to be “suspects” of “cross-border crime”, without the possibility for migrants to seek legal counsel. Debriefing interviews have been rightfully criticised for their absence of fundamental rights monitoring and their unfairness as they take place when a person is detained and lacks privacy.

A new “Online Monitoring and Response Centre” will also surveil social media platforms to identify “suspicious behaviours or trends” in people’s movements at the EU borders, and before that, in the countries of origin and transit. Aggregated data collected online will be fed into Frontex’s “risk analysis” to guide border forces’ deployment and reaction. Social media monitoring was already declared as carrying high-risk for violating the fundamental rights of people affected, and was banned by the European Data Protection Supervisor in 2019 when first implemented by the EU Agency for Asylum.

Frontex will also seek designation as a trusted flagger under the Digital Services Act (DSA), allowing the agency to report pieces of online content to platforms for removal, effectively giving the agency extrajudicial powers to police the internet. It may also recommend national authorities to issue binding take-down notices. Frontex depriving people from finding legal support, sharing their stories or expressing solidarity is undoubtedly a serious infringement of freedom of expression.

All information collected during debriefings and online monitoring activities will contribute to Frontex’s border surveillance intelligence …

author: TGEU
title: Join the HIV Awareness Week in Berlin to establish the Emergency Support Network
content:
We are organising two free-of-charge parallel training programmes for queer and trans people that will come together on Friday, 20 November, to establish the Emergency Support Network.


This network should help people navigate services, identify realistic pathways to HIV prevention and care, and receive support without having to navigate complex systems alone. We also want to recognise that Ballroom houses, queer and trans collectives, and migrant communities already provide essential care infrastructure. We intend to strengthen these existing relationships, rather than create a parallel system disconnected from the communities themselves.


The initiative is particularly focused on two target audience groups:


Queer and trans people living with HIV who face barriers to accessing healthcare, especially those without health insurance, appropriate documentation, or access to HIV treatment and other essential services.


Queer and trans people on the move, including migrants, refugees, asylum seekers and undocumented people, who face difficulties accessing healthcare, HIV prevention, testing, PrEP, PEP and treatment.


Community HIV Training — 16, 18 and 20 November


This programme is intended for queer and trans adults, particularly queer and trans youth aged 18 and over, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, undocumented people and other people on the move.


It is especially relevant to queer and trans people who are living with HIV and face difficulties accessing treatment or healthcare, as well as those who need access to HIV prevention, testing, PrEP, PEP and other sexual health services.


The sessions will be interactive and community-led, covering HIV prevention and care, PrEP, PEP, testing, treatment, U=U, sexual health, pleasure, harm reduction and navigating healthcare systems.


An important feature is that registration for this programme is anonymous.

 Participants are not asked to provide their names, email addresses or HIV status. Anyone who wants to receive practical information or reminders can voluntarily register their email address through a separate form, which is not linked to their anonymous demographic responses.


This distinction is particularly important for people who may be reluctant to engage with services or activities because of concerns about confidentiality, stigma or their migration status.


register here


Health Champions Training — 17, 19 and 20 November


This programme is designed for trans and queer community leaders, particularly people involved in Ballroom houses, collectives and grassroots networks.


The training follows a train-the-trainer approach and will cover HIV, STIs and other infectious diseases prevention, treatment and sexual and reproductive health knowledge, and other topics like U=U, harm reduction, structural barriers to healthcare, peer education and safe healthcare navigation.


Participants will work through practical exercises such as community mapping, HIV knowledge games, real-life scenarios, role-play and referral mapping. The objective is to equip them to become trusted points of connection between their communities and healthcare services, while recognising that Health Champions are not expected to act as clinicians, legal experts or crisis responders.


On the final day, Health Champions will meet healthcare professionals, service providers and participants from the other training programme to help establish practical referral pathways and community-based support structures.


register here


Building the Emergency Support Network

—


20 November


On Friday, participants from both programmes will come together with healthcare professionals, community organisations and service providers.


The aim is to establish direct connections between people who need support, trusted community leaders and organisations capable of providing services. Participants will learn what support is available, who can access it, what barriers remain and how to make safe referrals.


The week will culminate in

Under the Jellicle Moon Kiki Ball on Saturday, 21 November

, celebrating Ballroom culture, community leadership and the relationships developed throughout the initiative.


Note:

All workshop participants must be 18 or older and attend all three days of their respective training. Snacks and dinner will be provided each day.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: La crisis del capital es la crisis del pueblo
content:
La frase “la crisis del capital es la crisis del pueblo” no es una consigna menor ni una metáfora piadosa. Condensa una tesis política de fondo: las crisis capitalistas no son accidentes técnicos que ocurren en un plano separado de la vida social, sino procesos que se descargan sobre las condiciones materiales de existencia de las mayorías. Lo que para el capital aparece como una crisis de valorización, caída de la tasa de ganancia, sobreacumulación o estallido financiero, para el pueblo se traduce en desempleo, precarización, pérdida de derechos, ajuste, pobreza y exclusión. La frase invierte la mirada dominante: no hay crisis “económica” que no sea, al mismo tiempo, una crisis de la reproducción social de los de abajo.


István Mészáros, Antonio Gramsci, PRT


István Mészáros permite llevar esa intuición a su fundamento material. Su concepto de crisis estructural no describe un bache cíclico que se supera con más o menos sufrimiento, sino un continuum de crisis que revela los límites absolutos del capital. A partir de la década de 1970, el sistema entró en una fase de crisis universal, global, prolongada e irreversible dentro de su propia lógica. Para sostener la acumulación, el capital se ve empujado a prescindir de la fuerza de trabajo, única fuente de valor, y a organizar lo que Mészáros llama una producción destructiva: la autorreproducción del capital exige tornar dispensables a seres humanos, destruir condiciones de vida, desarticular la sociabilidad. La crisis del capital no es entonces un fenómeno externo al pueblo; penetra en todos los dominios y niveles de la reproducción social. Es la crisis de las condiciones materiales que hacen posible la vida popular. De ahí que la disyuntiva que plantea Mészáros sea tan brutal como precisa: socialismo o barbarie.


Antonio Gramsci añade la dimensión política y cultural. Para Gramsci, una crisis del capital es también una crisis de hegemonía. La clase dominante pierde capacidad de dirigir ideológica y culturalmente a la sociedad; su concepción del mundo se agrieta y ya no logra el consenso necesario para gobernar. La hegemonía no es un equilibrio estable, sino la gestión de una crisis latente o manifiesta. Cuando esa gestión fracasa, se abre un interregno en el que el viejo mundo no termina de morir y el nuevo no acaba de nacer. En ese momento, la crisis del capital se manifiesta como desorientación, ruptura del tejido social y disputa por la dirección. Es allí donde Gramsci introduce la categoría de pueblo-nación: la alianza de las clases subalternas capaz de constituirse en fuerza nacional y portadora del futuro. La crisis del capital es crisis del pueblo porque desarticula su vida material y su sentido común, pero también porque abre la posibilidad de que ese pueblo se constituya como sujeto hegemónico alternativo.


Retrato de José Carlos Mariátegui tomado por el fotógrafo Diego Goyzueta en 1919. Fuente: archivo.mariategui.org


El marxismo latinoamericano da a la frase una concreción histórica y política. José Carlos Mariátegui vinculó la crisis del capitalismo con la necesidad de una revolución socialista que integrara el papel de los pueblos indígenas y sus formas comunales de vida; la crisis del capital era también la crisis de un orden neocolonial, y la respuesta popular debía tener un carácter antiimperialista y de liberación nacional. Álvaro García Linera, desde Bolivia, sostiene que lo nacional-popular, la irrupción plebeya en la política, solo surge en momentos de crisis del régimen de dominación y de acumulación. La crisis del capital y de sus formas estatales debilita el horizonte predictivo, activa la disponibilidad colectiva a revocar creencias y permite que el pueblo desborde el Estado para disputar la dirección de la sociedad. En la periferia, la crisis del capital es crisis del pueblo porque golpea la vida de las mayorías y, al mismo tiempo, abre el momento en que ese pueblo irrumpe como sujeto que busca reconstruir la sociedad sobre nuevas bases.


El PRT argentino y su síntesis de marxismo-leninismo-guevarismo llevan esta lectura a un mandato estratégico. Para el PRT, la crisis del capital no es solo un diagnóstico ni una denuncia del sufrimiento popular; es la condición objetiva que agudiza las contradicciones y empuja a las masas hacia la lucha. El partido se pensó como vanguardia armada, y su IV Congreso de 1968, con “El único camino hasta el poder obrero y el socialismo”, formalizó la adopción del guevarismo: solo había un camino para …

author: Unknown
title: Can all the anti-capitalists stop reblogging this noble savage bullshit and start connecting with…
content:
diaryofandnwoman

:


Can all the anti-capitalists stop reblogging this noble savage bullshit and start connecting with the material reality of human well-being. There is no one way humans were ‘meant’ to live and this just stereotypes all pre-historical cultures into one hippy caricature.

But also, like quite a lot of anarchists: I’ve done most of this shit. I’ve lived in communities that camped in nature and cooked around a fire together and sang and danced and told each other about cool edible plants.

It certainly had some benefits for my mental health. It didn’t fix systematic oppression, it didn’t protect me from transphobia, it didn’t solve that I did’t have access to health care. Systemic problems require systemic solutions.

Having tried the community-in-nature life and being able to compare it to 'individualist’ 21st century life, I can say that access to a hot showed, heating, a bed that supports my back, a nutritionally balanced diet and medication also have pretty huge benefits for my mental health. Maybe, Idk… redistributing the fruits of our society according to everyone’s needs. That would be pretty good for our mental health.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Halloween riots as youth uprising pushes on
content:
Photograph: Alain Jocard/AFP


from

Freedom News

, 2 November 2026


Against efforts by systemic forces to keep youth discontent in check, decentralised insurrection and autonomy continue to break through


Blade Runner


Halloween weekend saw mass protests throughout

France

,

Albania

,

Germany

,

Switzerland

 and

Portugal

, with riots erupting across multiple cities.


As Gen Z–led insurrections flare up globally, a neo-fascist surge has risen steadily alongside them. In the UK, the

assault on Freedom Bookshop

 sounds a clear warning and a reminder that the street-level provocations escalating across the country over the past few years are happening for a reason.


Systemic actors seek to keep the

youth’s insurgent tendencies

 in check, deliberately redirecting anger toward vulnerable groups such as

migrants

. This manufactured resentment is predictable amid ever-increasing housing and living costs for the working classes, pushing an increasing number of people to the margins.


At a time when Western superpowers engage in proxy wars and genocides abroad while leading an arms race at home, they ask their citizens to live with less and prepare for disaster.


This dynamic stems directly from the neoliberal restructuring of Western production in the 1980s. Designed to crush the advances of previous labour movements, it enforced the TINA (“There Is No Alternative”) dogma across politics and culture alike. Consequently, it has become increasingly difficult to imagine alternative ways of surviving, let alone navigating complex issues like personal liberty, identity, equality, and disagreement.


What mainstream news decries as a “shocking” resurgence of patriarchal misogyny among young people is often just youth mimicking adult behaviour—mirroring the brutality of genocidal wars and the competitive ethos of streaming media. Reproduced in schools and everyday life, hegemonic neoliberal ethics instil a worldview based on survival of the fittest, top-dog dominance, and “kill or be killed.”


Yet what this apparatus of indoctrination tries to suppress is the simple fact that when left to their own devices, most people naturally build networks of communal solidarity and mutual aid. In Serbia, following the Novi Sad canopy collapse and subsequent police violence,

student movements organised

 their resistance through confederated horizontal councils, effectively shifting the national political narrative. When elections arrived, they took the difficult decision to form an independent list that won national elections on 25 October 2026, ousting the Vu?i? regime after 15 years in power.


Representative democracy may not be a vehicle for social revolution, but this effort demonstrates the power of prefigurative politics. It proves that young people can mock authority, circumvent top-down structures, and channel the rage generated by class war into creative, radical action.


Where horizontal councils represent

organised prefigurative power

, the unguided unruliness of marginalised youth represents its raw, volatile foundation. Neofascist networks, nurtured by neoliberal centres, actively attempt to capture this untapped energy—redirecting class anger away from the ruling class to protect existing power structures. Yet as Gen Z leads insurrections worldwide, state attempts to enforce “law and order” inevitably generate contested spaces of disorder.


Radical left and anarchist currents meet the youth in these spaces, where bands of poor kids raised in the hinterlands of 21st-century capitalism disrupt the peace of petty bourgeois business owners. Their unguided discontent with the commodity society is a crude but authentic attempt to claim back autonomy. When survival is squeezed down to petty crime and syndicate work, roaming the streets at night with loot in hand becomes simultaneously alienating and liberating—an experiential truth of street-level autonomy that no top-down political theory can fully capture.


This reality explains the state’s aggressive attempts to criminalise and persecute horizontal protest structures, such as

Palestine Action in the UK

, which has not only struck major blows against domestic arms supply chains but has inspired offshoots across Europe and the US. The state relies on an old tactic: conflating separate legal cases to try activists together as members of an organised crime enterprise. The goal is to prevent the generalisation of dissent.

title: Αύριο θα είναι η δική σου σειρά… Όταν ο καπιταλισμός κατασκοπεύει (Β’ Μέρος)
content:
Του Ν’ Γκουζότο


Εικοσιτρία χρόνια πριν γίνεται μια δημόσια συζήτηση, στην Ομοσπονδιακή Επιτροπή Εμπορίου των ΗΠΑ, σχετικά με την ανάγκη νομοθέτησης, για την ιδιωτικότητα των πολιτών. Είναι δύο ομάδες που συγκρούονται, μπροστά στα μέλη της επιτροπής που καλούνται να αποφασίσουν, αν θα μπουν κανόνες που θα ορίζουν τι αποτελεί παραβίαση της ιδιωτικότητας. Από την μια μεριά τα στελέχη της τεχνολογικής βιομηχανίας υποστηρίζουν ότι είναι απόλυτα ικανοί να ρυθμίσουν τα πάντα κι ότι κάθε κυβερνητική παρέμβαση θα ήταν εκτός από δαπανηρή και αντιπαραγωγική. Από την άλλη μεριά οι φιλελεύθεροι υποστηρικτές των πολιτικών ελευθεριών ωρύονται προειδοποιώντας ότι, οι δυνατότητες συλλογής και επεξεργασίας προσωπικών δεδομένων από την πλευρά των εταιρειών, αποτελούν μια πρωτοφανή απειλή για τις ατομικές ελευθερίες. Ζητούσαν από την επιτροπή να αποφασίσει

τι συνιστούν τα ανθρώπινα πλάσματα στην νέα ηλεκτρονική εποχή.

 Αν υπάρχει κάποιο όριο ή απλά θεωρούνται σαν δωρεάν πρώτη ύλη για το εμπόριο; Τότε ένα επίτροπος

αναρωτήθηκε

 που πρέπει να τεθεί αυτό το όριο;


Όπως εύκολα γίνεται κατανοητό, διανύοντας την χρυσή δεκαετία του νεοφιλελεύθερου καπιταλισμού όπου η αγορά αυτορυθμίζεται, το όριο που ζητούσαν οι πάντες ποτέ δεν μπήκε.


Η αγορά κέρδισε και έβαλε τα θεμέλια της ανάπτυξης μιας νέας οικονομικής λογικής, την οποία η

 Shoshana Zyboff

, την ονομάτισε

κατασκοπευτικό καπιταλισμό.


Η επιτυχία του βασίζεται στη δημιουργία σχέσεων με την μορφή ενός μονόδρομου καθρέφτη, οι τζαμάδες τους αποκαλούν και spyglass, όπου ενώ παρακολουθείσαι, εν αγνοία σου βαφτίζεσαι σε μια κολυμπήθρα μετα-αλήθειας. Κατόρθωσε να ριζώσει και να ευδοκιμήσει στο διαδίκτυο – που οριζόταν σαν ο μεγαλύτερος ακυβέρνητος χώρος στον κόσμο, και να το ελέγξει απόλυτα.


Όταν πρωτοεμφανίστηκε η Google, όλοι άρχισαν να χρησιμοποιούν τη νέα μηχανή αναζήτησης ψάχνοντας οτιδήποτε μπορούσαν να φανταστούν και μάλιστα δωρεάν. Κανείς δεν κατάλαβε ποτέ, ότι ταυτόχρονα τον έψαχνε και η Google. Το ίδιο έγινε και με το Facebook, όπου όλοι πίστεψαν ότι ήταν ένας πίνακας ανακοινώσεων όπου ο καθένας μπορούσε να καρφιτσώσει ένα σημείωμα. Σήμερα γνωρίζουμε ότι οι ψηφιακές πλατφόρμες είναι ένα μέσον που μπορεί ο καθένας να διασπείρει ψευδείς αλήθειες σαν επικίνδυνους ιούς γιατί γι’ αυτές δεν παράγεται κανένα εμβόλιο.


Όλα αυτά στηρίζονται στην ψευδαίσθηση, ότι η ζωή του καθενός είναι ιδιωτική υπόθεση κι ότι εμείς επιλέγουμε, πιο κομμάτι πληροφορίας ανταλλάσσουμε έναντι μιας επιθυμητής συναλλαγής. Μια παρόμοια συναλλαγή θα εμφανιστεί σύντομα και στην Ελλάδα, θα διαφημιστεί σαν ο πιο ασφαλής τρόπος συναλλαγών. Θα αντικαταστήσει την πιστωτική κάρτα, αυτή άλλωστε χάνεται ή κλέβεται και θα βασίζεται πάνω στην αναγνώριση του προσώπου, μέσω των βιομετρικών χαρακτηριστικών. Σιγά σιγά περνάμε σ’ έναν τρόπο ζωής που το πρόσωπο μετατρέπεται σε κάρτα εισόδου, στην οικονομική αλλά και κοινωνική ζωή, με δικαίωμα πρόσβασης. Είναι το πρώτο σημείο που φαίνεται να συναντιούνται οι δύο κυρίαρχοι τρόποι επιτήρησης στον σημερινό κόσμο, ο Κινεζικός και ο Αμερικανικός ή Δυτικός τρόπος. Το ξεκίνησαν οι Κινέζοι «κομμουνιστές», όταν δημιούργησαν ένα προσωποποιημένο σύστημα κοινωνικής πίστωσης, που βασιζόταν στην αναγνώριση προσώπου, αλλά και συναισθημάτων. Οι περισσότεροι Κινέζοι συμφώνησαν ότι ήταν ένα σύστημα που φυλούσε τους έντιμους.


Αλλά πολλοί και μεταξύ τους κι εγώ, πιστεύουμε, ότι ένα σύστημα που φακελώνει ενώ διαβάζει την συμπεριφορά μας, αποφασίζει αν αποτελούμε ή όχι κοινωνική απειλή αν μη τι άλλο, εκτός από βαθιά ταξικό είναι απόλυτα ολοκληρωτικό. Ήδη τα συστημικά μέσα και site διαφημίζουν τον τρόπο σαν πιο αξιόπιστο, μπορεί να ξεχωρίσει ακόμα και ομοζυγωτικούς διδύμους, διασκεδάζουν τα περί φακελώματος με την λογική ότι το πρόσωπο μας υπάρχει παντού στο Διαδίκτυο. Τα υπόλοιπα, φαντάζουν ψιλά γράμματα για τους ίδιους διότι θεωρούν τους εαυτούς τους, όπως και οι Κινέζοι, εκ των προτέρων αθώους. Άλλωστε είναι γνωστό ότι οι πρώτοι που επικροτούν αυτού του είδους τα συστήματα, δηλώνοντας ότι

οι ίδιοι δεν έχουν να κρύψουν τίποτα

, είναι οι μικροαστοί της μεσαίας τάξης.

author: Unknown
title: ‘Labor struggle against capitalism and exploitation’ discussed at women’s conference in Ankara
content:
The second session of the “Women Discuss the Future Side by Side” conference, held at the Chamber of Civil Engineers (İMO) of the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB) in Ankara featured discussions under the theme “Labor struggle against capitalism and exploitation.”


The conference is organized at the initiative of 80 women, including journalists, writers, academics, politicians, and activists.


Ayfer Koçak, Co-Chair of the Confederation of Public Employees’ Trade Unions (KESK), said, “If we are to organize against exploitation, we must create a society in which workers can receive what they are entitled to, a society we call a ‘democratic society.’”


Sabahat Tuncel, an activist with the Free Women’s Movement (Tevgera Jinên Azad – TJA), stated that exploitation could not be eliminated without abolishing the capitalist system. “Because this system itself generates inequality and labor exploitation. Consequently, it exploits women’s labor even further. What we really need to focus on is how to eliminate this system.”


Tuncel continued: “As Marx said, ‘Workers are free only insofar as they can sell their labor,’ but even those conditions have now changed. Workers can no longer even sell their labor freely. Wage increases should not be the sole concern of workers and laborers. Today, the working class is taking to the streets despite the trade unions. We can build democratic socialism through the liberation of labor. If we are not free, if labor is not free, we cannot build a new system. Let us change this system. We can replace it with democratic socialism. We can organize both elderly care and childcare communally. We can find ways to collectivize our labor.”


Emine Teğin, who became known for her speech at a public gathering organized by the DEM Party in Siirt, also addressed the conference, saying: “Why are our young girls and women being killed? Why can we not send our children to university? Why was Rojin Kabaiş killed? Why were Gülistan Doku and İpek Er driven to their deaths? As women, we demand answers to these questions. We want a life of justice, equality, and dignity.”


The conference will continue with its final session, titled “The struggle for gender equality and freedom.”

author: Unknown
title: Murray Bookchin - The Youth Culture
content:
Author

: Murray Bookchin

Title

: The Youth Culture

Subtitle

: An Anarcho-Communist View

Date

: 1970

Notes

: Published in

Hip Culture: 6 Essays on Its Revolutionary Potential; Yippie, Third World, Feminist, Marxist, High School Student, Anarchist

.

Source

: <

https://archive.org/details/HipCulture

>


 The “hip culture”—the word is really the youth culture and I will use it from now on—does not really need any “defenders”.

[1]

 As an elemental phenomenon, its own existence and development must eventually constitute its only “defense”. What the Youth Culture

does

 need, however, is a better interpretation than it has received up to now—and this would be impossible to achieve without dealing with its critics.


 Bourgeois critics may be dismissed out of hand. Generally, criticism of this kind takes the form either of a patronizing psychoanalysis (the classical image of the “rebellious sons” slaying their “fathers”) or simply a brute condemnation directed against the “impudence” of young people. The most serious criticism, or at least the most systematic, comes from the orthodox Marxists, who usually complain that the Youth Culture is not sufficiently “revolutionary”. On close inspection the criticism from this quarter centers around the notion that the Youth Culture is “elitist”, “escapist”, “bourgeois”, “anti-rational” and should all else fail—nonpolitical.


 Here, one comes up against a vexing problem. Polemics with orthodox Marxists usually appear in a false light—and for

both

 sides of the argument. Any revolutionary who attempts to interpret the Youth Culture from a non-marxian viewpoint tends to appear like a spiritualized vapor, or “worse” (horror of horrors!), a “petty bourgeois hedonist” who is far removed from the bread-and-butter issues and oppressions of daily life. The Old Left “critic” of the Youth Culture, in turn, seems to live in an unreality of his/her own, patently ignoring the brute fact that long-hairs and students are far in advance of the workers on all the critical issues of the day. The two sides become polarized into “either... or” positions, as though oppression can be defined in only one of two ways: spiritual

or

 material, psychic

or

 economic, alienative

or

 exploitative. This, or course, is pure bullshit. Both go together. They interpenetrate in varying degrees and assume different degrees of weight, depending upon the situation in question. The crisis of bourgeois society is

universal’,

 it can no longer be boxed into the neat little compartments that the orthodox Marxists have constructed, polished, and labored to preserve for nearly a century. As women and blacks well know, every form of material oppression is marked by spiritual oppression and every form of spiritual oppression by material oppression. In the case of many white young people, material oppression may not have as much

weight

 as spiritual, but it is nonetheless real and particularly visible on campuses, where students are processed by an “educational” system that operates along factory lines.


 The most astonishing thing about the traditional Marxists is their utter inability to see how enormously the terrain of the revolutionary struggle has expanded with the development of capitalism. Marxian orthodoxy is still fighting the battle of “socialism”: a very specific historical terrain, delimited by the old coal-steel technology of the Industrial Revolution, the cry for “justice,” the killing exploitation of the “factory hand,” and a conception of revolution mediated by “transitional stages” (the “proletarian dictatorship” and “socialist state”) designed not only to deal with counterrevolution but, in the words of Marx and Engels, “to increase the total of productive forces as rapidly as possible.” In the century and more since Marx and Engels penned these words, capitalism itself has increased “the total of productive forces” to a point where even toil, not only material scarcity, is being brought into question—and these new “productive forces” could easily be extended to the Third World following a revolution in America and Europe. What the traditional Marxists can’t get into their heads is that capitalism has finally created the material preconditions for

communism (libertarian

 communism, flttflrctocommunism), not “socialism”; for

freedom,

 not “justice” (or what used to be called “social democracy”).


 This enormous change has profoundly affected all the issues and movements of our …

author: Unknown
title: Пётр Кропоткин - Русская Революция и Анархизм.
content:
Автор

: Пётр Кропоткин

Название

: Русская Революция и Анархизм.

Подзаголовок

: Доклады, читанные на съезде Коммунистов-Анархистов, в октябре 1906 года. Под редакцией П. Кропоткина

Дата

: 1907


 В октябре 1906 года, перед тем как возобновить издание Листков «

ХЛЕБ и ВОЛЯ

», несколько товарищей коммунистов-анархистов собрались для обсуждения разных вопросов, выставленных опытом молодого анархического движения в России. Было прочтено для этого несколько Докладов, и приняты были Заключения.


 И те и другие были напечатаны в «Листках», а теперь печатаются отдельной брошюрой, как материал для товарищеского обсуждения в России.


ЗАКЛЮЧЕНИЯ СЪЕЗДА.


 –––––––––––––


1. – Политическая и экономическая

революция.


 1. – Наша цель – социальная революция, то есть полное уничтожение Капитализма и Государства, и замена их Анархическим Коммунизмом. Эту конечную цель мы всегда должны иметь в виду, и ею мы должны руководиться в оценке совершающихся событий.


 Характер революции, начавшейся в России, уже определился. Она происходит не в виде уличного бунта, ведущего к созыву парламента, а в виде народной революции, которая продлится несколько лет, низвергнет старый порядок вообще и глубоко изменит

все экономические отношения вместе с политическим строем

.


 В обоих этих направлениях мы и должны вести борьбу против старого строя. Делить её во времени на два периода: один для получения представительного правления, а другой – для получения экономических реформ, – мы считаем положительно невозможным. Мы утверждаем, наоборот, что народ только то и получит от революции в области экономической, что он сам возьмёт революционным путём. Самое «революционное» Учредительное Собрание будет только сделкой между старым порядком и новым, и сможет только утвердить на бумаге то, что народ сделает на деле.


 Из этого, однако, отнюдь не следует, чтобы мы могли относиться безучастно к борьбе, ведущейся теперь против самодержавия. Мы боремся против Государства, но не в отвлечённой идее, а в тех формах, которые оно принимает в жизни народов. Поэтому мы боремся против него всегда и везде, и очевидно не можем не бороться против самого худшего его воплощения – самодержавия, которое представляет собой самую сильную и самую стойкую форму государства, – самый сильный оплот крупного землевладения и капитализма – самое ужасное орудие богатых и властных для доведения народа до нищеты и духовного рабства.


 Чем сильнее – именно теперь – будет наша борьба против русского самодержавного государства, чем больше будет доля народа, а вместе с народом – и наша доля в ниспровержении теперешнего самовластия опричников, – тем слабее будет та новая форма государственного гнёта, которая может создаться на развалинах самодержавия.


 Если место самодержавия заступит всероссийский парламент, то чем сильнее выступят народные массы в свержении самодержавия, и чем больше будет их участие в созидании новых, местных форм жизни страны, – тем слабее будет власть буржуазии и помещиков в парламенте, и тем легче будет вести дальнейшую борьбу.


 В Думе нам делать нечего: у нас есть своя работа. Но наша работа – вовсе не в том, чтобы бороться против сторонников Думы, которые борются с самодержавием. Наше дело – в том, чтобы

проводить в народные массы идею захвата народом всего того, что нужно для жизни и производства

 – земли, фабрик, заводов, железных дорог и так далее – и бороться вместе с народом против мер, которые законодатели захотят принять в интересах капитализма и государственной централизации.


 Наше место всегда, везде – среди народа, вместе с народом, чтобы Русская Революция была шагом вперёд сравнительно с революцией французской и американской.


————


II. – О грабеже и экспроприации.


 На нашем съезде мы тщательно обсуждали вопрос о так называемой «экспроприации», личной и групповой, и собирались изложить наши мысли в виде докладов и заключений.


 Мы хотели указать на необходимость удержать слово «экспроприация» для такого насильственного

отчуждения

 земли, фабрик, заводов, домов и так далее, которое производится целым обществом – сельским, городским и так далее – в интересах всей деревни, города, области или народа; а не употреблять его для обозначения актов личного или группового

присвоения

 средств, – хотя бы и в видах революционных.


 Стремясь к экспроприации земли и всех средств производства русским народом, нам не следует, думали мы, заранее суживать смысл этой великой идеи – основе всего коммунистического миросозерцания.


 Мы хотели …

author: Wesley Whitman
title: လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ
content:
လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း ဆိုရှယ်ဒီမိုကရေစီ သီအိုရီ


Wesley Whitman

. Original:

Liberal-Anarchism

, September 14, 2025. Translated into Burmese by Hein Htet Kyaw.


လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒ ဆိုတာ သေချာနားလည်အောင်ကြည့်ရင် လွတ်လပ်တဲ့ဈေးကွက် ဒါမှမဟုတ် လွတ်လပ်ခွင့် (negative liberty) အတွက်တင် အကြောင်းပြချက် ပေးတာမျိုး မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။ အခြေခံအားဖြင့်ကတော့ ဖိနှိပ်မှုတွေကနေ လွတ်မြောက်ရေးဆိုင်ရာ ဒဿနတစ်ခု ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ အလားတူပါပဲ၊ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဆိုတာ မင်းမဲ့စရိုက် ဆုတောင်းပွဲ မဟုတ်ဘဲ မည်သူမျှ စိုးမိုးခြယ်လှယ်ခြင်းမရှိတဲ့ ဆန္ဒအလျောက် ဖွဲ့စည်းထားတဲ့ လူမှုအဖွဲ့အစည်းကို ဖန်တီးဖို့ ကြိုးပမ်းတာ ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ ဒီနားလည်မှု နှစ်ခုကို ပေါင်းစပ်ပြီး တွေးခေါ်မြှော်မြင်မှု ပရစ်ဇမ် (dialectical libertarian lens) နဲ့ ကြည့်လိုက်ရင်၊ အဲဒီအစဉ်အလာတွေကနေ ကျနော် “လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ” (liberal-anarchism) လို့ ခေါ်တဲ့ သီအိုရီသစ်တစ်ရပ် ဖြစ်ပေါ်လာပါတယ်။


အနုပဋိလောမ လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း နည်းလမ်း


လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဟာ သဘောတရားအခြေခံ လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်းဝါဒရဲ့ ယုတ္တိပေါ်မှာ အခြေခံထားတာပါ။ ဒါဟာ သေသူလို ပုံသေကားချပ် မူဝါဒတစ်ခု မဟုတ်ဘဲ အခြေအနေပေါ်မူတည်ပြီး ကြည့်တတ်တဲ့ နည်းလမ်းတစ်ခု ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ မူဝါဒ ဒါမှမဟုတ် အဖွဲ့အစည်း တစ်ခုခုကို “ပုံစံတကျ လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း ဟုတ်မဟုတ်” ဆုံးဖြတ်မယ့်အစား၊ ဒီနည်းလမ်းက အဲဒီအရာဟာ သီးခြားလူမှုအခြေအနေတစ်ခုမှာ “တကယ်ပဲ လူတွေကို ဖိနှိပ်မှုကနေ လွတ်မြောက်စေသလား” လို့ မေးခွန်းထုတ်ပါတယ်။ ဥပမာ- ခွဲခြားဆက်ဆံမှု ဆန့်ကျင်ရေး ဥပဒေတွေဟာ စီးပွားရေးလုပ်ငန်းရှင် တစ်ယောက်ရဲ့ ပုံစံတကျ လွတ်လပ်ခွင့်ကို ကန့်သတ်နိုင်ပေမယ့်၊ သမိုင်းကြောင်းအရ ဖိနှိပ်ခံထားရတဲ့ လူမှုအသိုင်းအဝိုင်းမှာတော့ ဖိနှိပ်မှုကို လျှော့ချပေးပြီး ဖိနှိပ်ခံရသူတွေရဲ့ တကယ့်လွတ်လပ်ခွင့်ကို တိုးတက်စေတဲ့အတွက် တကယ်တမ်းကျ လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း သဘောတရားနဲ့ ကိုက်ညီနေပါတယ်။


ဒီနည်းလမ်းကြောင့် အစိုးရရဲ့ ဝင်ရောက်စွက်ဖက်မှု တိုင်းကို ဖိနှိပ်မှုလို့ မမြင်တော့ပါဘူး။ တကယ်တော့ မြေယာတန်ဖိုးခွန် ဒါမှမဟုတ် လူမှုရေး အကျိုးအမြတ် ခွဲဝေမှု လိုမျိုး အစိုးရစွက်ဖက်မှုအချို့ဟာ လက်ဝါးကြီးအုပ် အခွင့်ထူးတွေကို ဖျက်ဆီးပစ်နိုင်ပြီး တစ်ဦးချင်းစီကို ပိုမိုလုပ်ပိုင်ခွင့် ပေးနိုင်ပါတယ်။ သမိုင်းဝင် အာဏာနဲ့ ကြွယ်ဝမှု စုစည်းမှုတွေ ကြောင့် ကစားကွင်းက မညီမညာဖြစ်နေတဲ့ လူအဖွဲ့အစည်းမှာ လွတ်လပ်ခွင့်ဆိုတာ ဝင်မစွက်ဖက်ဘဲ ဒီအတိုင်းကြည့်နေရုံနဲ့ မရဘဲ တက်တက်ကြွကြွ ပြန်လည်တည်ဆောက်ဖို့ လိုအပ်ပါတယ်။


ပြန်လည်ဖော်ထုတ်လိုက်သော လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒ


လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဟာ လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒရဲ့ သမိုင်းဝင် တိုးတက်ပြောင်းလဲမှု အပြည့်အဝကို လက်ခံထားပါတယ်။ အာဒမ် စမစ် (Adam Smith) နဲ့ ဂျွန် လော့ခ် (John Locke) တို့ရဲ့ တစ်ဦးချင်းစီရဲ့ လွတ်လပ်ခွင့်နဲ့ ပုဂ္ဂလိက ဦးဆောင်မှုကို အလေးပေးတဲ့ ဂန္ထဝင် လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒကိုရော၊ ဂျွန် ရောလ်စ် (John Rawls) ရဲ့ နိုင်ငံရေး လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒနဲ့ ဂျွန် မေးနဒ် ကိန်းစ် (John Maynard Keynes) တို့ရဲ့ စီးပွားရေး လက်တွေ့ဝါဒကိုပါ ပေါင်းစပ်ယူထားတာပါ။ ဒီတွေးခေါ်ရှင်တွေဟာ နိုင်ငံတော်ရဲ့ ဖိနှိပ်မှုပဲဖြစ်ဖြစ်၊ ဈေးကွက်ရဲ့ ဖိနှိပ်မှုပဲဖြစ်ဖြစ် ဖိနှိပ်ချုပ်ချယ်မှုတွေ ရှိနေသမျှ လွတ်လပ်ခွင့် ဆိုတာ ရှင်သန်လို့မရဘူးဆိုတဲ့ နားလည်မှုကို စေတနာတူ တူညီကြပါတယ်။


အာဒမ် စမစ် နဲ့ ဂျွန် လော့ခ် တို့လို ဂန္ထဝင် လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒီတွေဟာ မြေပိုင်ရှင် ဘုတ်ထိုင် စီးပွားရှာသူတွေရဲ့ အာဏာကို ကန့်သတ်ဖို့နဲ့ စီးပွားရေး သာယာဝပြောမှုကို ကျယ်ကျယ်ပြန့်ပြန့် မြှင့်တင်ဖို့အတွက် မြေယာတန်ဖိုး ခွန်ကောက်ခံတာကို ထောက်ခံခဲ့ကြပါတယ်။ ဂျွန် ရောလ်စ် က တရားမျှတတဲ့ လူအဖွဲ့အစည်းဆိုတာ အစဉ်အလာ ကင်းပီတယ်လစ်ဝါဒ ထက် ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှု ပစ္စည်းတွေကို လူထုကြား မျှမျှတတ ခွဲဝေပေးတဲ့ “ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှု-ပိုင်ဆိုင်သော ဒီမိုကရေစီ” ဖြစ်ရမယ်လို့ ဆိုပါတယ်။ ဒါ့အပြင် ရောလ်စ် က မညီမျှမှုတွေ ဖြစ်ပေါ်လာပြီးမှ ပစ္စည်းဥစ္စာတွေကို ပြန်လည်ခွဲဝေတာထက် မညီမျှမှုတွေ မဖြစ်ပေါ်အောင် အဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေကို ကြိုတင်ပုံစံထုတ်တာ က ပိုမိုထိရောက်ကြောင်း သဘောတရား ထည့်သွင်းခဲ့ပါတယ်။ တစ်ချိန်တည်းမှာပဲ ကိန်းစ် က အမှန်တကယ် ရှိနေတဲ့ ဈေးကွက်တွေရဲ့ မတည်ငြိမ်မှုကို အသိအမှတ်ပြုခဲ့ပြီး အလုပ်အကိုင် အပြည့်အဝရရှိရေးနဲ့ လူသားတွေရဲ့ သာယာဝပြောမှုကို ထောက်ပံ့ဖို့ သေချာစဉ်းစားထားတဲ့ စည်းမျဉ်းတွေ လိုအပ်တယ်လို့ အလေးပေးပြောခဲ့ပါတယ်။


ဒီသဘောအရ လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဟာ လက်ရှိ ဖြစ်ပေါ်နေတဲ့ အုပ်စုငယ်စု စီးပွားရေးစနစ် (ခရိုနီသဘော) ကို ငြင်းပယ်ပြီး၊ လစ်ဘရယ် ဒီမိုကရေစီနဲ့ ဈေးကွက်စနစ်တွေကို စည်းကမ်းချက်အချို့နဲ့ ထောက်ခံထားပါတယ်။ ဒါဟာ အာဏာရှင်ဆန်တဲ့ ကြွယ်ဝသူတွေရဲ့ စနစ် မဟုတ်ဘဲ ပိုင်ဆိုင်မှု-ပိုင်ဆိုင်သော ဒီမိုကရေစီကို ထောက်ခံပြီး၊ နိုင်ငံတော်ရဲ့ အတင်းအဓမ္မ ဖိနှိပ်ချုပ်ချယ်မှု ထိန်းချုပ်မှုကို သဘောတူညီချက်နဲ့ တာဝန်ယူမှုအပေါ် အခြေခံတဲ့ ဒီမိုကရေစီ အဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေနဲ့ အစားထိုးဖို့ ကြိုးပမ်းတာပါ။


အစွန်းရောက် လစ်ဘရယ်ဝါဒအဖြစ် မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ


လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ အခင်းအကျင်းမှာ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဆိုတာ စည်းစနစ်ပျက်ပြားတာကို ငြင်းပယ်တာမဟုတ်ဘဲ ဖိနှိပ်ချုပ်ချယ်မှုကို ငြင်းပယ်တာ ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ ပီးယား-ဂျိုးဇက် ပရူးဒွန် (Pierre-Joseph Proudhon)၊ ဖရက် ဖော့ဒ်ဗာရီ (Fred Foldvary) နဲ့ ပိုကျယ်ပြန့်တဲ့ အညမညသဘော နဲ့ ဂျီယို-လစ်ဘာတေးရီးယန်း အစဉ်အလာတွေကနေ ကူးစက်လာတဲ့ လစ်ဘရယ်-မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ ဟာ တရားဥပဒေနဲ့ စည်းစနစ်တွေဟာ ဆန္ဒအလျောက် ဖွဲ့စည်းထားတဲ့ အဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေကနေ ထွက်ပေါ်လာမယ့် လူအဖွဲ့အစည်းကို …

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Tolstoycu Köylülerin Kısa Tarihi
content:
Yazan: Cory Bushman


Çeviren: Gorthim


Çevirilen Asıl Metin


PDF Linki


“Özgür Hıristiyanlar” olarak da bilinen Tolstoycular, Rus edebiyat dehası Lev Tolstoy’un sadık takipçileriydi. Rus Ortodoks Kilisesi’nin yolsuzluk yaptığına dair algıları ve çarlık rejimiyle olan ilişkileri nedeniyle bu kiliseye karşı çıkmışlardı. Tolstoycular, Rus Ortodoksluğunu uygulamak yerine, Tolstoy’un “vahiy” yoluyla ortaya koyduğu “saf” bir dini izlediler. Tolstoy, organize bir din kurmadı; ancak “şu anda hüküm süren uyumsuzluk, aldatma ve şiddet”in yerine “özgür uzlaşma, hakikat ve kardeşçe sevgi”yi getirecek bir yaşam felsefesi geliştirdi.

1


Tolstoy’un hakikat ve kardeşçe sevgi felsefesi, tam anlamıyla şiddetsizlik, vejetaryenlik, komünal yaşam ve alkol, tütün ve küfürden uzak durmayı içeren bir ahlak kuralları üzerine dayanıyordu.


Tolstoycuların üye sayısı, 1917’de yaklaşık altı bin iken 1931’de binin altına düştü. 1940’larda, Bolşeviklerin şiddetli zulmünün bir sonucu olarak, sayıları neredeyse yok olma noktasına kadar azaldı. Sovyet Rusya’daki Bolşevik yönetimi sırasında Tolstoycular gibi dini mezheplerin sistematik olarak ortadan kaldırılması, iktidarı kaybetme korkusuyla sürekli yaşayan istikrarsız ve militarist bir hükümetin doğrudan bir sonucuydu.


1870’lerin ortalarında Lev Nikolayeviç Tolstoy, şiddetli bir depresyon dönemine girdi. İntihar düşünceleri giderek artan Tolstoy, zihnindeki yükü hafifletmek için Buda ve Schopenhauer gibi filozoflara yöneldi. Bu karanlık dönemde yaşamın anlamını arayışı, onu Hristiyanlığa kişisel bir dönüşüme götürdü. Daha sonra bu deneyimiyle ilgili şöyle yazdı: “Şimdi anlıyorum ki, kendimi öldürmemiş olmam, düşüncelerimin geçersizliğine dair içimde var olan belirsiz bir farkındalığın sonucuydu.”

2

 Hristiyanlığa dönüşünün kendisini ölümden kurtardığını defalarca ifade etti.


Tolstoy’un din değiştirmesi, onu daha sonra “gerçek” Hıristiyanlık olarak ilan edeceği şeyi aramaya yöneltti. Rus köylülerinin yalın inancını, peşinden gitmesi gereken bir şey olarak gördü. Tolstoy, Rus Ortodoks Kilisesi’nin dini gerçekleri çarpıtarak ve insanları felç eden batıl inançlar yaratarak köylüleri yozlaştırdığını düşünüyordu. Buna karşılık Rus Ortodoks Kilisesi, Leo Tolstoy’dan hoşnut değildi ve 24 Şubat 1901’de onu resmen aforoz etti. Kilise bu karara sadık kaldı; Tolstoy’un 1910’daki ölümünün ardından, onu bir heretik olarak nitelendirerek kilise cenazesi düzenlemeyi reddetti.


Zamanla Tolstoy’un felsefeleri yaygınlaştı ve öncelikle entelijansiya üyeleri ile Tolstoy’un yakın olduğu köylülerden oluşan küçük gruplar tarafından hayata geçirildi. Tolstoy’un dini felsefelerinin popülaritesi arttıkça, Çar tarafından eserlerine uygulanan sansür de şiddetlendi. Tolstoy’un eserlerinin çoğu, el yazısı ve hektografla çoğaltılmış kopyaların zamanında hazırlanması sayesinde dolaşımda kalabildi. 1893’te Tolstoy’un sekreteri Vladimir Chertkov, Tolstoy’un bazı yazıları korumak amacıyla İngiltere’ye gitti, ancak dönüşünde sürgüne gönderildi.


Tolstoy’un dini ve toplumsal değişim çağrısına yanıt veren bilinen ilk gruplardan biri Dukhoborlar’dı. Dukhoborlar sadece askerlik hizmetini reddetmekle kalmadılar, aynı zamanda silahlarını imha ettiler ve organize ayaklanmalar düzenlediler. En ünlü ayaklanmaları 1895 yılının Paskalya Günü’nde gerçekleşti. Ayaklanmanın gerekçesi olarak şu beş ilkeyi öne sürdüler:


“1. Çara karşı çıkma, 2. Askerlik hizmetine karşı çıkma, 3. Özel mülkiyete karşı çıkma, 4. Et yemeye karşı çıkma ve 5. Cinsel ilişkiye karşı çıkma.”

3


Paskalya Günü ayaklanmasından üç yıl sonra, Dukhoborlar Tolstoy’un maddi yardımıyla baskıcı çarlık yönetiminden kurtulup Kanada’ya göç edebildiler. Tolstoycular ise Dukhoborların aksine, yasaları tamamen reddetmeye daha meyilliydi ve eylemlerinin sonuçlarından kaçma lüksüne sahip değillerdi.


Tolstoycular, Tolstoy’un pasifizm felsefesini sadakatle takip ediyorlardı ve inançları uğruna fedakârlık yapmaya hazırdılar. Tolstoycu Vasya Kirin, ailesine askere gitmeyi reddettiğini açıkladığında, karısı “Seni öldüreceklerini biliyorsun” diye cevap verdi. O ise cesurca şöyle dedi: “Bırakın beni öldürsünler, yeter ki ben kimseyi öldürmeyeyim.”

4


Tolstoycuların vicdani retçi olarak üstlendikleri rol, yalnızca askerlik hizmetini reddetmekle kalmayıp, askeri vergileri ödemeyi ve okullarda verilen askeri eğitimi de reddetmeyi içeriyordu. Sıkı bir pasifist inanca sahip olsalar da, Tolstoycular her bireyin kendi vicdanına göre hareket etmesi gerektiğine inanıyorlardı. Tolstoycu …

author: Black Freighter
title: Anarchism and the Australian Labour Movement: Jean De Lisle's Letter from Newcastle, 25 June 1937
content:
Image: BHP at Port Waratah, Newcastle (University of Newcastle [Australia] Library)

This letter, dated 25 June 1937 and written by Jean De Lisle of Newcastle, NSW describes his involvement in Australian anarchist circles. It is unclear who the recipient was. He discusses the difficulties facing the labour movement, criticising the influence of the Santamaria Catholic faction in the Australian Labor Party and its support for Franco during the Spanish Civil War. He also describes the Communist Party's political compromises and intimidation and harassment by communist militants, whom he calls the 'Knuckle Duster Brigade'. A steelworker at BHP's Port Waratah works, De Lisle mentions his subscriptions to Italian and American publications and expresses interest in forming an anarchist group in Sydney.

The original document can be found attached, and was sourced from the Kate Sharpley Library.

168 King St Newcastle New South Wales Australia June 25 – 1937

I have received word from Fellow Worker A. Westbrook of Sydney that she received a letter from you. I am an anarchist and have been connected with a small Italian group in the North of Queensland. One of the comrades (whose name I will refrain from mentioning owing to the possibility of deportation to Fascisti Italy) is now residing near here, and the last time I called on him he gave me a copy of the paper "Spain and the World" which I gave to Fellow Worker Westbrook and she said she would write to you, and I can assure you we are very pleased to hear from you.

I only receive one Anarchist paper and that is in the Italian language which I am able to read write and speak, but I would prefer the English papers. The paper I receive is called "Il Risveglio Anarchico" printed in Geneva.

I also receive the I.W.W. Industrial Worker from Chicago U.S.A. I am a steel worker employed at the B.H.P. steel works Port Waratah, and I hope you will excuse my writing as my hand is cramped and sore.

The Labour Movement in Australia is in a very bad way, a number of the leaders openly support Franco in Spain.

This is due to the Roman Catholic Church, having gained nearly all leading positions in the Labor Party. The Communist Party will not expose them because it would break the unity of the Party; but instead plead mournfully for a People's Front. One of the Communist Party leaders died here recently and it said the Central Committee ordered them to get a parson to read the burial service which was done (a classic example of the "United Front").

The Comrades as we call here have the sight of us and me in particular and have tried to molest me on several occasions generally 5 or 6 together like a pack of wolves, but never one at a time.

We call them the Knuckle Duster Brigade; but they are losing ground and continue to go more to the right, many of their pamphlets would interest you particularly on the defence of Australia against the Japanese and I will send some the next time I go to Sydney and you no doubt would think they were issued by a capitalist class group.

We will most probably form a small group in Sydney in the near future and will be able to keep contact with you.

Anarchist Greetings Yours fraternally,

168 King St Newcastle N.S.W. Australia.

Reply Aug. 18/37 Papers + Lists

Enclosed cutting from the Communist Party Worker Weekly which has been damaged, but I think you can manage to read it - also photo of Comrade Oliver (capitalist press)

P.S. I am an Australian born Frenchman J.D.L.

I will give Fellow Worker Westbrook some money to forward for literature as soon as possible.

author: By Elvis Takahashi Mantello, Contributor
title: Inside Rouvikonas’ Push to Build a Nationwide Movement
content:
Athens, Greece — Best known for its direct actions in Greece’s capitol city, the anti-authoritarian collective

Rouvikonas

 has increasingly expanded beyond Athens. Over the past year, the collective has established a presence in Thessaloniki and Larissa, as well as in other parts of the country.


Their expansion, which includes mutual aid projects and volunteer firefighting, comes as they face new challenges including state repression. Greek Justice Minister Giorgos Floridis recently described

Rouvikonas

 as a “

criminal organization

,” arguing that its activities warranted consolidating criminal case files across the country, as had been done in the case of Golden Dawn.


Rouvikonas has rejected the characterization

, describing the government’s actions as

another

 attack by the Greek state who is attempting to quell their popular buildup. Unicorn Riot sat down with several members of the collective to learn more – see the

video

 below.


History and Expansion


Rouvikonas emerged in 2013, as Greece was still grappling with the aftermath of its financial crisis and years of austerity. Its name refers to crossing the Rubicon, the point of no return. Its signature phrase is “Not a Step Back.”


In the years following massive mobilization and civil expression, Rouvikonas maintained its political activity through direct action while building connections beyond traditional anarchist circles.


In recent years, Rouvikonas has gained greater public recognition and built a social media following of tens of thousands.


“The aim is one day to have a nationwide organization,” says Luka, a member of Rouvikonas. “We want common people, people from the working class, from the social base to join.”


This aim forces the collective to rethink how it organizes and builds relationships with emerging groups outside the capital.


Related:

Passing the Point of No Return: Interview with Rouvikonas Anarchist Collective


K-Vox: The Base


This year, K-Vox, a squat in the Exarcheia district of Athens where political history has made it synonymous with resistance, marked its

14th anniversary

 with several days of cultural events and open political discussions.


A rap performance inside K-Vox during its 14th-anniversary celebration, April 17, 2026. Photo contributed by Elvis Takahashi Mantello.


On a typical week, K-Vox operates as a bar and social space, drawing a mix of residents, activists and foreigners. Its walls echo histories of various movements beyond Greece, with murals and posters referencing the Paris Commune, Nestor Makhno’s Black Army and other revolutionary movements. Housed on the side of the building is a

free healthcare clinic

. The political character of the space is hard to miss.


But K-Vox is not a sanctuary free from external pressure. Riot police carrying shields, stun grenades, tear gas grenades and service pistols are stationed only a few hundred meters away. At the same time, metal barricades obscure what was once a

community park at Exarcheia Square

, now surrounded by construction for a new metro station.


A front view of K-Vox and the metro barricades along the streets of Exarcheia Square. Photo contributed by Elvis Takahashi Mantello.


Past coverage:

Altering Exarcheia From the Square to Strefi Hill: A Timeline and Film


And for years K-Vox has faced the threat of eviction. When the current government came to power in 2019,

cracking down on squats

 was among its

stated priorities

.


According to Periklis, a veteran member of Rouvikonas, authorities have tried to pressure or remove K-Vox over the years but have never successfully evicted the squat, even as they cleared other spaces.


Periklis argues that the government and police have struggled to confront Rouvikonas because the collective has broader support in society. Even if the government removed the space, he said, the movement behind it would remain.


The collective has responded by maintaining its everyday activities, said Periklis. This continuity is central to Rouvikonas’ relationship with the wider community. K-Vox functions not only as a space for political organizing but also as a means of sustaining the group’s social base.


From Base to Network


Rouvikonas establishes support through its social centers, providing practical assistance to people in need, from food to medical care. These activities have helped the collective build connections beyond its traditional political base.
