author: winter oak
title: Rallying the real anarchists!
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


The anarchist movement of which I became part in the 1990s was very much to my liking.


It took to the streets against the globalists and their summits, it fiercely defended nature against roadbuilding and other “development” and it was defiantly opposed to the plutocratic ruling class with all its exploitation, repression and warmongering.


Anarchists expressed themselves freely, clearly, angrily and often with a sharp sense of humour.


But, progressively, all of that changed.


Opposing globalist gatherings was deemed retrograde by many, nature was increasingly regarded as a suspect reactionary construct and the emphasis shifted to “critical whiteness” and “trans rights”.


Worst of all, the joy and humour seemed to drain completely away from the movement, being replaced by the dead-eyed and narrow-minded robotic dogmatism which I had always associated with the Marxist “left”.


I began to suspect that the anarchist scene had been deliberately infiltrated and corrupted by the ruling mafia in order to disarm it as a potential source of resistance.


This was confirmed for me six or seven years ago, initially by a general anarchist failure to call out the obvious

fakery

 of the “climate” movement and then, of course, by the appalling collaboration with the Covid manoeuvre.


I first confronted this issue in an article entitled ‘Anarchists and the Coronavirus’, published on April 3 2020, which analysed a wide range of anarchist responses to the scamdemic.


I

wrote

: “It seems that most fellow anarchists feel obliged to respect the prevalent social taboo. They insist that they are ‘not downplaying the seriousness of the COVID-19 pandemic’ and are anxious to distance themselves from the dreaded ‘conspiracy theorists'”.


I and others had already been accused of spreading “dangerous misinformation” by anarchists who nevertheless, at this stage anyway, continued to regard us as “comrades”.


By April 26 2020 the ongoing venom directed at me by so-called “anarchists” had totally confirmed what had been a somewhat tentative conclusion.


In ‘Anarchists against freedom’, I

warned

: “People are attaching the anarchist label, and a sort of shallow parody of anarchist ideology, to something which is not anarchism at all.


“This pseudo-anarchist thinking has not grown from anarchist philosophy and therefore can never be anything but a replica anarchism, a zombie anarchism which appears to be the real thing but lacks the anarchist soul.


“This fake anarchism is the sworn enemy of true anarchism. By stealing the body of anarchism, it banishes real anarchism from the world”.


Following this revelation, I dug deeper and in February 2021 published a

very detailed exposé

 showing exactly how the anarchist scene had been funded and thus manipulated by globalist “philanthropists” and their

impact investment

 industry.


I remarked: “The sterile, divisive mindset they have been spreading on behalf of their corporate paymasters should be thrown on the scrapheap of ideological history, where it belongs”.


In recent years I have often referred to my position as being

organic radicalism

, which is a broader philosophical concept than anarchism in that it includes non-anarchist thinkers.


But I also think it is important to maintain an understanding of


authentic anarchism and for that purpose I have set up a new Substack called

Real Anarchists

.


Although some of my own posts will be shared on that site, the idea is not to present my particular philosophical vision – paradoxically, real anarchism could also be regarded as broader than organic radicalism!


Instead, the goal is to restore the notion of an anarchism that can embrace a wide range of perspectives while retaining an overall fundamental coherence.


This

openness

 is central to the very character of true anarchism, which is not a set dogma but more like an

existential attitude

 and it is this

essence

 of anarchism which I seek to uphold.


I know full well that, historically, anarchism has not always reflected all my own beliefs – a blind faith in “science” and “progress” was very prevalent for a long time, for instance, and my interest in cultural rootedness is no doubt not shared by those anarchists who champion an internationalism that is hardly distinguishable from globalism.


But I would counter that anarchism is necessarily a call for decentralisation, not just down from the national-state level …

author: groundxero
title: The Twilight of Trumpism
content:
Contemporary Trumpism is not the conservative attempt to return US society back to the 1950s. It is the attempt to return US society back to the 1850s – an attempt which will fail completely, disastrously and totally.


 


By 

Dionysius


 


Between 2016 and 2026, the political system of the United States has been dominated by Trumpism, a.k.a. the US variant of billionaire fascism or plutofascism. Its domination was so complete that even when non-Trumpist politicians won elections, they did not question Trumpism’s single most compelling argument. This argument, in a nutshell, was that the United States could solve the 21st century problems of a

collapsing middle class

 and

an economy being looted by billionaire monopolists

 by a magical return to 19th century tariff walls, territorial imperialism and settler colonialism.


 


The year 2026 marks the moment when a majority of US citizens have stopped believing in 19th century magic. One of the most telling signs of this shift occurred on October 9, 2026, when Pete Hegseth, the Trumpist official in charge of the US military, announced that the US would broadcast the execution of a former US soldier on live television.


 


Hegseth had fully expected the announcement would create a wave of hurrah-patriotism. After all, the soldier in question, a former US Army major, had shot and killed 13 fellow soldiers and wounded 30 others at a military base in Fort Hood, Texas in 2009. The soldier also happened to be Muslim and the US-born son of Palestinian American immigrants, two groups which have been constantly scapegoated and persecuted by Trumpism.


 


Instead, the announcement triggered a firestorm of condemnation. Numerous former soldiers and Pentagon officials criticized the announcement as tantamount to a lynching, while human rights advocates pointed out that the only two countries which hold public executions are Taliban-ruled Afghanistan and theocrat-ruled Iran. Ten days later, overwhelming political pressure forced the Trump administration to back down and

call off the broadcast

.


 


To understand why Hegseth misread the situation so badly and why this moment is so significant, it is worth pausing for a moment to reflect on the group which forms the electoral core of Trumpism. This group consists of white males who are nostalgic for the settler colonial white masculinity which dominated US politics for almost two hundred years, i.e. between the creation of the US in 1783 and the civil rights and feminist struggles of the 1960s and early 1970s.


 


To understand why this group wants to return to the past, we must first understand that this white masculinity was responsible for 105 years of settler colonial land theft and genocide against the First Nations of North America. This period began with the 1785-1795 Northwest Indian War, and ended in the Wounded Knee Massacre in South Dakota committed by US soldiers against the Lakota people on December 29, 1890. Most of the surviving First Nations were confined to reservations thereafter, and none enjoyed full US citizenship rights until the Snyder Act of 1924.


 


This white masculinity was also crucial to perpetrating the horrors of 82 years of US chattel slavery (1783-1865) on African Americans and citizens kidnapped from Africa by slave traders. After the abolition of slavery in 1865, this white masculinity engineered systems of legal apartheid (commonly called “Jim Crow” laws) which privileged whites at the expense of African Americans. In addition to these laws, many US states had groups of white terrorists who regularly assaulted and murdered African Americans. The most notorious of these terrorists were the Klu Klux Klan, an organization so powerful that as late as August 12, 1925, an estimated 30,000 of their members marched openly through the US capital of Washington, DC without any legal repercussions whatsoever.


 


Official Jim Crow and unofficial racial terror ruled large parts of the US for 87 years (i.e. 1878-1965). They did not disappear until the 1965 Voting Rights Act granted African Americans the right to vote in all US states, and until Federal law enforcement agencies cracked down on white terrorist groups during the 1960s and 1970s.

author: winter oak
title: Calling on our ancestors!
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


After I published my articles on the Druids and ancient Celtic culture this summer, Franklin O’Kanu wrote on his

Unorthodoxy

 blog about the parallels to his own ancestral culture.


He

said

: “What’s interesting about all of this is how two cultures, across the world, Nigerian and Celtic, have the same spiritual view of the world”. [1]


And he

commented

 on one of my posts: “From the Yoruba and Igbo perspective, what the Celts experience in one continent is what the practitioners of Ifa experienced in another continent: the same honor of the Divine”. [2]


I have now discovered similar echoes from a reverse direction, as it were, through reading

Of Water and the Spirit: Ritual, Magic, and Initiation in the Life of an African Shaman

 by Malidoma Patrice Somé (1956–2021).


Somé belonged to the Dagara, a million-strong people spread across the artificially-created nation-states of Ghana, the Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso – he came from the latter, which was still called French Upper Volta when he was born.


The environment and particular customs of this African people are, of course, very different from those of the ancient Celts – roasted monkey would not have been on the menu at a Beltane feast in Ireland!


But there are similarities as well. In the essay series I

cite

 Jean Markale’s account of how at their celebratory events the Celts drank copious amounts of alcoholic drinks, producing “drunkenness, in other words the trance thanks to which one can go beyond apparent reality and see the supernatural”. [3]


He adds: “For Greek and Roman writers, Celts already had a reputation for being passionate lovers of fermented drinks. Drunkenness is an oft-occurring theme in the epics, especially in Irish accounts.


“Gods and heroes compete in their unquenchable thirst for alcohol, in the form of beer, wine or mead. A religious festival never went by without a serious drinking session”. [4]


In

his

 book, Somé writes: “Millet beer has always been a part of major rituals. Our rituals are long, and one gets thirsty”. [5]


He explains that his tribe was said to have been taught how to make beer by the Kontomboli, mysterious otherwordly beings who introduced a woman to their astonishing brew: “When she drank it, she was delighted. She felt merry and wanted to sing”. [6]


I was also intrigued to learn that the Dagara use a twenty-based counting system, so that eighty-three would be expressed as “four times twenty plus three”. [7]


In France the same number is

quatre-vingt-trois

, “four twenties and three”, after the old Celtic system, and we used to have the same concept in English with a score, meaning twenty, using which eight-three is “four score and three”.


A more important connection between ancient European and African societies has been the effects of colonisation.


From an African perspective it must be strange to hear a white man claim to be the victim of colonialism, but such is the case.


Following the destruction of our indigenous culture by the Roman empire and its religious wing, we were then

colonised

 by the empire of usury and commerce and used as fodder for its insatiable industrial Leviathan. [8]


With our true identities further smothered, our vital energy was hijacked to allow that same empire to enslave and exploit other peoples across the world, including the Dagara.


Somé writes: “My own elders had experienced French colonialism and the culture of the West as a force that used violence as a means to eradicate traditional lifeways.


“They had seen their own youth stolen from them as they vainly struggled against the incursions of these intruders.


“During these years, in which my people were trying to make sense of a people whose every action seemed to go against the natural order of things, creating chaos, death, and destruction, the sense of unified community that sustained their tribal life was profoundly destabilized. These foreigners seemed to have no respect for life, tradition, or the land itself…


“In spite of the best efforts of all my people, the whites kept on coming; kept on doing whatever they pleased; and kept on taking more and more of our land, our beliefs and our lives”. [9]


“It is a sad thing to realize how much my people have lost and how much yet of our reality is to be buried in the pit of oblivion”. [10]

author: Kalundi Serumaga
title: The Rise and Fall of Uganda’s Human Rights “Revolution” (1986-2026)
content:
It would not surprise me to see the emergence of a woman-led, woman-centred, or women-only political party in Uganda over the next few years, if not before the next election.


It would surprise me even less if such a party were to then fizzle out, after a brief moment of intense popularity, during which time a whole lot of new neoliberal schemes would be sold to the population as “liberation”.


Neoliberalism is basically the stage of capitalism where it seeks to return completely to its founding work methods. New governments are installed and encouraged to sweep aside all public policy aimed at shielding the vulnerable from the worst effects of those methods, and to instead facilitate a more thorough exploitation of labour and natural resources. Everything becomes a commodity.


Such a political project would simply be a more concentrated distillation of the plastic human rights revolution Uganda has undergone between 1986 and today. Because the performance of a human rights gospel was the thing that enabled the then-incoming National Resistance Movement (NRM) regime to sell and endear itself to a significant section of the Ugandan public after it seized power in 1986.


It would also be an attempt by the elite leadership of the women’s movement to hang onto the place of security and advantage they acquired through their historical strategic alliance with the NRM after it took power.


The plastic revolution grew out of the centring of human rights violations in the years of the political campaigns against the Amin regime, and the truly horrific further such violations meted out on civilians by the second Obote regime during the 1981–1986 civil war. 


Such a focus on human rights violations suited the NRA/M well as it worked to divert political discourse away from the deeper and more critical questions of imperialist domination – and also infantilism politics – by centring on a very emotive issue.


Equally practically, the cohort of feminists did sterling service in helping the NRM regime consolidate itself between 1986 and 1996. Their “gains” were to have the career concerns of elite women hard-wired into national policy at the constitutional level.


It would be the last card played by the imperialists’ hand, and our arrival at the very heart of what has been the success in managing the social damage caused by the neoliberal economic project in Uganda: the Uganda women’s movement.


The revolution was plastic because it relied heavily on external funding; it absorbed external ideas quite uncritically; it was rooted in the understanding and aspirations of the Ugandan middle class; and it was self-contradictory in many aspects, the key contradiction being the idea that there would be prosperity under neoliberalism.


These realizations unfold from the recent drama in which elements of the security forces hunted down, abducted, and detained the celebrated veteran Ugandan feminist Miria Matembe.


This was no small matter. Matembe had been an activist since the days before the current government took power. She had been a parliamentarian for a long time and had even served as a minister in the government whose agents were now inconveniencing her.


Initially denied bail when she was finally brought before the courts, Matembe spent a night in remand prison before being released on bail the following day, leading to a spontaneous, energetic celebration by a gathering of Ugandan women activists singing their English-language “anthem”, while the main character in this drama walked triumphantly from court declaring, “Jesus is king.”


This journey to such a disparate mix of wrong destinations – from illegal detention to an unquestioning court, and thereafter to an eventual release attributed to the god well used by colonialism, all the while as the English-singing cohort of feminists misattribute the initial injustice to the oppression of women, despite there being many more male Ugandans still detained and disappeared – requires a map for sure.


Destination: opportunism


The immediate starting point was the government’s announcement of the intention to create a new law regulating the way in which funds from abroad could be received and spent. This was called the “Sovereignty Bill”. As the arguments behind it rested heavily on the ruling party’s now extremely threadbare “anti-imperialist” credentials, it was said to be about “preserving Uganda’s independence”.

author: Monthly Review Press
title: LIVE Oct 30, in DC! See Aymeric Monville, Jennifer Ponce de León and Gabriel Rockhill, speaking on “Requiem for French Theory”
content:
NYC, on October 29th, at CUNY (25 Broadway) * DC, on October 30th at Busboys and Poets (235 Carol St NW) * (And a couple of days ago in Philly’s Free Library)


APPEARANCES


Coming from Left Field

 (Episode 152)


In this episode of Coming From Left Field, philosopher and cultural critic Gabriel Rockhill joins

Greg Godels & Pat Cummings

 to explore the Ford Foundation, the 1966 Johns Hopkins conference often cited as a launching point for French Theory in the United States, Cold War cultural politics, and the wider political economy of academic knowledge production. Rockhill argues for rebuilding a class-centered, internationalist Marxism and joins a thoughtful exchange on China, Vietnam, socialism, imperialism, inequality, and the challenges of assessing existing socialist projects without demonization or uncritical celebration….


Marx Memorial Library

in London hosted a dual book launch for

Requiem for French Theory

 and

Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism?

with Gabriel Rockhill, Aymeric Monville, and Jennifer Ponce de León, who engaged in a discussion regarding the effects of imperialism on the production and dissemination of knowledge.

Watch here

or below


Far from simply engaging in a critique of the faux radicalism of the prominent discourses within the imperial theory industry, the discussion was grounded in a reasoned defense of the vibrant international tradition of anti-imperialist Marxism. Topics included the imperial promotion of Western Marxism and postmodern French Theory, the international war of ideas, the failed efforts to discredit anti-imperialist Marxism, culturalism and identity politics vs. a materialist analysis of the colonial question, fascism past and present, the dialectics of actually existing socialism, and the current state of global class struggle in theory and practice.


REVIEWS


Marxism-Leninism Today,

 by

Greg Godels

:


“During the 1960s and 1970s, it was an oft-repeated quip that the European left was long on theory and short on practice, while the North American left was strong on action, but allergic to theory. In West Germany, Italy, and France, young leftists would often passionately debate theoretical questions deep into the night, while seldom coming to a common commitment to action the next day. Their youthful U.S. counterparts—revived after the retreat from High McCarthyism–counted on spontaneous action and a firm commitment to common, inherited political values rather than the ideas buried in deep theoretical tracts. But those observations were far from completely true. The often student-driven U.S. New Left developed a thirst for a broader, deeper explanation of the injustices that they were rejecting. Many of those committed to action turned to left classics–quite often a reconsidered Marx–and others favored a wave of West European radical-oriented thinkers….”

Read more…

“During the 1960s and 1970s, it was an oft-repeated quip that the European left was long on theory and short on practice, while the North American left was strong on action, but allergic to theory. title: Eine Welt zu Gewinnen! – Interview zur Konferenz und dem Anspruch des Internationalismus im 21. Jahrhundert
content:
„

In Zeiten der Zuspitzung der globalen Systemkrise und im Angesicht ihrer direkten Auswirkungen auf uns hierzulande wollen wir eine neue Debatte über internationalistische Praxis und Ausrichtung hier in Deutschland anstoßen. Wir stellen uns die Frage, wie sich unser Anspruch in einer an den konkreten Verhältnissen orientierten Praxis verwirklichen kann.“ – S

o wirbt die Tagung „Eine Welt zu Gewinnen“, die anlässlich des 109. Jahrestages der Oktoberrevolution am kommenden Wochenende in Berlin stattfinden wird.


Wir sprechen mit Ayşe vom Bund der Kommunist:innen

1

 in Berlin und Lena von YUNA – Demokratische Jugend

2

, welche die Konferenz zusammen mit der Akademie der demokratischen Moderne ausrichten.


In Berlin findet ja kommendes Wochenende die Konferenz „Eine Welt zu Gewinnen“ statt. Könnt ihr uns einen Einblick geben, was denn da so geplant ist?


Lena:

 Die Konferenz wird einen ganzen Tag lang gehen und ist in drei Blöcke aufgeteilt: Zu Beginn haben wir Brigitte Studer eingeladen, die ihre Recherchen zur KomIntern vorstellen wird. Dabei werden wir natürlich Publikumsfragen stellen können, um zusammen herauszufinden, welche Lehren wir aus der Vergangenheit ziehen können. Im zweiten Panel teilt dann Torkil Lauesen seine Analyse des globalen Kapitalismus und seine Perspektiven mit uns. Was vor allem im Hinblick auf eine spezifische Praxis in den Zentren des Imperialismus sehr spannend wird.


Ay

ş

e

:

 Das Podium im Anschluss ist ein Ausdruck von dem, was wir mit der gesamten Konferenz versuchen: Wir schauen uns nicht nur die Geschichte der imperialistischen Epoche des Kapitalismus an, sondern auch, was die Bedeutung des Internationalismus in den imperialistischen Krisen war. Wie war unsere internationalistische Praxis in Deutschland in den letzten Jahrzehnten und wie muss eine zukünftige internationalistische Arbeit aussehen? Wir sehen die imperialistische Weltlage einerseits und haben viele internationalistische Erfahrungen. Wenn wir uns zum Beispiel Kurdistan anschauen, vollzieht sich ja ein Umbruch. Deshalb muss die konkrete Analyse, zu der wir gemeinsam an dem Tag kommen, auch dazu führen, dass die Art und Weise, wie unsere Praxis aussieht, sich sozusagen daran anpasst. Und das werden wir eben auf dem Podium gemeinsam, auch aus unseren verschiedenen Erfahrungen und Perspektiven, zusammenbringen.


Worin seht ihr die Herausforderung eines proletarischen bzw. sozialistischen Internationalismus in der heutigen Zeit?


Lena:

 Was wir vielleicht erstmal grundsätzlich zum Verständnis von Internationalismus sagen müssen: Aufgrund des global organisierten Kapitalismus brauchen wir auch eine internationale Strategie. Probleme dabei gibt es viele. Die subjektive Situation, also die Situation von uns organisierten Kräften, müssen wir dabei hervorheben: Auch wenn wir sehen, dass es einen Aufschwung bei den sozialistischen Kräften gibt, sind wir nicht so breit aufgestellt und stabil verankert. Es braucht eine gut organisierte gesellschaftliche Bewegung, um mit einer Relevanz tatsächlich in internationale Beziehungen zu gehen. Ein weiteres Problem ist die Trennung, die wir sowohl als Jugendliche, Frauen, als auch ArbeiterInnen anhand von nationalen Grenzen als auch anderen Machtgrenzen erfahren.


Ay

ş

e:

 Ja, viele Sachen, die Lena genannt hat, würde ich genauso teilen. Ich würde noch hinzufügen, dass, wenn man sich spezifisch die Arbeiterklasse anschaut, das Problem eben die extreme Heterogenität dieser ist. Nicht nur innerhalb der globalen Waren- und Produktionskette, sondern selbst hier in den Betrieben in Deutschland sehen wir: Okay, es gibt eigentlich verschiedene Stellungen in jedem Betrieb, es gibt Festangestellte, Subunternehmer, ganz prekär arbeitende Leute, die ja nicht mal in einem Betrieb ein gemeinsames Interesse formulieren können. Wenn man sich das über nationale Grenzen hinweg anschaut, ist es noch schlimmer.


In Deutschland haben wir das Problem, dass wir es tatsächlich großflächig mit einer Arbeiteraristokratie zu tun hatten. Gerade da, wo eigentlich ganz viel Macht bei der Arbeit liegt: Die Leute, die bei BMW und Mercedes und Volkswagen an den teuren Anlagen sitzen, wo ganz viel Mehrwert in wenigen Sekunden produziert wird, das sind natürlich auch die Leute, die am meisten befriedet sind, weil es einen super Kündigungsschutz gibt, die ein ganz gutes Gehalt bekommen und so weiter und so fort.


Das hat historisch in Deutschland dazu geführt, dass es die Notwendigkeit nach einem Kampf …

title: La derrota de Bolsonaro es un golpe a los Trump y los Milei
content:
El candidato presidencial brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro, del Partido Liberal (PL), reacciona mientras habla tras perder la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales, en Brasilia, Brasil. 25 de octubre de 2026. Foto: REUTERS/Adriano Machado


La derrota de Bolsonaro es un golpe político a los Trump, Milei y toda la fracción del imperialismo que había apostado por el mentor de los “milicianos” (parapoliciales) brasileños. Flávio Bolsonaro ha anunciado que impugnará la segunda ronda. Le sirve para la tribuna: la mayor parte de la burguesía mundial ha cerrado filas con la victoria de Lula. El ecológico Lula ya ha anunciado la intención de instalar a Petrobrás en la Amazonía, con la vista puesta en la exportación de carburantes a China. Las empresas chinas de vehículos eléctricos se han asociado a europeas y norteamericanas, para distribuirse el mercado brasileño y las cadenas de exportación. Con el telón de fondo de esta crisis por arriba, la campaña del balotaje fue el escenario de movilizaciones imponentes, que por una simplificación de una situación compleja han sido consideradas de apoyo a la candidatura de Lula. No hay trabajador de a pie en Brasil, sin embargo, que no tenga críticas severas a Lula y a la burocracia política, sindical y educacional del lulismo. La segunda vuelta ha consagrado presidente a Lula, pero la primera vuelta le dio a la derecha el control de parlamentos, gobernaciones y municipios. Es una herencia del PT y de su sucursal política, el Psol, que reúne a la izquierda antisocialista. La victoria de Lula no abre una perspectiva para los trabajadores.

Por Marcelo Ramal y Jorge Altamira (Política Obrera).


Lula ha dado vuelta la elección del primer turno electoral y consiguió una victoria inapelable -más de tres puntos de diferencia- sobre Flávio Bolsonaro. El candidato del Frente Brasil Popular, una coalición con partidos de la gran patronal brasileña, obtuvo nada menos que 10 millones de votos más que hace tres semanas, ocasión en la que había perdido unos 3 millones de votos en relación al balotaje de octubre de 2022. La magnitud de la transferencia de votos de ayer es atribuida a la participación del electorado que no lo había hecho el 4 de octubre pasado y a la mayoría de los que habían votado por los candidatos que no llegaron al segundo turno, pertenecientes a la derecha. La manifestación de apoyo a Lula, en la avenida Paulista de la capital del Estado, habría reunido 1.300.000 asistentes, la mayor, según los entendidos, de la historia de Brasil.


La derrota de Bolsonaro es un golpe político a los Trump, Milei y toda la fracción del imperialismo que había apostado por el mentor de los “milicianos” (parapoliciales) brasileños. En alusión al cuarto mandato de Lula, Trump señaló que “los comunistas se perpetúan en el poder”, a sabiendas de que tiene un gran margen de entendimiento con el ganador. La frase no lo predispone bien frente a Xi Jinping, a quien quiere asociar a su ‘plan de paz’ para Ucrania. Dentro de diez días, Trump perderá distritos que los republicanos han conservado como propios durante los últimos cien años.


La media vuelta de los resultados electorales está asociada a un distanciamiento de la derecha brasileña con respecto a la candidatura de Bolsonaro, que tuvo su expresión en el acogimiento que Diputados y Senado, controlados por ella, dieron a diversos proyectos de ley de Lula para ser votados de inmediato, en el transcurso de la campaña del balotaje. Bolsonaro, en cambio, fue denunciado en la prensa por lo que en Brasil se conoce como “ja ganhou”, en referencia al inmovilismo de quien asegura que no habría una modificación de los resultados previos. Flávio Bolsonaro, cuyo partido pasará a controlar el Senado a partir del 1 de enero próximo, anunció que iniciaría un juicio político y destitución del establishment judicial de Brasil, algo divisorio en la derecha y considerado peligroso para la llamada institucionalidad. Esta amenaza convirtió a Lula en el único defensor del “orden” en Brasil. Flávio Bolsonaro se vio obligado a votar el proyecto de Lula que reduce la semana laboral de 6 a 5 jornadas y a apoyar, en el debate presidencial, las medidas asistenciales de Lula -Bolsa Familia, Sistema de Salud-, las cuales, bajo el propio gobierno del Frente Brasil Popular, se encontraban en la ruina.

title: 25 organizations in Europe seek to strengthen joint struggle and solidarity
content:
25 political and civil society organizations from Turkey and Kurdistan have agreed to establish a joint alliance for struggle and solidarity in Europe. The initiative aims to bring together different political currents and strengthen resistance against the rise of right-wing and fascist forces, imperialist war policies, and state repression. At the same time, the participating organizations intend to support the peace and democratic society process in Turkey and advocate for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.


The agreement stems from a meeting held on October 17 at the Cologne headquarters of the Federation of Alevi Communities in Europe (AABK). Representatives from various political traditions and social movements gathered at the invitation of eight organizations. In a joint final declaration issued today, the participants reaffirm their determination to preserve their organizational independence while establishing a lasting foundation for joint political action.


Against militarism, fascism and imperialist war policies


In their declaration, the organizations describe a world marked by growing international tensions. They warn that wars and conflicts driven by imperialist centers of power are increasing the risk of a broader military confrontation, potentially escalating into a new global war over the redistribution of power and resources. While ever-greater resources are being devoted to armament and warfare, they say, poverty and social inequality are deepening. The consequences, they argue, are borne primarily by working and oppressed sections of society, women, and the natural environment.


The signatories view the growing strength of right-wing and fascist movements as part of this development. They argue that militarism, racism, sexism, hostility toward refugees and migrants, and the destruction of the natural foundations of life are interconnected. At the same time, social forces opposing these developments are increasingly being criminalized.


The organizations therefore call for stronger international coordination among movements of struggle. They remark that resistance movements from India to France and the United States, as well as Yemen and Rojava, must not remain isolated from one another. “Their experiences must be brought together and transformed into a shared framework of internationalist solidarity. Peace, democracy, and social justice cannot be expected from the very power structures responsible for war, exploitation, and oppression. Instead, the key lies in strengthening ties between working and oppressed populations across national borders.”


Joint resistance against AKP-MHP policies


Another key focus of the declaration is the political situation in Turkey. According to the organizations, the AKP-MHP government is exploiting the international shift to the right to consolidate its authoritarian system of rule on a permanent basis. They point out that repression against the political opposition, arrests, bans, and restrictions on democratic rights are aimed at suppressing social resistance and weakening organized opposition forces.


According to the organizations, those particularly affected include workers, trade unions, democratic organizations, intellectuals, artists, and opposition political groups. At the same time, the collective rights of the Kurdish and Alevi populations continue to be disregarded. Women face patriarchal violence and discrimination, while the protection of children and the right to life of animals, as well as the preservation of nature, are systematically neglected.


The organizations do not regard these policies as an isolated development in Turkey. Rather, they see them as part of a broader authoritarian offensive through which capitalist centers of power and reactionary governments are responding to social crises. This, they argue, makes it necessary to connect democratic and social struggles in Turkey with those in Europe and other regions of the world.


Democratic solution to the Kurdish question as a shared responsibility


The participating organizations explicitly address the peace and democratic society process, stating: “Although Abdullah Öcalan and the PKK have paved the way for political and democratic dialogue through their decisions to end the armed struggle, the AKP-MHP government and the Turkish state continue to refuse to take the necessary steps toward genuine progress.”

POSICIÓN DEL COLECTIVX ANARQUISTA NOS EN LAS ELECCIONES GENERALES EN BRASIL EN 2026


A todxs


Este domingo, 25 de octubre de 2026, habrá segunda vuelta de las elecciones de la “democracia” burguesa en el espacio ocupado por la república Federativa de Brasil. Habrá elecciones para gobernador en algunos estados de la federación y para el cargo de presidente de la república. Los candidatos son: el actual presidente Lula da Silva en un intento de reelección; y Flavio Bolsonaro, senador e hijo del psicópata Jair Bolsonaro que gobernó Brasil entre 2019 y 2022.


Por un lado, Lula da Silva, representante de la izquierda institucional y del campo “progresista”. Notorio conciliador de clases y celoso gestor del capital en Brasil, Lula da Silva, su partido PT y su central sindical CUT representan la “democracia” de los ricos, con una política socialdemócrata disfrazada de socialismo donde las élites (financiera, industrial, terratenientes) siguen siendo élites y el pueblo permanece en una posición subalterna, con algunas migajas siendo distribuidas a los más pobres (subsidios en dinero, pequeños aumentos por encima de la inflación para jubilaciones y asalariados de bajos ingresos, ascenso social limitado para hijos de pobres a través del ingreso en universidades, etc.), y convivencia conciliadora más o menos pacífica con los dos bloques que se están formando en el mundo y que caminan hacia la Tercera Guerra Mundial: los Atlantistas (EE. UU., Unión Europea, “israel”) y el Mundo Multipolar (China, Rusia, Irán).


Por otro lado, Flavio Bolsonaro, representante de la extrema derecha y títere del imperialismo yanqui-sionista. Tan celoso como Lula da Silva en la gestión del capital, Flavio se diferencia de él por ser la figura clave en el proyecto del dictador yanqui Donald Trump de imponer gobiernos de extrema derecha en toda Sudamérica. Flavio mantiene una alianza con el dictador argentino Javier Milei y con el carnicero Benjamín Netanyahu, y ya ha advertido que aplicará la misma política económica que Milei en Brasil, que formará una alianza político-económica-militar con el Estado terrorista de “israel”, e incluso invitará a Marco Rubio, Secretario de Estado de Trump, A formar parte de su equipo de gobierno. Una de las principales bases de apoyo de Flavio son las iglesias evangélicas neopentecostales sionistas vinculadas a Estados Unidos y “Israel”.


Flavio es amigo íntimo del banquero Daniel Vorcaro, autor del mayor fraude financiero de la historia de Brasil, quien robó aproximadamente R$ 57.000.000.000,00 (US$ 11.000.000.000,00/EUR 10.000.000.000,00) de fondos de pensiones pertenecientes a empleados de empresas estatales, seguridad social y inversionistas privados. Flavio Bolsonaro recibió R$ 134.000.000,00 (US$ 26.000.000,00/EUR 23.000.000,00) de Vorcaro, supuestamente para la producción de la película Dark Horse, una biografía ficticia del psicópata Jair Bolsonaro. La mayor parte del dinero robado del pueblo fue desviado para el disfrute personal de la familia Bolsonaro.


Flavio tiene vínculos en el submundo del crimen con la cúpula de la organización mafiosa Comando Vermelho y con narcomilicias de extrema derecha.


Flavio actuó, sin cobrar honorarios, como abogado de Bruno Dias Delaroli, cabo de la despreciable PMERJ — Policía Militar del Estado de Río de Janeiro, quien en 2021 mató a la niña Ana Clara Gomes Machado, de 5 años, disparándole dos veces en la cabeza con un fusil de calibre 7,62x51mm NATO, sin motivo aparente alguno. Flavio y su asesora económica, Daniella Marques, han declarado que las políticas criminales de Milei constituyen un “excelente ejemplo”; planean reemplazar a los funcionarios públicos por inteligencia artificial, modificar la Constitución de Brasil sin contar con una asamblea constituyente elegida para tal fin y cancelar las elecciones burguesas de 2030, con el objetivo de que Flavio ejerza un mandato ilegal y dictatorial de ocho años para, supuestamente, “poner a Brasil en su lugar”.


En definitiva, Flavio Bolsonaro es una figura similar a un Ramfis Trujillo o un “Tachito” Somoza: un *playboy* y vividor, hijo de un dictador, elevado a la categoría de político; alguien incluso peor, más perverso y maligno que su propio padre, que pretende transformar Brasil en una dictadura narco-fascista, evangélica, sionista y personalista al servicio de la familia Bolsonaro.

author: Danica Rachel
title: Operation Paperclip: The Nazis behind the US space program
content:
The Apollo moon landings are some of the most impressive technical feats ever achieved, and, for capitalism’s boosters, definitive evidence of the superiority of Western capitalism over all other social systems. The United States beating the Soviet Union to the finish line in the space race is held up as the ultimate triumph of capitalism over communism. But the path that took humans to the heavens began in the depths of hell: the Mittelbau-Dora concentration camp in Nazi Germany.

Built near the town of Nordhausen in central Germany, Mittelbau-Dora provided its prisoners as slaves to the Mittelwerk. This was a factory built under a mountain for the mass production of the V2 rocket, the world’s first long-range guided ballistic missile. The several thousand civilians killed in London and Antwerp by V2s were not the only victims of these Nazi weapons: at least 20,000 prisoners died as a result of the conditions in Mittelbau-Dora and the Mittelwerk.

Edwin Katzenellenbogen, who was convicted for crimes committed as a doctor at the Buchenwald camp, described Dora as “the Hell of all the concentration camps”. Tens of thousands of prisoners worked in interchanging 12-hour shifts, first to dig the kilometres-long tunnels of the Mittelwerk, then on the dark production lines within.

Sanitation was absent, disease and starvation were rampant, and collective punishment was common. Prisoners were hanged in groups of up to a dozen at a time, and on at least one occasion, bodies were left to dangle over the areas where others were forced to continue working.

Wernher von Braun was an SS officer, scientific director of the V-weapons project, and head of the Mittelbau-Dora planning office. He came from an aristocratic family in the German empire, and was among the first pioneers of advanced rocket science. Through the interwar years, Germany was banned from investing in many kinds of weaponry under the Treaty of Versailles, but rockets were obscure enough to avoid being on the list. During this time, von Braun became a leading designer and inventor of the engines needed to propel explosive missiles over incredible distances.

He joined the Nazi Party in 1937. If you believe his version of events, he joined only to be allowed to continue his scientific work. Regardless of his political loyalty, he was at least comfortable enough with the genocidal policies of the Third Reich to enjoy the slave labour it provided to him from Mittelbau-Dora. He was certainly aware of the reality of the Mittelwerk, having visited the tunnels himself at least ten times.

As the walls closed in on the Third Reich, with US and British forces moving in from the west and Russians from the east, von Braun hid the most important of the design documents for constructing V2s. Alongside Major General Walter Dornberger, head of the German army’s weapons department, von Braun used the hidden documents as leverage to get an amnesty with the Americans, betting that the US wanted the weapons more than they cared about prosecuting war criminals.

He was right. Von Braun, Dornberger and many other German experts in weapons of many terrifying forms—ballistic, chemical, and biological—were brought across the Atlantic under a secret program known as Operation Paperclip. They began work in the US, making weapons for a new, but no less bloodthirsty, empire. Their pasts were whitewashed, with the story being that they were innocent scientists forced by circumstance into working for the Nazi regime.

For his part, Joseph Stalin got the Mittelwerk factory itself, which continued operation for a few years before its machinery was brought back to Russia, along with thousands of German technicians needed to operate it. The USSR also got the equipment and methods to manufacture sarin gas, a chemical weapon so potent that contact with a single droplet causes a painful death.

Sarin was invented by Nazi chemists, among them Otto Ambros, who tested it on Auschwitz prisoners. Ambros was convicted for crimes against humanity in the Nuremberg trials, but that wasn’t a barrier to later working for US chemical companies and the US army. Within a few years of the end of the war, both imperial superpowers were producing large quantities of sarin and other chemical weapons.

The Cold War and the arms race 

The new phase of world imperialism had the globe divided into the West, with the US on top, against the East orbiting the USSR. The prospect of direct hot war between the empires gave …

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: Int’l solidarity vs Pax Silica
content:
At the Shut the Pax Down: Resistance and Solidarity Against Imperialist Plunder workshop in Bangkok, Thailand on October 14, 2026. (Photo from ILPS Philippines Facebook page)

Despite the advancements of AI technology, there is also the growing resistance.

BANGKOK – Organizations from different parts of the world are now united against the Pax Silica Initiative to be signed by the United States and the Philippines in November. US President Donald Trump reportedly will visit the Philippines to sign the agreement.

“We are in a period of extreme conflict between two very powerful and imperialist countries and the US is trembling and shaking. We have to maintain that fervor of revolution, that ability to throw stones at them, to bring them down and to make sure that the US imperialist power is no more,” said Azra Sayeed, secretary-general of the International League of Peoples Struggles (ILPS) during an activity in Bangkok, Thailand dubbed “Shut the Pax Down: Resistance and Solidarity Against Imperialist Plunder” on October 14.

The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank (IMF-WB) held its annual meeting in Bangkok from October 12 to 18. Participants included central bank governors, economic policy makers and business leaders.

In a statement, the Campaigners of the Peoples Global Campaign (PGC) Against IMF and World expressed concern over IMF-WB’s push for new technologies, including the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in Global South economies.

The group said that the “frantic race” for AI dominance intensified mining and extraction in resource-rich countries in the Global South. Transnational corporations are extracting rare earth elements (REEs) and other critical minerals to meet the growing demand for AI infrastructure. To secure control over the AI supply chain, countries like the US initiated the formation of Pax Silica and other similar formations.

“We know that imperialism is about world domination and control over resources. In the previous century, the rivalry among imperialist powers centered on oil because whoever controlled oil could wield significant influence over the military and the economy,” Arnold Padilla, secretary-general of ILPS-Philippines said during the event.

Now, he stressed, the battle is over critical minerals as whoever controls AI and the critical minerals needed to build its infrastructure could gain a significant advantage in dominating the world. “Essentially, that’s the battle now between the US and China. So, who will control this critical sector?”

This is why, Padilla said, the Philippines is up for a major battle to halt the signing of the US-led Pax Silica Initiative this year in time for the Asean Summit from November 16 to 18.

He said that AI is not just about the software that people use but also about weapons like drones “that can make decisions in actual battles without any human intervention.” He added that these sophisticated weapons will be made of minerals to be extracted from the Philippines.

Read: Critical minerals policy framework linked to Pax Silica? Read: War and plunder: US imperialism in the Philippines

“Pax Silica is made up of 24 countries, of course, led by the US. And it’s a special coalition. Specifically chosen by the US because countries that belong to Pax Silica perform a specific specialized role because it’s about controlling the supply chain,” Padilla said. “We don’t have high technology, we don’t have the logistic network, we don’t have capital or energy. But what do we have? We have the critical minerals. So for us in the Philippines, this is all about plunder.”

Donna Denina, secretary-general of International Women’s Alliance (IWA), said that US Undersecretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg, former tech executive and adviser tied to the controversial software firm Palantir, designed Pax Silica to give the US control over the global technology supply chain.

Palantir is a technology firm with clients from the Pentagon and foreign militaries including the Israeli government. But Denina said that Palantir is now expanding its influence beyond military tech into the health care sector.

In the US, she said that Palantir’s AI software is being used to manage hospital staffing and scheduling. This raised concerns among healthcare workers and prompted protests.

She said that more than 1,000 nurses from the National Nurses United union protested against healthcare institutions’ contracts with Palantir …

title: Jugendstreik Basel
content:
Aufruf zum Jugendstreik am 20.11. in Basel


Als Jugendorganisationen aus ganz Europa, und darüber hinaus, rufen wir Unter dem Motto «FIGHT FOR OUR FUTURE, NOT THEIR WARS» zum Internationalen Jugendstreik auf.


Auch in Basel gehen wir am 20. November auf die Strasse.


Demo: 14:00 De-Wette Park


Fest: ab 17:00 (Genauere Infos werden über die Instagramkanäle bekanntgegeben)


Wieso streiken wir?


Unsere Staaten rüsten auf. Die Jugend wird darauf vorbereitet, in den Krieg zu ziehen. Während die Regierungen Milliarden in Aufrüstung investieren, wird der Sozialstaat kaputt gesparrt.


Auch die Schweiz macht mit. So plant der Bund zum Beispiel einen Rüstungsfonds in der Grösse von 24 Milliarden Franken. Das Budget für die Armee für den Zeitraum 2025–2028 wurde bereits um 4 Milliarden Franken erhöht. Gleichzeitig wird mit dem Entlastungspaket 27 in über 60 Bereichen gespart, unter anderem bei der Bildung, der Gesundheit und beim Klimaschutz.


Es zeigt die Priorität dieses Systems: Die fortlaufende Erweiterung des Kapitals.


Der Kapitalismus kann der Jugend keine Zukunft garantieren!


Die Armee dient der Interessen der herrschenden Klasse. Die neuen militärischen Kapazitäten erweitern dabei den Handlungsspielraum zur Durchsetzung dieser Interessen.


Beispiele dafür sind der Einsatz des Militärs an der Demonstration gegen den G7 Gipfel, die laufende Grenzmilitarisierung oder die Waffenexporte nach Israel.


Wir sterben nicht für ihre Kriege!


Wir schauen solidarisch nach Deutschland und Frankreich wo sich bereits hunderttausende Jugendliche gegen die Militarisierung und Kürzungen wehren.


Für uns ist klar: Unsere Antwort auf die Militarisierungsspirale muss international sein.


Wir sterben nicht für ihre Kriege – Wir streiken!


Basel:


Demo 14:00 De-Wette Fest ab 17:00 (Infos werden auf Instagramkanälen publiziert)


Streiken ist ein Grundrecht. Wenn du aber aufgrund von allfälligen Repressionen deines Betriebes, der Schule oder Polizei verhindert bist, ist es auch möglich, deine Solidarität in Form eines Banners zu zeigen.

title: Heilige Drecksarbeit – Die deutsch-israelischen Militärbeziehungen und die Staatsräson
content:
Der vorliegende Text ist eine gekürzte Fassung des gleichnamigen Beitrags aus dem Sammelband „

Trümmer auf Trümmer. Zur Kritik der deutschen Staatsräson

“, erschienen bei der Buchmacherei. Das Autor:innenkollektiv beschäftigt sich hier ausführlich mit der historischen Genese der militärischen Beziehungen zwischen der Bundesrepublik und dem zionistischen Staatsprojekt sowie der Geschichte des Existenzrechts Israels als deutsche Staatsräson. Neben diesem Beitrag finden sich im Sammelband zahlreiche weitere Texte, die sich aus historischer, juristischer und politischer Perspektive mit dem Thema der „Staatsräson“, deren Bedeutung für einen neuen deutschen Nationalismus, dem Phänomen der „Antideutschen“, kolonialen und antikommunistischen Kontinuitäten und der aktuellen Bedeutung im Bezug auf den Genozid in Gaza auseinander setzen.

von

AK Beau Séjour


Wirft man einen vergleichenden Blick auf die Zahlen der deutschen Waffengeschäfte im Jahr 2024, so fällt auf, dass Israel mit 161 Mio. Euro nur an sechster Stelle steht. An erster Stelle stand im Jahr 2024 die Ukraine mit 8,1 Milliarden Euro, gefolgt von Singapur (1,21 Mrd. Euro), Algerien (558,7 Mio. Euro), den USA (319,9 Mio. Euro) und der Türkei (230,8 Mio. Euro). Es gehe, so wird immer wieder zu Recht angemerkt, den Herren Rheinmetall und Thyssenkrupp nicht um die konkrete Tötung palästinensischer Kinder, sondern um das allgemeine Geschäft mit dem Tod. Die militärischen Beziehungen zwischen Deutschland und Israel müssen, das ist fraglos richtig, auch als gewöhnliche deutsche Handelsbeziehungen zwischen handelsüblichen Schurkenstaaten betrachtet werden. Doch dieses profane globale Geschäft mit dem Tod braucht, insbesondere in Deutschland, einen robusteren Überbau als das Geschäft mit Autos oder Kosmetikartikeln. Laut Marx spricht die »scheinheilige und heuchlerische Ideologie der Bourgeoisie ihre aparten Interessen als allgemeine Interessen« aus.

1

 Und in Bezug auf Wirklichkeit und Ideologie der bürgerlichen Familie schreibt er weiter, dass »[i]hrer schmutzigen Existenz […] der heilige Begriff in offiziellen Redensarten und in der allgemeinen Heuchelei« entspricht.

2

 Die schmutzige wirkliche Existenz deutscher Außen- und Handelspolitik muss in vergleichbarer Weise sakralisiert und den Deutschen als ihr allgemeines und moralisches Interesse verkauft werden, insbesondere deshalb, da sich nach 1945 jedes deutsche Großmachtstreben verbot. Gerade hierbei spielt Israel eine zentrale Rolle. Die umfassende und bedingungslose Unterstützung Israels wird in einen Akt höchster Sakralität verwandelt – eine sakralisierte Beziehung, hinter der sich, wie noch zu zeigen ist, die aparten Interessen der deutschen Bourgeoisie verbergen.


Diese Sakralisierung staatlicher Gewalt drückt sich in zahlreichen Reden deutscher Politiker:innen aus. So verkündete Angela Merkel in ihrer berühmten Staatsräson-Rede von 2008: »Deutschland und Israel sind und bleiben – und zwar für immer – auf besondere Weise durch die Erinnerung an die Shoah verbunden«. Die ehemalige deutsche Außenministerin Annalena Baerbock leitete aus dieser Erinnerung zum ersten Jahrestag des 7. Oktober im deutschen Bundestag die Legitimität von Gewalt ab: »Die Sicherheit Israels ist deutsche Staatsräson, unabhängig davon wer regiert, unabhängig davon, wer Außenpolitik macht […] Das Selbstverteidigungsrecht Israels ist auch unsere Verantwortung. Dazu stehen wir nicht nur mit Worten, sondern auch mit Taten, und zwar jeden Tag.« Zwar gehören, so Baerbock, laut deutscher Staatsräson »das humanitäre Völkerrecht und das Existenzrecht Israels auf das Engste zusammen«, doch Selbstverteidigung bedeute selbst verständlich auch die vollständige Zerstörung des Gegners und »wenn sich Hamas-Terroristen hinter Menschen, hinter Schulen verschanzen, dann kommen wir in ganz schwierige Bereiche. Aber wir ducken uns davor nicht weg. Deswegen habe ich vor den Vereinten Nationen auch deutlich gemacht: Dann können auch zivile Orte ihren Schutzstatus verlieren; weil Terroristen diese missbrauchen. author: Tom Bramble
title: US imperialism in the 21st century
content:
At the start of this century, US imperialism was at its peak. It had been a decade since its chief adversary, the Soviet Union, had crumbled; the country was now the unchallenged global superpower. Washington was bringing countries into the North Atlantic Treaty Organization that had been the USSR’s satellites in Europe, and it could rely on its allies to extend US influence into every corner of the world.

The US dominated the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund and was the most powerful nation in the United Nations. Its economy was booming, and the federal government ran surpluses. US multinationals found new markets and investment outlets worldwide. It was the heyday of “globalisation”. The US ruling class boasted that the country was a beacon to the world. As Democratic candidate Al Gore put it in one of the presidential debates in 2000:

“It is a great tribute to our founders that 224 years later this nation is now looked to by the peoples on every other continent and the peoples from every part of this Earth as a kind of model for what their future could be … The power of example is America’s greatest power in the world.”

Twenty-five years later, US rulers are not so assured. The country has suffered a series of crises, and the global balance of power has shifted. The US remains the world’s leading power, but it is wracked by dysfunction on a series of fronts. Its allies are increasingly estranged. Wars in the Middle East have exposed its diminished military power. Its tech sector and banks still lead, but its industrial base is now much weaker. Its political system is seen not as a model for what to do, but what to avoid. 

The decay of US power can be understood as the result of four interrelated phenomena: an imperial crisis in the Middle East, an economic crisis that crashed the world, the challenge from China and a political crisis that reflects and exacerbates these three trends.

The imperial crisis

The 9/11 attack on the World Trade Center in 2001 was a devastating blow to America’s sense of invulnerability. But US strategists also recognised the attack as an opportunity to advance US power—justification for a new round of wars that would intimidate the country’s rivals and allies alike and overcome the Vietnam-era legacy of widespread domestic opposition to far-flung and lengthy land wars. 

The idea of an aggressive revival of US military interventionism had been germinating in the ranks of the Republican Party for some years in its “neoconservative” wing. The leading think tank was the Project for a New American Century, founded by William Kristol and Robert Kagan. Its supporters and associates included Dick Cheney, Donald Rumsfeld, Paul Wolfowitz and John Bolton, all of whom held senior positions in the George W. Bush administration, which had won the 2000 election. 

The October 2001 invasion of Afghanistan was the first step in this wider project. Bush’s cabinet believed that the US would topple the ruling Taliban in Kabul and then lead a triumphal march through the capitals of its defeated enemies. Iraq, Iran and Syria were the main targets and, further afield, North Korea. Regime change was the objective.

In the short term, the invasion of Afghanistan was a stunning success. The Taliban were overthrown within two months. Domestic support for the war was overwhelming. It seemed US imperialism was back. Next was Iraq. The Bush administration justified its invasion by associating the country’s president, Saddam Hussein, with the 9/11 attacks and claiming that he had built an arsenal of weapons of mass destruction to threaten the West. On 19 March 2003, the US and its allies invaded Iraq. Within three weeks, US forces had taken Baghdad, and on 1 May Bush appeared on the deck of the

USS Abraham Lincoln

 to declare “mission accomplished”. 

Yet things turned bad for the US in both countries. In Iraq, local resistance to the occupation soon emerged. By the following year, it was raging. The US responded by flattening whole neighbourhoods, deploying white phosphorus and uranium-tipped weapons. Regular sweeps of suspected resistance activists terrified neighbourhoods and filled the jails. The US destroyed civilian infrastructure providing clean water, power and health care. And it sacked more than 100,000 government employees, creating mass unemployment and impoverishing millions. The death toll rose steadily. A study by the

Lancet

 journal in 2006 estimated 655,000 excess deaths in …

title: Συγκεντρώσεις αλληλεγγύης, Δευτέρα 2/11
content:
>Κάλεσμα στο δικαστήριο για την υπόθεση της εκκένωσης Ya Basta, 9:00 δικαστικό μέγαρο Ιωαννίνων


>Καμιά ποινή στις συναδέλφισσες του 3ου Δ.Σ. Ραφήνας, 13:00 Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο ανθρώπινου δυναμικού δημόσιου τομέα


Κάλεσμα στο δικαστήριο για την υπόθεση της εκκένωσης Ya Basta


ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗ ΣΤΑ 2 ΔΙΩΚΟΜΕΝΑ ΣΥΝΤΡΟΦΙΑ ΓΙΑ ΤΗΝ ΕΚΚΕΝΩΣΗ ΤΗΣ ΚΑΤΑΛΗΨΗΣ YA BASTA


Στις 23 Σεπτεμβρίου του 2024 εκκενώνεται η Κατάληψη Ya Basta στο Πανεπιστήμιο Ιωαννίνων μετά από επιχείρηση της τεχνικής υπηρεσίας μαζί με ομάδες της ΟΠΚΕ και της κρατικής ασφάλειας. Ο χώρος σφραγίστηκε προσωρινά, έγινε κατάσχεση αντικειμένων και συλλογή δαχτυλικών αποτυπωμάτων και DNA. Στο σήμερα 2 συντρόφια μας διώκονται για παρακώλυση δημόσιας υπηρεσίας και διατάραξη οικιακής ειρήνης (καθώς η κατάληψη στεγαζόταν στο κτίριο των Ά Εστιών) με μοναδικά αποδεικτικά στοιχεία δαχτυλικά αποτυπώματα πάνω σε κινητά αντικείμενα.


Χρειάζεται αρχικά να πούμε ότι η Κατάληψη Ya Basta ήταν ένα ακόμα λιθαράκι στην καταληψιακή – κινηματική ιστορία της πόλης. Δεν θα επιτρέψουμε επομένως σε κανένα καθίκι, είτε θεσμικό είτε με την προβιά του αγωνιστή, να λασπολογεί απέναντι σε καταλήψεις και στέκια, εκκενώντας χώρους και στοχοποιώντας συντρόφια, στο βωμό της πολιτικής καριέρας. Η Ya Basta ήταν ένας απελευθερωμένος χώρος από το 2011 και είχε ενεργή παρουσία μέχρι και το 2013. Με την αυτοδιάλυσή της, ο χώρος παρέμεινε έρμαιο στα χέρια ενός τυχοδιώκτη που παρασιτούσε εκεί για προσωπικό του όφελος. Το Δεκέμβρη του 2023 ομάδα συντροφιών αποφάσισε να ανακαταλάβει τον χώρο προσδίδοντας του ξανά πολιτικά χαρακτηριστικά και ανοίγοντας τις πόρτες του. (

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1628942/

). Από το 2024 και με την επανοικειοποίηση της κατάληψης ο χώρος απέκτησε ξανά ζωή με συνελεύσεις και δομές, προϋπάρχουσες στην κατάληψη, παίρνοντας την σκυτάλη από την πολιτική παρακαταθήκη του χώρου και με τακτικά ανοίγματα επιτρέποντας την ελεύθερη αλληλεπίδραση και επικοινωνία ατόμων αντιιεραρχικά και αυτοοργανωμένα (

https://yabastasquat.espivblogs.net/

). Παράλληλα, υπήρχαν καταλήψεις εστιών που πρόσεθεταν μια διάχυτη αυτοοργανωμένη λογική και μια κοινοτική κάλυψη των βασικών αναγκών αλληλοτροφοδοτώντας την αυτοπραγμάτωση του καταληψιακού αξιακού.

Ενάντια στην αποστειρωμένη και αποξενωμένη πραγματικότητα που επιβάλλει το σύγχρονο ελληνικό πανεπιστήμιο οι καταλήψεις και συλλογικές διαδικασίες είναι αγκάθι και αντιπρόταση στην ζοφερή αυτή πραγματικότητα.


Ξετυλίγοντας, λοιπόν το νήμα της καταστολής του Σεπτέμβρη του 2024, οι πρωτοστάτες στην επιβολή του νόμου και της τάξης δεν είναι όπως θα περιμέναμε μπάτσοι ή ρουφιάνοι της Άννας Μπατιστάτου (πρύτανης του Πανεπιστημίου Ιωαννίνων), αλλά οι πεμπτοφαλαγγίτες της αριστεράς αυτή τη φορά με το προσωπείο της Τετάρτης Διεθνούς. Το οργανωτικό σχήμα ΟΚΔΕ/ΣΣΠ με πλήρη και χρόνια εργαλειοποίηση του Συλλόγου Εστιακών Φοιτητών επιτέθηκε κυκλωτικά και υπεράριθμα σε σώμα συντρόφων μετά την κατάληψη φοιτητικής εστίας.(

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1631698/

 ,

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1631724/

)


Την επόμενη μέρα κι ενώ αλληλέγγυος κόσμος βρισκόταν στην κατάληψη για συνέλευση ενάντια στους ηγεμονισμούς και τραμπουκισμούς των παρακρατικών της ΟΚΔΕ η ασφάλεια του Πανεπιστήμιου Ιωαννίνων χτυπάει την πόρτα και ανακοινώνει την άμεση εκκένωση του χώρου μέχρι το βράδυ της ίδιας μέρας. (

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1631706/

) Ακολουθεί ένα 10ήμερο κινητοποιήσεων στο Πανεπιστήμιο με μικροφωνικές, αφισοκολλήσεις, παρεμβάσεις και ανοιχτές διαδικασίες για την υπεράσπιση της κατάληψης. Τα ξημερώματα στις 23 Σεπτέμβρη μπάτσοι και υπάλληλοι της τεχνικής υπηρεσίας εισβάλλουν στον χώρο και μέσα σε λίγες ώρες τον αδειάζουν και κατάσχουν όσα αντικείμενα υπάρχουν μέσα προκειμένου να μεταφερθούν για αποτυπώματα και DNA (

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1631858/

). Μέτα από 5 μήνες γίνεται επιχείρηση “σκούπα” από μπάτσους στις εστίες του πανεπιστημίου κάνοντας ντου στα κατειλλημένα δωμάτια με ασφαλίτες να ρωτάνε για τον κόσμο που συμμετείχε στην Κατάληψη Ya Basta.


Ερχόμενα στο τώρα, μετά από 2 χρόνια έρχεται δικογραφία σε 2 συντρόφια μας, διωκόμενα από την Πρύτανη Α. Μπατιστάτου για παρακώλυση δημόσιας υπηρεσίας και διατάραξη οικιακής ειρήνης με μόνο αποδεικτικό στοιχείο τα δαχτυλικά αποτυπώματα σε 3 κινητά αντικείμενα (2 βάζα και 1 ετικέτα από μπουκάλι νερού). Τα δαχτυλικά αποτυπώματα είναι πρωτοφανής μέθοδος δίωξης για τα δεδομένα της πόλης, αλλά εννοείται ότι δεν μας εκπλήσσει, καθώς ξέρουμε πολύ καλά ότι οι κατασταλτικοί μηχανισμοί …

title: Emeklilerin üçte ikisi çalışmak zorunda, ileri yaşta iş cinayetleri tırmanıyor
content:
Andaç Aydın Arıduru [email protected]

Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan 26 Ekim tarihli kabine toplantısının ardından yaptığı açıklamada, “Sosyal adalet ilkemiz gereği, devletimizin şefkat elini ihtiyacı olan her bir vatandaşımıza ulaştırmak boynumuzun borcudur” ifadelerini kullandı. Erdoğan’ın açıklamalarının ardından AKP kanadından emekli maaşlarında “refah payı” veya “seyyanen zam” seçeneklerinin değerlendirildiği açıklamaları geldi. Milyonlarca emekli açlık sınırının altında, asgari ücretin gerisinde aylıklara mahkum. AKP’li yıllarda emekli olup çalışmaya devam etmek zorunda kalanların sayısı 4 kattan fazla arttı. Emekli aylığıyla geçim, ülkenin en yoksul kesiminin verdiği geçim mücadelesi haline geldi.

En düşük emekli aylığı 23 bin 552 TL seviyesinde. Her ay Türk-İş tarafından açıklanan ve 4 kişilik bir ailenin sadece beslenebilmek için gıda masraflarını içeren açlık sınırı Ekim ayında 38 bin 24 TL oldu. Emekli aylığı, açlık sınırının yüzde 38 altında kalıyor. Gıda ile birlikte diğer tüm temel harcamalar için haneye girmesi gereken toplam gelir tutarı olan yoksulluk sınırı ise 123 bin 856 TL. Emekli aylığı yoksulluk sınırının yüzde 81 altında kalıyor.

Zam senaryoları en düşük emekli aylığını dahi açlık sınırına ulaştırmıyor. Gündemdeki zam senaryolarına göre seçeneklerden biri tüm emekli aylıklarına seyyanen zam, diğeri ise enflasyon artışının üzerinde refah payı verilmesi. Sabah Gazetesi yazarı Faruk Erdem, emeklilere yönelik hazırlıkların detaylarını aktarırken ocak ayında refah payı artışının da gündemde olduğunu ileri sürdü. Haberde verilen örnek hesaba göre, 3 bin liralık seyyanen zam yapılırsa 23 bin 552 TL olan en düşük emekli aylığı 26 bin 552 TL'ye yükselecek. En düşük emekli maaşı (23 bin 552 TL) ocak ayında yüzde 10 zam yapılması durumunda aylık 25 bin 907 TL'ye yükselir. Yüzde 5 refah payı verilmesi durumunda emekli aylığı 27 bin 202 TL'ye, yüzde 20 refah payı verilmesi durumunda 31 bin 88 TL olabilir.

3 bin liralık seyyanen zam yapılsa bile en düşük emekli aylığı açlık sınırının yalnızca yüzde 69.8'ine ulaşacak. Yüzde 10 zamda bu oran yüzde 68.1, yüzde 5 refah payında yüzde 71.5, yüzde 20 refah payında ise yüzde 81.8 olacak. En yüksek senaryoda dahi emekli aylığı açlık sınırının 6 bin 936 TL altında kalacak. Yoksulluk sınırı karşısındaki tablo ise daha ağır: En yüksek, yani yüzde 20 refah payı senaryosunda bile aylık yoksulluk sınırının yalnızca yüzde 25.1'ine ulaşacak ve 92 bin 768 TL altında kalacak.

Emekli aylıklarının Gayrisafi Yurtiçi Hasıla (GSYH) karşısındaki kaybı da derinleşti. 2002’de ortalama emekli aylığının kişi başına milli gelire oranı yüzde 46.4 iken 2025’te yüzde 31.6’ya düştü. 2019’da ortalama emekli aylığı en düşük aylığın yüzde 91.7 üzerindeyken, bu fark 2025’te yüzde 18’e indi.

2025 yılı için 14 bin 469 TL olarak uygulanan taban aylık dikkate alındığında 14 bin 469 TL olan en düşük emekli aylığıyla geçinen bir hanenin yıllık geliri 173 bin 628 TL’de kaldı. Bu tutar, en yoksul yüzde 20’lik kesimin 200 bin 100 TL’lik ortalama yıllık gelirinin de altında kaldı.

TÜİK verilerine göre emekli hanelerinin konut ve kira harcamalarının bütçedeki payı 2018’de yüzde 28.55’ten 2025’te yüzde 38.66’ya çıktı. Kira yükü artarken gıdanın payı yüzde 25.52’den yüzde 22.66’ya geriledi. En yoksul hanelerin gelirinde emekli aylığının payı da 2018’de yüzde 13.70’ten 2025’te yüzde 20.29’a yükseldi. Böylece emekli aylığının en yoksul hanelerin bütçesindeki ağırlığı yüzde 50’den fazla arttı.

TÜİK’in 2025 verileri, temel geçim kaynağı emekli aylığı olan hanelerin tüketim harcamalarının en yoksul yüzde 20’lik kesimle eşitlendiğini ve yer yer gerisine düştüğünü gösteriyor. Her iki grubun bütçesinin yaklaşık yüzde 39’u konut ve kiraya giderken, eğlence, kültür ve giyim harcamaları yüzde 1-3 bandında kalıyor. Gıdanın payı ise artan gıda enflasyonu nedeniyle emekli hanelerinde yüzde 22.66’ya kadar düşüyor.

Emekli aylıklarının erimesi ve artan barınma giderleri, milyonlarca emekliyi yeniden çalışmaya zorladı. DİSK-AR’ın SGK ve TÜİK verilerine göre 2002’de 4.3 milyon emeklinin 1.6 milyonu (yüzde 36.6'sı) çalışırken, 2025’te 12.3 milyon emeklinin 8.5 milyonu (yüzde 69’u) çalışıyor veya iş arıyor. Yani her üç emekliden ikisi emeklilik hakkını fiilen kullanamaz hale geldi.

TÜİK işgücü göstergeleriyle yapılan karşılaştırmalı hesaplama, emeklilerin genel işgücü içindeki ağırlığının tarihi bir sıçrama yaptığını gösteriyor: 2005 yılında çalışan veya iş arayan 1.9 milyon emeklinin, Türkiye'de işgücü olarak ölçülen 21.3 …

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Federal government says lack of housing on First Nations ‘strictly’ a funding issue
content:
During the final hour of a two-day hearing at the Federal Court of Appeal, lawyers representing First Nations and Canada argued whether the matter of water and housing on reserve land was about money or human rights.

Canada asserted that when it comes to providing housing, the government “is limited” to providing funding for the homes, making the issue a matter of financial duty.

“First Nations manage their own housing,” said one of Canada’s lawyers. “Leadership determines what is to be built, where it is to be built, and how it will be contained.”

However, lawyers representing Shamattawa and St. Theresa Point First Nations asked how that could be possible, when the Indian Act had caused the housing shortages that are affecting Indigenous communities in the first place.

“There’s such extreme harm that we can say that there’s no way a First Nation would have brought this on itself if it could have afforded it,” said Michael Rosenberg, one of an equally plentiful team of lawyers representing the Nations.

The federal government had recently appealed two decisions made by Federal Court Justice Paul Favel in December 2025, when he had concluded that Canada had the obligation to provide Shamattawa and St. Theresa Point First Nations access to housing and clean drinking water.

“The lawsuit at its heart is about funding and increased funding, not an abstract separation of right,” said a lawyer representing the Liberal government on Wednesday.

Over a phone call, Rosenberg also confirmed to APTN News that, in alignment with that claim, the government was also asking for court costs alongside the appeals.

Back in court, he said the communities were not able to properly provide for themselves without financial and structural support from the government, and Canada did, in fact, still have control over all of the houses on a reserve.

“Part of what has kept these First Nations in this state [of poor housing] has been Canada’s part in the Indian Act, constructed to deprive them,” he said.

Rosenberg argued that according to a report from the Auditor General of Canada submitted to Parliament in 2024, Canada was still in the process of transferring control of housing back to the First Nations.

In the report he referenced that the auditor general had also concluded that, “We found that Indigenous Services Canada was at the early stages of transferring control of housing to First Nations, but no overarching policy framework was in place to guide the department’s work in transferring its programs to First Nations communities.

“Under the Department of Indigenous Services Act,” the report continued, “Indigenous Services Canada is mandated to work with First Nations to gradually transfer departmental responsibilities to First Nations, including housing. As of 31 March 2023, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation did not have the legislative mandate to transfer its responsibilities to First Nations.”

The report also stated that this transfer process “is not imposed” on the First Nations, and they need to want to take over those responsibilities.

Rosenberg said many communities have not expressed that interest because they “aren’t able to provide that support,” without money from Canada.

He said, according to evidence from the original lawsuit, the Assembly of First Nations (AFN) even “resisted the idea of moving Canada’s commitment to First Nations,” which he described as “divesting itself [Canada] of its own commitment.”

Instead, the AFN, a political organization that represents more than 600 First Nations in Canada, has been developing a National First Nations Housing and Infrastructure Strategy, which is a lengthy transition period done in collaboration with ISC, since 2018.

The proposed strategy would include transferring control of funding as well.

“The success of any recognition of First Nations complete authority over their housing depends on a federal initiative to transfer control of housing programs and services funds that is broadly flexible enough to accommodate the wide range of First Nations preferences,” the national organization stated in a release.

This is in part due to “circular funding,” he said, as the government will fund housing projects that require rent, and the rent then paid to the government by members will be dollars collected from government checks.

“That is the dynamic here, however it is dressed up,” he said.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Santiago del Estero: Corrupción y desalojo contra comunidad originaria La Armonía
content:
Un operativo policial intentó desalojar este miércoles a una familia del territorio ancestral de la comunidad indígena Lule Vilela La Armonía, en el Departamento Copo de la provincia de Santiago del Estero, a instancias de una persona ajena a la comunidad, Isabel Salas, que reclama la tierra comunitaria como propia y pretende venderla. La resistencia frenó el desalojo y la orden fue temporalmente suspendida.


Intento de desalojo en la comunidad La Armonía. Captura de video de MOCASE VC


“Así es el atropello para desalojar a campesinos indígenas de la comunidad indígena Lule Vilela La Armonía”, denunció el Movimiento Campesino de Santiago del Estero (MOCASE) Vía Campesina al publicar un video del despliegue policial ocurrido durante la mañana de este miércoles 28 de octubre.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por MOCASE VC (@mocase_viacampesina)


“Así es la mafia de la venta ilegal de tierras a los que les gusta la plata”, agregaron desde la organización, y responsabilizaron a una persona llamada Isabel Salas, alias “Chabela”, de la localidad de Monte Quemado, como la impulsora del operativo. Desde la comunidad La Armonía agregaron que se trata de una situación repetida, y que Isabel Salas “le paga al Oficial de Justicia”.


Vender el territorio ancestral


Rosa Córdoba, Consejera de la Comunidad Lule Vilela La Armonía, detalló la situación que están enfrentando: “Hemos sufrido un atropello aquí en la comunidad, en el lugar denominado 5 Hermanos donde vive la familia Tévez y Salto. La familia está conformada con 5 hijos, nietos, yerno, nueras. Ellos viven de hace más de 10 años en el lugar, pero es territorio relevado, ancestral de la comunidad. Como la comunidad siempre ha tenido una idea de eso, de los territorios que están relevados y vacíos, que se le den a hijos de compañeros del lugar, y esto ha sucedido así”.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Rosa-Cordoba-Consejera-MOCASE-La-Armonia.ogg


Audio: Rosa Córdoba


El campesinado santiagueño, criollo e indígena,

sufre históricamente situaciones de violencia e indefensión jurídica y social

 ante sujetos que buscan apropiarse de tierras comunales y fiscales, muchas veces con la complicidad activa y manifiesta de funcionarios judiciales y de las fuerzas de seguridad.


Así ocurre en este caso. Rosa cuenta que “esta mujer, Isabel Salas, alias Chabela, conjuntamente con su hijo, Federico Guzmán, se quieren apropiar del lugar diciendo que es de ellos, y tan solo se quieren apropiar para venderlo. Ya esta mujer lo ha vendido varias veces haciendo esas solicitudes truchas, que desde Colonización

(nota: se refiere a la ex

Dirección de Colonización

 de Santiago del Estero)

, lo sabía hacer a estas solicitudes que se le daba a cualquiera y en cualquier lugar, sin importarle quién viviese en el territorio ese. Entonces, estas personas vendían esos lugares a cordobeses, a chaqueños, y ellos se iban apropiando así de los lugares. Entonces, llega esta mujer queriendo vender cierta cantidad de hectáreas que dice que son 3200 hectáreas, que es territorio ancestral de la comunidad”.


Intento de desalojo en la comunidad La Armonía. Captura de video de MOCASE VC


La resistencia frenó el desalojo


“Nosotros estamos organizados con el MOCASE en la comunidad La Armonía, y nos despertamos con esta noticia”, contó Rosa.


“En realidad, no nos despertamos porque todos aquí estamos trabajando en las tareas laborales en el campo, y todo el mundo se ha puesto alerta, dejando lo que teníamos que hacer, por ir a solidarizarse con el compañero para que no sea desalojado. Entonces, ahí nos damos que todo ha sido arreglado, como esta mujer le paga al Oficial de Justicia, le paga a la Policía de Santiago del Estero para que haga este desalojo”.


“Entonces, aquí, como nosotros vamos al lugar y comenzamos a resistir en el lugar, a decir que no lo van a desalojar al compañero, porque el lugar es de la comunidad, es del compañero, está produciendo en el lugar. Que nos oponíamos a todo eso. Entonces, al ver toda esta resistencia de la comunidad que hubo, el juez dictamina que se cancele el desalojo y que hagan todo un inventario y que hagan una investigación profunda”.
