author: Hayley Tsukayama
title: Why VPNs Are Worth Defending
content:
Developers of virtual private network (VPN) apps are reporting that their products are again being pulled from Apple’s App Store in Russia. This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online.

Why? VPNs give people a way to control their own online activities. When you visit a website through a VPN, that website only sees the VPN server's location (well, IP address) rather than your actual location. It's like sending a letter through a P.O. box so the recipient doesn't know where you really live. It can also disguise where you’re accessing information from, which can make it possible to access information banned by your government.

This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online.

Going after tools that give people the space to communicate and access information freely is a common tactic from the totalitarian playbook. This latest demand comes after several steps the Russian government’s taken to surveil speech specifically on Apple products. In 2024, the Moscow Times reported that Russia’s state media watchdog, Roskomnadzor, went after VPN apps on the Apple App Store, after banning access to Western social media platforms and blacklisting opposition media sites. Russia then blocked Apple’s FaceTime software in 2025, according to Apple Insider.

Bloomberg also recently reported that the Russian government has added Apple and Microsoft to its state surveillance registry. This gives Roskomnadzor access to local users’ correspondence, Apple Insider reported, and puts both companies in a position to turn over customer information to the country’s security services as required.

With government control encroaching on their devices and less access to tools that give them alternate methods, people in Russia are left with shrinking options to communicate online or find information that isn’t state-sanctioned.

While Russia’s actions offer a more extreme vision of what happens when the government tries to enforce speech rules by attacking vital privacy tools, it is far from the only government doing so. Several states in the U.S., bent on making it difficult to circumvent invasive age-gating laws, have suggested banning VPNs—either to access certain content or in some cases to simply ban them outright. EFF has publicly (and loudly) criticized these proposals, because going after VPNs is a dangerous step down the road of censorship.

Attacks on speech and privacy online are deeply troubling, no matter where they happen. What those in power may see as a “loophole” in their invasive laws is actually an expression of user control. We’ll continue to speak out when we see governments going after them to take that control away.

author: rezgar2
title: The Dark Side of the “Machine God”: 5 Unsettling Truths About Big Tech’s AI Obsession
content:
Silicon Valley routinely promises a sparkling utopia where artificial intelligence will cure complex diseases, optimize global labor, and render the very concept of money obsolete. Yet behind the polished keynotes and corporate public relations, a far more unsettling reality is taking shape. A small handful of ultra-wealthy tech oligarchs, the heads of Meta, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, are making unilateral decisions about the collective future of humanity, operating entirely outside democratic oversight or public accountability.

Silicon Valley routinely promises a sparkling utopia where artificial intelligence will cure complex diseases, optimize global labor, and render the very concept of money obsolete. Yet behind the polished keynotes and corporate public relations, a far more unsettling reality is taking shape. A small handful of ultra-wealthy tech oligarchs, the heads of Meta, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, are making unilateral decisions about the collective future of humanity, operating entirely outside democratic oversight or public accountability.

This concentration of power exposes a jarring central paradox: the exact same tech CEOs who claim AI will solve humanity’s greatest challenges simultaneously warn that the technology could trigger civilizational extinction, openly describing their pursuit as “summoning the demon.” Rather than pausing development, these executives have accelerated an apocalyptic arms race to build ultra-powerful systems, framing themselves as indispensable guardians of human survival.

To understand where artificial intelligence is truly taking society, we must look past corporate marketing and examine the underlying worldviews, historical lineages, and material harms driving the tech elite. Moving beyond superficial consumer hype reveals how a toxic mix of fringe ideologies, extractive labor practices, and authoritarian state alliances is steering Silicon Valley toward what critical theorists and legal scholars call “techno-fascism.”

To make sense of Silicon Valley’s relentless drive toward Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) and Artificial Superintelligence (ASI), one must understand the bizarre ideological framework shaping its leaders. Coined by philosopher Emile Torres and computer scientist Timnit Gebru, the acronym TESCREAL encapsulates a bundle of tightly interwoven worldviews: Transhumanism, Extropianism, Singularitarianism, Cosmism, Rationalism, Effective Altruism, and Longtermism.

Dr. Emile Torres highlights a critical historical truth at the heart of this ideology: transhumanism is fundamentally “eugenics on steroids.” Unlike nineteenth-century eugenics, which sought merely to optimize the existing human species through selective breeding, transhumanism seeks to use radical technology to completely replace and transcend humanity, engineering an entirely new posthuman species. Within Silicon Valley AI circles, this hypothetical superintelligence is explicitly referred to as a “Machine God.” Tech CEOs effectively act as high priests, competing to bring an all-knowing digital deity into physical existence.

This radical ideology shapes corporate roadmaps in concrete, disturbing ways:

Sam Altman (OpenAI): In a blog post titled “The Merge,” Altman argued that AI surpassing human intellect is inevitable, framing un-merged human beings as a temporary “biological bootloader” for digital intelligence that will ultimately fade into an evolutionary side-branch. Altman notably paid $10,000 to join a brain-uploading waitlist with Nectome and co-founded a brain-computer interface venture to facilitate digital integration.

Ray Kurzweil & Demis Hassabis (DeepMind): Representing Extropianism and Singularitarianism, Kurzweil champions the doctrine of living long enough to achieve digital immortality, targeting a self-improving “singularity” by 2032. Hassabis, DeepMind’s co-founder, operates under a similar singularitarian impulse to engineer self-evolving intellect.

Eliezer Yudkowsky (Rationalism): A foundational figure in modern rationalist thought who famously posited a utilitarian moral calculation arguing that forcing a single person to endure 50 years of relentless torture is ethically preferable to an unfathomable number of people experiencing the mild inconvenience of a speck of dust in their eye.

Elon Musk (xAI/SpaceX): Demonstrating classic Longtermism, Musk explicitly cites the expansion of the Sun billions of years in the future to justify prioritizing …

author: Nolan Higdon
title: AI Techno-Utopianism and Doomsday Threats Distract From Big Tech’s Current Harms
content:
The industry uses fantasies of technological dominance to paper over financial shortcomings and demands for regulation.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

During a September 2026 visit to Ireland, President Donald Trump declared, “We’re leading China in AI [artificial intelligence]. We’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins.” His remarks arrived after months of calls from the public and tech industry insiders to slow AI development. These concerns were triggered by revelations that foundational models from Anthropic, Gemini, Meta, and OpenAI had bypassed safety protocols, accessed networks without authorization, and carried out illicit intrusions. These revelations fueled public panic that tech firms had created superintelligence — an AI exceeding human capability that posed an existential threat to humanity — even though no such breakthrough had actually been achieved.

Public concern intensified in October 2026 when cybersecurity firm Wiz revealed it had used AI tools from Google and OpenAI to identify critical security flaws in PHP: the programming language powering roughly 70% of the web. Although developers quickly released a patch, once the vulnerability was made public hacking attempts surged. In response, the governments of the Netherlands, France, Denmark, and Finland temporarily took several official websites offline.

Widespread panic over AI yielded little legislative action, as lawmakers refused to regulate or tax the industry out of fear that doing so would handicap domestic innovation and yield ground to China. However, the core threat to human existence lies neither in a lost geopolitical race nor in muted technological growth, but rather in the ubiquitous rollout of non-autonomous systems falsely hailed as artificial intelligence.

Big Tech was built on state-funded innovation, with core technologies like the internet, Global Positioning Systems (GPS), and touchscreen displays originating in public institutions. Yet during the deregulation and privatization waves of the 1980s and 1990s, lawmakers sheltered these emerging tech monopolies through minimal taxation and oversight. Most notable was Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, which insulates platforms from liability for content posted by third parties. Without this protection, social media as we know it would cease to exist. Section 230 absolves tech firms of responsibility for architectures that foster misinformation, even as research confirms that the platforms themselves, not just user posts, are responsible for accelerating the spread of falsehoods over truth.

Lawmakers’ opposition to regulation is rooted in techno-utopianism, the ideological premise that technological progress inherently benefits society. Lawmakers operated under the assumption that any taxation or regulatory oversight would stifle innovation and ultimately harm consumers. Indeed, in 1997, then-President Bill Clinton wrote in an Executive Order “governments attempts to establish technical standards to govern the Internet would only risk inhibiting technological innovation.”

Without meaningful regulation, Big Tech rapidly consolidated into lucrative monopolies — collectively known as FAANG (Facebook, Apple, Amazon, Netflix, and Google) or GAMMA (Google (Alphabet), Apple, Meta (formerly Facebook), Microsoft, and Amazon) conglomerates. Their vast wealth is powered by surveillance capitalism: an economic model that treats human experience as free raw material to be extracted, analyzed, and commercialized. Under this economic order, data is systematically mined through “smart” devices — where “smart” is merely a euphemism for active, continuous monitoring, including the collection of biometric data. This wholesale erosion of privacy has proven extraordinarily lucrative for Big Tech. By feeding this extracted data into algorithms, these firms build detailed psychographic profiles on users and sell the insights to insurance companies determining coverage premiums, employers screening job applicants, and law enforcement agencies evaluating security threats.

Absent meaningful government oversight, Big Tech has been left to police itself. Take the moral panic over fake news after the 2016 Presidential Election, when politicians warned that election meddling in the form of disinformation online was harming a defining feature of the U …

author: Adetokunbo Abiola
title: Nigeria’s AI Ambitions vs. The Regulatory Void–Who Protects the Citizens?
content:
Last year, scammers launched a deepfake videos of popular Nigerian social media influencer,

Martins Vincent Otse

, through a fraudulent Facebook campaign. The cybercriminals superimposed a fabricated AI-generated audio on a genuine video of Otse from early 2024.


Martins Vincent Otse


In the cloned voice, Otse introduced an online chatting scheme where viewers could earn up to $1,000 monthly. By cloning the influencer’s face and reputation, the scammers not only harmed Otse’s reputation as a respected influencer, they also preyed on the poverty of many Nigerians, tricking them into becoming a member of an online platform created to appropriate their personal information and savings.


On

October 5

, to show that the issue still mattered, the Nigeria Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) warned organisations and staff against sharing sensitive data with public AI tools.


As the federal government shapes  its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy with the aim to leapfrog development, doctors and nurses use clinical Al tools without standardised verification methods and companies run systems without Al oversight structures. Banks move transactions to automated and Al-driven solutions to combat soaring transaction fraud and manage financial risk, while


87.5 percent

 of  fintech companies now deploy Al for automated fraud detection. In theory, the

Nigeria Data Protection Act

 gave citizens the right to object to automated decision-making; in practice, the abuse of enforcement renders it non-justiceable when Al systems cause harm.


For instance, during the lead up to the 2023 presidential elections, a simulated audio clip went viral, purportedly featuring

former Vice President Abubakar Atiku

 and other members of his party  discussing plans to rig the election. Fact checkers labelled the audio false and generated by artificial intelligence tools. Investigations opened, but there was no prosecution. Defamation laws exist in Nigeria, but none existed to assign blame for the creation of a lie by generative models.


In another instance, unverified screening AIs missed the detection of over

1,247 tuberculosis cases

, as well misclassified

342 high-risk pregnancies

, with

186 preventable patient deaths

 linked to Al diagnostic errors. The tools involved were not registered as medical devices by the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control ( NAFDAC), but registered as “wellness” apps.


Driven by the Ministry of Communications and NITDA, the National AI Strategy sets normative ambitions — to align AI deployment with human rights. But with internet penetration now at

68.3 percent penetration

 at

148.2 million

 subscribers, that ambition is no longer aspirational; the state has a functional duty to protect citizens from algorithmic harm at scale.


The issue remains implementation. NITDA has put together a draft

Al Code of Practice

, and the Nigerian Data Protection Commission is enforcing data protection. But broader analytics from NITDA suggest that more than

56 percent

 of government IT projects fail to meet expectations due to procurement, design and implementation flaws. This exposes sensitive consumer data to hackers, increasing the risk of identity theft and digital fraud from design flaws.


In the UK and EU, high-risk AI systems are subject to mandatory pre-deployment conformity assessments. In Nigeria, where banks now use AI-powered tools to identify and prevent fraudulent transactions, no equivalent requirement exists for auditing models against local fraud patterns before they go live.


This institutionalises systemic weaknesses. Angela Olusola was a 46-year-old mother of three. After an unaudited AI flagged her successive transaction as suspicious fraud behaviour, it froze her account. Unfortunately, she lacked financial buffers, with the 48-to-72-hour account freeze meaning she could not buy food, pay her transport fares or restock her business. Since she lived from hand-to-mouth, the algorithm error triggered an immediate poverty crisis.


Algorithmic biases in micro-lending are not abstract. A poor trader who uses a cheap phone and constantly changes SIM cards is flagged as “high risk”. The algorithm sees her behaviour as an indicator of low financial standing or attempts to cheat, resulting in instant loan rejections.


The training data is heavily skewed to salaried, urban, Android users in Lagos.

title: EDRi-gram, 29 October 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Celebrating end-to-end encryption, and the digital justice community in Europe and beyond

We’re still riding the high from October milestones showcasing the strength of our community. We had the pleasure of greeting many of you in person and online for #PrivacyCamp26 two weeks ago to discuss the origins of technology and how to pivot from conversations around “sovereignty” to meaningful, community-led self-determination. If you weren’t able to make it but you’re curious about the conversations, you can rewatch the livestream of some of the panel discussions.

Then, on October 21, we celebrated Global Encryption Day, highlighting end-to-end encryption as a crucial foundation to our right to safe and secure communication online and to life as we know it. Thanks to our members and partners, our message of protecting encryption was visible across several European capitals – from the metro trains of Prague to key landmarks in Berlin, Paris and Dublin with mobile “encryption trucks”. We also worked with European Sex Workers Alliance and Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement to raise awareness on the importance of safe and secure communications for sex workers as well as womens’ rights. You can read more about the action in this edition, and stay tuned for more updates coming soon on our social platforms.

Yet another win for digital rights this month came with the news of Norway’s data protection authority imposing a fine of 92 million Norwegian crowns (roughly EUR 8.8 million) on Microsoft’s adtech unit Xandr for unlawfully sharing ​Grindr users’ sensitive data with thousands of advertisers.

While we’re bolstered from the wins and community spirit, there’s a lot more to resist and much work to be done. We are still reeling from the EU governments’ final position on the Digital Omnibus on Data, which amongst other unsavoury things, will to allow companies to use our data to develop or use their AI systems if it serves a ‘legitimate interest’ – without us knowing or accepting. This is a blank cheque for tech corporations to indulge in outrageous data grabs and exploit potentially sensitive information about us.

Earlier this week, the European Commission also announced a revamp of Frontex, EU’s border agency, that is set to double its budget and expand its role in deportations and surveillance. Not only will this turn Frontex into EU’s ICE equivalent, the new Regulation also wants to allow Frontex to be able to monitor social media for information that may forecast people’s movements at EU borders. Let alone leading with solidarity and care, the EU seems intent on violating people’s freedom to move and to express themselves. Keep your eyes out for an analysis of the new proposal from the Protect Not Surveil coalition.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Cyberlibel complaints vs journalists strengthen calls to decriminalize libel
content:
The criminal sanction for Philippine libel laws is “excessive” and is in violation of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) to which the Philippines is a signatory.

Libel complaints were recently filed against journalists and media company executives. For a journalists’ group, these validate the previous calls to decriminalize libel.

The GMA chapter of the National Union of Journalists of the Philippines (NUJP) stressed that libel laws silence journalism. “[C]riminalizing speech only undermines the public’s fundamental right to know,” the chapter said in a statement.

Davao City 1st District Rep. Paolo Duterte filed libel and cyberlibel complaints against GMA executives and broadcast journalists which stemmed from the network’s report about alleged cash deliveries to the Dutertes claimed by dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.

Duterte filed the complaint before the Davao City Prosecutor’s Office on October 23, more than two weeks after his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, made a joke about filing a multimillion-peso libel case against GMA Network. Her remarks happened during a press conference on October 6 while reading her affidavit which answers Gracioso’s claims.

Among the respondents were GMA executives Felipe Gozon and Gilberto Duavit, as well as journalists Mel Tiangco, Vicki Morales, Emil Sumangil, Darlene Cay, Marvin Parado, Joel San Luis, and other unidentified individuals.

In a statement released on October 23, the TV network said that they have not yet received the complaints.

Gracioso and National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) director Melvin Matibag were also named as respondents.

Meanwhile, veteran journalist Philip Lustre Jr. was arrested on October 24 over a cyberlibel complaint reportedly filed by Mans Carpio, Sara’s husband. He was unaware of the complaint, according to his legal counsel. He was released on bail on the same day.

NUJP has been campaigning for the decriminalization of libel, echoing the views of the United Nations (UN) Human Rights Committee that the criminal sanction for Philippine libel laws is “excessive” and is in violation of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) to which the Philippines is a signatory.

Right(s) Up: Why journalists and advocates push for decriminalization of libel

On September 18, NUJP released its policy review on libel laws, stating that the high court has already identified the problem of these laws but reform requires legislation. The review, to name a few, cited Justice Marvic Leonen’s opinion in Disini, Jr. v. Secretary of Justice which stated that libel was unconstitutional as penal sanctions impose “an invidious chilling effect.”

It added that removing jail time alone, as proposed by some legislators, is not decriminalization because of limitations of a fine-only regime, saying that if the accused cannot pay, subsidiary imprisonment may follow.

The review cited the data obtained from the Office of Cybercrime of the Department of Justice (DOJ), indicating that 3,770 cyberlibel cases had been filed, as of May 2022, since the enactment of the Cybercrime Prevention Act. More than 2,500 cases remained pending in courts and before the prosecution level. There were already 12 convictions.

In the 2023 study by NUJP, 61.5% of the libel cases against 50 journalists from 2021 to 2023 were filed by politicians.

ML Party-list Rep. Leila de Lima said that filing a libel suit against journalists and media workers for doing their job sends a “chilling message” to other members of the press. Parties being accused can just respond to the allegations, she wrote in a Facebook post.

Under the Journalist’s Code of Ethics approved by media groups, journalists shall recognize the duty to air the other side and the duty to correct substantive errors promptly.

“Contrary to allegations of malice or unverified reporting, the report went through standard, multi-layered editorial and legal verification procedures,” the NUJP GMA Chapter said. “The team conducted due diligence—verifying information through official sources, law enforcement documents, and background checks—and obtained proper clearance from network leadership and legal counsel before airing the story.”

In the subject report, the reporter, Cay, and anchor Tiangco mentioned that they were trying to get the comments of the people implicated by Gracioso, including the Dutertes, but they did not receive a response when the report was aired …

title: La bande à « Balance ton Claude »
content:
Nous avons déjà longuement abordé les ressorts de l'« affaire Thélyson Orélien » dans nos pages (nous renvoyons, entre autres, à

cet excellent texte de Jean Claude Noel

). L'enquête qui suit porte sur ses délateurs, la bande à « Balance ton Claude » du nom du compte X à l'origine de la polémique. On y découvre que l'affaire Thélyson Orélien, est un double écran de fumée qui masque une convergence d'intérêts, financiers, idéologiques et géopolitiques, entre l'industrie de l'IA, les libertariens de la Silicon Valley, les christo-fascistes de l'administration Trump, et leurs imitateurs bien-de-chez-nous.


« Démarche complètement apolitique », « lanceur d'alerte », anonymat nécessaire pour éviter les attaques

ad hominem

… Toutes ces auto-justifications offertes par la bande à « Balance ton Claude », qui est derrière la polémique Thélyson Orélien, servent à ripoliner une opération idéologique, menée par un groupe de jeunes « libéraux-conservateurs » (doux euphémisme), très actifs dans l'espace médiatique, depuis les colonnes du Figaro, et les fabriques à propagande du projet Périclès. En outre, ces alarmes hypocrites s'inscrivent dans les récits

IApocalyptiques

 déployés par l'industrie pour faire gonfler investissements publics et privés. Une bulle profitant surtout aux nouveaux technoligarques, qui sont prêts à jeter la démocratie et l'humanité entière dans le chaudron de la valorisation et de la domination sans partage.


Les problèmes posés par la rédaction

I

A

ssistée

cachent une autre forme d'imposture : les allégations de neutralité politique répétées par la bande à « Balance ton Claude ». Une fine équipe, composée de cinq membres, d'après le premier accusateur anonyme sorti du bois

 [

1

]

, et qui n'a pas eu droit à la même attention que Thélyson Orélien.


«

Notre démarche était complètement apolitique

 [

2

]


 »

, déclarait ainsi Samuel Fitoussi dans

Le Point

, après avoir tombé le masque. Pourtant, le profil de nos Claudettes risque d'affoler votre détecteur à

bullshit

. Pas besoin du logiciel Pangram, vous allez voir, pour confondre ces immenses tartufes, présentés comme des «

lanceurs d'alerte

ayant

 l'amour de la vérité chevillé au coeur

et dénonçant les impostures intellectuelles

 [

3

]

 ».


Samuel Fitoussi


Commençons par vous donner une idée de l'honnêteté intellectuelle de M. Fitoussi. Quelques heures après avoir lancé la polémique sur le livre de Thélyson Orélien depuis le compte X « Balance ton Claude » (encore anonyme à ce moment-là), le chroniqueur du

Figaro

 intervient sur Radio J, où il déclare : «

comme aujourd'hui, le RN n'est pas un parti particulièrement violent ou antisémite ou quoi que ce soit, [renvoyer dos à dos les extrêmes] c'est en fait banaliser la dangerosité de cette gauche pro-Hamas...

 »


La journaliste lui fait alors remarquer que l'extrême-droite est quand même «

très proche de l'AfD, un parti néo-nazi

 ». Réponse de Samuel Fitoussi : «

J'ai beaucoup de critiques à l'égard de ces partis. Pour le RN, par exemple, je les trouve étatistes, socialistes, relativement incompétents

 […]

mais je pense qu'il faut reconnaître que les choses ont évolué, que le RN n'est plus le RN d'il y a 30 ans, et c'est même plus le RN d'il y a dix ans, qui voulait sortir de l'Union européenne, et c'est plus le RN antisémite

 [

4

]

 ».

L

'amour de la vérité chevillé au cœur

, on vous dit.


Par ailleurs, l'intérêt de M. Fitoussi pour les implications de l'IA générative n'est pas pure curiosité, étant donné qu'il travaille pour le fonds d'investissement FRST CAPITAL, spécialisé dans l'industrie naissante du

machine learning

(un des domaines informatiques que l'on trouve derrière la formule générique « IA », et dont les avancées ont notamment permis le développement des « grands modèles de langage » – ou

LLM

 – comme le célèbre ChatGPT).


Incidemment, FRST CAPITAL est une ancienne filiale d'OTIUM CAPITAL, la holding de Pierre-Edouard Stérin, milliardaire christo-libertarien qui utilise ses gains pour financer un projet de conquête politique par l'extrême-droite, baptisé « Périclès » (pour Patriotes, Enracinés, Résistants, Identitaires, Chrétiens, Libéraux, Européens, Souverainistes), et doté d'un budget de 150 millions d'euros

 [

5

]

.


Cerise sur le gâteau : FIRST CAPITAL n'investit pas seulement dans les « laboratoires d'IA », mais également dans la fabrique d'opinion, en produisant des sondages douteux sur la popularité d'Elon Musk ou …

title: Terminal Kadıköy’ün reklam ekranı hack’lendi: “Bu bina kent suçudur”
content:
İstanbul'un Kadıköy Söğütlüçeşme’deki Terminal Kadıköy’de bulunan bir reklam ekranı, “BU BİNA KENT SUÇUDUR” yazısıyla hack’lendi. Kent hakkı savunucuları, deprem toplanma alanı ve yeşil alanın alışveriş merkezine (AVM) dönüştürülmesine tepki göstererek kentlerin her alanının kâr maksimizasyonuna göre planlandığını vurguladı.


ETHA’daki habere göre, Söğütlüçeşme Tren İstasyonu’nun viyadük altındaki alanında kurulan Terminal Kadıköy, Nisan 2025’ten bu yana işletiliyor. Açıldığı günden bu yana onlarca dükkânın faaliyet gösterdiği alan, yeni bir tüketim merkezine dönüştü.


Kent hakkı savunucuları, ekoloji örgütleri ve Kadıköylüler, projeye karşı yıllardır itirazlarını sürdürüyor. Haydarpaşa Dayanışması, projeyi “soylulaştırma merkezi” olarak nitelendirerek “Kamusal alanlar ticarileşiyor, bu bir kent suçudur” açıklamasını yapmıştı.


Savunucular, AVM’ye dönüştürülen alanın geçmişte sokakta yaşayan hayvanların kent sakinleri tarafından beslendiği geniş bir yeşil alan olduğunu belirtiyor. Bölgenin yıllarca “izbe bir alan, güvensiz bir yer” olarak tanımlandığını aktaran kent hakkı savunucuları, bu söylemle projeye toplumsal rıza oluşturulmaya çalışıldığını ifade ediyor.


500’den fazla ağaç kesildi


Proje kapsamında bölgede 500’den fazla ağaç kesildi. Kent hakkı savunucuları, Söğütlüçeşme’deki alanın deprem toplanma alanı niteliği taşıdığını ve projenin bu işlevi fiilen ortadan kaldırdığını belirtiyor.


Savunucular, “Hem bir deprem toplanma alanı hem kentsel bir yeşil alanın tümü, bir avuç AVM’ye kurban edildi” diyerek kamusal alanın sermayeye peşkeş çekilmesine tepki göstermişti.


Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı ise proje için “ÇED Gerekli Değildir” kararı vermişti.


Terminal Kadıköy sonrası Kadıköy’de artan yoğunluk ve trafik baskısı


14 Nisan 2026


(EMK)

title: Eisenhower’ın dünya küresi Pentagon'da taşınırken nasıl kırıldı?
content:
Pentagon’un koridorlarından birinde 1930’lardan kalma, çapı 75 santimi geçen bir dünya küresi duruyor. Amerikan ordusu bu küreyi seksen yılı aşkın süredir kuşaktan kuşağa koruyor. Yaygın inanışa göre General Dwight Eisenhower, 1942’de savaş planlarını hazırlarken kürenin başında çalıştı. Yanındaki plakette bunun yalnızca popüler teori olduğu yazıyorsa da efsane plaketten daha güçlü görünüyor.

Bu yılın başında Amerikan Fox News kanalının eski sabah programı sunucusu, bugünün Savunma Bakanı Pete Hegseth küreyi makam odasında görmek istedi. Böyle eserleri normalde ordunun askeri tarih uzmanları taşıyor. Ancak o günlerde hükümet kapanmıştı ve uzmanlar zorunlu izindeydi. Bakanın ekibi beklemedi. Şubat ayında küreyi kendileri kaldırmaya çalıştılar ve düşürdüler. Küre, oyma ahşap ayağının içindeki metal eksenden koptu ve alt tarafında, tam Antarktika’nın üzerinde yarık açıldı.

Olay aylarca gizli kaldı. Washington Post, ekim ayında fotoğraflarla ortaya çıkarınca Pentagon önce kazaların olabileceğini, kimsenin yaralanmadığını ve kürenin tamir edildiğini söyledi. Ardından düşenin replika olduğunu öne sürdü. NBC News ise üç yetkilinin anlatımına ve fotoğrafa dayanarak kırılanın orijinal küre olduğunu doğruladı. Düşürenler için orijinal ya da replika fark etmeyebilir, sonuçta boya ve alçıydı. Oysa bazı eşyalar döneminin bütün hafızasını taşırlar.

Eisenhower o küreyi döndürdüğünde dünya savaştaydı. Washington’da savaş planlarının başındaydı. İki yıl sonra Normandiya çıkarmasını yönetecekti. Savaşın ardından Avrupa’nın ortasına demir perde indi ve dünya iki kampa bölündü.

Türkiye savaşa fiilen girmemişti fakat perdenin tam ucundaydı ve güvenlik kaygısı her şeyin önündeydi. Savaş boyunca tarafsız kalan ülke, barışta kendini yalnız buldu. 1947’de Truman Doktrini’yle Amerikan yardımı geldi, ardından Marshall Planı’nın traktörleri köy yollarına çıktı. Zorlanan Batı kapısını Kore Savaşı açtı. 1950’de Meclise bile danışılmadan Kore’ye gönderilen Türk tugayı, Kunuri’de ve sonrasında ağır kayıplar verdi. Bu bedel Batı’nın Türkiye’ye bakışını değiştirdi. Karara karşı çıkan Barışseverler Cemiyeti üyeleriyse tutuklanıp yargılandı.

Eisenhower o yıllarda yeniden üniforma giymişti. Aralık 1950’de NATO’nun ilk Avrupa başkomutanı oldu ve ittifakın askeri karargahını Paris yakınlarında kurdu. Türkiye 18 Şubat 1952’de onun komutasındaki ittifaka katıldı, Başkomutan Eisenhower üyeliği yerinde mühürlemek için Ankara’ya kadar geldi. Küreyi döndüren el, Türkiye’nin yerini de haritada işaretlemişti.

Eisenhower Ankara’ya ikinci kez 6 Aralık 1959’da, bu kez ABD başkanı olarak geldi. Türkiye’yi görevdeyken ziyaret eden ilk Amerikan başkanıydı. Cumhurbaşkanı Celal Bayar onu Esenboğa’da karşıladı. Eisenhower Anıtkabir’e çelenk bıraktı, ardından Bayar, Başbakan Adnan Menderes ve Dışişleri Bakanı Fatin Rüştü Zorlu ile Çankaya’da görüştü. Ankara Üniversitesi ona fahri doktora verdi, caddeler el sallayan kalabalıklarla doldu. Ertesi sabah Karaçi’ye uçarken Türk halkına olağanüstü karşılama için teşekkür etti.

Ancak ziyaretin ardından yapılan görüşmelerden Türk hükümetinin umduğu büyük ekonomik yardım çıkmadı. Eisenhower’ı uğurlayan liderlerin iktidarı yalnızca beş ay daha sürdü. 27 Mayıs 1960’ta ordu yönetime el koydu, bir yıl sonra Menderes ve Zorlu İmralı’da idam edildi.

Eisenhower ocak 1961’de, görevi devretmeden önce Beyaz Saray’dan Amerikalılara veda konuşmasını yaptı. Normandiya’yı yönetmiş beş yıldızlı general, ülkesini kendi kurduğu makineye karşı uyardı: Devasa ordunun büyük silah sanayisiyle iç içe geçmesi Amerikan tarihinde yeniydi ve oluşan askeri-sanayi kompleksinin haksız nüfuz kazanmasına karşı uyanık olunmalıydı. Yeni gücü dizginleme görevini de uyanık yurttaşlara bıraktı.

Pentagon’daki küre şimdi tamir ediliyor. Kırığı onarılınca yeniden ayağına oturtulacak ve dönebilecek. Ama Antarktika’nın üzerindeki iz, dikkatli bakan gözlerden kaçmayacak.

İttifaklar kuşaklar boyunca, sabırla ve uzmanların eliyle taşınır. Kore’de dökülen kanla, Ankara sokaklarında sallanan ellerle örülür. Eisenhower savaştan sonra bakanlığın adının savaştan savunmaya çevrilmesini desteklemişti, savaşı en iyi bilen general, barışın adını seçmişti. Bugün onun küresini odasına isteyen bakan ise adı yeniden savaş yapmaya çalışıyor.

Pentagon, küre olayını önemsiz olmayan bir haber diye geçiştirdi. Bakan küreyi istedi ama Eisenhower’ın sözlerine hiç kulak vermedi. Türkiyeli biri olarak bu kazayı izlerken aklıma bir soru takılıyor: Ortak tarihin ağırlığını taşıyamayan …

author: David Swanson
title: Canada’s Minister for Artificial Intelligence Defended His Meetings With Israel, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar
content:
By Alex Cosh,

The Maple

, November 2, 2026


Canada’s Minister for Artificial Intelligence Evan Solomon defended his meetings with Israel, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Qatar over the past year during an AI funding announcement in Montreal today.


Solomon and Prime Minister Mark Carney announced an investment of up to $1.6 billion in Canadian AI company Cohere, with Carney stating that the company “will stay Canadian.”


However, Solomon has also held talks regarding AI development and cooperation with a number of foreign states, including some that have weaponized AI to commit war crimes and/or other alleged abuses.


When asked about a meeting he

held

 with Israeli Ambassador Iddo Moed in January, Solomon said: “We have met with many countries around the world. I have been obviously travelling the Middle East extensively.”


“We were in the U.A.E., and we welcomed a delegation. We’ve been in Qatar, we’ve been in Saudi Arabia.”


“I did have a meeting with the Israeli ambassador as we meet with many ambassadors to discuss ongoing issues. That was one of them.”


“We will continue to build out, as we have today, Canadian technology in a safe, appropriate, reliable way.”


Israel has extensively

used

 AI for targeting purposes during its genocide in Gaza and its military operations in the occupied West Bank.


This technology includes “

Lavender

,” which is used to create automated “kill lists,” and “Where’s Daddy?,” a tracking system which alerts Israeli forces to strike when Palestinian men return home to their families.


Solomon

travelled

 to the U.A.E. and Qatar last year, and in the former he signed an agreement to develop “the sharing of technical expertise, support for investment in advanced technology, and collaboration on the development and deployment of safe and responsible AI.”


The U.A.E. faces significant scrutiny over its use of AI, as the Gulf monarchy

has

 previously

deployed

 unlawful hacking and surveillance technologies against political opponents. Qatar has

faced

 scrutiny for similar uses of such technology.


This week, the Carney government signed a number of additional MOUs with the U.A.E.,

including

 on military affairs.


The U.A.E. is widely accused of funding and arming the Rapid Support Forces in Sudan, which has carried out massacres against civilians since April 2023.


In a statement, Rachel Small with the advocacy group World Beyond War said: “The Canadian government’s decision … to sign a Memorandum of Understanding on Defence Cooperation with the U.A.E. is shameful and unjustifiable.”


“The U.A.E. military has played a well documented and horrific role in supporting war crimes in Sudan and Yemen. It’s completely unacceptable for Canada to be rewarding this military with increased cooperation and support instead of holding them to account.”


Solomon visited Saudi Arabia in February. An official statement published by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

said

: “Discussions focused on advancing practical cooperation in AI, digital infrastructure and emerging technologies.”


“Both sides noted the strong fit between Canada’s AI strengths and Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 priorities, including building domestic capability, expanding compute and data systems, and accelerating innovation-driven economic growth.”


Saudi Arabia, in addition to using AI to surveil its own population, has reportedly used American AI-targeting systems to

combat

 the militant group Ansar Allah in Yemen.


Since 2014, Saudi Arabia’s attacks on Yemen have resulted in the deaths of more than 377,000 people.

World BEYOND War

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Activists Destroy Military Equipment at ‘Death Factory Supplying Israel’
content:
Activists opposing Israel’s genocide in Gaza broke into a factory in Tring, Hertfordshire, on Monday morning, before smashing equipment there with hammers. 


Three members of the group People Against Genocide (PAG) were arrested after the break-in at the facility, which is owned by military technology firm Ultra Intelligence & Communications (I&C).


The activists say Ultra I&C is a key supplier of UAV Tactical Systems, which is owned by Israeli weapons firm Elbit Systems. Novara Media contacted Ultra I&C for comment but had not received a reply at the time of publication.


Ultra I&C makes military satellite and cybersecurity technology. Video posted by PAG on social media showed people destroying what appeared to be large parabolic antennas.   


Monday’s break-in was timed to coincide with the 109th anniversary of the Balfour Declaration, a statement issued by the British government in 1917 that is widely seen as laying the foundation for the colonisation and ethnic cleansing of Palestine. 


“Not only did the British government sign away a country that was not theirs to give, they have continued to assist in the Zionist occupation of Palestine, and in the murder of its native population, right up to the present day,” the group said in a statement. “Chief among the other foreign actors actively assisting the genocide is, of course, Britain’s unruly offspring, the US, where Ultra I&C is headquartered.”


It added: “By shutting down the Tring death factory today, and dismantling the weapons inside, our action-takers are aiming to save lives in Palestine, and uphold international law. 


“The Labour governments of both Burnham and Starmer have not only failed to do anything to stop the genocide, abandoning their commitments to international law, and to simple human decency, they have actively assisted the Israeli military with spy flights and arms shipments.”


The group has targeted Ultra I&C on several occasions. During a previous raid on the Tring facility on 9 July, its activists allegedly caused £1.3m of damage. Its members have also staged actions at sites in Cambridge, Aberdeen and Maidenhead this year.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Nobel Peace Laureate Navi Pillay on ICC, Gaza, Rape as War Crime, Her South African Roots & Mandela
content:
We speak with the acclaimed South African human rights lawyer and international jurist Navi Pillay, who was awarded this year’s Nobel Peace Prize. Pillay has been the United Nations high commissioner for human rights and a judge at both the International Criminal Court and at an international tribunal investigating the 1994 genocide in Rwanda. Most recently, she led the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Hours after Pillay was announced as winner of the Nobel Prize, the United States imposed sweeping new sanctions against the International Criminal Court.


“It’s extremely shocking to me, totally unacceptable, that the United States administration can today impose sanctions against the International Criminal Court,” says Pillay, speaking to

Democracy Now!

 from The Hague.


Navi Pillay is now 85 years old. She was born into an Indian Tamil family in apartheid South Africa in 1941. The first woman to start a law practice in Natal, South Africa, in 1967, Pillay began her legal career defending anti-apartheid activists including Nelson Mandela, exposing torture, and helping establish key rights for prisoners on Robben Island. Mandela, as president, later appointed Pillay to the High Court of South Africa, making her the first woman of color on that bench.

title: SOLIDARITY WITH ALL ANTI-WAR PRISONERS IN RUSSIA & DRAFT DODGERS IN UKRAINE
content:
Beneath is the text of the leaflet distributed outside both the Russian and Ukrainian embassies in London by members of the Anarchist Communist Group and the Network of Anarchist Internationalists (NAI) on Saturday October 31st


For the past five years, the warring states of Ukraine and Russia have been sending the working class to die on the battlefields, killing civilians across the war zone and destroying critical infrastructure with missiles and drones. European states are arming Ukraine, helping to keep the war of the trenches going on indefinitely—a war that has already lasted longer than WWI—in order to lay the groundwork for the revitalisation of their declining industry by shifting it more and more toward a war economy. The endless war, financed by loans from Europe and the USA, allows states to carry out their ideological, bureaucratic and technical “defensive” restructuring, as well as the broader restructuring of production, at a time when the US is pulling back from funding the war in the region and the whole planet is beginning to smell of gunpowder. The loans under the Rearm Europe arms program and the record ‘defence’ budgets being pushed by Europe point with certainty toward war austerity, in other words an even harsher exploitation of the working class, as its future wages are put up as collateral for current spending. In 2025, global military spending reached $2.887 trillion, the highest level ever recorded by SIPRI, while Europe increased its military spending by 14% in a single year. European military spending reached an average of 3.2% of GDP, up from 2.8% in 2024.


The Death Camp that is Ukraine, hemmed in on all sides, built jointly by Russia on the one hand and the USA and Europe on the other, plays a key role in spreading militarisation throughout European societies: expanding the arms industry, increasing military spending, intensifying and generalising conscription, recruiting men and, to

some extent, women into the armed forces with the lure of a career, and repressing those who refuse to take part.


Within this process, desertion and draft resistance movements play an important role in undermining the ideology of national unity and the state’s ability to keep mobilising entire populations for war. This is why the widespread draft resistance and desertion in Ukraine and Russia—300,000 deserters and 2,000,000 draft dodgers in the former, and more than 75,000 deserters and 260,000 draft dodgers as early as September 2022 in the latter—is so significant and deserves the support of the antiwar movement. The stories of violence and imprisonment suffered by those resisting mobilization on both sides of the front show what the militarisation of society means

in practice, and what it costs to refuse to fight for the state and the bosses.


In Russia, which has recently entered a phase of silent mass mobilisation, deserters—most of them forcibly recruited through coercion and blackmail—are being summarily executed on the spot by their own commanders (zeroing out). Along the borders of Ukraine, men trapped inside the country by martial law—which prevents them from leaving for safer countries—are trying to cross frozen mountains and rivers to escape

mobilisation. Some freeze to death; others drown. Those forced to remain in the country are left at the mercy of the TRCs, a special military unit that rounds up men from the streets, their workplaces, public transport stops, cafés and outside schools. They are thrown into vans and taken to the front in a practice that has become known

as busification’. Those who physically resist busification or take part in armed resistance inside training centers end up facing crushing prison sentences. When an army lifer is killed in such an incident, the sentence is life imprisonment.


Bogdan Koshel, 27, was drafted in Kyiv in June 2025. After contemplating suicide, he eventually turned his weapon on the military bastards who were training him and was sentenced to life in prison on June 9, 2026, for the deaths of two of them. Twenty three-year-old Oleg Gavrilov and five others arrested under martial law for

“obstructing mobilization” during the July 8, 2026 uprising in a neighborhood of Lviv against a busification operation are being prosecuted for assault against police officers. Twenty-seven-year-old Ukrainian Trotskyist Bogdan Syrotiuk was sentenced to 15 years in prison not for any physical attack or act of resistance, but simply for expressing antiwar …

author: labor4pal
title: Dockworkers Global Strike to Halt Militarization of Ports (Countercurrents)
content:
Dockworkers on this International Day of Action, October 30 objecting to the “militarization” of European and Mediterranean ports today held strikes across the region bringing cargo handling to a halt at 111 ports. Striking workers, activists along with several hundred students shut down the Port of Trieste for more than an hour while rallying on numerous issues. Across Europe 40 other port blockades halted operations as workers protested in France, Greece, the Basque Country, Turkey, and Morocco in North Africa under the rubric “Ports for Peace – Jobs with Dignity.”

The port blockades, described as one of the largest coordinated international strikes in history is intended to send the message that workers refuse to participate in warfare and genocide by disrupting the military logistics networks and to end the use of commercial ports as “instruments of the military machine.” In compliance with the May 2026 Istanbul Declaration published by unions at over 35 European ports, they are demanding “that port facilities not be used to transport weapons destined for war zones nor be transformed into military bases serving NATO, the United States, or the European Union” with a special focus on “the genocide against the Palestinian people and the US-Israeli war of aggression in the Middle East and against Iran.”

In Italy, the grassroots 100,000-member strong Unione Sindacale di Base (USB) along with four other unions organized the general strike and called for all sectors of the country to participate in support of their blocking military shipments to Israel for its genocide in Gaza.

The unions have declared bluntly that “We do not load death. We do not transport bullets, bombs, and missiles so children can be killed. Workers will not pay for the war economy, inflation, armaments, and the profits of the monopolies.” They have also expressed “Full solidarity with the peoples of Cuba, Venezuela and Sudan.”

Other issues to be resolved revolve around worker safety, cargo transparency, decent wages, reduced working hours, fair pension provisions, and a stop to the implementation of the “highly automated port.” This concept is being promoted by internation shipping and container transport companies, which would require fewer union workers in favor of “semi-automated crane systems, driverless transport vehicles and automated container storage planning to increase efficiency and simplify processes.”

The morning blockade at the Port of Trieste saw operations come to a halt as 5,000 people flooded into the main entry point of the normally busy port as a heavy police presence stood nearby. Before departing on a march across the city, the crowd heard from several speakers on a variety of issues, including “housing expenses and soaring rents – increases in energy costs and household utility bills,” along with the inflationary impact of escalating fuel prices. All issues which resonate with working-class people from across Europe and around the world.

Other topics broached by speakers were the continual erosion of public worker’s salaries due to high inflation and increased energy costs and the government’s preference, in claiming that there are no available funds, while spending public funds on “armaments rather than essential services.” Additionally, there were calls for an end to fossil fuels and in ending military propaganda in school curriculum.

To illustrate the issue of misplaced spending the Unione Sindacale Italiana (USI) handed out a broadsheet showing the cost of various military armament and how many new schools and hospitals could be constructed instead, for the equivalent of the billions of Euros being spent by the government. As an example, one Eurofighter jet aircraft could fully fund 25 schools and two hospitals. An obscene misuse of public funds that was reflected in numerous handmade signs carried by protesters.

After rallying, the crowd marched across the city carrying signs along with Palestinian and union flags while chanting loudly and clapping to, “Siamo tutti antifascisti” (we are all anti-fascists) and in calling for an end to the Genocide in Gaza.

title: Pisa: Rivendicazioni della Sapienza Occupata. “Noi la guerra non la paghiamo”
content:
Ripubblichiamo il comunicato del

Collettivo Universitario Autonomo di Pisa

 in merito alle rivendicazioni dell’occupazione avvenuta a conclusione del corteo del 30 ottobre in occasione dello sciopero generale.


Ieri 30 ottobre 2026 siamo scese in piazza per lo sciopero generale chiamato da USB e molti sindacati di base, uno sciopero internazionale contro il carovita e la guerra: più di 100 porti sono stati bloccati per interrompere i flussi della guerra e la sua logistica. Le piazze gremite in tutta Italia hanno detto una cosa molto chiara: noi la guerra non la paghiamo.


Investire sulla guerra è una scelta politica, non solo di questo governo ma di tutta l’oligarchia globale.


La guerra non è solo un’ipotesi futura, la guerra occupa già il nostro presente: la paghiamo con il rincaro dei prezzi al supermercato, sui trasporti, sul carburante, sulle bollette. La paghiamo quando il nostro diritto allo studio viene eroso di giorno in giorno, e quando le nostre università, spolpate di fondi e definanziate, devono convertire la propria ricerca agli interessi delle aziende e dell’industria bellica.


Le tante voci alzatesi in corteo oggi nella nostra città si sono unite nella decisione di occupare il palazzo della Sapienza, sede storica dell’università di Pisa, sempre meno a disposizione dellə studentə e sempre più rifunzionalizzata per essere vetrina dell’istituzione. La Sapienza, però, è anche il luogo dove si sono prodotte nel 1967 le

Tesi

, documento programmatico del movimento studentesco che avrebbe trasformato l’università negli anni successivi. Nelle

Tesi della Sapienza

L’università è di chi ci studia e di chi ci lavora. Chiediamo condizioni dignitose per chi le nostre università le tiene aperte, le pulisce e le vive. V ogliamo ribellarci al futuro che ci viene prospettato fatto di precarietà e di saperi svenduti alla guerra e alla devastazione del territorio. Università e conoscenza sono beni pubblici, di cui dobbiamo prenderci cura. L’università deve essere un luogo accessibile a tuttə, che rispetti il nostro tempo e i nostri bisogni, in cui crescere insieme, costruire un futuro collettivo, dove custodire i saperi e metterli a disposizione di un territorio da tutelare.


Immaginiamo un’università che non sia un’autostrada da percorrere per la propria carriera, ma una piazza dove condividere il nostro desiderio di conoscenza e di trasformazione. In tutto il mondo le persone riempiono le strade e dalle università ai porti tutto si può bloccare: l’occupazione della Sapienza è solo una prima pietra lanciata nella nostra città nella nuova ondata di rabbia e desiderio di riscatto che sta animando tutto il Mediterraneo.


Con questa occupazione vogliamo avanzare pretese rivolte al Governo, al Ministero dell’Università e della Ricerca, all’Università di Pisa e all’Azienda Regionale per il Diritto allo Studio (DSU Toscana).


Al governo – contro la finanziaria di guerra, contro il carovita


Chiediamo:


1. Il reinvestimento in istruzione, ricerca e sanità di tutti i fondi aggiuntivi previsti per la difesa nella nuova legge di bilancio del 2027.


2. Il ripristino del taglio delle accise sui carburanti di 24,4 centesimi complessivi.


3. La modifica del Codice degli appalti, affinché ci sia una progressiva internalizzazione dellə lavoratorə, a partire dalle università.


4. Un aumento di 5 miliardi di euro del Fondo di Finanziamento Universitario.


Al Ministero – contro la privatizzazione degli studentati, contro l’università trattata come fosse


un’azienda

Chiediamo inoltre che vengano resi disponibili gli altri 27 mila posti letto promessi dal PNRR e non ancora realizzati.


2. La modifica dei criteri di premialità nella distribuzione dei finanziamenti all’Università.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: No fue una guerra civil: fue un golpe de Estado contra la República española
content:
Una república legítima.


Lo que nos enseñaron como «guerra civil» empezó como un golpe de Estado contra un régimen legítimo. La República había nacido de las urnas en 1931 y, el 16 de febrero de 1936, el pueblo volvió a elegir un Gobierno del Frente Popular. Los militares que se alzaron el 18 de julio habían jurado lealtad a la República y rompieron su palabra para tomar el poder por la fuerza. Eran militares traidores, y su golpe fue ilegítimo: pretendía quebrar la legalidad y acabar con la democracia.


Un golpe fallido, salvado desde el extranjero.


El golpe fracasó en Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia y buena parte del país, porque el pueblo salió a defender su República. Con la flota republicana vigilando el estrecho de Gibraltar, el Ejército de África no podía cruzar. Fueron los aviones alemanes e italianos los que hicieron posible el traslado de las tropas. El propio Hitler lo reconoció años después: dijo que Franco debería erigir un monumento al Junkers Ju 52. Sin esa ayuda, el golpe no habría podido continuar.


Hitler, Mussolini y las tropas coloniales.


Alemania envió la Legión Cóndor, con aviación, artillería, carros de combate e instructores. Italia envió decenas de miles de soldados, una cifra que, según las estimaciones más altas, rondaría los 100.000 efectivos si se cuentan aviadores, marinos y relevos, además de aviones, submarinos y buques de guerra. Las aviaciones alemana e italiana bombardearon a la población civil: Madrid desde noviembre de 1936, Gernika en abril de 1937 y Barcelona en marzo de 1938. Franco, además, trajo de África entre 60.000 y 80.000 soldados marroquíes, integrados en buena parte en las tropas regulares indígenas, los Regulares, que fueron empleados contra el pueblo español. Sin esa ayuda y sin esas tropas, los sublevados no lo habrían tenido tan fácil para doblegar a un pueblo que defendía su libertad, su democracia y su derecho a decidir.


Una República abandonada.


Francia, el Reino Unido y casi todas las democracias europeas le dieron la espalda a la República mediante la política de No Intervención, que Alemania e Italia violaron a la vista de todos. Churchill, que se negó a estrechar la mano del embajador republicano, encarna bien esa actitud: las élites europeas temían más una República con reformas sociales que a Hitler y Mussolini. La Unión Soviética fue el principal apoyo estatal en el envío de armas, mientras que México también prestó ayuda a la República. A ello se sumaron unos 35.000 voluntarios de las Brigadas Internacionales, llegados de decenas de países para defenderla.


Terror y exterminio.


Los sublevados no querían solo ganar: querían exterminar al adversario político. En Badajoz, en agosto de 1936, las columnas del Ejército de África asesinaron a miles de personas; en Málaga, en febrero de 1937, la población civil que huía por la carretera hacia Almería fue ametrallada desde el mar y desde el aire. En Galicia, donde el golpe triunfó de inmediato, miles de personas fueron asesinadas por ser sindicalistas, alcaldes, maestros o, simplemente, por ser de izquierdas. Las mujeres sufrieron violaciones, torturas y rapados de cabeza, prácticas que el general Queipo de Llano alentó desde la radio.


La Iglesia bendijo el golpe como una «cruzada» y siguió legitimando la dictadura. Franco fue presentado como «Caudillo de España por la gracia de Dios». Hoy, más de cien mil desaparecidos siguen en unas 6.000 fosas, y no hay herida que pueda cerrarse sin verdad ni justicia.


La Transición que no hizo justicia


Después de la dictadura no hubo juicio, ni verdad, ni reparación suficientes. La Transición fue un borrón y cuenta nueva: la Ley de Amnistía de 1977 contribuyó a garantizar la impunidad de los responsables de los crímenes del franquismo. Los franquistas no rindieron cuentas por sus crímenes y muchos de ellos se incorporaron a la política. De Alianza Popular, fundada por antiguos ministros de Franco, surgió el Partido Popular, y de ese espacio político nació Vox.


Décadas de silencio permitieron que las mentiras se repitieran y que la historia se prostituyera. Hoy, un partido como Vox se niega a condenar el golpe y la dictadura; hay quien convierte en héroes a los fascistas y hay jóvenes que levantan el brazo y gritan «¡Viva Franco!». Rajoy dejó a cero la partida presupuestaria destinada a la memoria histórica, y el PP ha gobernado de la mano de Vox en comunidades autónomas y ayuntamientos.


Había que hacer justicia, reparar a las víctimas y contar la verdad …

author: Mitchell Plitnick
title: As US and Israel Plot Iran Escalation, Regional Powers Scramble to Avert It
content:
Saudi, Pakistani, and Turkish leaders met with Iranian officials in Tehran, signaling their reticence to renew the war.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The first of two elections that many believe are the final bell before all out war is resumed against Iran is now complete. Although it seems likely that the efforts to cobble together a governing coalition in Israel, if that is even possible, will take weeks, the American midterms are expected to be the last milestone before the United States and Israel launch a massive attack on Iran.

There is no doubt that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is almost bursting with anticipation of the bloodshed to come. Donald Trump, as always, seems unsure of how to proceed, but seems very uncomfortable with the situation as it stands, while also being unwilling to make the concessions necessary to end this futile, destructive war he started for no good reason.

Iran can do little to deter an American attack, if that is what Trump decides to do. But it can retaliate with devastating consequences, which will be felt by its Gulf Arab neighbors, Israel, and the global economy.

That is why the countries of the newly created Mecca Pact — Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Türkiye — took the dramatic step of meeting Iranian officials in Tehran.

Iran trumpeted the meeting as demonstrating the seriousness with which the Sunni Muslim states take the Islamic Republic, meeting in the Iranian capital rather than in a third country.

Saudi Arabia said the meeting was aimed at mediating between the United States and Iran, but there is no evidence the United States had any part in the planning of this meeting. Indeed, the indications are the opposite; one purpose of the confab was to establish regional dialogue specifically on security matters.

Participants included Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff Field Marshall Asim Munir, Saudi Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Turkish Director of National Intelligence Ibrahim Kalin. They met with Iran’s Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei.

The fact that the meeting included leaders of the countries’ respective militaries indicates that the description of the meeting — that it was to deal with regional security — is likely accurate.

And, while little has been made public about the substance of the meeting, it also seems fair to say that there was little progress that could have been made on the major issues—the war with U.S. and the ongoing battles between Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni Ansar Allah.

Regarding Ansar Allah, Saudi Arabia was feeling Iran out to see if they would intervene with the Yemeni fighters whom the Saudis have been unable to defeat.

But Iran doesn’t have much reason to do so. While they could benefit from pulling the Saudis away from the American war effort, the compromises Tehran would have to make are far too great.

Reports out of Israel state that the Saudis offered Ansar Allah $1 billion for a ceasefire. But the Yemeni group will not budge on its understandable demand that Saudi Arabia drop its air blockade of Yemen.

This is not an issue Iran can try to mediate. If they try to get Ansar Allah to compromise on the air blockade, it undermines their argument that the United States must end its sea blockade of Iran.

Iran supports Ansar Allah’s cause, but if they thought they could get concessions from the Saudis on the kingdom’s support for American military efforts, Ansar Allah might find it reasonable to agree to a temporary ceasefire to help their ally.

But they cannot compromise on the air blockade, nor would Iran want them to. As long as Saudi Arabia maintains its efforts to block air traffic in Yemen, they can’t buy their way out of Ansar Allah attacks.

On the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, the Saudis are very worried, as are all the countries of the Gulf and their neighbors. They should be, given that Trump has warned the Gulf states to get ready for a “short, intense military campaign.” Considering that the war started on February 27 was supposed to end in just a few days, or weeks at most, no one is counting on the “short” part. But it is likely to be intense, and that intensity will be felt in Iran and the Gulf Arab states.

The problem for Iran is that its interlocutors can do little to turn Trump’s mind. Even Saudi Arabia, which is in a terrible position …

author: webadmin
title: No Land, No Hunting
content:
Thank you to West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs for this guest article.


On Thursday 8th October, West Midlands Hunt Sabs (WMHS) held a protest outside The Bower House in Shipston on Stour. The restaurant is owned by Andrew Stephen Bower Knight, who continually allows, not only the Warwickshire Hunt to illegally hunt foxes on his land at Compton Scorpion, but the North Cotswold Hunt too.


The protest caused quite a stir amongst the pro-hunt community prompting the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) to publish a social media post stating

“Rural businesses are under attack by urban saboteurs.”


Visitors to The Bower House in Shipston on Stour were made aware that business owner, Andrew Stephen Bower Knight, enables illegal fox hunting.


The campaign against the Warwickshire Hunt is one that spans back years and is steeped in controversy, including the fact that Warwickshire Police entered into a “secret deal” with the hunt when they withdrew the Community Protection Notice that they had been issued.


WMHS have always highlighted the importance of holding landowners to account, something which featured heavily in the campaign against the now defunct Atherstone Hunt. The Hunting Act stipulates that should a landowner allow the hunting of a wild mammal with dogs on their land then they are breaking the law.


Demonstrations took place outside businesses that supported the now defunct Atherstone Hunt.

© West Midlands Hunt Sabs


Section 3.1 of the Hunting Act 2004 states;

“A person commits an offence if he knowingly permits land which belongs to him to be entered or used in the course of the commission of an offence under Section 1.”

Section 1 of the Hunting Act states;

“A person commits an offence if he hunts a wild mammal with a dog.”


“Trail” hunting does not exist, a fact which was openly discussed during a 2020

webinar

 held by the then Hunting Office, now the BHSA. It was the hunting community who coined the term “smokescreen” to describe “trail” hunting, as they discussed ways that hunts could continue to break the law. Now they are acting the victim, especially when landowners are reminded of their part in this pantomime.


WMHS work alongside other anti-hunt groups such as Locals Against the Warwickshire Hunt and Warwickshire Hunt Watch to use a varied approach to their campaigning. One of which is writing to landowners to remind them of their responsibilities and to inform them of what the Warwickshire Hunt are capable of.


As well as detailing the contents of the Hunting Act, the letters remind landowners that only last year, Ben Halsall of the Warwickshire Hunt was convicted under the Hunting Act after a fox was killed. The letter also states that the presiding judge at the trial made a statement that there was

“no evidence at all of any trail being laid.”


In 2023 this fox was killed by the Warwickshire Hunt, on land owned by Marcus Dill of Idlicote House Estate. Hunt member Ben Field was found guilty; however, no charges were brought against Marcus.


The letter goes on to say that

“The new huntsman, Jack Weedon has previously been caught on camera blocking an active badger sett in a Site of Special Scientific Interest and has recently been cautioned under a Section 4a Public Order offence.”


The protest held on 8th October took place during a book signing event by Dame Prue Leith. The aim; to make people aware of the fact that the business, through its owner, is linked to illegal fox hunting. However, the pro-hunt community have tried to claim that by protesting, sabs are putting people’s livelihoods at risk, rather than focusing on the fact that the only person putting any livelihood at risk is Andrew, by continuing to break the law and enable an illegal fox hunt.


If people choose to not use an establishment or support a business because they facilitate fox hunting, that’s their prerogative.


The Warwickshire Hunt have already lost a lot of land, some of which is through landowners rescinding their permission due to public outcry. In October 2025 Warwickshire Christmas Tree Farm very publicly withdrew permission for the hunt to use their land, stating that due to the public’s disgust at their affiliation with the Warwickshire Hunt they were left with no choice.


Warwickshire Christmas Tree Farm publicly withdrew permission for the Warwickshire Hunt to use their land.


This has a knock-on effect as more and more landowners begin to feel empowered to stand up to the hunt and this has …

title: Elisée Reclus - The Vivisection of China
content:
Author

: Elisée Reclus

Title

: The Vivisection of China

Date

: 1898

Notes

: From the September 1898 issue of The Atlantic

Source

: Retrieved on October 22, 2026 from an archived copy of https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/1898/09/the-vivisection-of-china/636369/


 THE great events which are creating such an excitement in the West Indies over the last shreds of the ancient colonial empire of Spain will undoubtedly have consequences of extreme importance, and become, in the fullest sense of the term, a part of history. But, however intense their interest, and however marked the change which they are certain to occasion in the equilibrium of the world, they remain altogether inferior in real significance to the revolutions which are taking place in the Far East.


 War of some sort between America and Spain on the subject of Cuba had long been unavoidable. No less than a century ago, — at the time when France lost her plantations in San Domingo, and the republic of Hayti was born, — it was easy to foresee the rupture of the ties which had bound to the Spain of Cortez and Pizarro the insular fragments of the great hemisphere appropriated by Pope Alexander VI. The various colonies were sure to break away, one by one, from their metropolitan stepmother, set up for themselves, and live their own life. Cuba and Porto Rico, sucked into the whirlpool of war, are but accomplishing their “manifest destiny,” and fulfilling the prophecies repeatedly uttered by the historians of the last generation but one.


 The progress of events in the eastern portion of the Asian continent had by no means been so fully anticipated. One might certainly have ventured to predict that there, also, populations long crushed by civil and military oppression would one day lay claim to the rights of free men; but it could never have been foreseen under what amazingly dramatic conditions the claim would be asserted. Our ancestors, at the beginning of the nineteenth century, would never have harbored, in their wildest dreams, the fantastic notion that Japan, the empire of the Rising Sun, would spontaneously transform itself into a “European power;” European, at least, if not in language, history, and traditions, in the complete recasting of its administration, institutions, customs, and theories, in its devotion to science, and in its entire and unreserved acceptance of a policy based on observation and experience.


 This is the great event of the century, — one which casts into the shade all the other occurrences of an epoch which has nevertheless been rich in memorable events. And it will be no solitary

avatar;

 there are unmistakable signs that other transformations of the same character are about to take place in the vast empire of China, and in all those countries where inhabitants of different race, yellow, red, or black, are brought into close contact with the men of our own Aryano - Greco - Latin civilization. So vanishes that oft-repeated assertion of the ethnologists, that

race

 is a final and irreducible fact, and that no possible progress in the perception of scientific or moral truths can ever prevail against it. It is from this point of view that the recent history of the Far East presents phenomena to which it behooves us to devote our most serious attention.


 There are those, of course, who tell us that all these events are illusory; that the prodigious changes which have taken place in the Japanese world are a lying phantasmagoria and a vain show; that the national mind and character have undergone no real modification; and that the Japanese are sure to escape, sooner or later, from the sphere of European attraction. We hear them compared to savages, who, having learned in the schools of London or Paris the customs of civilization, make haste, as soon as they get back to their forests and savannas, to cast aside their conventional garments, and array themselves in the toggery consecrated by ancestral instinct and hereditary custom.


 Such assertions appear to us to rest on a complete misconception of indisputable facts. The Japanese have most certainly entered into that realm of civilization on which Bacon and Darwin have set their seal; for if imperial caprice and the spread of bourgeois fashions have power to alter the external aspect of a nation, such influences can have but little effect on its underlying moral sense, its religious beliefs, its educational theories, and the essential principle of its …

author: Benji
title: Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies
content:
Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies

Tiere leiden vor dem Schlachten Höllenqualen bei CO₂-Betäubung

ARIWA veröffentlicht jetzt erstmals umfangreiche Aufnahmen aus einem Schlachthof von Tönnies. Schlachthöfe gehören zu den schwierigsten Herausforderungen für Undercover-Aufnahmen, da sie extrem gut gesichert sind. Die Betreiber setzen alles daran, dass das, was dort geschieht, nicht an die Öffentlichkeit gelangt.


19.10.2026, Deutschland


 NDR berichtet mit Videomaterial von ARIWA.


Er ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie: Tönnies. Als Marktführer produziert er 30 Prozent des gesamten deutschen Schweinefleischs. Allein 2023 meldete der Konzern einen Jahresumsatz von über 7 Milliarden Euro. Dafür tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen


Schweine. 


Das uns vorliegende Material zeigt, wie Mitarbeiter*innen die Tiere beim Zutrieb schlagen und sie unter automatischen Toren eingeklemmt werden. Es zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf in der CO₂-Anlage mit Tieren, die in Gondeln vor Angst schreien und versuchen zu fliehen. Und es zeigt zahlreiche Verstöße gegen die gesetzlichen Vorschriften vor und während der Schlachtung.


Von der Ankunft bis zum Tod:

Erste Undercover-Aufnahmen aus Tönnies Schlachthof


Das vorliegende Material dokumentiert erstmals unabhängig den gesamten Ablauf der Schlachtung von der Ankunft der Tiere im Schlachthof bis zur Tötung. Die Aufnahmen zeigen, wie leidvoll die letzten Stunden im Leben der Tiere sind. Das liegt auch an einer Maschine im Schlachthof, die grausamer nicht sein könnte: Die sogenannte CO₂-Betäubungsanlage.


Die Betäubung vor dem Schlachten ist gesetzlich vorgeschrieben. Die Tiere sollen so vor Schmerzen und Stress geschützt werden. Auch zur Betäubung selbst gibt es eindeutige Vorgaben: Paragraf 12 der Tierschutz-Schlachtverordnung legt fest, dass Tiere “schnell und unter Vermeidung von Schmerzen oder Leiden in einen (…) Zustand der Wahrnehmungs- und Empfindungslosigkeit” versetzt werden müssen. Der Betäubungsvorgang darf also keine Schmerzen oder Leid auslösen und muss bis zum Tod des Tieres anhalten. Doch die Aufnahmen zeigen eindeutig, dass die Betäubung mit CO₂ gegen diese Vorschrift verstößt!


Ankunft im Schlachthof


Am frühen Morgen kommen die ersten LKWs auf dem Schlachthof an. An den aufgenommenen Tagen werden mindestens fünftausend Schweine pro Tag hier angeliefert und getötet. Tönnies verfügt über ein riesiges Netz von Zulieferbetrieben in ganz Deutschland.


Nach ihrer Ankunft werden die Tiere in enge Wartebuchten gebracht. Hier läuft sanfte Musik, sie soll die Tiere entspannen. Es wirkt makaber. Neunzig Minuten lang sollen sich die vom Transport und Ausladen gestressten Schweine hier beruhigen, dabei ist zu erkennen, wie ängstlich sie sind.


Doch das wahre Grauen kommt erst noch. Nach anderthalb Stunden öffnet sich ein Tor. Ein Mitarbeiter beginnt, die Tiere in einen Treibgang zu scheuchen. Dabei kommt Gewalt zum Einsatz: Wenn die Schweine panisch versuchen zu fliehen, schlägt der Mitarbeiter mit der Treibstange zu, auch ins Gesicht. Die Schweine werden nach und nach in Sechsergruppen aufgeteilt. Als nächstes geht es für sie in die Betäubungsanlage.


Per Gondel in den Erstickungskampf


Die Schweine sind jetzt in einem engen Abteil, aus dem es kein Zurück gibt. Ein Mitarbeiter treibt die Gruppen nacheinander in die Gondelkäfige, mit denen es in wenigen Augenblicken gut 9 Meter nach unten in eine mit CO₂ gefüllte Grube geht. Manche Tiere werden von den schweren hydraulischen Trenngittern eingeklemmt und können sich nicht alleine befreien. Sie schreien vor Schmerz.


Sobald die erste Gruppe von Schweinen in ihre Gondel getrieben wurde, schließt sich der Käfig aus dicken Metallstangen. Kurze Zeit später setzt sich die Gondel in Bewegung. Die versteckte Kamera fährt mit. Innerhalb weniger Sekunden reagieren viele Schweine mit Panik. Viele schreien, schnappen nach Luft, werfen sich gegen die Gitterstäbe und steigen aufeinander. Die Fluchtversuche können so heftig sein, dass manche Tiere sich verletzen und Blutspuren an der Anlage zurücklassen.


Je tiefer die Tiere in den Schacht fahren, desto heftiger werden ihre Fluchtversuche. Die CO₂-Konzentration beträgt nach wenigen Metern schon 80 Prozent. Zeitgleich wird oben die nächste Gruppe in die Gondeln getrieben. Sie können die Angstschreie ihrer Artgenossen aus den Gondeln unter ihnen hören.
