title: Stevens Endorsed Rogers Right After He Touted His Support of Abortion Bans
content:
Mike Rogers once co-sponsored a federal bill that would ban abortions from the point of conception.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Rep. Haley Stevens’s (D-Michigan) surprise endorsement of Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers for Senate over Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday came amid renewed attention on Rogers’s anti-abortion views after he bragged about his stance in an appearance on a conservative radio show last week.

Last Thursday, as the Detroit Metro Times noted, Rogers touted his stances against abortion and trans rights.

“Is it safe to say that we don’t have to worry about you joining Democrats when it comes to things like … supporting gender mutilation surgery for minors, abortion through all nine months of pregnancy for any reason whatsoever?” Dutko said, overexaggerating stances on both issues. “Can we feel confident as evangelical Christians that you’re going to be on our side on some of these social issues?”

“You don’t even have to think about it twice. I’ve been very open about all of those issues — including, for the time I was in Congress, having a 100 percent pro-life rating. I am actually the guy who will stop trangender mutilation of our kids with these trangender surgeries,” Rogers said.

Rogers said the members of his family “are all conservative Christians. This is the only way that I know how to be.”

The clip was posted by Democrats and El-Sayed, who criticized the stance and highlighted Rogers’s history of backing extreme anti-abortion legislation.

“A vote for Mike Rogers is a vote for a national abortion ban,” said El-Sayed in a post on social media.

As Reproductive Freedom for All pointed out on Sunday, Rogers voted for a national abortion ban that would prohibit abortions past 20 weeks as a House member in 2013, and has even cosponsored radically dangerous bills to ban all abortions from the point of conception. Additionally, Rogers said in 2010 that he thinks abortion “should be legal only to prevent the death of the mother” — meaning that he doesn’t support exclusions for rape, incest, or when continuing pregnancy could harm the pregnant person or the fetus.

Rogers’s campaign responded to those posting about the clip by saying that he’s against a national ban. In a post on social media on Saturday, he highlighted a clip in which he said that “Michigan voters have already decided the issue, and I respect that decision” and that he “won’t do anything to change it.”

Abortion rights advocates were skeptical. “Nothing can erase Mike Rogers’ votes or make him any less dangerous to our reproductive freedom,” said Reproductive Freedom for All President and CEO Mini Timmaraju in a statement after Stevens’s announcement on Sunday.

Timmaraju also condemned Stevens for backing Rogers. “Haley Stevens is giving cover to a politician who spent his career trying to ban abortion and was still bragging about that record just days ago,” Timmaraju said.

Stevens has previously touted her support for abortion rights, including during her primary campaign this year. In a speech on the House floor in 2023, she pledged to the women of her state that she would “return to the House of Representatives and seek to enshrine your rights into law” and combat the overturn of Roe v. Wade. “I will not stop until we enshrine women’s rights into the law of this land,” she said.

On the campaign trail for her House seat in 2022, Stevens had suggested that her opponent, incumbent Rep. Andy Levin, was not as committed to abortion rights as she was because he is a man.

On Sunday, however, Levin pointed out that Stevens’s view on abortion was compromised by conservative super PACs that were backing her campaign at the time. Stevens’s ascendancy that year was buoyed by a $5.4 million injection into her campaign by the pro-Israel lobby, including AIPAC, which wanted Levin ousted over his criticism of Israel’s occupation of Palestine.

That year was “the summer of the Dobbs decision, and ultimately voters placed their trust in a ‘pro-choice’ woman who promised to protect their reproductive freedoms,” wrote Levin in a thread on X. “Our campaign pointed out time and again how Democrats should not welcome outsized spending by Super PACS that support anti-choice, MAGA insurrectionists into our primaries, and today we see the logical conclusion of those alliances.”

Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Michigan, has long been a vocal ally to transgender people. In the 2026 midterms, he has not wavered in that support, despite the hundreds of millions of dollars in attack ads, much of which has been focused on transgender people, that have poured into this year’s elections from the Republican Party and, even at times, from the Democratic Party as well. Rather than capitulate to those ads, as some Democrats have done, El-Sayed has defended transgender people outright, on sports, on education and on health care. That was certainly true in his 60 Minutes interview released Sunday, in which Ross Douthat, the conservative columnist Bari Weiss brought to the program this summer, pressed him multiple times on his support for transgender people.

Douthat, the interviewer, started with a question as to whether El-Sayed’s faith puts him in conflict with “a very socially liberal and culturally liberal party,” listing “abortion, same-sex marriage, transgenderism [sic]” as issues on which “a lot of Muslims, like a lot of Christians,” hold conservative positions. Notably, “transgenderism” is a far-right term used to frame transgender people as an ideology rather than a class of people. In doing so, those who use it seek to paint transgender people’s existence as a matter of faith or belief rather than a fundamental characteristic of a person. In its most extreme form, the claim is that gender itself does not exist.

El-Sayed then rejected the premise that his faith puts him in conflict with the values of a secular liberal society, pointing instead to the importance of standing for all people’s rights: “I believe in rights. And even though somebody might use rights that you don’t understand, you never mean to use yourself, you still got to show up and fight for those rights. And that’s the thing about this moment. I think it is a responsibility for us to stand up against the risk of government making incursions on any of our rights, to build the kind of continuum, the kind of coalition where any of us and all of us who have our rights at risk are standing up and fighting for all of our rights. And I think this is an important responsibility. So in conversations with folks in the Muslim community, conversations with folks in the LGBTQ community, the point I always make is to say, listen, I don’t care whether or not you will ever use a right that you were fighting for, understand that a failure to show up and fight for that right is a failure to show up and fight for your own.”

Douthat attempted to pin El-Sayed down on transgender people, asking: “What about the rights of parents to control over their children’s education? Because a lot of places where there’s tension between Islam and Muslim voters and what I’m calling cultural liberalism are around issues like what is taught in school, what happens with transgender kids on sports teams, and so on, right? Like these are places where rights are in conflict, right? What do you think happens there?”

El-Sayed forcefully rejected it, pointing out that it is unrealistic to expect that kids will not learn about transgender people in the age of the internet: “The notion somehow that you are going to prevent your child from being exposed to something that you may find disagreeable, and that that is going to be because of school, is so profoundly outdated, because of course you have all the information and they have all the information. So here’s the thing about it. I think it’s really important for us to recognize that the free flow of information is actually a beautiful thing. It’s really important, and the most important thing you can do is not try to protect a person from seeing a thing. It’s about trying to make sure that as you coach your kid through the world, that you are engaging with them and saying, here’s what I believe, here’s what you may see in the world, you get to make your choices about who you’re going to be in the world.”

author: Leanne Sanders
title: First Nations in B.C., environmental group call out foreign investment in liquid natural gas
content:
An announcement by the Mitsubishi Corporation (MC) Monday, which says it will partner with Blackstone Credit & Insurance in its liquefaction infrastructure holding company for the LNG Canada project in British Columbia, isn’t sitting well with some First Nations and environmental groups.

The transaction is valued at approximately US$1.6 billion.

“By investing billions in LNG Canada through American private equity funds, four of Canada’s largest pension funds have ignored their core obligations to their contributors and beneficiaries,” said Shift Action for Pension Wealth and Planet Health. The charitable organization works to protect pensions and the climate by bringing together beneficiaries and their pension funds to engage on the climate crisis.

“These pension funds are gambling their own members’ retirement savings on a high-risk, highly-polluting LNG facility that’s harming local residents and contributing to catastrophic climate change,” a news release from the group said.

On Monday, an investor consortium led by Blackstone, in partnership with the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB), Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System (OMERS), Investment Management Corporation of Ontario (IMCO) and Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP), announced that it would invest billions to acquire a 49.9% stake in a Mitsubishi Corporation (MC) subsidiary that holds MC’s stake in LNG Canada – a giant liquefied natural gas (LNG) export terminal near Kitimat, British Columbia (BC).

Shift said the LNG industry is “already propped up by generous public subsidies and tax shields in Canada, (and) is now relying on billions of dollars invested from Canadian workers and their retirement savings” to support the project.

The group said LNG Canada is a “high-carbon project that has been plagued by severe and ongoing operating issues. It is estimated that LNG Canada flared more gas in 2025 than any other facility in the world.”

Natural gas flaring is the controlled burning of waste or excess natural gas through a flare stack or boom at oil and gas extraction sites, refineries, and processing plants.

Among the environmental affects, it produces black carbon particles that settle on ice and snow, accelerating Arctic melt and regional warming.

The group also stated that New York-based Blackstone Inc has likely expanded its ownership into LNG Canada, and already holds existing ownership in Ksi Lisims LNG, Canada’s two largest liquefied natural gas projects.

Ksi Lisims LNG is a proposed floating natural gas liquefaction production, storage, and offloading facility with a marine terminal located on the north coast of British Columbia. Prime Minister Mark Carney referred Ksi Lisims LNG to the Major Projects Office on Nov. 13, 2025.

The project referral also includes the 800-kilometre Prince Rupert Gas Transmission Project to supply feed gas for liquefaction, and a 95-kilometre electrical transmission line to supply electricity to the facility.

“As Indigenous Peoples, we follow our LAW to protect Land, Air, Water, all humans depend on these. These projects destroy our law – yet our pension funds are choosing to ignore our laws and our rights when investing in LNG Canada,” said Chief Na’Moks, Hereditary Chief of the Tsayu (Beaver Clan) of the Wet’suwet’en Nation.

“Just last month, I spoke to the CPP executives about the lack of consent for major parts of this project, and they heard overwhelmingly from other pension members and beneficiaries that we do not want our hard-earned dollars to be invested in oil and gas projects that are destroying our climate,” Chief Na’Moks said.

“Why are they choosing to ignore Indigenous leaders and a clear chorus of voices who are opposed to this move. Why would we allow this?”

On October 6, Indigenous leaders and health and environmental groups also hold a news conference on Parliament Hill to announce a challenge over Export Development Canada’s financing of maritime liquefied natural gas (LNG) infrastructure.

In April 2026, it was revealed that LNG Canada has been excessively flaring up to an average of 40 times more gas than its permits allow and continues to experience ongoing operational issues due to a defect in the main flare stack.

The groups also emphasize that LNG Canada’s expansion modules will be built in China, and Ksi Lisims LNG’s modules by Samsung Heavy Industries in South Korea, and claim both projects’ primary economic benefits will not remain in Canada.

author: Jen Fifield
title: Voting Rights Experts Are Monitoring These 5 Issues as the Midterms Unfold
content:
Courts have thwarted most of the administration’s plans to assert federal control, but Trump has kept up the pressure.

Courts have thwarted most of the administration’s plans to assert federal control, but Trump has kept up the pressure.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

As Americans head to the polls on Tuesday, voting experts are watching to see how the Trump administration’s unprecedented efforts to assert more federal control over elections will play out.

Since President Donald Trump retook the White House, his administration has tried to force states to turn over their unredacted voter rolls and to restrict mail-in voting. The Department of Homeland Security has used its resources to identify and prosecute noncitizen voters, an effort that has unfolded alongside the agency’s massive crackdown on immigrants.

The president has justified these steps by claiming, without evidence, that American elections are beset by fraud and that illegal voting is tipping the scales in favor of Democrats.

Courts have thwarted most of the administration’s plans to date, but Trump and his top deputies have kept up the pressure. Most recently, they’ve threatened to prosecute election officials who don’t reject ballots from people that the federal government has identified as likely noncitizens.

The administration hasn’t explicitly ruled out sending federal agents to the polls or seizing ballots or voting machines.

Election experts say the cumulative effect has been to ramp up anxiety about the midterms and to erode voters’ trust in the system.

“The administration has been creating a lot of noise, a lot of confusion, a lot of doubt,” said Ben Hovland, whom Trump fired as a commissioner for the bipartisan Election Assistance Commission earlier this year. He said he worries that this will make voters “sit it out” and “throw their hands up.”

In an emailed response to questions, a DHS spokesperson said Immigration and Customs Enforcement “is not planning operations targeting polling locations,” adding that the agency would only arrest people at the polls to address a safety threat as part of “intelligence-driven targeted enforcement.”

The DHS and the Justice Department “are laser focused on identifying, prosecuting and removing aliens who vote and dilute the votes of U.S. citizens,” the spokesperson added. “Our message to aliens who vote in American elections is clear: we will find you, arrest you, and you will face the consequences — including criminal charges and deportation.”

Before and on Election Day, it’s typical for the major political parties to mount poll-watching operations, but both Democrats and Republicans say they’ve expanded these activities in this pressurized midterm.

Republicans will focus on issues such as voter eligibility and voter-roll accuracy, according to Ally Triolo, the Republican National Committee’s election integrity communications director. Democrats will concentrate on voter intimidation and other hurdles to voting, Angelo Fernández Hernández, a Democratic National Committee spokesperson, said.

Here are five issues that voting rights experts say they’re watching as this year’s election unfolds:

An incident in Leon County, in the Florida Panhandle, illustrates the widespread anxiety about law enforcement at the polls.

Mark Earley, the county’s supervisor of elections, told ProPublica he was “furious” when two marked U.S. Customs and Border Protection vehicles parked outside the county’s busiest early voting location last month, after he’d been repeatedly reassured by the administration that agents would not do this.

He reported the sighting to the FBI, then learned that the agents, who were headed out of state, had just stopped by to try to vote themselves. The episode generated a flurry of news coverage.

“Given the negative media coverage regarding federal agents at the polls, it shows pretty bad judgment that they showed up in their official vehicles,” Earley said.

It’s against the law for federal law enforcement to be near polling places.

Nick Brown, Washington’s attorney general, leads a group of Democratic state officials and voting rights advocates who have been planning how to respond if, indeed, there is real federal interference. The group has “war-gamed” how to react if government agents attempt to commandeer voting equipment or ballots.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: NHS Claims Palantir’s Tech Helps Hospitals That Are Not Even Using It
content:
The NHS claimed dozens of hospitals had benefited from a platform built by spytech firm Palantir despite the hospitals not even using it, an investigation has found.  


Medical charity Medact revealed that 29 NHS Trusts supposedly “realising benefits” from the AI-powered federated data platform (FDP) have either said the system is not live or that they are not using any of its applications.


The revelations, based on freedom of information requests, add weight to widespread calls for Andy Burnham’s government to cancel the NHS’s £330m deal with the US firm. 


Those calls are based on fears that patient data could be misused by Palantir, which has worked closely with Israel’s military amid its genocide in Gaza and also sells its services to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).


Labour MP Chi Onwurah, who chairs the parliamentary science and technology committee, said the government should exercise a 2027 break clause in the NHS contract. 


“If many NHS trusts don’t see the value of the FDP, serious questions need to be asked about whether the hype surrounding Palantir’s products matches reality,” she

told the Guardian

. 


Analysis by the think tank Health Foundation

found in July

 that a patient discharge tool from Palantir made “no meaningful difference” in discharge delays despite claims by NHS England to the contrary. 


In response to public

pressure to exclude Palantir

 from UK government contracts, the company has ramped up lobbying efforts. In September, it appointed former Labour deputy leader Tom Watson as a senior vice president, and he has since said that

“mob rule”

 should not dictate how public contracts are awarded.


Last month,

Novara Media revealed

 that Palantir has sent “intimidating” letters to British MPs who have criticised the company. 


Former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn was among those to receive a letter from Palantir’s UK CEO Louis Mosley, who is the grandson of deceased fascist leader Oswald Mosley. 


“Their tactics of intimidation will not work and they will not shut me up,” Corbyn said.  


A spokesperson told the Guardian that Palantir’s software “is helping to deliver better care” including more operation and lower discharge delays.

title: Fatma Ünsal Bostan: Security Council's role draws criticism
content:
The current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process aimed at resolving the Kurdish question, the linking of legislation passed by Parliament to decisions of the National Security Council, and the social and political dimensions of the process continue to be debated. Corruption and investment fund investigations, parliamentary disputes, match-fixing investigations and interventions against municipalities have also become major issues on Turkey's political agenda.


Political scientist Fatma Bostan Ünsal spoke to ANF about how different sections of society perceive the process, the prominent role given to the National Security Council and the impact of political developments on efforts to achieve peace.


‘Different sections of society perceive the process differently’


Fatma Bostan Ünsal pointed out that different sections of society define the Peace and Democratic Society Process in different ways, contributing to a lack of trust. 


Fatma Bostan Ünsal said: "We can see that different sections of society in Turkey perceive this process very differently, from its name to its content. One section, to which I belong and which unfortunately does not constitute the majority of society, calls it the 'Peace and Democratic Society Process' and expects corresponding changes in legislation and practice. However, a larger section, which is in power and therefore has the ability to introduce certain legislative and practical changes, calls the process 'Terror-Free Turkey'. This section approaches the issue within a security framework and appears prepared to make only very limited changes.


Alongside these two groups, another significant section of society is following the process while feeling that it is among those most directly affected by the country's increasing departure from democracy. This section does not trust political actors. Although more than two years have passed since the process began, it can be said that no policy has been pursued to bring these different perceptions and expectations closer together.


The recent division of the main opposition party through judicial intervention, alongside the perception that judicial interventions against municipalities are politically motivated, has fuelled widespread distrust towards the process."


‘The National Security Council's role on 28 February evokes negative associations’


Fatma Ünsal stated that the government's decision to give the National Security Council a prominent role in the process had created problems of trust within society and politics. Ünsal said: "The government is presenting the National Security Council as the principal institution in the process, in line with its understanding of the process as 'Terror-Free Turkey'. The National Security Council does not evoke particularly positive associations, especially because of its role in the 28 February process, when 'reactionism' was identified as the primary threat in the national security policy document known as the Red Book, and its involvement in the 'postmodern coup' that resulted in the fall of the then REFAH-YOL coalition government. The Council's prominent role in the current process is also being criticised because it has very limited channels for communicating directly with society."


‘The investment fund crisis could force the government towards transparency’


Fatma Ünsal also drew attention to the crisis caused by the investment fund fraud scandal within circles close to the government. She said that public pressure could force the authorities to become more transparent. 


Ünsal said: "The fact that both the perpetrators and victims of the investment fund fraud, involving billions of lira, largely come from circles close to the government has created a political crisis. The government, which has repeatedly managed to avoid transparency in the past, has been unable to close the matter because of public pressure surrounding the investment fund crisis. Hundreds of thousands of people close to the Justice and Development Party (AKP), many of whom belong to networks connected to government circles, remain outraged. They believed they would earn high returns through people they trusted, but their savings have largely disappeared because of negligence and abuses by those responsible.


The opposition's existing demand for transparency could now gain strength through the support of governing party voters, even if not its politicians, and could force the government towards greater …

title: Peace Mothers arrive in Ankara
content:
Members of the Peace Mothers’ Assembly, who set out from 24 cities demanding that Abdullah Öcalan’s physical freedom be secured, that prisoners be released, and that concrete steps be taken as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, have arrived in Ankara.


The mothers gathered at the headquarters of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) in Balgat.


The Peace Mothers will make a statement at Parliament Park to publicize their demands, then hold a tent vigil at Kurtuluş Park.


Buses from Istanbul, Izmir, Van and Amed


The Istanbul Peace Mothers’ Assembly traveled to Ankara by bus last night. 


Members of the Izmir Peace Mothers’ Assembly held a press conference last night at the Izmir provincial headquarters of the Democratic Regions Party (DBP), where they had gathered before setting off for Ankara. During the statement, slogans were repeatedly chanted, including “There can be no life without the Leader,” “Long live Leader Apo,” and “Woman, life, freedom.”


Speaking on behalf of the group, Peace Mother Behiye Yalçın recalled that the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began with Öcalan’s 27 February call, had been underway for two years.


Behiye Yalçın said: “There are certain deadlocks. Peace Mothers from Turkey and Kurdistan have been turning toward Ankara since early this morning. We will set off for Ankara shortly. Tomorrow, we will all come together and begin our Peace Vigil. It is not possible for the process to move forward in a healthy way through unilateral steps alone. If there is a prospect of peace, the state must also take responsibility and take action.


At this point in the process, only Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish people are responding in practice, and this cannot continue like this. We are calling on Turkish mothers to extend a hand toward peace. Come and welcome us tomorrow morning, and let us struggle together for peace.”


Mothers who gathered in Van and Amed also set off for Ankara last night. The women, including mothers aged 70, boarded the buses amid chants of “Long Live the Resistance of the Mothers” and “Woman, Life, Freedom.” Taking their demands for peace and a solution to Ankara, the mothers spoke to our agency’s microphones before departing, explaining the reasons for their action and their expectations.


Let mother's tears come to an end


 


The Peace Mothers said they were traveling to Ankara to demand Öcalan’s freedom, the successful conclusion of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, an end to the serious human rights violations taking place in prisons, and an end to the suffering of mothers. They stressed that the demand for peace is a shared responsibility of all sections of society.


[album=22829]


Emphasising that they would continue their struggle until their demands were met, the mothers called on all sections of society to support the Peace and Democratic Society Process and the Peace Vigil they will hold in Ankara.

title: Independent Engineers and Architects: It is not natural disasters but greed and negligence that kill
content:
Heavy rainfall affecting many cities, particularly Istanbul, has once again exposed the inadequacy of urban infrastructure and the devastating consequences of profit-driven urban development policies. Flooding turned underpasses and tunnels into lakes, bringing transport and daily life almost to a standstill. Five people lost their lives in the floods. According to the governor's office, authorities recorded 1,277 flooding incidents, 15 landslides, 47 reports of people stranded, 13 fallen trees, and reports involving 76 vehicles, 808 homes and 280 workplaces.


The Istanbul Platform of Independent Engineers, Architects and Urban Planners spoke to ANF following the devastation, which has reached deadly proportions. The platform stressed that the real cause of the disaster was not the weather but a profit-driven and negligent mentality that disregards both nature and human life.


‘Disadvantaged sections of society are once again paying the price’


The platform drew attention to the political and social realities behind the destruction, which the government and business interests have sought to dismiss as a 'natural disaster'. It stressed that, as always, low-income and disadvantaged sections of society were bearing the heaviest burden. The platform described the profound social and spatial inequalities created by profit-driven planning decisions: “Construction that disregards a city's carrying capacity and ecological limits places the resulting costs on society as a whole, while concentrating economic gains in the hands of certain groups. However, these costs are not borne equally. People living in basement and ground-floor flats, low-income households, workers in insecure employment, those forced to work outdoors, people with disabilities and older people can be more severely affected by disasters. Disruptions to transport, loss of employment, damage to homes and workplaces, and reduced access to safe housing deepen social inequalities beyond the immediate physical destruction.”


‘The problem is not the rain but capital-driven urban planning’


The platform said: “The recent loss of life and flooding cannot be explained by heavy rainfall alone. Extreme rainfall is a trigger, but whether it turns into a disaster is directly related to how a city is planned and managed.” It stressed that urban infrastructure and architectural practices had increasingly departed from scientific principles, despite years of warnings from scientists, urban planners and engineers.


The platform pointed out that valley floors and streambeds had been opened to construction for profit, while natural water catchment areas had been covered with concrete and asphalt.


The platform identified the main factors contributing to flooding: “The rapid expansion of concrete and asphalt surfaces, the destruction of green spaces and the declining capacity of soil to absorb water cause rainfall to turn rapidly into surface runoff. Narrowing streambeds and allowing uncontrolled development in valleys and low-lying areas directly increase the risk of flooding. Inadequate stormwater drainage capacity, non-functioning pumping stations, missing drainage lines and the failure to maintain drainage grates and pipelines regularly make disasters worse. Transforming urban land from a public living space into an instrument of speculative profit, and maximising economic gains at the expense of ecological balance and the public interest, creates systemic vulnerabilities.”


The Istanbul platform stated that ecological balance had been sacrificed for the sake of capital accumulation: “The transformation of urban land from a shared social living space into an instrument of speculative profit drives the destruction of natural areas. Urban development strategies that maximise economic returns at the expense of ecological balance and the public interest deepen systemic vulnerabilities to disasters. The safe absorption of water into the soil following heavy rainfall has been obstructed. Valley corridors, underpasses and surfaces stripped of their permeability have become threats to people's lives.”


‘Ecological oversight and the public interest must take priority’


The platform stressed that routine maintenance and technical solutions are insufficient in times of crisis, and that the problem requires a fundamental change in mentality and the system itself. title: Peace Mothers: There will be no peace until our leader reunites with his people
content:
Peace Mothers from 24 cities gathered in Ankara to demand the physical freedom of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan and concrete steps within the framework of the peace and democratic society process. The mothers, who are set to hold a “Peace Vigil,” issued a statement at Parliament Park. Carrying a banner reading “Take steps for peace, Parliament must act,” the mothers chanted slogans including “A thousand greetings to Imralı,” “Long live the resistance in the prisons,” and “Women do not want war, they want peace.”


Speaking on behalf of the group, Peace Mother Meryem Korkmaz stated that Öcalan’s legal status had still not been recognized. “The architect of peace is still on Imralı. We demand that the promises made be fulfilled and that steps be taken toward peace. We have always stood for peace. We do not accept any interruption of this process. Steps must be taken without delay. Our leader’s status must be secured, and the prisoners must be released. Only then can peace be achieved,” she said.


Peace Mother Mürvet Demir stated: “We will not stop until peace is achieved. There will be no peace until our leader’s status is secured and those in prison and in the mountains return. There will be no peace until our leader reunites with his people. That is why we are here.”


Kezban Kalın, the mother of an army lieutenant, also addressed the gathering, saying: “I wholeheartedly share the suffering of these mothers. If they are calling for peace, we cannot remain indifferent after so much suffering. Justice is necessary for all of us. Everyone must take responsibility and do their part.”

author: Unknown
title: Aygül Yağış: Save our young people from drugs
content:
Alongside special warfare policies, drug use, betting, gambling, gang activity and incidents of individual violence are among the major social problems in Kurdistan. Field studies conducted by civil society organisations and bar associations indicate that addiction is becoming increasingly widespread, particularly among young people, while families continue to call for solutions. According to available data, the age at which children begin using drugs has fallen to as low as nine, while a significant proportion of users are first introduced to drugs through their friends.


Reports published in the media indicate that 71.2 percent of drug users were first introduced to drugs between the ages of 15 and 24, while 74.4 percent first obtained drugs from friends or people in their immediate social circles. The Turkish Green Crescent's 2025 Gambling Report also highlighted that the age at which people begin gambling has fallen to 15.


According to data from the Diyarbakır (Amed) Bar Association, lawyers were appointed to represent 2,173 people prosecuted for drug production and trafficking between 1 January and 9 September 2023. Lawyers were also appointed to represent 291 people accused of drug use or purchasing, accepting or possessing drugs for personal use.


Growing concerns include young people being drawn into addiction, the weakening of social ties and the increasing economic vulnerability of families, while special warfare policies continue to be systematically implemented in the region.


Aygül Yağış, who said that many families around her were struggling with similar problems, has been fighting for years to free her son from drug addiction. Yağış stated that young people were being drawn into drug use very quickly and found it difficult to overcome addiction. She drew particular attention to the targeting of young people and children from patriotic families.


‘We did everything we could, but we could not save him’


Aygül Yağış described the difficult experiences her son had endured because of drug addiction. She said that the family had searched for a solution for a long time but had been unable to achieve any results. Yağış, whose son struggled with addiction for six years, said: "Recently, almost everyone around us and in our families has been affected by these policies. The person closest to me who was affected was my son. Unfortunately, he went through a long and difficult period because of drug addiction and was eventually arrested.


My son was working in another city. When he returned here, he started using drugs. He began taking drugs while spending time with his friends. We did everything we could and tried every possible intervention, but we could not save him from addiction. Eventually, he completely lost control of himself. When he was under the influence of drugs, he was not himself and was constantly aggressive. When he came to his senses, he apologised to everyone. He was suddenly drawn into this situation, and before we could understand what was happening, he had become addicted."


‘Even his arrest did not free him from addiction’


Aygül Yağış said that her son sometimes told her about what he was experiencing. She explained: "Sometimes he would tell me, 'Mum, the police come and see us, then take notes and leave.' I repeatedly told him that this was not happening for no reason. Many investigations were opened against him after his arrest. From the day he started using drugs, I never once saw him in a good condition. We tried everything, but we could not persuade him to stop. He remained in this situation for six years and was eventually arrested.


I thought he might get better after his arrest. Even he used to say, 'Maybe I can overcome this if I go to prison.' But despite being imprisoned, nothing has changed in his condition. Moreover, it is not only my son. Many people around him are struggling with the same problem. All these people live here. We also see people coming here from other provinces to use drugs."


‘Everyone, from children to the elderly, is gambling’


Aygül Yağış pointed out that betting and gambling, as well as drug use, were becoming increasingly widespread among young people, placing families under economic and social strain. She said that families were worried about protecting their children and were being forced to send them elsewhere.

title: Peace Mothers begin vigil in Ankara
content:
Members of the Peace Mothers’ Council from 24 cities are continuing their protest in Ankara, where they gathered earlier today. Following a press statement at Parliament Park, the mothers moved to Kurtuluş Park, where they began their vigil.


The mothers, who will maintain their vigil in a tent throughout the night, began their protest by singing songs. After spending the night in the park, they are expected to attend the parliamentary group meetings of political parties represented in Parliament tomorrow.


The mothers are drawing attention to their demands for the physical freedom of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan and concrete steps within the framework of the peace and democratic society process.

author: Unknown
title: ‘No independent investigations conducted into murders of journalist in the Kurdistan Region’
content:
The Metro Center for Journalists’ Rights and Advocacy issued a statement on the occasion of November 2, the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, designated by the United Nations (UN) in 2013.


The statement read: “In the Kurdistan Region, no independent investigations into the murders of journalists have been conducted because the judiciary is under the influence of the ruling political parties. Cases that have sparked widespread public outrage, such as the murders of Soran Mame Heme, Serdeşt Osman, Kawa Germiyani, Vedat Hüseyin, and Abdülstar Tahir Şerif, remain unsolved. Neither those who carried out the murders nor those who ordered them have been identified or brought to justice.”


Calling for the investigations into these cases to be reopened, the Metro Center drew attention to statements issued by UNESCO, stating: “Impunity for crimes leads to an increase in murders and violence and undermines the legal and justice systems. UNESCO warns that such impunity allows serious human rights violations and corruption to be concealed, causing harm to society as a whole. For this reason, the government, civil society organizations, and media outlets are being urged to uphold the rule of law and support international initiatives aimed at putting an end to such practices.”

content:

author: dev
title: Thèses sur le concept de compétence (Suite 7/9)
content:
La lutte contre la pénétration du concept de compétence dans les établissements d'enseignement se poursuit. Le comité d'action contre les compétences Pontcerq est intervenu de manière un peu vive à l'Université de Nantes (avec

certaines conséquences

). En marge des manifestations et blocages des lycées circule par ailleurs, depuis Rennes pour l'instant, une « Lettre aux lycéennes et lycéens sur la compétence ».


Lundimatin a déjà publié, dans cet ordre, les thèses n° 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 et 7 (voir

ici

 et

ici

), les n° 16 et 18 (voir

ici

 et

ici

) et les n° 15 et 19 (voir

là

). Voici la thèse n° 12 – qui manquait.


SITUATION


La thèse n° 12 sur la compétence, qu'on va lire in extenso ci-dessous, permet des clarifications d'importance. Certaines lectrices et lecteurs des précédentes thèses avaient pu en lisant vite croire pouvoir (ou vouloir) les disqualifier en parlant de propos conservateurs (parce que les questions de l'imitation, du maître, de la note, de la discipline, de l'approche actionnelle, de l'apport des sciences de l'éducation, etc., y étaient réinterrogées toutes de manière un peu vertigineuse, ou inhabituelle). La quadripartition proposée ci-dessous en nota bene (n° 3) donne une géographie – qui aidera les uns et les autres à se repérer mieux politiquement : à se situer soi ; à nous situer nous ; et à situer nos adversaires (possiblement

communs

).


La compétence est le nom d'un projet pédagogique-politique étendu à l'ensemble de la société. Ce projet court de la maternelle à l'université : mais il ne se limite pas même à la question scolaire. Il est un concept social totalisant. (Ce sur quoi la thèse n° 13, en cours d'écriture, reviendra.)


Nous rappelons qu'un « Appel contre les compétences » circule actuellement en France, et alentour, dans tous les lieux d'enseignement. L'Appel est à lire

ici

. Il a déjà été signé par plus de 600 universitaires. Il peut être également signé électroniquement,

là

. Il s'adresse à toutes les enseignantes et tous les enseignants, depuis la maternelle jusqu'à l'enseignement supérieur. (Merci à toutes celles et ceux qui œuvrent à faire connaître cet appel, et les questions qu'il soulève, dans les établissements scolaires, en particulier dans le primaire et le secondaire : autour d'eux, auprès de leurs collègues, comme aussi auprès des syndicats ; et auprès des élèves, premiers

concernés

.)


J.-A. Marie

, octobre 2026


Thèse n° 12

Compétence et démocratisation de l'enseignement


La compétence comme

renoncement

 de l'enseignement


(à enseigner, au sens le plus fort).


La compétence comme démission.


Un bouleversement d'ampleur eut lieu dans l'édifice scolaire au cours des années 1960 et 1970 ; on a parlé à son sujet de « démocratisation » ou de « massification » de l'enseignement. (Replacer la notion de compétence sur le fond de cette transformation


va permettre de la faire apparaître dans un éclairage nouveau ; en particulier, l'un de ses sens politiques se laisse apercevoir et déterminer, sous ce jour, plus nettement.) Alors qu'aux classes les plus basses de la société n'avait été le plus souvent accordée jusqu'ici que la fréquentation d'un enseignement primaire (clos par le certificat d'études, à 12 ou 13 ans), et que la poursuite d'un cursus dans l'enseignement secondaire, jusqu'au baccalauréat, était réservée dans les lycées presque exclusivement à la petite, moyenne et grande bourgeoisie, des politiques nouvelles – volontaires, de grande ampleur – furent gouvernementalement adoptées : c'est, en France, en particulier la création d'institutions d'enseignement secondaire inédites, dans les années 1970 : les collèges ; par quoi l'on fit que la plus grande partie d'une classe d'âge, indépendamment des origines sociales des élèves, puisse désormais poursuivre au-delà du seul enseignement primaire son parcours, et accède au lycée

 [

1

]

. Cette transformation eut pour conséquence simple l'arrivée dans les établissements secondaires d'une population toujours plus nombreuse – mais aussi plus socialement bigarrée. (C'est toute la société désormais, sur l'ensemble de son spectre ou presque, qui entrait dans les collèges, les lycées : les enfants des paysans des campagnes reculées, ceux des petits commerçants, ceux des ouvriers immigrés du Maghreb ou d'Afrique noire, etc.

 [

2

]

) Il est utile de distinguer ces deux points : 1° l'augmentation en nombre de cette population scolaire (massification) ; 2° sa bigarrure sociale (diversification) …

content:

.


ᐅᓇ ᓖᑎᐊ ᑲᓪᓗᒃ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᐃᙱᐅᓯᖓᓂ

ᒫᓐᓇ

ᒥ ᓵᓚᒃᓴᐅᓯᐊᕋᓱᒃᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᓄᓇᑦᓯᐊᕐᒥ, ᖃᐅᔨᒪᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᙱᑦᑐᖅ ᑖᓐᓇ ᓂᓪᓕᐊᑎᑕᐅᓂᐊᕆᐊᒃᓴᖓᓂ ᐱᙳᐊᕈᑎᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᒥᒃ ᐱᐅᓯᕚᓪᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᒃᑐᒥ ᐃᓱᒪᒃᑯᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᑦᑕᐃᓕᓂᕐᒥᒃ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᐃᓅᓱᒃᑐᖏᓐᓂ.


ᐅᕙᓂ

ᑕᕐᕆᔭᒐᖅ ᖃᒡᒋᖅᒥ,

 ᐅᖃᐅᓯᐅᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᖅᐹᖑᓂᖓᓂ ᐃᓄᖕᓄᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓱᖅᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᓂᖓᓂ ᑕᕐᕆᔭᒐᖅ ᐱᙳᐊᕈᑎ ᐅᖄᓚᐅᑎᕋᓛᓄᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᑕᐅᓂᐊᖅᖢᓂ, ᐃᓄᒃᑎᑐᑦ ᐃᙱᕐᑐᒥ ᑐᓴᕐᓴᐅᔪᖃᖅᖢᓂ ᐃᓐᓇᕐᓂ ᑕᕐᕆᔭᒐᕐᓂ ᓴᖅᑭᔮᖅᑎᑦᑎᓕᕌᖓᑕ.


“ᐃᙱᐅᑎᐅᑉ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᑕᐅᓯᒪᓂᖏᑦ ᐃᒪᓐᓇᐸᓘᕐᑐᑦ, ‘ᐊᖑᑎ ᖃᐅᔨᒪᑦᑎᐊᖅᑐᐊᓗᒃ ᐅᕙᓐᓄᑦ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᖕᒪᑦ ᓱᓕ ᒪᒃᑯᒃᑐᑎᑦ. ᐃᓅᓯᖃᕈᑎᖃᐅᖅᖢᑎᑦ. ᓄᓇᕐᔪᐊᕐᓗ ᑕᑯᐊᓂᒃᓯᒪᙱᖢᒍᑦ,” ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᑲᓪᓗᒃ, ᐃᒃᐱᐊᕐᔪᒃᒥᐅᑕᖅ, ᐊᐱᕐᓱᖅᑕᐅᑎᓪᓗᒍ.


“ᐅᓇ ᐱᐅᔪᐊᓗᒃ [ᐃᓅᓱᒃᑐᓄᑦ] ᑐᓵᑎᖢᒋᑦ ᐃᖏᐅᑎᓂ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᖏᑦᑎᒎᖓᔪᓂ. ᐅᕙᓐᓄᓪᓕ ᐃᓗᐊᕈᑎᒻᒪᕆᒐ ᐃᙱᕐᑎᐅᓪᓗᖓ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᖃᕈᓐᓇᕋᒪ ᑖᔅᓱᒧᖓ.”


ᔪᐊᒃ ᓯᓚᑦᑐᖅᓴᕐᕕᐊᓗᒃᒥ ᖃᐅᔨᓇᓱᒃᑎᐅᔪᑦ, ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᐃᓅᓱᒃᑐᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓕᖅᑯᓯᕐᒥ ᖃᐅᔨᒪᔨᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓱᐃᕙᓪᓕᐊᓕᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᑦ ᐱᙳᐊᕈᑎᒥ 2022-ᖑᑎᓪᓗᒍ.


ᐅᓇ ᒪᓕᒃᑐᖅ ᐊᓛᓱᐊᒥ, ᐱᙳᐊᖅᑎᓪᓗᐊᑕᐅᔪᖅ, 7-ᓂ ᐊᔾᔨᒌᙱᑦᑑᑎᓂ ᐊᓂᒍᐃᕙᓪᓕᐊᓇᓱᒃᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᓴᓇᔭᐅᓯᒪᓪᓗᓂ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᐃᓕᖅᑯᓯᖓᒍᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᓯᕐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓱᒪᒃᑯᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᑦᑕᐃᓕᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᒃᓴᓂᒃ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒧᑦ ᑐᑭᒧᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᔨ ᔪᒌᑕ ᓯᖕ.


ᐊᑕᐅᓯᖅ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᒥ ᓂᕐᔪᑎᙳᐊᖅ ᐃᒥᖅᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᒃᖢᓂ ᐱᐅᙱᑦᑐᕈᓗᒥ ᐊᓛᓱᐊᒥ ᑲᑎᕐᓱᐃᓂᕐᒥᓂ ᐃᒪᑦᑎᐊᕙᒃᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓂᓚᖕᓂ. ᐱᙳᐊᖅᑐᑦ ᐊᔪᕈᓐᓃᕈᓐᓇᖅᑐᑦ ᑖᔅᓱᒥᖓ ᐱᑦᑕᐃᓕᒪᓂᕐᒥᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑎᒋᔭᐅᔪᑦ ᐊᓂᒍᖅᑎᑕᐅᔪᓐᓇᕐᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᒥᐊᓗᙱᒃᑲᓗᐊᕐᓗᑎ, ᓯᖕ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᓂᐱᓕᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐃᓚᖃᕐᒥᔪᖅ ᐃᙱᑦᒥ ᑭᖓᕐᓂᑦ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑐᒥ ᓘᓚ ᐅᓱᐃᑦᑐᒃ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᕿᓚᐅᔾᔭᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᑭᒻᒥᕈᒻᒥᐅᑕᖅ ᓕᐅ ᑎᒥᓚ, ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑲᑕᔾᔭᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᔭᓗᓇᐃᒥᐅᑖᖕᓂ ᑎᕕᓂ ᑯᓕᒃᑖᓇ ᐊᔭᓕᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑲᐃᓕ ᐃᓄᒃᓱᒃ ᒪᒦ, ᖃᐅᔨᒪᔭᐅᖕᒥᔪᖅ ᐱᖅᓯᖅᒥ.


ᐱᙳᐊᖅ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐅᕙᙵᑦ ᐅᒃᑑᐱᕆ 2025-ᒥ ᒪᐅᖓ ᔪᓚᐃ 2026-ᒧ, 276 ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᐃᓅᓱᒃᑐᑦ ᓄᓇᓕᖕᓂᙶᖅᑐᑦ 21-ᓂ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ 16-ᓂ ᐊᓯᖏᓐᓂ ᓄᓇᓕᖕᓂ ᑲᓇᑕᒦᑦᑐᓂᒃ ᐃᓚᐅᑎᑕᐅᓪᓗᑎᒃ, ᓯᖕ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᐱᙳᐊᑲᑕᒃᑐᑦ ᐱᐊᓂᒃᓯᓚᐅᕐᑐᑦ 39-ᓂ ᐊᐱᖅᑯᑎᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᖃᓄᐃᑦᑕᐃᓕᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᙳᐊᒥ ᐱᙳᐊᓚᐅᖅᑎᓐᓇᒋᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᙳᐊᕌᓂᒃᓯᒪᓕᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ, ᐱᓕᕆᑎᑕᐅᓪᓗᑎ ᐊᔪᕈᓐᓃᕐᓴᓯᓐᓈᑦ ᐅᑯᓇᓂ ᓄᓇᓕᖕᓂᑦ ᐃᒃᐱᐊᕐᔪᒃ, ᑭᖓᐃᑦ, ᐸᓐᓂᕐᑑᖅ, ᐃᖃᓗᐃᑦ, ᖃᒪᓂᑦᑐᐊᖅ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐋᑐᕚᒥ. ᐊᓯᖏᑦ ᐊᖏᕐᕋᖏᓐᓂ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᓚᐅᕐᑐᑦ ᐱᙳᐊᕈᑎᒥ, ᓯᖕ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


“ᐃᓅᓱᒃᑐᐃᑦ ᐃᓱᒪᓚᐅᕐᑐᑦ ᐊᔪᕈᓐᓃᕐᓂᕋᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᒃᓴᓂᒃ ᐃᖕᒥᖕᓂ ᐃᑲᔪᕈᑎᒃᓴᖏᓐᓂ ᑯᕕᐊᓇᙱᓗᐊᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐃᓱᒪᓗᐊᓕᕌᖓᑕ, ᐃᖕᒥᖕᓂ ᖃᓄᐃᑦᑐᓐᓃᕐᑎᑦᑐᕐᓇᕐᒥᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓗᐊᕐᓴᕐᓂᖅᓴᐅᓕᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑕᐅᔪᒪᓗᑎ ᐊᐱᕆᔭᕆᐊᒃᓴᖅ, ᓲᕐᓗ ᐃᒪᓐᓇ, ᖁᕕᐊᓇᙱᑦᑐᖅᓯᐅᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᓕᕈᓂ,” ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᐃᕚᓐ ᐳᐊ, ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᒧᑦ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᕆᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᖃᐅᔨᓇᓱᖃᑦᑕᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᐅᕙᓂ ᔪᐊᒃ ᓯᓚᑦᑐᖅᓴᕐᕕᐊᓗᒃᒥ.


“ᐃᒪᓐᓇᐅᓂᕐᓴᐅᕙᒃᖢᓂ ᑕᒪᒃᑯᐊ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᕈᑎᒋᔭᕗᑦ ᐃᓛᓐᓂ ᑐᑭᓯᑲᐅᑎᒋᕙᙱᖢᑎᒍᑦ, ᑭᓯᐊᓂᓕ ᐊᓯᔾᔨᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᓂᕐᑕᖃᓚᐅᕐᒪᑦ ᑭᖑᓂᑦᑎᐊᑯᓗᐊᒍᑦ ᑖᓐᓇᓗ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒻᒪᕆᐅᓪᓗᓂ,” ᐅᖃᒃᑲᓐᓂᖅᑐᖅ.


ᖃᐅᔨᓇᓱᒃᑐᑦ ᓇᓂᓯᓚᐅᙱᒻᒥᔪᑦ ᓈᒻᒪᙱᓕᐅᕈᑎᐅᓇᔭᕐᑐᓂ ᐃᓚᐅᑎᑕᐅᔪᓄᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᑦᑕᐃᓕᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᙳᐊᑲᑖᓚᓚᐅᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᐱᙳᐊᕈᑎᒥ.


ᑲᓪᓗᒃ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐃᑲᔪᓚᐅᕐᓂᕋᖅᖢᑎ ᑐᑭᓕᐅᕆᓂᕐᒥ 12-ᓂ ᐊᐱᖅᓱᖅᑕᐅᔪᕕᓂᕐᓂ ᐃᓐᓇᑐᖃᕐᓂ ᐃᒃᐱᐊᕐᔪᒃᒥ, ᑭᙵᓂᑦ, ᖃᒪᓂᑦᑐᐊᕐᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐸᓐᓂᕐᑑᕐᒥ, ᑕᒪᒃᑯᐊᓗ ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᐅᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐱᙳᐊᖃᑦᑕᖅᑐᓄᑦ ᖃᕋᓴᐅᔭᒃᑯᑦ ᖃᒡᒋᖅᒥ, ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᐃᓕᖅᑯᓯᑎᒍ ᑲᑎᒪᖃᑎᒌᖕᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᙳᐊᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ.


“ᑕᕐᕆᔭᒐᕐᑕᖃᐅᕌᕐᔪᒃᑐᖅ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᖃᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐃᖃᓗᒐᓱᖕᓂᕐᒥᒃ, ᐊᖑᓇᓱᒋᐊᕐᓂᕐᒥᒃ, ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐃᓱᒪᒃᑯᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᖅᑕᐃᓕᓂᕐᒨᖓᔪᓂᒃ. ᐃᓐᓇᑐᖃᐅᑉ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᖏᑦ ᐱᒻᒪᕆᐊᓘᖕᒪᑕ, ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐱᒻᒪᕆᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᑕᒪᒃᑯᓂᖓ ᐃᑲᑎᖃᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᖅ ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᐃᓅᓱᒃᑐᓄᑦ,” ᑲᓪᓗᒃ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᐱᓕᕆᖃᑎᒌᒃᑐᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᕐᑐᑦ ᑖᒃᑯᐊ ᐱᙳᐊᒐᒃᓴᐃᑦ ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᐅᓕᕈᓐᓇᕐᓗᑎᒃ ᑕᕐᕆᔭᕈᓐᓇᐅᑎᓂ ᑎᒍᒥᐊᒐᕐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᖃᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᖅᑐᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᓐᓂ ᐊᑐᕈᓐᓇᕆᐊᒃᓴᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᕐᕕᖕᓂᑦ.


ᓯᖕ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐃᓱᒪᓂᕋᖅᖢᓂ ᐅᓇ

ᑕᕐᕆᔭᒐᖅ ᖃᒡᒋᖅᒥᑦ

ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᐅᔪᓐᓇᕐᓯᓂᐊᕐᓗᓂ 2027 ᐱᒋᐊᓵᖅᓯᒪᓕᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᒪᑯᑎᒎᖓ ᐅᖄᓚᐅᑎᕋᓛᑎᒍᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑎᒍᒥᐊᒐᖅᑎᒍ ᑕᕐᕆᔭᕈᓐᓇᐅᑎᑎᒍᑦ.


“ᐊᒃᓱᐊᓗᒃ ᐅᕙᓐᓂ ᐅᐱᒋᕙᒃᑐᖓ ᐃᓅᓪᓗᖓ ᑕᐃᒪᐃᑦᑐᓕᐅᖅᑐᓂ ᐃᓚᐅᓂᓐᓂ, ᐅᓇ ᐱᒋᐊᓕᓵᕈᑎᒻᒪᕆᒃ ᐃᓅᓱᒃᑐᓄᑦ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ,’ ᑲᓪᓗᒃ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Juicio Mercedes Benz: “Fueron los empresarios quienes empujaron a los milicos a llevar a cabo el golpe de Estado”
content:
El pasado 22 de octubre comenzó la primera audiencia en la causa de lesa humanidad Mercedes Benz, donde declaró el único imputado Juan Ronaldo Tasselkraut, gerente de producción de la filial argentina de la empresa alemana durante la última dictadura militar. Tasselkraut está acusado de privación ilegítima de la libertad que sufrieron Héctor Ratto y Diego Núñez. Ratto logró sobrevivir y dio cuenta de haber sido secuestrado dentro de la empresa y haber escuchado cómo Tasselkraut le pasó a la patota la dirección de Núñez, quien fue secuestrado y permanece desaparecido.


Por Christian Madia para Agencia Andar


El caso de la empresa Mercedes Benz es similar al de la automotriz Ford, donde los integrantes de la comisión gremial interna fueron secuestrados dentro de la misma fábrica. A finales de la década del ’60, los trabajadores de Mercedes Benz insistían en la conformación de comisiones internas independientes de los gremios cabecera (por ejemplo SMATA) para poder profundizar los reclamos salariales y por mejoras en las condiciones laborales.


El trabajador Héctor Ratto había ingresado a la automotriz en 1967, luego de haber estudiado en la escuela fábrica de la misma Mercedes Benz, por entonces tenía 19 años. Una década después, el viernes 12 de agosto de 1977, en la planta que Mercedes Benz tenía en la localidad de González Catán, Ratto fue convocado a la oficina del gerente de producción, Juan Ronaldo Tasselkraut, que lo esperaba junto a dos personas de civil que “lo venían a buscar”.


En diálogo con ANDAR, Ratto recuerda aquel día: “ya venían desapareciendo varios compañeros de la empresa. Ese 12 de agosto, cuando llego a la fábrica, ya se habían llevado a un compañero que tenía mi mismo apellido, lo habían metido en un cuarto que tenía la policía en la entrada de Mercedes Benz y lo estuvieron golpeando. Cuando se dieron cuenta de que no era el ‘Ratto’ que buscaban, me vinieron a buscar a mí. Se acercó un tipo de vigilancia con la intención de que saliera de la fábrica, con el cuento de que me llamaban por teléfono desde mi casa. Eso resultaba imposible porque para una comunicación telefónica en aquella época tenías que llamar a la operadora y tardaba dos horas como mínimo y yo recién ingresaba a mi turno laboral”.


Esa misma mañana, el grupo de tareas ya había secuestrado a otro operario de la sección que era hijo del capataz de la línea de montaje y el mismo padre les había comunicado al resto de los trabajadores, que habían secuestrado a su hijo. Aquel hecho ya ponía en alerta a Ratto, sospechando que la intención era hacerlo salir de la fabrica para llevárselo.


“Me quedé adentro de la fábrica para resguardarme porque me sentía seguro junto al resto de mis compañeros. Cuando vino el capataz general del turno tarde, me dijo que yo tenía permiso de salida porque estando ahí adentro lo comprometía. Yo le expliqué las razones por las cuales decidía quedarme en la fábrica. Varias horas después, se acercó el capataz del turno noche y me dijo que lo acompañe afuera, ante mi negativa, él elevó el comunicado al gerente de producción. Al rato aparece el propio Tasselkraut y me dice: ‘te llevamos porque hay dos personas ahí que te quieren llevar con ellos’ y me pide que lo acompañe a la oficina. Cuando ingreso, estaban estos dos tipos sentados muy confianzudamente, eran policías, yo me senté en la punta del escritorio, hasta que vinieron los milicos, en ese interín de 20 minutos, suena el teléfono. Tasselkraut atiende, y le pasan la dirección del compañero Diego Núñez”.


Ratto conocía el domicilio de Núñez debido a que un mes antes éste había ido a donar sangre para la esposa de Ratto que estaba internada en la clínica “Los Cedros” de San Justo. “Cuando vuelvo a escuchar la dirección, me di cuenta que era la casa de Núñez. Era obvio que la llamada provenía de la oficina de personal de la empresa. Tasselkraut le pasó el teléfono a uno de los tipos y éste se pone a repetir y escribe en un papelito la dirección”, agrega Héctor. Unas horas después, se llevan a Ratto a la comisaría de Ramos Mejía, donde queda detenido hasta el 17 de agosto. Luego le hacen firmar un papel diciéndole que lo liberarían, pero no fue así. “Estos mismos tipos que habían estado en la oficina de Tasselkraut, me encapuchan y me llevan a lo que después reconozco como el centro clandestino de detención ‘El Campito’ (también conocido como “Los Tordos”), dentro de la guarnición Campo de Mayo”.


Estando en cautiverio, Ratto pudo reconocer a varios …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Milei y Jalil le abren las puertas al saqueo minero: Catamarca, zona de sacrificio
content:
El Gobierno nacional aprobó el ingreso de Agua Rica al Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (RIGI), un proyecto de Glencore, multinacional denunciada por contaminación y vulneración de derechos en distintos países. La decisión se produce mientras las comunidades de la Región Albigasta vienen desarrollando movilizaciones contra otro proyecto minero en la zona de El Alto, a cargo de Litios del Norte S.A. Las asambleas socioambientales advierten que no permitirán que el avance de la minería ponga en riesgo el agua, los bosques y las actividades productivas locales.


Por Adrián Flores, Red Eco


Mientras Javier Milei y el gobernador Raúl Jalil garantizan beneficios fiscales, aduaneros y cambiarios a las grandes corporaciones, las comunidades deben enfrentar los riesgos de un modelo que exporta minerales y deja a su paso contaminación, crisis hídrica, pérdida de biodiversidad y pasivos ambientales y sociales.


El 27 de octubre, el Gobierno de Javier Milei oficializó la adhesión de Agua Rica al RIGI mediante la Resolución 1854/2026 del Ministerio de Economía. El proyecto, presentado por Minera Agua Rica LLC, Sucursal Argentina, pertenece a Glencore y prevé una inversión total declarada de 6.393 millones de dólares para explotar cobre, oro, plata y molibdeno en Catamarca.


Esta decisión no puede separarse de la política económica del Gobierno nacional, que convierte la entrega de beneficios al gran capital en moneda de cambio para obtener las divisas necesarias para pagar la deuda externa a la usura internacional: el FMI, el Banco Mundial y los fondos buitre. El RIGI no representa simplemente un mecanismo para atraer inversiones, sino una herramienta que profundiza un modelo de subordinación económica en el que los bienes comunes se entregan a las grandes corporaciones a cambio de divisas destinadas a sostener el pago de una deuda que recae sobre el conjunto de la sociedad.


Se configura así un doble saqueo: por un lado, la apropiación y depredación de los bienes comunes, el agua, los minerales, los bosques y los territorios; por otro, la extracción de las divisas que genera esa explotación para alimentar el circuito del endeudamiento externo. La riqueza se extrae, se exporta y se convierte en ganancias corporativas y recursos destinados al pago de la deuda, mientras en los territorios quedan la contaminación, la degradación ambiental, la pérdida de las economías locales y la pobreza. Se saquean los bienes comunes y también la riqueza que se produce con ellos.


Esta orientación política quedó expuesta casi al unísono. El miércoles 28 de octubre, apenas un día después de la resolución sobre Agua Rica, Javier Milei encabezó en Catamarca un acto para inaugurar la expansión Fénix 1B y la operación Sal de Vida, dos proyectos de Río Tinto que representan una inversión cercana a los 1.400 millones de dólares.


Durante su discurso, el Presidente defendió el rumbo económico de su gestión y reivindicó el Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones como herramienta para atraer capitales y acelerar la actividad minera.


La secuencia habla por sí sola: mientras el Ministerio de Economía habilitaba el ingreso de Agua Rica al régimen de privilegios para las grandes inversiones, el Presidente celebraba junto a Jalil la expansión de otros dos emprendimientos mineros. No son hechos aislados, sino expresiones de una misma política: poner los territorios, el agua y las condiciones de vida de sus comunidades al servicio de la rentabilidad de las corporaciones y de una estrategia económica subordinada al pago de la deuda externa.


Glencore: una trayectoria que atraviesa fronteras


Detrás de Agua Rica está Glencore, una de las grandes corporaciones mineras y comercializadoras de materias primas del mundo. Su trayectoria internacional acumula denuncias ambientales, investigaciones, sanciones administrativas y cuestionamientos por vulneraciones de derechos humanos. En Argentina, su historia está vinculada a Bajo de la Alumbrera, cuyos antecedentes judiciales vuelven especialmente urgente examinar los riesgos de la nueva explotación.


En noviembre de 2020, la Cámara Federal de Apelaciones de Tucumán confirmó el procesamiento del entonces gerente general de Minera Alumbrera por contaminación ambiental de la cuenca Salí-Dulce.

author: Mag
title: [Deutsches Schulbarometer] Erschöpfte Lehrkräfte leiden unter Gewalt, Personalmangel und mangelder Ausstattung
content:
Dossier


„… Das Verhalten und die Vielfalt ihrer Schüler:innen stellen Lehrkräfte derzeit vor die größten Herausforderungen. Das sind Ergebnisse der aktuellen Befragung des Deutschen Schulbarometers unter Lehrkräften an deutschen Schulen. Fast jede zweite Lehrkraft sieht an der eigenen Schule ein Problem mit psychischer oder physischer Gewalt unter Schüler:innen.Gewalt an der eigenen Schule erhöht das Burnout- und Stressrisiko von Lehrkräften deutlich, wie die Befragung ergab. Mehr als jede dritte Lehrkraft fühlt sich mehrmals pro Woche emotional erschöpft, das sagen vor allem jüngere und weibliche Lehrkräfte sowie Grundschullehrer:innen…“

Vorstellung der Studie 2014 durch Michael Herm und Claudia Hagen am 24. April 2024 bei der Robert-Bosch-Stiftung


 („Jede zweite Lehrkraft beobachtet Gewalt an der eigenen Schule“) und mehr daraus/dazu:


[Wie der Lehrerjob Nächte und Beziehungen bestimmt] Feierabend – aber die Arbeit geht mit nach Hause


„22:45 Uhr. Eine Klasse ist vorbereitet, die andere noch nicht. P. Barbanegra erzählt, wie der Lehrerjob Nächte und Beziehungen bestimmt. Wir fragen: Was ist daran mehr als ein persönliches Zeitproblem – und wer entscheidet über die Arbeit?


Es ist 22:45 Uhr. Die Vorbereitung für eine Klasse ist fertig, für die andere fehlt noch alles. P. Barbanegra erzählt aus seinen ersten beiden Jahren als Lehrer in den USA: von Nächten am Computer, fehlendem Schlaf und dem Wunsch, Unterricht zu machen, der mehr ist als Prüfungsvorbereitung. Gerade dieser Anspruch gerät zur Falle. Zu wenig bezahlte Vorbereitungszeit, starre Stundenpläne und unsichere Jahresverträge greifen ineinander. Der Text zeigt, wie schwer es sein kann, Feierabend zu machen, wenn man die eigene Arbeit ernst nimmt und zugleich um den Job fürchtet. Die beschriebenen Schul- und Vertragsbedingungen lassen sich nicht eins zu eins auf Deutschland, Österreich oder die Schweiz übertragen. Die Frage reicht dennoch über diesen Arbeitsplatz hinaus: Wer bestimmt, wie viel Arbeit in einen Tag passen soll? Der Bericht erzählt noch nicht von gemeinsamer Gegenwehr. Er gibt uns aber einen Anlass, darüber zu sprechen, wie Kolleg:innen nicht nur Entlastung erreichen, sondern mehr Einfluss auf Zeit, Ablauf und Zweck ihrer Arbeit gewinnen könnten. (…)


Viele Leute verstehen nicht, wie anspruchsvoll das Unterrichten tatsächlich ist, geschweige denn das Unterrichten dieser fortgeschrittenen Kurse zu einem so frühen Zeitpunkt in der Karriere. Das Unterrichten auf diesem höheren Niveau setzt voraus, dass man die Inhalte gut beherrscht, und obwohl ich mich selbst als überdurchschnittlich gut in US-merikanischer und Weltgeschichte auskenne, erfordert mein Bestreben, kritische Perspektiven auf diese Themen einzubringen, dass ich mehr Zeit für die Recherche und Planung aufbringe. (…) Als Lehrer (…) fühle ich also ein größeres Bedürfnis, Zeit mit der Erforschung und Planung von Unterrichtsstunden zu verbringen, die meinen eigenen Vorstellungen von einer wirklich radikalen Pädagogik entsprechen. Während ich gleichzeitig mit den institutionellen Zwängen zu tun habe, die darin bestehen, größtenteils auf einen Test hin zu unterrichten, und das in einer Umgebung, die größtenteils davon geprägt ist, Kreativität und intellektuelle Neugierde zu ersticken. (…)


Wenn die Schulbezirke zwei Schichten einführen würden, eine vormittags und eine nachmittags, hätten Lehrer*innen wie ich möglicherweise die Chance, später mit der Arbeit zu beginnen, selbst wenn das bedeuten würde, etwas später Feierabend zu machen. So wie der Schultag derzeit gestaltet ist, müssen alle in unserem Bezirk, die an der High‑School unterrichten, um 7:10 Uhr am Arbeitsplatz sein und um 7:20 Uhr mit dem Unterricht beginnen. Dieser Zeitplan beeinträchtigt nicht nur die Fähigkeit vieler Schüler*innen zu lernen, sondern in meinem Fall auch meine Fähigkeit zu unterrichten, da die meisten Leute im Raum unter Schlafmangel leiden. (…) Ich höre oft von alten Häs*innen, dass man dranbleiben soll und dass die ersten zwei Jahre die schwersten sind. Ich habe das Glück, eine unterstützende Freundin und Genoss*innen zu haben, aber ich frage mich, was ich gemacht hätte, wenn ich das nicht hätte. Die Statistik in den USA besagt, dass 50 Prozent der neuen Lehrer*innen innerhalb ihrer ersten fünf Jahre aufhören, und nachdem ich erst zwei Jahre dabei bin, verstehe ich vollkommen, warum.“

 Bericht von Pablo Barbanegra aus der Veröffentlichung „Spuren der Arbeit. Geschichten von Jobs und Widerstand“ vom …

title: "Princes and Thieves" Author Matthew Cole on Jared Kushner & the "Secret Plot to Remake Middle East"
content:
Vanity Fair

 recently published an

excerpt

 from longtime investigative reporter Mathhew Cole’s new book,

Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East

.


The excerpt alleged that during President Trump’s first term, Saudi and Emirati leaders secretly put at least $2 billion into bank accounts and gave access to Kushner. At the time, Jared Kushner was serving as senior adviser to President Trump, his father-in-law. He is now Trump’s special envoy. Kushner’s lawyers responded by demanding that

Vanity Fair

 retract the article and threatening legal action against the book publisher, Simon & Schuster.


Jared Kushner denied the report, saying, “The allegations made by this author are completely insane, categorically false, and never happened. We denied every one of these claims on the record, yet the author failed to provide a single shred of evidence to substantiate any of them.” His lawyers say no such bank accounts existed and that the allegations are unsupported by the verifiable evidence.


In an extended interview with

Democracy Now!

, author Matthew Cole stood by his reporting. “This book is a result of more than 50 sources. There was an enormous amount of fact-checking and legal vetting that went into this book,” says Cole. “There’s plenty of information and reporting in the book that lets us establish and understand that there was … an unholy alliance between Jared Kushner and the leader of the

UAE

, the leader of Saudi Arabia and, at the time, Benjamin Netanyahu, the prime minister of Israel.”


On Friday, Congressmember Jamie Raskin, the ranking Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, called on Kushner to recuse himself from Middle East and Ukraine negotiations and to produce a “comprehensive list of bank accounts or other financial instruments” that he had access to during his time in government.

title: Rechtsextremismus in der Schweiz: Die unterschätzte Gefahr
content:
„In Tuggen ereignete sich die erste rechtsextreme Gewalttat mit Todesfolge seit einem Vierteljahrhundert. Antifa-Recherchen zeigen: Am oberen Zürichsee hat sich weitgehend unbemerkt eine neonazistische Szene verfestigt.  Der gewalttätige Rechtsextremismus schien zuletzt kaum noch existent in der Schweiz. Doch nun hat er sich ins öffentliche Bewusstsein zurückgedrängt: In der Nacht auf den 18. Oktober wurde ein 27-jähriger Besucher eines Oi-Punk-Konzerts in einer Eventhalle in der Gewerbezone von Tuggen erschlagen. Noch ist die exakte Todesursache nicht restlos geklärt. Die Umstände hingegen sind weitgehend klar: Gemäss Staatsanwaltschaft Schwyz kam es kurz vor ein Uhr morgens während einer Afterparty «zu einer körperlichen Auseinandersetzung zwischen ca. 5 bis 10 Personen», und zwar «mutmasslich deshalb, weil mehrere der anwesenden Personen den Hitler-Gruss gezeigt haben»…“

Artikel von Jan Jirát in der WOZ vom 29. Oktober 2026


 und mehr daraus:


Weiter aus dem

Artikel von Jan Jirát in der WOZ vom 29. Oktober 2026


: „

… Gemäss Recherchen des «SonntagsBlicks» gehört der mutmassliche Täter dem internationalen neonazistischen Netzwerk Blood and Honour an. (…) Bewahrheiten sich die vorliegenden Zeugenaussagen und Indizien, handelt es sich um die erste öffentlich bekannte rechtsextreme Gewalttat mit Todesfolge seit einem Vierteljahrhundert. 2001 war der neunzehnjährige Marcel von Allmen als angeblicher Verräter von seinen rechtsextremen «Kameraden» im Berner Oberland getötet worden. (…) Wie sehr die Gefahr neonazistischer Aktivität und Gewalt in letzter Zeit unterschätzt wurde, zeigt sich exemplarisch an den offiziellen Einschätzungen des Nachrichtendiensts des Bundes. Im aktuellen Lagebericht «Sicherheit Schweiz 2026» steht, dass «Exponent:innen der gewalttätigen rechtsextremistischen Szene im Vergleich zu früheren Jahren häufig unscheinbarer und verbal überlegter auftreten» würden. Das bringe einzelnen Gruppen neue Anhänger:innen. Eine Bedrohung durch gewalttätige Rechtsextremist:innen bleibe zwar bestehen, aber «ausserhalb organisierter rechtsextremistischer Strukturen agierende Personen stellen die grössere Bedrohung dar als ganze Gruppierungen». Diese Einschätzung hat sich nach der Gewaltnacht von Tuggen als falsch erwiesen. title: Bukele invade Haití: ¿el primer gendarme de Trump en América Latina?
content:
Imagen: @Reuters


El envío de 2.000 soldados salvadoreños a Haití coincide con la doctrina de seguridad de Estados Unidos, que propone apoyarse en “campeones regionales” capaces de imponer estabilidad más allá de sus fronteras. La alianza entre Trump y Bukele ya había convertido al CECOT en una cárcel externalizada para deportados desde Estados Unidos. ¿Es Bukele el primer y nuevo «brazo armado» de Trump en América Latina?

Por Manuel Medina (*) para Canarias Semanal.


   Haití

ha vuelto a

 aplazar las elecciones

cuya celebración estaba prevista el próximo mes de

diciembre.

 La primera vuelta presidencial y legislativa se celebrará ahora en

 julio del próximo año de 2027;

 la segunda, junto a las elecciones locales, en

 octubre.

Si el nuevo calendario llegara a cumplirse,

será la primera convocatoria nacional desde 2016.

 La presidencia permanece

vacante

 desde el asesinato de

Jovenel Moïse

 en 2021 y el país continúa

dirigido por un primer ministro sin mandato electoral.


Ese vacío político coincide con el envío de unos

2.000 soldados salvadoreños

 ordenado por

Nayib Bukele.

 La explicación oficial es el rescate de cuatro técnicos de aviación desaparecidos el 18 de octubre tras una emboscada en

Croix-des-Bouquets

, cerca de

 Puerto Príncipe.


Bukele

 ha insistido en que la misión concluirá

cuando sus compatriotas regresen a casa y ha rechazado, naturalmente, que se trate de una invasión.


Pero el

tamaño del contingente

, la ausencia de información precisa sobre su mandato y el apoyo logístico estadounidense obligan a mirar más allá de esa explicación. No es frecuente que un país centroamericano de poco más de

seis millones de habitantes

 proyecte de

golpe miles de militares sobre un tercer país latinoamericano.

 Menos aún en

 Haití

, donde toda presencia armada exterior despierta inevitablemente la memoria de pasadas

ocupaciones, tutelas y misiones internacionales

que no han resuelto la

 destrucción del Estado

 ni

la inmensa pobreza

de la mayoría de la población.


La cuestión central no consiste en si

Washington

 ha dictado a

 Bukele

cada movimiento. No existen pruebas tangibles de una orden directa de

Trump

 al presidente salvadoreño. La cuestión es otra: es si

El Salvador

 está asumiendo, bajo una bandera propia, una

 tarea de seguridad regional

que

conviene a Estados Unidos,

 evitando a

Washington

 el desgaste político de intervenir de manera abierta.


EL “COROLARIO TRUMP” DE LA DOCTRINA MONROE


La

Estrategia de Seguridad Nacional

estadounidense presentada por la

Administración Trump

 a finales de

2025

 ofrece una clave para entender el escenario. El documento anuncia un

 “corolario Trump”

de la

Doctrina Monroe

 y plantea restaurar la

“preeminencia”

 de

Estados Unidos

 en el hemisferio occidental. No se limita a la competencia con

China, Rusia o Irán:

 incluye

migración, narcotráfico, rutas marítimas, infraestructuras estratégicas y crisis políticas

 capaces de afectar a los intereses norteamericanos.


La formulación es significativa.

Washington

 declara que debe

 “reclutar y ampliar”:

 reclutar gobiernos amigos para controlar los flujos migratorios, combatir las drogas y

reforzar la seguridad;

 ampliar esa red mediante

nuevos socios

. El texto añadía que

Estados Unidos

 debe apoyarse en

“campeones regionales”

capaces de crear una

 “estabilidad tolerable”

 incluso

más allá de sus fronteras

.


Soldados salvadoreños. Foto: AFP


 


La idea está muy clara.

Estados Unidos

 no necesita situarse

siempre en primera línea

si para ese tipo de menesteres  drásticos y directos puede disponer de

gobiernos aliados

 que compartan sus prioridades politicas y estén dispuestos a asumir una parte de las tareas

represivas, policiales o militares.


   Washington

 conserva

inteligencia, financiación, logística, capacidad diplomática y dirección estratégica

; los

gobiernos subsidiarios

 que se prestasen a ello aportarían 

cárceles, tropas, territorio, policía o cobertura regional.


Bukele

 encaja con especial facilidad en

 esa función

. Su gobierno ha convertido

la guerra contra las pandillas

en la

principal fuente de legitimidad interna

, ha hecho de la excepcionalidad jurídica una forma estable de gobierno y ha presentado las

 detenciones masivas

 como un

modelo exportable

.


Para

 Washington, El Salvador

 ofrece algo

más que afinidad ideológica

: dispone de una

gran cárcel

 de máxima seguridad, una …

title: De la misère en milieu lycéen
content:
1969, la crise de mai et juin 1968 ne s'est toujours pas refermée. La politisation de la jeunesse est constante et ses sursauts spontanés jalonnent les mois. Les lycéens se sont lancés dans la bataille d'abord par les comités Vietnam, puis dans l'explosion du joli mois de mai et ses comités d'action lycéens (CAL). Ils s'activent pour défaire les carcans : séparation des genres, interdiction des activités politiques dans les lycées, refus des lycées-taules ou lycées-casernes. Pour accompagner cette agitation constante, un groupe autour du journal

Passer outre

 [

1

]

 édite une brochure

De la misère en milieu lycéen (et autres scolarisés)

. Notre archiviste est parvenu à mettre la main sur un exemplaire. Cette brochure nous informe sur les préoccupations de la jeunesse de l'époque qui n'apparaissent finalement pas si éloignées de celles d'aujourd'hui.


1 • Dernier sermon dans le désert


Ce qui caractérise a priori le lycée c'est, outre le caractère d'immuabilité de son institution, sa similitude avec l'ensemble superstructurel de la société et son corollaire immédiat : l'aberration de sa double aliénation physique et mentale. L'incroyable institution est née d'un régime politique et social qui ne pouvait produire dans sa conception fasciste, que des entreprises de déshumanisation : des prisons, des casernes et des lycées. Ainsi depuis le factieux du dix-huit Brumaire il a traversé les années, les gouvernements, les régimes, dûment protégé par le pouvoir, qui de tout temps y a vu le moule, parfait producteur des générations de chiens de garde. Dès la fin de son enfance l'individu se trouve ainsi propulsé dans une micro-société où l'on se chargera de l'introduire dans les formes et le contenu de l'aliénation généralisée. Le lycée apparait comme un des stages de redressement et comme une des périodes de matraquage et de répression intellectuels qui jalonnent la non-vie accordée par le pouvoir.


Premier appareil répressif ; le lycéen apprend le respect de la pléthore administrative. Du pion au surveillant général la dépendance est totale. Imbriqué dans un système horaire qui délimite son temps de déglutition culturelle, il partage son aliénation entre la dictature de professeurs fossilisés et celle de garde-


chiourmes au titre évocateur de surveillant. Asservi, réprimé, brimé, le lycéen apprend vite la soumission. Par le système de valeur établi, il comprend que la condition de sa « réussite scolaire » dépend de sa capacité d'adaptation à l'appareil. Par suite la condition de sa « réussite sociale » dépend du succès de cette adaptation. L'échelle des valeurs entre récompense et punition, assez justement répartie dans les classes primaires entre conduite et travail, permet facilement le clivage entre l'adapté et l'inadapté.


Le premier poursuivra une scolarité dont l'éclat sera proportionnel à son taux progressif d'asservissement, et le deuxième se verra rejette hors de l'entreprise et de fait hors de toute possibilité d'accession aux parcelles de pouvoir. On aperçoit donc facilement, dans sa structure hiérarchique et autoritaire, le tremplin que le


lycée constitue à court terme pour les jeunes rejetés vers les emplois d'éxécutants et de manœuvres au sens large du terme (ils auront tout le loisir d'apprécier la servitude du travail dans les délais les plus brefs), et à long terme pour ceux qui constitueront la docile technocratie de relève. Ceux-ci seront généralement transférés à leur sortie du secondaire dans les « grandes écoles » scientifiques où l'achèvement de leur formation se fera dans des cadres para-militaires. La garantie de leur adaptation, et par suite de leur aptitude dans leur future fonction, est ainsi totale par le conditionnement de leur milieu scolaire.


Etabli de manière autoritaire, le temps de présence est rendu obligatoire et le système punitif est conçu bien souvent sur un allongement de ce temps. Le principe des colles est le constat de l'esclavage physique que représente le temps de présence.


Micro-société jusque dans sa juridiction, le lycée possède ses lois (les règlements), ses flics (l'appareil de surveillance), ses tribunaux (le conseil de discipline). Le lycéen dans son lycée évolue dans des rapports disciplinaires comparables à ceux du soldat dans sa caserne.


Caserne, le lycée l'est dans sa forme architecturale comme dans sa forme sociale. Divisé bien souvent entre lycée de filles et lycée de garçons, la sectorisation interne est poussée au maximum : année, section …

title: Profanations
content:
D'un pur point de vu comptable, le butin des pillages du 17 octobre reste assez modeste. N'importe quelle inondation, sécheresse, catastrophe écologique ou

piratage de frigos de supermarché

 s'accompagne de son lot de marchandises perdues. Comment s'expliquer alors que les évènements récents aient suscité pareille terreur dans les ministères et sur les plateaux télé ? Peut-être que les manifestants d'octobre n'ont pas seulement volé, redistribué ou détruit des marchandises mais qu'ils ont d'abord et par-dessus tout

profané

 quelque chose de sacré.


Que font ces ordres de vandales, en ce mois de mars 1871, déferlant des Aventins Grand-parisiens sur le centre de la capitale ? C'est la ville qui libère la ville ; c'est la marge qui récupère sa ville.


Que font ces ordres de vandales, en ce mois d'octobre 2026, déferlant des Aventins ultra-parisiens sur le centre de Paris ? C'est la banlieue qui braque la ville ; c'est le ban qui se libère.


* * *


Que signifie libérer ? Libérer signifie restituer au monde commun ce qu'une pernicieuse opération avait préalablement retranché de l'usage, du monde, du quotidien : libérer veut dire

profaner

.


Les communards, les communardes, celles et ceux qui prennent les rues, les arrondissements, les diocèses, qui grouillent désormais dans l'étendue parisienne, qui prennent finalement l'hôtel de ville en soirée, ce 18 mars 1871, proclament, véritablement et d'abord sans besoin de cérémonie officielle, que cette ville leur appartient. Ces communardes et communards achèvent – pour 72 jours à tout le moins – la reconquête de la ville par la ville

 [

1

]

. C'est cela que Commune veut dire : non pas ce qui nous appartient en propre, mais ce que l'on reprend. Profaner est une action ; cela nécessite de disputer une chose que le pouvoir avait rendue

indisponible

, c'est-à-dire sacrée.


On s'est souvent demandé si la Commune constituait le crépuscule des révolutions politiques ou l'aube des révolutions sociales ? Question oiseuse, dans la mesure où celles et ceux qui œuvraient sur les barricades, occupaient les églises, s'écharpaient dans les clubs, organisaient les bureaux de bienfaisance, tenaient des cantines populaires, patrouillaient dans les bataillons sédentaires ou marchaient dans ceux de guerre, n'avait que faire de donner l'heure aux historien

·

nes du futur. Ce que ces gens faisaient, c'était restituer au libre usage des hommes et des femmes un espace que l'on avait minéralisé

 [

2

]

, muséifiée ; ou, pour faire plus 19

e

, haussmannisé.


Paris fut « libérée » bien avant 1944. La ville avait été d'abord sacrifiée aux forces de l'Empire et de l'Église, haussmannisée deux fois : rationalisation urbaine + rationalisation religieuse. La destruction du bâti ancien et la construction d'avenues immenses percèrent la ville pour la rendre lisible, fluide à la circulation des marchandises et des lignards. Ces percées étaient aussi religieuses, sacrés. Le diocèse partait à l'exploration de cette nouvelle ville grouillante, peuplée de nouveaux arrivé

·

es monté

·

es à la capitale et peuplant les communes suburbaines, bientôt intégrées au « grand Paris » d'alors – les Batignolles, Montmartre, Belleville, Charonne…


Ces trouées missionnaires et policières participaient d'un processus de sanctuarisation de l'espace – Paris avait été, littéralement, sacrifiée, c'est-à-dire en partie retirée à l'usage des personnes qui la peuplait. La consécration de Paris, capitale du 19

e

 siècle, des Expositions universelles, vitrine du commerce du luxe et du colonialisme, minéralise la ville : embellit au centre, honteuse à ses abords. Paris devint un Musée. Le

« Musée

, écrit Agamben,

ne désigne pas ici un lieu ou un espace physiquement déterminé, mais la dimension où est transféré ce qui a cessé d'être perçu comme vrai et décisif »

.
