title: People of Kobanê celebrate World Kobanê Day
content:
World Kobanê Day was marked with a public celebration in Kobanê on November 1. Under the slogan “In memory of the heroic martyrs – Long live World Kobanê Day,” large numbers of people gathered to commemorate the resistance against the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS) in 2014 and those who lost their lives. The event focused on the historical significance of the resistance, the leading role of women, and the defense of the achievements of the revolution in Rojava.


The celebration began with a minute of silence in memory of the martyrs. Ferhan Hec Îsa then addressed the gathering on behalf of the people of Kobanê. He paid tribute to those who had defended the city against ISIS attacks and made its liberation possible.


“November 1, World Kobanê Day, is not merely a day of remembrance on the calendar. This date represents the epic resistance through which the people of Kobanê rose up against the attacks of dark forces in 2014 and emerged victorious. Today, Kobanê is known worldwide as a city that has entered the history of resistance and dignity through its struggle against ISIS,” Hec Îsa said.


He called for the achievements won through the struggle to be preserved: “Kobanê is a city that belongs to all of us. We must defend the achievements of the resistance of Kobanê.”


Women paved the way for victory


Perwîn Yûsif, Co-Chair of the Democratic Union Party (PYD), spoke on behalf of the women’s movement. She highlighted the crucial role of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) and the People’s Protection Units (YPG) in the liberation of Kobanê.


“The resistance, which has continued under women’s leadership to this day, has brought about major achievements. The resistance in North and East Syria has become a symbol for the entire Middle East. ISIS mercenaries and their supporters had no regard for human values. They murdered women and children and destroyed entire cities. Yet thanks to the resistance of YPJ and YPG fighters, the fight to push back ISIS began in Kobanê.”


Yûsif emphasized that defending the revolution remained a central responsibility: “What is required of us today is to protect the achievements of our revolution, continue the struggle in the spirit of November 1, and achieve historic victories.”


The celebration then continued with a cultural program featuring performances by kamancheh player Zêrîn Ararat and musician Xelîl Can. The event concluded with slogans including “Long live the resistance of Kobanê,” “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî,” and “No life without the leader.”

author: Unknown
title: Women’s conference in Ankara criticizes stagnation in the peace process
content:
The stalled peace process in Turkey and the responsibility of politicians and society to achieve a democratic solution to the Kurdish question dominated the second day of the women’s conference in Ankara. Discussions focused on the lack of concrete political steps, the unequal conditions surrounding negotiations with Abdullah Öcalan, and how women from different social and political backgrounds could work together to achieve lasting peace. Participants made it clear that while they regarded an end to the armed conflict as a crucial step forward, they did not consider it sufficient in itself to guarantee peace in society.


The conference, titled “Women Discuss the Future Side by Side,” was initiated by 80 women and opened on Saturday with more than 500 participants. On the second day, female politicians, academics, and activists gathered at the Chamber of Civil Engineers to discuss political responsibility for peace, the role of parliament, and opportunities for grassroots organizing.


Buldan warns of deadlock in the peace process


Pervin Buldan, a DEM Party MP and member of the Imralı delegation, recalled the failed peace negotiations between 2013 and 2015 and the subsequent ten years of armed conflict. She emphasized that the most significant achievement of both the previous and current talks was the protection of human lives. At the same time, she pointed to the unequal conditions under which the political actors involved were operating. While President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and MHP leader Devlet Bahçeli are able to carry out their political duties freely, she said, Abdullah Öcalan is attempting to advance the process from a prison cell. She explicitly expressed her gratitude to him for his efforts.


However, Buldan expressed concern about the current state of the talks. T”he Imralı delegation last visited Öcalan on September 13. There has been no further meeting since that day. So, there is something of a deadlock. Overcoming this impasse should not be left solely to the political negotiators. Women in this room can decide today that we need peace. They can become an organized force that puts pressure on the government and the actors involved in the process to ensure that it continues,” she said.


Buldan also proposed establishing dedicated women’s committees within the structures responsible for overseeing and monitoring the peace process. She stressed that women must come together not only in conference halls but also in public squares and on the streets.


Criticism over the delayed implementation of the framework law


Gökçe Gökçen, an MP from the YENI Party, criticized the government’s approach so far. She emphasized that the Kurdish question and the democratization of Turkey were inseparably linked, arguing that limiting the process to disarmament alone would be insufficient. “One side says that this is exclusively a matter of security and therefore calls the entire process a ‘terror-free Turkey.’ We, on the other hand, speak of a ‘democratic Turkey,’” Gökçen stated.


She stressed that laying down arms was important but must be accompanied by democratic reforms. Lasting social peace, she argued, required equality to become a lived reality and public confidence in justice to grow.


Gökçen was particularly critical of the delays in implementing the framework law passed by parliament on August 10. She said the text of the law had been presented only at the last moment, without allowing for a broad political debate. Unlike other political groups, her party was not invited to participate in the discussions, she added.


“Distrust of the process is, in fact, distrust of the government,” Gökçen said. She argued that the government had had numerous opportunities to take confidence-building measures but had failed to do so. She stressed that making the implementation of the law dependent on a decision by the National Security Council (MGK), thereby postponing it indefinitely, was neither politically nor legally justifiable.


“Peace is too serious a matter to be left to men and governments”


Former HDP MP Filiz Kerestecioğlu emphasized society’s responsibility in the peace process. Peace negotiations, she argued, should not be treated as a technical matter reserved for political decision-makers. “Peace is too serious a matter to be left to men and governments. It is also too serious to be treated as a purely technical issue. Society must be convinced of the process and actively participate in shaping it,” …

author: Unknown
title: TEV-DEM calls for guarantees for Kurdish rights and protection of achievements
content:
On the occasion of World Kobanê Day on November 1, the Movement for a Democratic Society (TEV-DEM) and its Women’s Council issued separate statements commemorating the historic resistance against the so-called Islamic State (ISIS).


While TEV-DEM emphasized Kobanê’s significance in the struggle for democracy and human dignity and warned against one-sided integration in Syria, the Women’s Council focused on the role of women in defending the city and safeguarding their political and social achievements.


‘Integration does not mean assimilation’


TEV-DEM described the resistance of Kobanê as a historic process whose significance extended far beyond geographical and political boundaries. The movement pointed out that the defense of the city had become a global symbol of freedom, social diversity, and the protection of human dignity. “The international solidarity shown by democratic movements, intellectuals, and numerous prominent figures demonstrated that the struggle for humanity transcended both national and religious boundaries,” it underlined.


Regarding the political restructuring of Syria, the movement warned against attempts to exclude Kurds from the process of building the new state or disregard their achievements. It cautioned that any attempt to impose integration unilaterally would pose significant risks. “Integration does not mean assimilating a people’s identity or demanding that they abandon their national identity, culture, and political rights. Instead, integration must be a collective process of state-building in which the distinct identities, rights, and achievements of all social groups are protected,” TEV-DEM stated.


The movement emphasized that those who defended Kobanê against ISIS deserved to live in peace, security, freedom, and dignity. It called on national and democratic forces, as well as intellectuals and prominent figures who had supported the resistance, to continue advocating for the rights of the Kurdish people.


Women’s Council pledges to continue the struggle


In its statement, the TEV-DEM Women’s Council described November 1 as a historic day symbolizing the collective resistance of peoples against terrorism and their determination to defend themselves. The Council emphasized that ISIS, through its ideology and violence, had particularly targeted the existence and freedom of women.


“The people of Kobanê, along with young men and women in the ranks of the People’s Protection Units (YPG) and Women’s Protection Units (YPJ), stood up against this threat. With the support of the Peshmerga, historic resistance emerged, sparking solidarity worldwide and leading to the declaration of World Kobanê Day.”


The Women’s Council highlighted the fact that Kurdish women had not only played a leading role in the military defense of the city but had also demonstrated their capacity for social self-governance and shaping a democratic future. The Council pledged to continue their struggle to defend the rights and achievements won through their resistance at the political, social, cultural, diplomatic, and constitutional levels.

title: İlk yarıda öne geçti, ikinci yarıya golle başladı: Beşiktaş farkı açtı
content:
Süper Lig'in 10. haftasında Beşiktaş, Kasımpaşa deplasmanında 2-0 öne geçti. İlk yarıyı Leandro Trossard'ın golüyle 1-0 önde tamamlayan siyah-beyazlılar, ikinci yarının ilk dakikasında Dusan Vlahovic'in golüyle farkı ikiye çıkardı.

Süper Lig'in 10. haftasında Beşiktaş, Kasımpaşa'ya konuk oldu. Recep Tayyip Erdoğan Stadı'nda saat 19.00'da başlayan karşılaşmayı hakem Reşat Onur Coşkunses yönetiyor.

Ev sahibi Kasımpaşa ise 16 puanla mücadeleye çıktı. Lacivert-beyazlı ekip, Beşiktaş karşısında galip gelerek üst üste üçüncü galibiyetini almak istiyor.

Kasımpaşa: Andreas, Arous, Ilie, Winck, Ayberk, Kerem, Mendes, Hajradinovic, Rak-Sakyi, Ali Yavuz, Benedyczak.

6' Kasımpaşa'nın kart itirazının ardından Beşiktaş gole yaklaştı. Kaleciyle karşı karşıya kalan Trossard, fırsatı değerlendiremedi.

7' Hakeme yoğun itirazlarda bulunan Kasımpaşa Teknik Direktörü Emre Belözoğlu sarı kart gördü.

15' Beşiktaş gole yaklaştı. Cerny'nin ceza sahası içinden yaptığı vuruşta top, kalenin sağından auta çıktı.

28' GOL | Beşiktaş öne geçti! Rıdvan Yılmaz'ın pasında topla buluşan Leandro Trossard, fileleri havalandırdı: 0-1.

title: Enes Ünal gol attı, Getafe Sevilla'yı 3-1 mağlup etti
content:
Fotoğraf: www.realvalladolid.es/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 4.0

İspanya LaLiga'nın 11. haftasında Getafe, milli futbolcu Enes Ünal'ın gol attığı karşılaşmada Sevilla'yı 3-1 yendi. İlk yarıyı geride kapatan Getafe, ikinci yarıda bulduğu gollerle galibiyete uzandı. Sevilla'da Manu Bueno, 90+1. dakikada kırmızı kart gördü.

İspanya Birinci Futbol Ligi'nde (LaLiga) Getafe ile Sevilla karşı karşıya geldi. Coliseum Stadı'nda oynanan mücadeleyi ev sahibi Getafe 3-1 kazandı. Milli futbolcu Enes Ünal, Getafe'nin ilk golünü kaydederek takımının geri dönüşünde rol oynadı.

Karşılaşmada Sevilla, 19. dakikada Kike Salas'ın attığı golle 1-0 öne geçti ve ilk yarıyı bu skorla tamamladı.

İkinci yarıda baskısını artıran Getafe, 68. dakikada Enes Ünal'ın golüyle eşitliği sağladı. Ev sahibi ekip, 74. dakikada Martin Satriano'nun golüyle 2-1 öne geçti.

Sevilla'da Manu Bueno, 90+1. dakikada kırmızı kartla oyun dışında kaldı. Getafe, 90+4. dakikada Orel Mangala'nın golüyle farkı ikiye çıkardı ve sahadan 3-1 galip ayrıldı.

Bu sonuçla Getafe puanını 12'ye yükseltti. Sevilla ise 17 puanda kaldı.

title: Humanitarian conditions deteriorate in Washokani and Al-Talae camps
content:
The humanitarian conditions of displaced families living in the Washokani and Al-Talae camps in Syria’s Hesekê Governorate have further deteriorated following recent rainfall and flooding. The Serêkaniyê Displaced Persons Committee has called for urgent shelter assistance ahead of winter season and for the process of returning families to their hometowns to be expedited.


Speaking to Shafaq News, committee spokesperson Mahmud Cemîl said that the tents in both camps had deteriorated and could no longer provide adequate protection against rain, cold weather and extreme heat. Cemîl said the committee had been requesting support and new tents from humanitarian organisations for seven years, but these requests had not been adequately addressed.


Returns should accelerate


Cemîl said that displaced families were facing administrative delays and various obstacles in returning to their hometowns. He called on the Syrian government to expand organised return convoys and increase the number of families able to return.


Cemîl also urged the Syrian presidential delegation overseeing the return process, international organisations and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to support efforts to accelerate returns before winter conditions make life in the camps even more difficult.


3,278 families returned in six convoys


Since August, a total of 3,278 families have returned to their hometowns through six organised return convoys.


Some of the families returned to Serêkaniyê and its surrounding countryside, while others returned to settle in villages around Til Temir, Zirgan and Abu Rasin, north of Hesekê.

title: 7,000-year-old architectural model discovered in Soran
content:
The General Directorate of Antiquities and Cultural Heritage of the Kurdistan Region has announced a significant archaeological discovery at Banahîlk Hill in the Soran district, northeast of Erbil.


In a statement, the directorate said that a rare model of an ancient building's roofing system, dating back more than 7,000 years and belonging to the Halaf culture, had been discovered. Describing the find as a first in archaeological history, the statement noted that it demonstrates the advanced engineering and architectural skills of communities during that period.


The discovery was announced to the public at a press conference held on 28 October at the Scientific Research Centre of Soran University. The archaeological project was carried out in cooperation with the Soran Directorate of Antiquities and Culture, the Autonomous University of Barcelona (UAB) and Salahaddin University.


The Halaf culture, dating approximately from 6100 to 5100 BC, was influential mainly across the lands of Southern Kurdistan (Başûr), Western Kurdistan (Rojava) and Northern Kurdistan (Bakurê Kurdistan). Known for its distinctive pottery decorated with geometric patterns and animal motifs, this culture provides important archaeological evidence of the prehistoric history of Mesopotamia and the Near East.

author: Unknown
title: DEM Party’s message on 1 November, World Kobanê Day
content:
The DEM Party’s Central Executive Board (MYK) issued a written statement to mark 1 November, World Kobanê Day. The statement said: "On 15 September 2014, ISIS, which is hostile to different faiths, identities, cultures and the will of peoples to live together, launched a major attack on Kobanê. In response to the ISIS gangs’ assault on Kobanê, the peoples of the world—particularly the Kurdish people—and internationalist resistance fighters who travelled to Kobanê from all corners of the globe waged an epic resistance against ISIS.


Faced with this historic resistance, which lasted 134 days, the ISIS gangs and the forces behind them suffered a major defeat. The victory won in Kobanê, embraced by peoples across the world and marking a turning point in the beginning of a new history in the Middle East, carries even greater international significance today."


The statement added: "Developed under the leadership of the women’s struggle, the Kobanê resistance laid the groundwork for the Kurdish people to secure their identity-related, cultural and historical rights. It also enabled the development of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which today represents a hope for an equal and free life.


The devastating social consequences of the wars of interest waged by imperialist and regional powers, particularly in the Middle East, during this historic period we are living through have once again demonstrated just how vital Mr Abdullah Öcalan’s Call for Peace and a Democratic Society, issued on 27 February 2025, truly is."


The statement continued: "In the 12th year of the Kobanê resistance, we salute the struggle, led by women, through which a great victory was achieved against the order hostile to humanity that the ISIS gangs sought to establish. May 1 November, World Kobanê Day—proclaimed through the united struggle of peoples around the world against those seeking to destroy human values—be a blessed day for all the peoples of the world, especially the peoples of the Middle East.


We respectfully commemorate those who lost their lives in Kobanê, particularly women, who sacrificed themselves to protect humanity."

author: Unknown
title: Kongra Star calls to continue to protect the city on World Kobanê Day
content:
Kongra Star issued a statement to mark 1 November, World Kobanê Day. The statement commemorated the historic sacrifices made in the fight against ISIS mercenaries in 2014, while highlighting the current and future challenges Kobanê is facing.


The statement paid tribute to the martyrs of the resistance, particularly Arin Mirkan. It stressed that the determination demonstrated by the resistance was no longer confined to the city's geographical boundaries, but had become deeply rooted in humanity's collective memory and conscience as a struggle for freedom and human dignity, placing an ongoing responsibility on everyone to preserve these values.


The statement noted that 1 November represents an "epic of resilience" by a people who refused to bow to darkness. It said that, through their unwavering determination and international solidarity from across the world, the resistance fighters managed to break the siege of the city and repel ISIS attacks, turning Kobanê into an international symbol of ISIS's defeat and a renewed source of hope for peoples worldwide.


Kongra Star underlined that what happened in Kobanê went beyond the military defence of a city, representing instead a defence of a model of coexistence, equality and solidarity that transcends political, linguistic and ideological boundaries. It noted that the experience demonstrated how local resistance can become a universal human value.


Kobanê still needs to be protected


The statement warned of the current threats surrounding Kobanê's future, rejecting any attempt to reduce its cause to mere "administrative arrangements, political calculations or pressure over borders."


Kongra Star said that any harm to Kobanê's social fabric and spirit would constitute an attack on the shared memory of the resistance. It called for the city's security concerns and future to be addressed with the utmost seriousness, while warning against any acts of revenge or settling of scores that could pave the way for terrorist organisations to regain strength.


Kongra Star ended its statement calling on "democratic, socialist and internationalist forces, as well as human rights defenders worldwide, to fulfil their responsibilities towards Kobanê's security and the will of its people. It stressed that protecting the city today is an extension of the spirit of international solidarity witnessed in 2014 and an effort to keep the light of freedom from being extinguished."

author: Unknown
title: Mining destroys Chaldean village's nature and heritage
content:
Aksu (Harbol in Syriac), a historic Assyrian settlement located at the foot of Mount Cûdî in the Silopi (Silopiya) district of Şırnak (Şirnex), is just one of countless places affected by the destruction of nature for the benefit of capital.

Yeni Yaş

am

 said in a feature that mining operations established in the village's rural areas and on the slopes of Mount Cûdî over the past decade have completely transformed the landscape. The surroundings of the village, which were covered in greenery in 2015 and earlier, are now almost entirely devoid of vegetation. The mining sites are reportedly located on the village's former settlement area, and almost no trees remain in the region. Ecological destruction in Botan accelerated with the intensification of the war in 2015.


For years, Botan's natural environment, much of which has been declared off-limits, has been destroyed under military supervision and through the activities of village guards. The ecological destruction that began with forest fires has continued through tree felling, mining and oil exploration.


The mountain's silhouette has changed


Satellite images and photographs showing the surroundings of the village reveal terraced excavations and exposed layers of soil across much of the mountainous area. The mines, which threaten village life, are located just a few hundred metres from the settlement. The excavations have exposed successive layers of the mountainside, revealing different soil colours ranging from red to white. The mountain's silhouette has been visibly altered. Another striking aspect is that these operations have been carried out for years in an area where civilian access is prohibited. The extent of the destruction on one side of the mountain can be clearly seen by comparing it with the preserved vegetation on the opposite slope.


The village's historical remains have been destroyed


Satellite images of the mining area also show the remains of Harbol's former settlement. The mining operations have not only devastated the natural environment but have also destroyed the village's historical remains, erasing traces of its past. The large number of gendarmerie stations at the village entrance and in the surrounding area is reportedly linked to the provision of security support for mining operations. Soldiers are said to have prevented residents from filming or photographing the environmental destruction. This militarised dimension, in which extractivism operates alongside security-driven policies, is also examined in the 2025 position paper

Militarisation Is Extractivism: From Mines to Missiles

, translated into Turkish by the Polen Ecology Collective. The paper explores the relationship between mining and militarism on a global scale.


The village was evacuated in the 1990s


Harbol, located on the slopes of Mount Cûdî in Şırnak's Silopi district, was forcibly evacuated between 1990 and 1993 on the grounds of "security". The village's entire population consisted of Assyrian-Chaldean residents. Those forced to leave migrated to major cities in western Turkey, as well as France and other European countries. Returns to the village began in 2014. Today, only seven families live in Herbol. Other former residents visit temporarily before returning to the places where they settled after being displaced.


Destruction across Mount Cûdî and the Euphrates-Tigris Basin


The Extractivism Map shows that intensive mining and other environmentally destructive projects are continuing across the Euphrates-Tigris river basin, which covers an area of 176,258 square kilometres, alongside active projects on Mount Cûdî. In Şırnak alone, 135 mining projects entered the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) process between the beginning of 2023 and 8 February 2026. The Extractivism Map illustrates the extent of these activities across Mount Cûdî and the wider Euphrates-Tigris Basin.

author: Unknown
title: Özgür Sevgi Göral: France’s dilemmas also exist in Turkey - Part One
content:
Academic Özgür Sevgi Göral said that a strong voice had emerged against inequality in Paris, adding, "Reducing the revolt of the suburbs, which demands profound transformation, to presidential elections would dilute the movement's anger and enthusiasm." Göral said that all the dilemmas facing France were also present in Turkey.


The streets of Paris have witnessed some of the most intense social mobilisation of recent times. Protests that began in September, led by high school students, grew into a mass movement day by day.


ANF spoke to Özgür Sevgi Göral, who is currently in Paris and has participated in the demonstrations, about the historical foundations of the protests and their potential.


Academic Özgür Sevgi Göral emphasised that the protests were rooted in a historical accumulation of struggles, saying, "This history includes the inequalities created by racialised capitalism and the many different forms of violence it has spread throughout everyday life."  Göral stressed the importance of the struggle, saying, "The struggle truly is endless, and despite all the difficult conditions, millions of people around the world refuse to abandon the streets."


Göral argued that the protests should be understood less in relation to 1968 and more in the context of the political mobilisation and suburban uprisings that emerged in the 1970s and 1980s and continued strongly throughout the 2000s. Göral also warned that directing the anti-fascist stance solely towards the April 2027 presidential elections risked alienating young people from the suburbs in particular.


Göral also assessed what kind of political ground, language and methodology were needed today to address the Kurdish question. Göral emphasised the importance of convincing broad sections of society that the current process could provide a foundation for a shared life based on equality and freedom and said: "Since the state will not provide this foundation, it will have to be built by all movements for equality, freedom and liberation, particularly the Kurdish Freedom Movement, by drawing on their capacities and establishing the broadest possible alliances. In fact, all the dilemmas we have discussed in relation to France are also present in Turkey, although, of course, in different forms."


You also participated in the demonstrations in Paris. What were your observations on the streets? What were the differences between the official narrative and the situation on the ground?


The high school protests in Paris are actually rooted in a particular historical background. This history includes the inequalities created by racialised capitalism and the many different forms of violence it has spread throughout everyday life. The more immediate historical background to this movement includes the severe class inequalities experienced during last year's extreme heatwaves in Paris, which claimed thousands of lives, particularly in schools in the suburbs. Even when temperatures reached 40 degrees Celsius, secondary schools were not provided with fans. There are also the structural inequalities associated with Parcoursup, the university admissions system, which separates students attending privileged high schools from those attending schools in working-class neighbourhoods, and the experience of collapsing public services, including education and healthcare, in suburban neighbourhoods.


The mobilisation began after the teachers' strike held in Paris and its suburbs on 29 September, which demanded greater public funding for public services. One of my favourite slogans, "The suburbs influence Paname, and Paname influences the world" (Paname is another name for Paris), resonated strongly. The blockades of high schools, which first began in Seine-Saint-Denis, gained strong support first in Paris's privileged high schools and then in higher education institutions. Saturday demonstrations in Paris, led by youth movements, attracted enormous crowds. Despite the extraordinary level of police violence, participation did not decline but continued to increase. According to figures from the General Confederation of Labour (CGT), 250,000 people participated in the Paris demonstration on 24 October, while more than 800,000 people joined demonstrations across France.


From the outset, the official narrative framed the wave of protests within a security paradigm. It categorically refused to discuss the profound structures of inequality highlighted by the demonstrations, the class …

title: İpek Er’s mother: My daughter was killed a second time
content:
“My daughter was killed a second time today.” With these words, Hikmet Kılınç, the mother of Kurdish woman İpek Er, who died in 2020, protested the recent acquittal of former gendarmerie officer Musa Orhan at a women’s conference in Ankara. Six years after her daughter’s death, she has leveled serious accusations against state officials and announced her determination to continue her fight for justice all the way to the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR).


The protest follows a ruling issued on October 22 by a criminal court in Batman. Musa Orhan, who was sentenced to ten years in prison in 2021 for a serious sexual assault against İpek Er, was acquitted of the charge of incitement to suicide in a separate trial. According to Kılınç, the decision represents another setback in her years-long struggle to secure legal accountability for her daughter’s death.


Addressing more than 500 participants at the “Women Discuss the Future Side by Side” conference, Kılınç recounted her experiences since her daughter’s death. She accused state authorities of exploiting her hopes for justice and attempting to exert political pressure on her. “For six years, they told me: If you stay away from the Kurdish parties, we will ensure justice for your daughter. After six years, they acquitted him,” Kılınç said. She explained that she had sold all her possessions and moved to Batman. “Under the pretext of defending my daughter’s rights, they deceived me.”


The mother also directed her criticism at former Turkish Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu, accusing him of protecting Orhan and facilitating his acquittal. At the same time, she appealed to Kurdish members of parliament not to lose sight of the case. “My daughter’s blood must not go unavenged. As long as I live, I will fight for her rights. I will pursue this case all the way to the ECtHR,” Kılınç said. “My daughter was killed by someone who wielded state power. As long as the perpetrator walks free, there can be no talk of justice.”


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/b62c3f26_20261031121003_2026-10-31-ankara-hikmet-kilinc-ipek-er-annesi-kadinlar-yan-yana-gelecegi-konusuyor-konferansi-cagri-1.mp4


Allegations of threats and abuse


In her speech, Kılınç also described the violence and intimidation her daughter had endured. According to her mother, İpek had been manipulated and subjected to pressure. She had been threatened with the killing of her father and brother, and there had even been an attempt to sell her. “İpek’s hair is evidence of the torture she suffered. I still have my daughter’s bloodstained clothes,” Kılınç said. She said she continues to preserve her daughter’s personal belongings to this day.


Kılınç made these statements at the two-day women’s conference held at the Chamber of Civil Engineers in Ankara. Since Saturday, journalists, academics, politicians, and activists have been discussing peace, justice, equal citizenship, and the struggle against patriarchal violence.


Six years of legal proceedings


On July 7, 2020, İpek Er filed a criminal complaint against Musa Orhan with the public prosecutor’s office in Siirt. Orhan was serving as a professional soldier in the district of Beşiri at the time. Er stated that he had been raped by him. On July 16, she attempted suicide after leaving a farewell letter. After spending 34 days in hospital, she died on August 18, 2020.


Orhan was initially detained but subsequently released under judicial supervision. Following public protests, he was remanded in custody on August 19, 2020, but was released just one week later after an appeal. He was later dismissed from the gendarmerie.


In December 2021, a criminal court in Siirt sentenced Orhan to ten years in prison for sexual assault, applying mitigating circumstances. Despite his conviction, he remained free. A separate criminal case was also brought against him in Batman on charges of incitement to suicide. That trial ended in an acquittal on October 22. The ruling concerns only this second charge and does not overturn his earlier conviction for sexual violence.

title: Shengal People’s Council call for the recognition of the city’s special status
content:
The Shengal People’s Council issued a statement regarding the democratic integration process underway in the city. The statement, which also marked World Kobanê Day on November 1, recalled that both Shengal and Kobanê were besieged by ISIS militants in 2014 and that a new phase of struggle had begun in both Rojava and Shengal after 12 years of resistance.


The Council welcomed the democratic integration process, describing it as the first time in more than a thousand years that a state had recognized the will of the Yazidi community and announced an agreement reached with the freely chosen representatives of the Yazidi people.


The Council further stated that democratic integration in Shengal encompassed not only the YBŞ-YJŞ and Êzîdxan Asayiş, but also all institutions of the Yazidi community.


“The integration of military forces into Iraq’s security institutions is not a project imposed from outside, but a process that has developed through the will of our people and guarantees the preservation of our achievements and lasting security for our community. Those who seek to portray this as a threat are themselves the ones attempting to profit from our community’s suffering and leave Shengal defenseless once again,” the statement said.


The Council pointed out that Shengal has been classified as a disputed territory for 23 years, yet the problems facing the Yazidi community remain unresolved. “We see addressing these historical and social issues together with the central government as the first step in this process,” it added.


The statement emphasized that the issue of Shengal concerns an entire community and its faith, and therefore cannot be reduced to a single armed force, nor can a solution be expected from any one force alone. It stressed the need to address the Shengal issue within the framework of the Iraqi Constitution and in cooperation with the Iraqi Federal Government.


Recalling that the Yazidi people have never accepted any agreement reached without regard for their will, the statement continued: “A genuine solution requires recognition of Shengal’s special status and local administration, as well as guarantees for our rights to self-governance and self-defense. These are the legitimate and natural rights of the Yazidi people. Shengal, the faith center of the Yazidi people, cannot be governed or protected against the will of the Yazidi community. We believe that a lasting solution lies in local self-government, and we demand recognition of this will. Our struggle for the recognition of local self-government will continue.”


The Council called on all relevant parties and individuals, particularly the KDP leadership, to respect the will of the Yazidi community and act accordingly: “The Yazidi cause is both a national and an international issue. No force or party has the right to downplay or distort this reality. They have attempted to frame the Shengal issue around whether or not Yazidis are Kurdish. This is a deliberate distortion and an agenda designed to obscure the truth. Through such agendas, they seek to divert attention from the will of the Yazidi community, create issues that do not serve the interests of the Yazidi people, and distract us from our fundamental demands.”


The statement further called on all Yazidi parties, organizations, women, and young people to set aside their differences and unite under one umbrella.


Amid these developments, the statement said, the 12-year period following the genocide against the Yazidis cannot be assessed without acknowledging the efforts of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement.


“They came to our aid when we had been forgotten and saved our community from the most brutal genocide of the century. We have reached this stage through the philosophy of a free society. Today, the People’s Council, YBŞ, YJŞ, and all Yazidi institutions are products of these ideas and this philosophy. Following Leader Öcalan’s initiation of the democratic society process and development of the democratic integration project, negotiations with Iraq began. The stage we have reached today is the result of these efforts and initiatives. We call on all friends of the Yazidi people to continue supporting this process and contribute to a democratic solution,” the statement concluded.

title: YPJ: Kobanê became the place where the star of freedom rose once again
content:
The General Command of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) released a statement marking November 1 – World Kobanê Day.


The statement on Sunday reads as follows:


“History is not merely a witness to eras of darkness; it is also a witness to the resistance that shatters that darkness. Kobanê is not merely a city in the memory of humanity; it is a line of honour and resistance, a battlefield where life triumphed over death, and a stronghold of the unique resistance of the Women’s Protection Units.


During the years when waves of darkness swept across the world and brutal gangs sought to destroy humanity, Kobanê became the place where the star of freedom rose once again. In its streets, coloured with the blood of heroes, the will of free women demonstrated that no force of darkness could stand against the aspiration for a free life. Just as Arîn Mîrkan, through her sacrificial act, turned the towers of this city into beacons of light, heroic commanders and comrades such as Gêlhat, Diyar Bagok, Rêvan, Herdem, Destîna Qendîl, Viyan Peyman, Zehra, and Îvana Hûvmên also became symbols of this struggle. Today, every woman in the Women’s Protection Units follows in their sacred footsteps.


What made the resistance of Kobanê an unprecedented epic was the unity and national consciousness of our people.


During that historic period, Kobanê became a symbol of national unity, not only through the heroism of its people, but also through the dignified stance and enthusiastic participation of young women and men from all four parts of Kurdistan (North, South, East, and West), from Serhed to Botan, and from Germiyan and Hewlêr to Mahabad and Sine. Particularly significant was the support and uprising of the people of North Kurdistan, which continued for several days along the border. Thousands of freedom volunteers crossed the drawn borders and fought shoulder to shoulder with the fighters of the Women’s Protection Units and the People’s Protection Units (YPG) against the forces of darkness. This stance demonstrated that the heart of Kurdistan beats as one in Kobanê.


At the same time, Kobanê became the conscience of the world. On November 1, when people across the world took to the streets, from Paris to Berlin, from New York to Abya Yalla, and from Tokyo to Amed and Qamişlo, chanting, “We are all Kobanê,” they demonstrated that the resistance of Kobanê was not the resistance of the Kurds alone, but the resistance of all freedom-loving humanity. This global solidarity was the force that shattered the darkness of ISIS.


As the Women’s Protection Units, on November 1, World Kobanê Day, we reaffirm that the resistance of Kobanê is the foundation of our people’s victory and proof of our free unity. This epic demonstrated that women are capable of organising themselves in accordance with the philosophy of “Woman, Life, Freedom”, and that our people, united around this line across the four parts of Kurdistan, are capable of changing the destiny of an entire century.


On this basis, we bow in reverence before the memory of all our heroic martyrs who sacrificed their lives so that we may live proudly on this land today.


Our pledge to our martyrs and our patriotic people is that we will defend the path of resistance until the very end, uphold the achievements of this land, strengthen national unity, and turn our homeland into a beacon of light in the face of every form of darkness.


Long live the unity of women and freedom-loving peoples! Martyrs Never Die!”

author: Unknown
title: MSD: World Kobanê Day carries renewed significance amid deep transformations across Syria
content:
The Syrian Democratic Council (MSD) released a statement marking World Kobanê Day.


Titled “From Resistance to Political Presence,” the statement reads as follows:


“On November 1, the Syrian Democratic Council (MSD) marks World Kobanê Day, reflecting on its profound historical, humanitarian, and political significance. Today, Kobanê and its people play a pivotal role in shaping Syria’s future. In 2014, the resistance of Kobanê transcended geographic borders. It became a global symbol of human resolve against terrorism and a testament to the defense of freedom, dignity, and diversity.


When Kobanê faced ISIS’s brutal offensive, its people made immense sacrifices to protect their city, identity, and right to live. Their resistance marked a critical turning point in the global fight against terrorism. It sparked widespread international solidarity that went beyond supporting a besieged city. Ultimately, Kobanê represented a global stand against violent extremism and a victory for human dignity, freedom, and self-preservation.


The battle of Kobanê proved that the will of the people and their right to self-defense are a vital shield against projects of exclusion and annihilation. Protecting human life and society is inseparable from preserving history, identity, and the right to self-determination. The significance of Kobanê lay not only in its military triumph, but in demonstrating a community’s ability to transform resilience into a powerful force on the regional and global stage.


Amid deep transformations across Syria, World Kobanê Day carries renewed significance. In 2014, Kobanê embodied the struggle for survival against terrorism. Now, the priority has shifted from protecting existence to securing political representation, and from defending rights to anchoring them within the state structure, institutions, and constitution. The immense sacrifices made by the people of Kobanê must not remain merely a heroic chapter in the history of counterterrorism. Instead, they must serve as the foundation for active political participation, real decision-making power, and a meaningful role in shaping Syria’s future.


From this perspective, Kobanê —which defended its existence and dignity against terrorism—deserves renewed solidarity today that supports its right to participate actively in shaping Syria’s future. The people of Kobanê must have a political role proportionate to their sacrifices and experience. Their resilience must translate into meaningful political and civic participation in state-building, rather than being confined to the history of resistance.


The MSD believes that building a united Syria does not mean erasing local identities or forcing a uniform model. Instead, it requires recognizing national, religious, and cultural diversity, establishing equal citizenship, and providing constitutional guarantees that protect fundamental rights and freedom. A democratic state cannot be built through exclusion or imposed reality; it requires genuine partnership, mutual recognition, and a fair distribution of authority. This empowers local communities to manage their affairs and contribute directly to Syria’s collective future.


In this context, the MSD emphasizes that national issues—foremost among them the Kurdish cause—require a serious political and constitutional approach. Solutions must be built on dialogue, mutual understanding, and full recognition of rights rather than unilateral measures. Current transformations cannot succeed through administrative and security arrangements alone. Success depends on building an inclusive national partnership and establishing binding political, legal, and social guarantees that build trust and deliver lasting stability.


On World Kobanê Day, the MSD pays tribute to the people of Kobanê and honors its martyrs. We express deep gratitude to all international forces and nations that stood alongside the city against ISIS. Honoring this legacy requires more than commemoration. It demands translating these sacrifices into a new political reality where Kobanê’s people are full partners in building a democratic, pluralistic, and decentralized Syria that guarantees dignity, equal citizenship, and protection for all identities.


The international solidarity that enabled Kobanê to defend its existence in 2014 must be renewed today—empowering its people to secure their rightful political presence and help shape the future of Syria.”

author: Novara Media
title: Boots Riley: Watch My Movie Then Go on Strike
content:
You’ve probably heard of Boots Riley’s work – Sorry To Bother You starring LaKeith Stanfield was a surprise hit, and his series I’m A Virgo got picked up by Amazon Prime. But the Oakland-raised rapper-turned-director doesn’t just want you to leave the cinema having had a good time: he wants you to start a revolution.


His new film I Love Boosters – starring the incredibly charming Keke Palmer – is about three women who shoplift from high end boutiques, and sell the clothes at a cut price in the hood. But it wouldn’t be a Boots Riley film if it stopped there. What starts as a paean to shoplifters turns into a story of working class shop floor organisation – and international communist action.


Is all art propaganda? Is shoplifting a revolutionary act? What role does style play in the revolution? And what’s it like being the most high profile communist in Hollywood, in Trump’s America?

title: Dünya Kobanî Günü: DEM Parti’den ‘demokratik Suriye’ çağrısı
content:
1 Kasım Dünya Kobanî Günü dolayısıyla Türkiye’nin birçok kentinde açıklamalar yapıldı.


1 Kasım, 2014’te Avrupa Birliği Türkiye Yurttaş Komisyonu (EUTCC) ve Peace Camping inisiyatifinin, Kobanî’de IŞİD kuşatmasına karşı süren direnişe destek amacıyla yaptığı “Kobanî ve insanlık için küresel seferberlik” çağrısının ardından Dünya Kobanî Günü olarak anılmaya başlandı.


Mezopotamya Ajansı

’nın aktardığına göre


Adana, Mersin, Urfa Suruç, Konya, İzmir, Van, Erzurum, Bitlis Tatvan, Antalya ve Şırnak’ta düzenlenen açıklamalarda Kobanî’de IŞİD’e karşı verilen mücadele anıldı.


Eylemlerde, Suriye’de eşit yurttaşlık, demokratik çözüm ve birlikte yaşam talepleri öne çıktı.


*Adana


Açıklamalarda konuşan Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi (DEM Parti) temsilcileri, Kobanî’deki mücadelenin farklı halklar ve inançlar açısından ortak yaşam fikrini güçlendirdiğini savundu.


Urfa Suruç’taki etkinlikte konuşan DEM Parti Milletvekili Ferit Şenyaşar, Kobanî direnişinin Kürtlerin dünya kamuoyunda görünürlüğünü artırdığını söyledi. Şenyaşar, “Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci”ne de değinerek devletin somut adımlar atması gerektiğini belirtti.


İzmir’deki eylemde konuşan DEM Parti Milletvekili Burcugül Çubuk, Kobanî’yi Ortadoğu’daki savaş politikalarına karşı barış ve ortak mücadele açısından bir ‘pusula’ olarak tanımladı. Çubuk, farklı halkların birlikte mücadele ederek barışı örgütlemesi gerektiğini söyledi.


*İzmir


Şırnak’taki açıklamada DEM Parti Milletvekili Mehmet Zeki İrmez, Suriye’de demokratik bir sistem kurulması ve bütün halkların haklarının güvence altına alınması gerektiğini söyledi. İrmez, Kürtlerin dil, kültür ve kimlikleriyle Suriye’nin geleceğinde yer alması gerektiğini belirtti.


Antalya’da DEM Parti Milletvekili Saruhan Oluç da Kobanî’de IŞİD’e karşı yürütülen mücadelenin yalnızca Kürtler açısından değil, bölgede yaşayan halklar açısından da önem taşıdığını söyledi.


*Bitlis


“Demokratik bir Suriye inşa edilmeli”


DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tülay Hatimoğulları, 1 Kasım dolayısıyla yaptığı açıklamada Kobanî’yi “kadınların öncülüğünde yükselen, halkların ve inançların ortak yaşam iradesiyle büyüyen” bir mücadele olarak tanımladı.


Hatimoğulları, X sosyal medya hesabından Türkçe, Kürtçe ve Arapça yaptığı paylaşımda Suriye’nin geleceğine ilişkin şu çağrıyı yaptı:


Kobanî’nin tarihsel mirasına yakışır demokratik bir Suriye inşa edilmelidir. Başta yaşam hakkı olmak üzere, Kürt halkının ve Kuzey ve Doğu Suriye’deki tüm halkların kimlikleri, dilleri, siyasi ve kültürel hakları güvence altına alınmalıdır. Demokratik Suriye, eşit ve özgür ortak yaşamın güvencesidir.


DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tuncer Bakırhan da Kobanî’deki mücadelenin “halkların eşit ve özgür bir yaşam kurma iradesinin simgesi” olduğunu söyledi.


Bakırhan, X sosyal medya hesabından Türkçe, Kürtçe ve Arapça yaptığı paylaşımda Kobanî direnişinin mirasının bugün Suriye’nin geleceği açısından yol gösterici olduğunu belirtti:


Kalıcı barış ve demokratik çözüm; Suriye’de yaşayan tüm halkların kimliklerinin ve siyasi, kültürel ve toplumsal haklarının güvence altına alınmasından geçer.


Suriye’nin bütünlüğü, farklı halkların ve inançların kimliklerini yok saymakla değil, eşit ve özgür bir ortak yaşamla mümkündür. Tüm halkların haklarının tanınması, demokratik entegrasyonun ve kalıcı barışın güvencesidir.

title: Romería 11 de septiembre 2025
content:
Romería del año pasado hacia el cementerio general en Santiago de Chile, conmemorando a los detenidos desaparecidos, torturados y asesinados de la dictadura de Pinochet. Marcha histórica en Chile para no olvidar, y que jamás vuelva a pasar.

Η εισαγωγική ομιλία της Πρωτοβουλίας Πανεπιστημιακών ΑΠΘ, ΠΑΜΑΚ, ΔΙΠΑΕ,

 παρουσίασε ορισμένα προγράμματα εξοικείωσης με τη χρήση και τον σχεδιασμό όπλων στο Ισραήλ, τα οποία απευθύνονται σε παιδιά από 12 ετών, στο πλαίσιο του επαγγελματικού προσανατολισμού στα σχολεία από εταιρείες όπως η Elbit και κρατικές υπηρεσίες Σιν Μπετ και Μoσάντ. Αναφέρθηκε και το πρόγραμμα που ίδρυσαν το 2013 βετεράνοι των μυστικών υπηρεσιών για νέους, που βρίσκονται, σύμφωνα με την επίσημη διαφήμιση του προγράμματος, «στο φάσμα του αυτισμού αλλά χρήζουν μικρής φροντίδας». Είναι σαφές ότι  τόσο εταιρείες όσο και ακαδημαϊκά προγράμματα που αναζητούν χορηγίες μπορούν να επιδιώκουν πολύ μεγαλύτερο κέρδος από τα όπλα και την πολεμική τεχνολογία από ό,τι σε οποιονδήποτε άλλον τομέα παραγωγής.


Αυτά μας ενδιαφέρουν γιατί είναι πολύ κοντά μας και γεωγραφικά και συμβολικά. Ας πούμε στα Διαβατα υπάρχει ένας καταυλισμός ρομά με 3.000 πληθυσμό. Η ΕΛΒΟ που ξανανοίγει πλέον ως μέλος της ισραηλινής εταιρείας παραγωγής “αμυντικών” drones SK Group λίγο πιο δίπλα στη Σίνδο είναι πολύ πιο ορατή.


Αναφέρθηκε κατόπιν ότι έχει αναδυθεί στην Ελλάδα μία νέα κοινωνική τάξη νέων που εργάζεται στις ναυτιλιακές εταιρείες, οι οποίες με σλόγκαν όπως “ανακάλυψε τον κόσμο, ζήσε μια μοναδική εμπειρία” και άλλα εφάμιλλα της ρητορικής που χρησιμοποιεί η στρατιωτική βιομηχανία του Ισραήλ, προσελκύουν ένοπλους φρουρούς για τα δεξαμενόπλοια, τα παγοθραυστικά και τα εμπορικά τους πλοία.  Οι υπηρεσίες ασφαλείας στις «αποστολές υψηλού ρίσκου» για την περιφρούρηση του εφοπλιστικού κεφαλαίου από τα νέα αυτά μισθοφορικά σώματα-ιδιωτικούς στρατούς επιτρέπεται δια νόμου ήδη από το 2011 στην Ελλάδα,τη χρονιά των μνημονίων και των τεράστιων κινητοποιήσεων. Οι καπιταλιστές σήμερα δεν έχουν τίποτα να κρύψουν. Ο πόλεμος δεν είναι αναγκαίο κακό ούτε ατυχής συγκυρία, είναι ευκαιρία και θα κάνουν το παν για να τον κρατήσουν ενεργό. Τον συζητούν πλέον στα στα πανεπιστήμια, σχεδιάζουν όπλα και πολεμικές τεχνολογίες, μιλούν για τις ζημιές που θα επιφέρει η παύση των συρράξεων. Έτσι κι αλλιώς, η χώρα διαθέτει εθελοντικό στρατό στην υπηρεσία του εφοπλιστικού κεφαλαίου, την Χ.Α. και άλλα ακροδεξιά μορφώωματα. Ανάχωμα στον μιλιταρισμό και τον διαρκή πόλεμο των καπιταλιστών μικρές και μεγάλες κινήσεις παντού (global sumud flotilla, march to Gaza, μπλοκαρίσματα στη Rheinmetall, οι απεργίες λιμενεργατ(ρι)ών) όπως η σημερινή.

author: CNT Madrid
title: Los teatros de Madrid vulneran el derecho a la huelga
content:
La convocatoria de Huelga General para el 11 de noviembre ya se está haciendo notar en determinados espacios escénicos de la Comunidad de Madrid. Algunos espectáculos programados para ese día están siendo cancelados o desplazados a otras fecha diferentes. Esto, según denuncian los sindicatos CNT y CGT, implica una vulneración del derecho a secundar la Huelga General a numerosas personas trabajadoras de estos espacios escénicos madrileños.


Estas situaciones se están produciendo por ejemplo en Stage Entertainment, la empresa que programa el musical El Rey León en el teatro Lope de Vega y El Alma Al Aire en el Coliseum. En ambos casos, la empresa desplazó ambas funciones del miércoles 11 al lunes 9, poniendo el día 11 como el día de libranza del personal, tal como se informó mediante comunicación interna hecha a las jefaturas de los departamentos técnicos. Lo mismo ha sucedido en el músical Six, en el teatro Gran Vía, gestionado por el grupo Smedia, y en otros teatros de este mismo grupo, como el Alcázar (Un Dios salvaje) o el Fígaro (Victoria).


Un caso similar se ha dado en los teatros Luchana, donde se ha cancelado toda la programación, dando también el día libre al personal y vulnerando así su derecho a secundar la huelga.


Se han producido también irregularidades en el musical Los Miserables, representado en el teatro Nuevo Apolo, donde ATG Entertainment ha actualizado su calendario para mover la función del día 11 al domingo 8. La plantilla de ATG fue informada del cambio mediante comunicación interna. Otros espectáculos de esta misma productora han sido cancelados ese día, como es el caso de los musicales Querido Evan Hansen en el teatro Rialto, Wicked en el Nuevo Teatro Alcalá y La función que sale mal en el Amaya.


Además se han aplazado los conciertos programados para el 11 de noviembre en el Auditorio Nacional de Música, dependiente del Ministerio de Cultura, siendo reprogramados otros días de esa misma semana.


Para los sindicatos mencionados estos son hechos muy graves que el público asistente a esos espectáculos debe conocer. Por esa razón, tanto CNT como CGT avanzan la realización de piquetes informativos en diferentes teatros madrileños. Ambas centrales anarcosindicales también hacen un llamamiento al público madrileño que hubiera adquirido entradas para el día de Huelga General, el 11 de noviembre: rechazad el cambio de fecha y solicitad la devolución de los importes abonados.

title: The Kurdistan Region’s experience of government – III
content:
In the previous part of our series, we examined the common causes of government formation crises that have recurred in the Kurdistan Region over the past three decades, as well as the election process of 20 October 2024. This part examines the demands put forward by the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) in negotiations, the institutional vacuum created by the failure to form a government and the price the people are paying for it.


The KDP's demands


Iraqi media reported that the negotiating delegations of the two parties reached an agreement on 4 February 2025 on a draft joint government programme comprising nine sections and 15 articles. The programme covered parliament, finance, foreign relations, relations between Erbil (Hewlêr) and Baghdad, the peshmerga, energy and the judiciary. However, negotiations over the distribution of government positions lagged behind agreement on the programme.


The KDP's offer expanded over time. In April 2025, the PUK was offered only the ministries of Peshmerga Affairs and Finance. On 6 November 2025, however, the KDP announced that it had offered the PUK the parliamentary speakership, the vice-presidency of the Kurdistan Region, the deputy premiership, eight or nine ministries and "influential positions" within the security institutions.


Three issues remained outside the scope of the offer. A KDP representative announced on 8 October 2025 that the party would not hand over the Ministry of Interior to the PUK and would not negotiate on the matter. The KDP also refused to negotiate over the Security Council, which oversees the KDP's Parastin intelligence agency and the PUK's Zanyari intelligence agency, remaining under Masrour Barzani's authority. Masrour Barzani's position as prime minister and Nechirvan Barzani's position as President of the Kurdistan Region were likewise excluded from negotiations.


The KDP insisted that cabinet positions should be distributed according to the number of parliamentary seats held by each party. Masrour Barzani said in June 2025 that his party was "making serious efforts to form a government based on the majority". The KDP began adopting a more conciliatory tone from August 2026 onwards.


The PUK's demands


The PUK demanded the ministries of Interior and Natural Resources, the chancellorship of the Security Council and a written definition of the deputy prime minister's powers in April 2025. In the following months, its demands took shape around authority over either the Ministry of Interior or the Security Council, a senior executive position and the headship of the Presidency Office of the Kurdistan Region. The KDP also rejected the PUK's demand for the headship of the Presidency Office.


PUK officials stressed that the dispute was not about the number of positions. Deputy Prime Minister Qubad Talabani said on 31 May 2026 that the problem concerned the "philosophy of partnership". The PUK declared that it continued to insist on a 50–50 division of power and genuine partnership, and that it would not join the government until it was certain that the "mistakes of the past" would not be repeated.


The PUK's second demand concerned the decentralisation of powers. Qubad Talabani cited disparities in public services between Duhok and Germiyan, calling for greater authority to be granted to governors and mayors.


The PUK's position became more flexible in the autumn of 2026. Bafel Talabani addressed the KDP in a speech on 12 October, saying: "The PUK does not want to govern without you, nor can it govern without you."


The PUK-New Generation alliance


Bafel Talabani and New Generation Movement leader Shaswar Abdulwahid signed an alliance agreement on 2 July 2026. The agreement reportedly provided for the adoption of a regional budget law, full transparency over oil revenues, independent financial oversight, the reimbursement of part of the deducted salaries and marriage loans for young people. However, the agreement contained no provision specifying which party would hold the premiership.


The alliance with New Generation gave the PUK a combined strength of 38 parliamentary seats at the negotiating table, but did not commit New Generation to joining the government. On 24 June 2026, New Generation leader Shaswar Abdulwahid said that the next prime minister should come from the alliance. author: Andrea DiP
title: Eleger Lula não basta: “Se não radicalizar a gente não sobrevive”, diz editor do Revelando
content:
A disputa presidencial no Brasil chegou ao fim, no último domingo (25), com a quarta vitória de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). Lula venceu o segundo turno das eleições e foi reeleito com a maior votação já obtida por um candidato à Presidência, com 64.256.232 votos – 51,79% dos votos válidos contra 48,21% obtidos pelo adversário, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).


“O que a sociedade brasileira foi capaz de fazer no último domingo foi a salvação do nosso sistema democrático”, afirma o editor-chefe do canal Revelando, Bruno Torturra, convidado do

Pauta Pública

 desta semana.


A disputa foi marcada pela intensa mobilização nas redes socias e nas ruas contra o bolsonarismo. Além disso, também foi fundamental o papel do jornalismo e do combate à desinformação, muitas vezes por meio de novos formatos e narrativas que se adaptaram à lógica dos algoritmos para jogar luz sobre histórias que a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro escondia.


O canal Revelando, lançado em setembro, produz reportagens e investigações jornalísticas em formato de documentário. Em conversa com Andrea Dip, Torturra fala sobre a iniciativa, analisa o cenário político pós-eleições, e destaca como a mobilização em torno da vitória de Lula representa também um desfecho biográfico significativo para o presidente e uma tomada de consciência cívica.


Para o jornalista, no entanto, a esquerda precisa ir além da resistência e articular ações de longo prazo capazes de propor avanços: “Se a gente não radicalizar a gente não sobrevive, isso aí não tem a menor dúvida.”


Leia os principais pontos da conversa e ouça o podcast completo abaixo.

				Editor-chefe do canal Revelando fala sobre os bastidores e o papel do jornalismo para a mobilização social nas eleições

Como você avalia esse momento pós-eleições, depois dessa gigantesca mobilização? Tem precedentes?


Foi uma manifestação histórica. A sociedade brasileira foi capaz de fazer no domingo de eleições. Acho que tem um significado nacional gigantesco, uma salvação do nosso sistema democrático, um desfecho biográfico muito bonito para o presidente Lula. É uma mobilização, uma tomada de consciência cívica, já vi várias desse tipo na minha vida, mas nunca com esse foco, com essa clareza, vontade e gana.


E com um significado mundial também muito grande. Acho que não é à toa que a gente tá vendo gringo chorando em todo o país do mundo, uma doideira, justificadamente. A gente deu uma demonstração muito linda, mesmo, de como é que se faz para derrotar – não digo nem só a extrema direita fascista que o Flávio, de certo, representa, mas até a tecno-oligarquia, a nova utopia antidemocrática desses mesmos oligarcas, o que a digitalização da nossa vida pública representa. Então, foi uma vitória colossal.


O Trump falou hoje que ele acha que as eleições brasileiras foram manipuladas. E eu concordo com ele: elas foram, e a gente ganhou mesmo assim. A gente ganhou apesar da manipulação, não é pouca coisa o que aconteceu. E também do ponto de vista emocional – que é uma parte crucial da política que, às vezes, a gente desmerece – mas o meu coração, e acho que o coração de todo mundo que entendeu o que estava em jogo, está descarregado. Ele continua batendo forte e eu continuo emocionado, mas agora é com mais serotonina e dopamina.


Na questão da mobilização, fortificada pelo jornalismo independente, o Revelando se destacou como um dos veículos mais importantes. Sobretudo, porque a gente também viu esses boicotes dos Estados Unidos, das Big Techs e da grande imprensa. Então, queria te ouvir sobre o formato muito acertado do Revelando e qual foi o papel do jornalismo independente nesse processo?


Antes de qualquer coisa eu queria valorizar o trabalho do jornalismo tradicional brasileiro, que foi no qual nós nos embasamos para fazer o Revelando. Nós tivemos muito pouca apuração própria, no sentido de que não tivemos nenhum grande furo de reportagem nem dados inéditos. Mas o que a gente fez, e que é algo que a gente tinha uma escola muito interessante no Greg News e também no Calma Urgente, que é algo que o jornalismo tradicional tem muita dificuldade de fazer – porque eu acho que ele é um pouco preso no formalismo temático.

title: Yeni SPK Başkanı Muhsin Atcı kimdir?
content:
Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan’ın imzasıyla yayımlanan karara göre, Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK) Başkanlığına Muhsin Atcı, Başkan Vekilliğine Ersin Başar Ekmekçi, kurul üyeliğine ise Yasemin Girici atandı.

Peki, SPK başkanlığına atanan Muhsin Atcı kimdir? İşte hayatı…

1979 yılında Konya'nın Ereğli ilçesinde doğan Muhsin Atcı, ilk öğreniminin ardından ortaokul ve lise eğitimini İvriz Anadolu Öğretmen Lisesinde tamamladı. Ardından İstanbul Üniversitesi Siyasal Bilgiler Fakültesi Kamu Yönetimi Bölümünden mezun olan Atcı, 2014 yılında ABD'deki Duke Üniversitesinde Kalkınma Politikası alanında yüksek lisans yaptı.

2003 yılında Vergi Denetmen Yardımcısı olarak mesleğine başlayan Atcı, 2005 yılında Stajyer Gelirler Kontrolörü, 2008 yılında Gelirler Kontrolörü ve 2010 yılında İdari ve Mali İşler Daire Başkan Yardımcılığı yaptı.

2011 yılında Vergi Denetim Kurulunun kurulmasıyla Vergi Müfettişi olarak atandı. 15 Eylül 2014 ile 7 Temmuz 2017 tarihleri arasında Ankara Büyük Ölçekli Mükellefler Grup Başkanı olarak görev yaptı.

31 Temmuz 2017'de Vergi Denetim Kurulu Başkan Yardımcılığına getirilen Atcı, bu görevini 18 Nisan 2019'a kadar sürdürdü. Daha sonra özel sektörde görev alarak Gürok Grubu bünyesinde vergi, mali işler ve risk yönetimi alanlarında çalıştı.

7 Ekim 2023'te Vergi Denetim Kurulu Başkanlığına atanan Muhsin Atcı, 1 Kasım 2026'da yayımlanan 2026/367 sayılı Cumhurbaşkanlığı Kararı ile Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu Başkanı oldu.

title: AKOM'dan İstanbul için uyarı: Salı ve çarşamba sağanak bekleniyor
content:
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi (İBB) Afet Koordinasyon Merkezi (AKOM), İstanbul için haftalık hava tahmin raporunu yayımladı. Rapora göre İstanbul başta olmak üzere Türkiye'nin büyük bölümü, Orta Akdeniz üzerinden gelen yağışlı hava sistemlerinin etkisi altında kalmaya devam ediyor.

Önümüzdeki 7 günlük süreçte İstanbul'da çoğunlukla kapalı ve bulutlu bir havanın etkili olması bekleniyor. Hafta boyunca belirli aralıklarla sağanak yağış geçişlerinin yaşanacağı tahmin edilirken, yağışlı havanın özellikle haftanın ilk günlerinde etkisini sürdüreceği öngörülüyor.

Haftanın ilk yarısında yağmur ve sağanak yağışın etkili olması beklenirken, perşembe günü de aralıklı yağış geçişlerinin görüleceği tahmin ediliyor. Cuma günü ise havanın parçalı ve çok bulutlu olması bekleniyor.

content:

author: Aaron Ernest Cruz
title: Police withdraws from Kasibu as residents stand their ground against mining
content:
Local community maintained the barricade while police forces gear up to dismantle it, Screengrab from Nhe Riz

Alyansa ng Novo Vizcayano para sa Kalikasan (ANVIK) argued that the court should hold NLMRC accountable rather than target the people’s barricade, which residents put up in response to the company’s activities.

The people of Kasibu have once again demonstrated its steadfast defense of their land after the police withdrew from enforcing the temporary restraining order (TRO) filed by the North Luzon Mineral Resources Corporation (NLMRC) and the Bugkalot Confederation.

On Friday, October 30, the news broke that the police came to the people’s barricade in Kasibu attempting to dismantle it through a court order. This is after the NLMRC and Bugkalot Confederation filed a complaint seeking an injunction and a temporary restraining order to stop residents from maintaining barricades along the roads of Pao, Catawaran, Kakidugen, and Paquet. Once cleared, this would allow the company to proceed with its mining exploration activities.

Rights group Karapatan hailed the withdrawal of the police, saying that the community’s strong resistance against large-scale mining only proved that they are determined to defend their rights and their livelihood.

“Their struggle must be respected, not met with police deployment, threats, arrests, fabricated charges, and legal harassment,” the group said in a statement.

“The enforcement of the temporary restraining order sought by NLMRC must not be used to suppress community resistance and advance corporate mining interests at the expense of the people,” Karapatan stated.

The court order was issued on October 28 by Regional Trial Court Branch 30 Judge Paul Attolba Jr. following a complaint filed by NLMRC and Bugkalot Federation of Nueva Vizcaya against members of the anti-mining community for blocking their mining equipment. The company holds a mining exploration permit covering 4,456 hectares, including ancestral lands, granted by Mines and Geoscience Bureau (MGB) in June 2025.

The anti-mining community asserted that the people’s barricade is legitimate and justified, as residents are only defending their rights, environment and livelihood.

They also questioned the validity of the mining exploration permit, saying it was granted without genuine consultation with the affected communities. Members of the community themselves have experienced the effects of the mining exploration on their community, saying it is affecting their crops and access to clean water.

The Center for Environmental Concerns (CEC) said the TRO reflects how the state treats the environmental defenders and the communities that will be affected by mining exploration activities.

“Rather than criminalizing defenders and putting their lives at risk, the judiciary and local government units must fulfill their mandate to serve the public good, uphold human rights, and environmental protection,“ the CEC said in a statement.

Meanwhile, the Climate Change Network for Community-based Initiatives (CCNCI) accused Attolba Jr. of serving the interest of the mining company instead of the community and the environment.

The group said that the same RTC also issued writ of preliminary injunction against the people’s barricade in Dupax Del Norte against Woggle Corporation’s mining exploration that led to the violent dispersal of the said barricade and unjustly arrested seven residents on January 23 this year.

“The dispersal is a blatant example of the NLMRC’s corporate greed and to the lengths they are willing to go for their own interests – weaponizing legal mechanisms, state-mandated violence, and the destruction of the environment for the sake of their profits that does not benefit local communities,” CCNCI said in their statement.

Since May, the affected community has maintained the barricade, effectively halting NLMRC’s mining exploration activities and causing the company to incur an estimated P8 million ($125, 201) losses.

Alyansa ng Novo Vizcayano para sa Kalikasan (ANVIK) argued that the court should hold NLMRC accountable rather than target the people’s barricade, which residents put up in response to the company’s activities.

“In a desperate attempt to push through their destructive large-scale mining that the community is vehemently rejecting, they colluded with the police to get the NLMRC’s mining equipment inside,” ANVIK said in their statement.

author: Kalikasan PNE
title: Debt, plunder and disaster
content:
Southern Leyte during the aftermath of Typhoon Odette (Photo by LCDE)

Public money pays for transmission lines, ports, and guarantees, while private firms collect profits for decades. The public absorbs the risk and the debt; the corporations keep the gains.

Every year, typhoons, floods, and landslides batter the Philippines, and every year the same story follows: the country is among the most climate-vulnerable in the world. In recent years, the Marcos Jr. administration’s answer is to borrow from private banks and international financing institutions (IFIs) such as the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF-WB).

The Philippines contributes very little to the greenhouse gases warming the planet, yet we are forced to take on debt to address a crisis we did not create. The IMF-WB has helped imperialist countries, primarily the United States, shape our economy around debt repayment, raw-material exports, and foreign control. For more than half a century, their intervention has driven the depletion of our natural resources, widespread poverty, and environmental destruction. A real alternative exists, and it begins with cutting our financial dependence on these institutions and breaking US imperialist control over our country.

The Philippines was among the earliest testing grounds for structural adjustment: World Bank loans in 1980 and 1987, and 23 IMF programs between 1962 and 2000. From Marcos Sr. in the 1970s to Marcos Jr. today, the conditionalities of this debt trap have been implemented. Key measures included:

World Bank structural adjustment loans (1980–1987): tariff cuts, import liberalization, and a push toward export-oriented industry.

IMF programs (1980s): peso devaluation and floating, austerity, and prioritizing debt service. Automatic appropriation for debt payments dates back to Marcos-era decrees.

Privatization: the Asset Privatization Trust (1986), the Manila water concessions (1997), and the power sector under Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) (2001).

Deregulation: Oil industry deregulation (1996–1998) and the Mining Act of 1995.

Investment liberalization: the Foreign Investments Act (1991) and the Build-Operate-Transfer law (1990).

Tax reforms: the Value-Added Tax (VAT) (1988) and its 2005 expansion, both pushed by IMF programs.

The script was consistent: lower or eliminate taxes on foreign and big firms, open our markets to imports and investment, privatize public services, cut public spending, and expand raw-material exports like minerals. The result was an economy kept agrarian, underdeveloped, and reliant on foreign capital.

Also linked to foreign debt is the devaluation of peso which made the situation worse. When the peso drops, our debt in foreign currency increases. To earn dollars, we must export more timber, minerals, and agricultural products, and to entice foreign investment, wages and labor rights must be suppressed. The burden has fallen hardest on landless farmers, fishers pushed out by commercial fleets, upland Indigenous communities, and low-wage workers who keep losing their livelihoods.

The Bataan Nuclear Power Plant shows how foreign debt burdens the people twice. Built under Marcos for roughly $2.3 billion, it never produced a single watt of electricity, yet Filipinos paid for it for decades. When the debt crisis hit in the 1980s, the government automatically allocated its budget to debt repayment while cutting funds for health and education.

Then came the Mining Act of 1995, which allowed 100-percent foreign-owned companies to hold large mining agreements. World Bank documents of the period treated limits on foreign ownership as an obstacle to be removed. Our minerals were extracted and shipped abroad, leaving communities with lost forests, poisoned rivers and seas, mine waste, militarization, and displacement. We never built the heavy industry that could have turned our own minerals into goods and jobs.

Today, the same institutions tell vulnerable countries they must fund climate resilience and clean energy. Since 2021, we have borrowed from the World Bank through disaster loans, policy loans, a community-resilience loan, and energy-transition loans. That adds up to more than $4 billion in under six years, every centavo to be repaid. Civil society research shows that in 2024, nearly 99 percent of climate- and disaster-related assistance came as loans, not grants. author: Kodao Productions
title: Sara’s dust and shadow
content:
As the nation gears up for the celebration of All Souls Day, it is not only fitting to remember the departed, it is likewise important for the living to look into how they comport themselves from the time they were born to the time they have to depart. As one poet described it, the dash between the date of birth and the date of demise should be the basis for determining whether someone led a wholesome life, or scuppered it altogether for the sheer greed for power and pelf.


That dash indicates the arrival and departure, and covers the life work of someone. It is the dash that starts in 1978 for Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio, when she was born to the couple Elizabeth Zimmerman and Rodrigo Duterte. One can be measured by how the departed used his dash and poet Linda Ellis’ copyrighted piece “The Dash” has been recited in countless funerals since 1996. The dash embodies a compete performance and there is no encore for this unique show. Will Sara make peace with the marauding devils that occupy her cerebrum and cast away all the lies thus far disseminated to misinform and delude the Filipino people on her culpability for maintaining hidden wealth that lawyer and forensic analyst Alex Cabrera estimated conservatively to be at least P871.71-million at most P1.5-billion?


To avoid getting sued for reading or reciting Ellis’ poem, Sara might just as well recite tonight and tomorrow Robert Louis Stevenson’s “Requiem,” which reads: “Under the wide and starry sky/Dig the grave and let me lie/Glad did I live and gladly die/And I laid me down with a will///This be the verse you grave for me: Here he lies where he longed to be/Home is the sailor, home from sea, And the hunter home from the hill.” How will Sara eulogize the departed while in real life she has been throwing her own father, her brother Baste, her own husband Mans and everybody else just to wiggle herself out of the impeachment trap she had plunged herself into?


There is a Latin phrase for the brevity of life, its mirth and its harshness, and the lesson, shared by the Scripture and the Torah, that one must make the most of it:

Pulvis et umbra


sumus

 – We are dust and shadow. But before Sara contemplates about her mortality, or immortality as her solipsistic reality, she has to contend with the reality that she has to contend with her defense and her date with the daunting task is on Nov. 9, 2026. After whining about her fears that assassins are on the prowl to do her in, with the courts, the police, the Senate and Congress, as well as the elevators and stairs, conspiring to end her triumphant march to Malacanang in 2028, she eventually sought succor from the Supreme Court (SC) to throw her grave threats case. The High Court dumped her plea.


However, Sara is a prisoner of the present, a detainee in a space open and wide, for she has failed to read the room, that all her arguments for her perceived persecution cannot save her from her own submissions before the Senate impeachment court. As one wag said: “Ignorance has never looked so confident.” Surely, Sara would visit the graves of the victims of Davao City bombings but she would find it beneath her dignity to spend a second saying a prayer, or *Kaddish, if you will, for even one of the 30,000 victims of the “tokhang” war. All those photo ops about planting tree seedlings, visiting graves and doing her **lachrymal scenes from a script by her image makers mean nothing when ranged about her record of indolence in the past four years, her being absent when people were drowning by the successive typhoons “Crising,” “Emong” and “Dante” in July 2025 and her journey to Germany to watch a Taylor Swift concert as “Carina” battered Luzon in 2024 proved to all and sundry that empathy is not in her vocabulary. Yet, she uses social media to even brag how she can ***fudgel her way at the DepEd and Office of the Vice President (OVP).
