title: Ballon d’Or’da "sonuçlar sızdırıldı" şüphesi: 200 bin dolarlık bahis inceleme altında
content:
Ballon d’Or (Altın Top) ödülünde ilk beş sırayı eksiksiz tahmin ederek yaklaşık 200 bin dolar kazanç sağlayan şüpheli bahisler üzerine soruşturma başlatıldı. Organizasyonu düzenleyen France Football’un, sonuçların tören öncesinde sızdırılmış olabileceği şüphesiyle konuyu incelemeye aldığı ve polisle de temasa geçtiği belirtildi.

Fransa merkezli medya kuruluşu Upside’ın araştırmasına göre, kripto para tabanlı tahmin platformu Polymarket’teki 12 hesap, pazartesi günkü törenden önce sonuçlar üzerine toplam 264 bin doların üzerinde bahis oynadı. Hesaplar, farklı ihtimallere dağılmak yerine Harry Kane’in birinci, Kylian Mbappé’nin ikinci, Lamine Yamal’ın üçüncü, Rodri’nin dördüncü ve Lionel Messi’nin beşinci olacağı sıralamaya odaklandı. Londra Palladium’daki törende açıklanan sonuçlar bu tahminlerle birebir örtüştü.

Upside’ın kurucu ortağı Raphaël Pautard, söz konusu hesapların 1–20 Ekim arasında açıldığını ve birbirlerine oldukça benzeyen işlem örüntüleri sergilediğini söyledi. Bu benzerlikler, hesapların aynı kişi ya da grupla bağlantılı olabileceği şüphesini doğurdu. İncelenen 12 hesaptan yedisinin başka hiçbir bahis piyasasında işlem yapmadığı, altısının ise açıldıktan yalnızca 15 dakika sonra ilk bahislerini oynadığı belirlendi.

Araştırmada, şüpheli bahislerin finansmanında kullanılan işlemlerden birinin izi Fransa merkezli bir platforma kadar sürüldü. Pautard’ın aktardığına göre Upside ekibi, ilgili blokzincir işlemlerini ve dijital cüzdan adreslerini şirketle paylaştı. Platform da bahisleri finanse eden hesaplardan birinin arkasındaki kişinin kimliğini tespit ettiğini bildirdi. Kimliği kamuoyuna açıklanmayan bu kişinin belirlenmesinin, hesaplar arasındaki bağlantıların ve para akışının ortaya çıkarılmasına yardımcı olabileceği ifade edildi.

İşlemlerin zamanlaması ve bahis stratejisindeki değişiklikler de incelemede dikkat çekti. Bir hesabın, Kane’in kazanacağına ilişkin kontratı 37 sentten satın aldığı, fiyat 67 sente yükseldiğinde sattığı ve elde ettiği parayı belirli sıralamalara yönelik bahislere aktardığı kaydedildi. Bu bahisler arasında Yamal’ın üçüncü olacağı tahmini de bulunuyordu.

Bulgularını France Football’a ileten Upside’ın, cuma öğleden sonra soruşturma açıldığına ilişkin teyit aldığı belirtildi. Groupe Amaury bünyesindeki France Football, ödülü 1956’dan bu yana düzenliyor. Kuruluştan konuya ilişkin yorum istendiği de aktarıldı.

Tören öncesinde kazananı yalnızca birkaç kişinin bildiğinin açıklanmış olması, olası bilgi sızıntısına ilişkin kuşkuları artırdı. Eski France Football editörü Pascal Ferré de önceki hafta, kazananın kimliğini gizli tutmanın yolunun bilgiyi mümkün olduğunca az kişiyle paylaşmak olduğunu söylemişti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Pakistan Abruptly Cancels Taiwanese Overflight Routes Then Reverses Course
content:
IN AN UNUSUAL series of events, in short order, Pakistan declared that Taiwanese airlines would not be allowed to fly over the country, then reversed course on the decision.

The decision was announced by Pakistan’s Minister of Defense Khawaja Asif, who stated that the new policy was made to comply with Pakistan’s One China Policy. Originally, Taiwanese airlines EVA Air and China Airlines had been cleared for overflight privileges by Pakistan from October 28 of this year through March 27, 2027, as approved by the country’s Civil Aviation Authority.

This would be the first time that a country has revoked overflight privileges for Taiwanese air carriers, on the basis of a claimed One China Policy. If so, it could be that Pakistan would be seeking closer ties with China, and hitting out at Taiwan would be a means of doing so. Or Pakistan could have been acting on China’s behest, with China expected to try and constrain Taiwan’s international space ahead of the upcoming local elections next month. As for why Pakistan later reversed course, this is also unclear, except perhaps that international backlash was larger than expected–or perhaps there was pressure behind the scenes from the US.

This is not the only time that similar events have occurred in recent memory, however. Earlier this year, a planned trip by President Lai Ching-te to Eswatini, Taiwan’s only African diplomatic ally, to mark King Mswati III’s 40th anniversary of accession to the throne, as well as Mswati’s 58th birthday, was abruptly cancelled. Specifically, countries that Lai would have passed over on his flight to Eswatini, Madagascar, Mauritius, and the Seychelles revoked overflight permissions shortly before Lai was to set out on his trip.

The sudden cancellation was largely interpreted as China flexing its muscles in terms of its influence in Africa, with the Lai administration suggesting that China threatened to revoke debt cancellation for Madagascar, Mauritius, and the Seychelles if they did not comply. It is unclear, then, whether something similar could have occurred with Pakistan, in that the attempt to revoke overflight privileges could have occurred because of Chinese pressure, but also could have occurred as a result of actions by the Pakistani government.

It is to be seen if this is a new tactic in China’s playbook, then, seeking to limit travel by Taiwanese airlines as a sign of Chinese displeasure. Still, such actions may ultimately anger Taiwan, reminding the public shortly before elections of Chinese coercion and its bullying on the international stage. One may perhaps perceive reports of Taiwanese having their passports confiscated by Ugandan and Kenyan authorities with the demand to provide Chinese travel documents in a similar vein, even if Kenya later reversed course. This, too, could occur at the initiative of these countries’ governments or because of Chinese pressure, with China using its substantial economic and political heft globally in order for this to occur.

title: Muş'un Xwarik köylüleri mera savunmasında: JES projesine direnişin 180. günü
content:
Muş'un Varto/Gimgim ilçesine bağlı Çalıdere/Xwarik köyünde, ABD şirketi IGNIS H2 Enerji Üretim AŞ'nin jeotermal kaynak arama projesine karşı çadır nöbeti, Jinnews'ın haberine göre 180. gününe girdi. 


3 Mayıs'ta başlatılan direnişte köylüler, projenin su kaynaklarına, meralara, hayvancılığa ve doğal yaşama zarar vermemesi için sondaj faaliyetlerinin durdurulmasını istiyor.


Varto Ekoloji Platformu Gençlik Meclisi öncülüğünde sürdürülen nöbeti cuma günü Segiran, Dapak ve Muzuran köylüleri devraldı. Nöbet alanında "Varto halkı jeotermal enerji santrali istemiyor. Suyuma, toprağıma dokunma" pankartı taşındı.


2 Kasım'da gerçekleştirilecek bilirkişi keşfi öncesinde direnişin 180'inci gününe ulaşması, bölgedeki hareketliliği artırdı. Köylüler ve ekoloji örgütleri, Bingöl İdare Mahkemesi'nin yaptıracağı incelemede bölgenin doğal ve toplumsal özelliklerinin dikkate alınmasını istiyor.


Bakanlık: Jeolojik ve hidrojeolojik veriler eksik


Köylülerin su kaynaklarına yönelik kaygıları, Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığının 21 Ekim'de TBMM'ye gönderdiği resmî yanıtta yer alan eksikliklerle de gündeme geldi.


DEM Parti Muş Milletvekili Sümeyye Boz Çakı'nın 27 Şubat tarihli yazılı soru önergesine sekiz ay sonra yanıt veren Bakanlık, jeotermal arama projesinin tanıtım dosyasında bölgeye ait ayrıntılı jeolojik ve hidrojeolojik verilerin bulunmadığını bildirdi.


Bakanlık, yeraltı su kaynakları ve içme suyu rezervleri üzerindeki olası etkileri değerlendiren hidrojeolojik raporun da sunulmadığını belirterek eksikliklerin giderilmesini ve su temini ile çevre mevzuatına ilişkin gerekli taahhütlerin dosyaya eklenmesini istediğini açıkladı.


Yanıtta, proje alanının Güllüce Regülatörü ve Hidroelektrik Enerji Santrali'nin iletim hattı güzergâhıyla doğrudan etkileşim içinde bulunduğu da belirtildi. Bakanlık, çalışmaların ilgili iletim hattını etkilemeyecek biçimde sınırlandırılması ve sondaj sonrasında Devlet Su İşleri'nden yeniden görüş alınması gerektiğini bildirdi.


Bakanlık, mera tahsislerinde çiftçilerin görüşlerinin dikkate alındığını ve faaliyetlerin çevresel etkilerinin mevzuat çerçevesinde değerlendirildiğini savundu.


Köylüler ise karar süreçlerine yeterince katılamadıklarını ileri sürüyor.


4 bin hektarlık sahada 10 sondaj kuyusu


Şirketin Güzelkent sahası için hazırladığı projede, yaklaşık 4 bin 38 hektarlık ruhsat alanında toplam 10 jeotermal arama kuyusu açılması öngörülüyor. Sondajlar için belirlenen ÇED alanı ise 8 hektar.


2025 tarihli proje bilgilerine göre yaklaşık 95 milyon lira yatırım bedeli öngörülen arama çalışmalarının 20 ay sürmesi, 30 kişinin istihdam edilmesi planlanıyor.


Proje dosyasından aktarılan verilere göre bir sondaj noktası Küçüktepe köyündeki bir konuta yaklaşık 160 metre, bir diğeri Mengeneç Çayı'na 103 metre uzaklıkta bulunuyor. Bazı sondaj noktaları orman alanları içinde yer alıyor.


IGNIS, kendi internet sitesinde Güzelkent sahasının Kuzey Anadolu ve Doğu Anadolu faylarının kesişimine yakın bir bölgede bulunduğunu belirtiyor. Şirket, jeolojik ve jeofizik araştırmalar yürüttüğünü, rezervuar özelliklerini belirlemek amacıyla yeni sondajlar planladığını açıklıyor.


Henüz faaliyette bir elektrik üretim santrali bulunmuyor. Tartışma, ileride santral yatırımına dönüşebilecek jeotermal kaynak arama ve sondaj aşamasında yoğunlaşıyor.


Köylüler jeotermale neden karşı çıkıyor?


Bölgenin başlıca geçim kaynakları hayvancılık, küçük ölçekli tarım ve arıcılık. Köylüler sondaj sahalarının yalnızca kapladıkları alanla değil, su dolaşımı, otlaklar ve doğal yaşam üzerindeki olası etkileriyle değerlendirilmesini istiyor.


Jeotermal enerji, fosil yakıtlara alternatif yenilenebilir bir kaynak olmakla birlikte, çıkarılan sıcak ve mineralli akışkanların yönetimi özel önlemler gerektiriyor. Kuyuların sızdırmazlığının sağlanamaması, sondaj atıklarının uygunsuz depolanması veya kullanılmış jeotermal akışkanın güvenli biçimde yeniden yeraltına basılamaması halinde su ve toprak kirliliği riski doğabiliyor.


Jeotermal akışkanların kimyasal bileşimi sahadan sahaya değişiyor. Bazı alanlarda bor, arsenik ve çözünmüş başka minerallerin çevreye yayılması tarımsal üretim açısından sorun oluşturabiliyor. Bu risklerin Varto'da gerçekleşip gerçekleşmeyeceği ise saha ölçümleri ve bağımsız bilimsel incelemelerle belirlenmek zorunda.


Sondaj ve akışkan enjeksiyonunun fay sistemleri üzerindeki olası etkileri de bölge halkının itirazları arasında. Jeofizik uzmanları, deprem tehlikesi bulunan alanlarda doğal sismik hareketliliğin …

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Feds declare Roberts Bank 2 expansion ‘project of national interest’
content:
A large-scale port expansion to be located off the coast of Delta, B.C., has been labelled as a ‘project of national interest,’ a designation which, according to environmental advocates, could result in the extinction of the Southern Resident Killer Whales.

In an email sent to APTN News on the heels of the announcement, Julia Levin, the associate director of national climate at Environmental Defence, wrote that not only is this “bad news for orcas,” but that it may be “a run-around on the Species at Risk Act, given that was the only approval that the project didn’t have.”

Robert Banks Terminal 2 is an expansion of the Port of Vancouver, operated by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority (VFPA) and located on 130 hectares (about 200 soccer pitches) of marine land off the B.C. coast.

According to a release from Ottawa, the project would add 2.4 million containers of annual capacity, increasing it by “approximately 50 per cent.”

It would also support “up to $100 billion in annual trade,” therefore “helping Canada achieve its goal of doubling non-U.S. exports by 2035.”

It meets the criteria of what can be considered a project in the national interest, according to Bill C-5, the Building Canada Act, which are that it must “strengthen Canada’s autonomy, resilience, and security”; “provide economic or other benefits”; “advance the interests of Indigenous Peoples”; and “contribute to clean growth and to meeting Canada’s climate change objectives.”

Once this criteria is met, major projects may be exempt from certain laws, such as the Species at Risk Act.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement that, “By listing Roberts Bank Terminal 2 as a project of national interest, we are better connecting our economy with the world and diversifying our trade. As the world competes for capital, Canada will not wait. We are building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive Canadian economy.”

However, the project is also slated to be built in the Fraser River Estuary, which has already lost more than 85 per cent of floodplain habitat and supports 102 species at risk, according to Levin.

“The estuary is critical habitat for salmon and SRKW, southern resident killer whales, as confirmed by DFO and the environmental assessment of the project – which assessed that the new terminal would result in destruction of the legally protected Southern Resident Killer Whale’s critical habitat,” she wrote.

A 2020 environmental assessment for the project determined that it would cause “significant adverse environmental effects” on Chinook salmon, wetlands, and the resident whales, which have been listed as critically endangered since 2003.

An application for a Species at Risk permit, which would allow the building of the Roberts Bank 2 port in the habitat, was filed on Oct. 28, 2024, with a deadline of Oct. 28, 2026 — two days ago, as of publishing.

‘An incredible animal’: B.C. port expansion could drive southern resident killer whales to extinction, advocates warn

As of Friday morning, the tool used to track the permit’s progress on Canada’s website indicated it was overdue, but by the afternoon, the page had been wiped.

Canada held a consultation period while it considered the national interest designation, which began

In a letter sent to the Major Projects Office by Raincoast Conservation Foundation, the advocacy and research organization wrote that “Designation as a PONI is not an appropriate use of the Building Canada Act.

“Raincoast is concerned that the national interest cannot be reduced to container capacity, trade volume and construction speed when the proposal is in the Fraser River Estuary. Promises and investments announced by the federal government … to ensure prosperity by combining regulatory certainty with environmental protection are an insufficient guarantee given the level of harm identified from this project.”

Levin stated that, “by declaring this mega-port as a ‘project of national interest,’ Prime Minister Carney has dealt a devastating blow to the last remaining Southern Resident Killer Whales.

“This political moment will pass, but extinction is forever.”

Emma is a Red River Métis with family roots in St. Malo, Manitoba. She graduated from RRC Polytech’s Creative Communications program in 2023 and went on to serve as a community journalist and photographer for the Free Press Community Review until she joined APTN in 2026. title: What can a global strike of dockworkers achieve for Gaza? (Al Jazeera)
content:
More than 25 dockworkers’ trade unions in at least 110 ports in 22 countries are going on strike on October 30.Listen (7 mins)

Dock and port workers have long had a tradition of solidarity with the oppressed, upheld by strong labour unions and workers’ rights.

In February 2025, nearly a year and a half into Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, dockworkers’ unions from Mediterranean countries came together to disrupt weapons shipments to Israel and Western countries’ military support of the onslaught.

list 2 of 4Hundreds protest in Tunisia for release of jailed Gaza flotilla activists

list 3 of 4Gaza flotilla activist on hunger strike in Tunisia jail ‘on verge of death’

list 4 of 4Detained Tunisian flotilla activists: Worsening health amid family anguish

“Weapons need transport, infrastructure, and workers’ hands to reach their destination,” Markos Bekris, leader of Greece’s dockworkers’ union, ENEDEP, at the Port of Piraeus in Athens, told Al Jazeera. “That is where our power lies.”

Now, dock and port workers in 22 countries across five continents are holding a strike on Friday, which workers and researchers told Al Jazeera is expected to be “historic” in scale. The International Day of Action of Dockworkers and Port Workers – also called “Dockworkers do not work for war” – involves 110 ports and 25 trade unions.

“Every union will do what they choose, but be connected to the same principles and struggle,” Francesco Staccioli, the national secretary of transport and ports in Italy’s USB trade union, told Al Jazeera.

The unions’ main demand is “an immediate end to the genocide of the Palestinian people and all imperialist wars”.

Mohammed al-Attar, a dockworker who left Gaza in 2015 and is now based in Hamburg, Germany, said the workers “are the power”.

“We can save thousands of lives if we stop working just for two days,” he said.

Al-Attar feels hopeful about the global strike, but is “deeply disappointed” in his trade union Ver.di in Germany, which he accused of “incomprehensible silence” over Gaza.

In early 2025, dockworkers in the Mediterranean area came together to discuss how to concretely act “against privatisation, and against the genocide in Palestine”.

The original meeting included five unions organising in 20 ports across five countries, but continued to grow. The unions met several times, first in Athens, then in Genoa, and later in Istanbul. That was where unions from more than 35 ports published the Istanbul Declaration in May this year, and declared October 30 as their day of action.

In a statement, the unions called for the “recognition of an independent Palestinian state, recognised by the international community, within the 1967 borders and with East Jerusalem as its capital”, and “an end to the US-Israeli wars of aggression in the Middle East and against Iran, and full solidarity with the peoples of Cuba, Venezuela and Sudan”.

“Refusing the war is giving humanity a chance to live better. This is what I’m really convinced about,” the USB’s Staccioli told Al Jazeera.

More than 25 dockworkers’ trade unions, representing more than 110 ports in 22 countries and regions across five continents, are taking part. Most of the strikes will happen at regular working hours, but in France, Italy, India, Greece and Turkiye, 24-hour strikes have been called.

Strikes of up to two hours have also been announced in Morocco, Cyprus and other ports.

Organisers told Al Jazeera that workers and trade unions from other sectors have been called on to join with port workers, notably in Greece, while in Italy the USB has called for a general strike.

“It’s bigger than we thought,” Staccioli said. “This has spread all over the world.”

No Harbour for Genocide (NHG), a campaigning collective that researches weapon supply chains, supports the action. A spokesperson told Al Jazeera that maritime infrastructure was important in “facilitating military trade within the context of the genocide in Palestine”.

Dockworker unions in India, Sweden, Denmark, Australia, Brazil, Mexico, Uruguay and the west coast of the United States have all pledged to take part, the spokesperson added.

The Palestinian labour movement endorsed the strike and called on more to join, urging unions to “escalate Boycott, Divest, Sanctions …

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Family of Miranda Mamakwa seeking criminal investigation into ‘negligent’ death of mother
content:
The family of a woman who died after a federal program did not arrange transportation to medical appointments is asking for a criminal investigation.

“The criminal justice system should only be invoked where grounds exist to believe a crime has been committed,” read the statement from the family. “Public officials are as accountable as anyone else in this country for reckless acts that endanger those in their charge.”

According to her family, Miranda Mamakwa died on Sept. 8 after she didn’t receive transportation to multiple important appointments following an open-heart surgery.

She was 31 and the mother of three kids.

“Literally, the blood of Indigenous people is required for any kind of meaningful change,” said Julian Falconer, legal counsel for the family. “We have created a pattern of behavior where we only get their attention once they [Canada] have killed somebody.”

Mamakwa was a member of Fort Severn First Nation, the northernmost community in Ontario, and was relying on transportation from the Non-Insured Health Benefits Program (NIHB) to get to follow-up appointments in Thunder Bay after her surgery in April 2026.

NIHB is a federal program provided by Indigenous Services Canada (ISC), and is mandated to provide medical transportation services, alongside other supports such as medication and vision care, to First Nations and Inuit people.

Her first appointment following her return home was scheduled for May 28, and the local nursing station had sent a request by fax (the only method of communication with NIHB offices available to them, Falconer confirmed) for NIHB to provide transportation.

However, the nearest office, located in Sioux Lookout, never got back to them.

Despite multiple requests and letters from her doctor, she missed four appointments, including “an appointment with a vascular surgeon about blood clots,” according to the backgrounder provided to the media.

The backgrounder also stated that, following the surgery, Mamakwa had been put on blood thinner medication for blood clots, and was visiting the Nation’s nursing station once a week for blood work.

She eventually became lethargic and “began to lose feeling in her fingers,” the backgrounder noted, and she ultimately died of a brain haemorrhage after being transported to Thunder Bay.

Brain haemorrhages are caused by a blood vessel leaking or bursting in the brain, essentially drowning it.

Prior to her death, on Aug. 19, Mamakwa had made a grim post on social media: “If I die, please go after them.”

On Friday, Falconer and Mamakwa’s parents, Eva Mamakwa and Mike Bluecoat, issued a statement announcing they had sent a formal request to Ontario Provincial Police Commissioner Thomas Carrique.

“The wanton and reckless disregard shown for Miranda’s health, and ultimately her life, by those public officials responsible for arranging her medical transportation makes such an investigation a necessity,” the statement said.

Eva and Mike are staying out of the public eye, but did comment in the statement.

“This should never have happened to Miranda. She should be alive today,” they said. “We deserve to know how something like this happened, and we want the individual or individuals responsible for failing to respond to these urgent requests for transportation to be held accountable. They cost Miranda her life. They cost her children a future without their mother.”

Mother of First Nations woman who couldn’t get medical transport and died seeks reform

Falconer said he does not take criminal cases lightly, but that this circumstance was “wonton neglect.”

“Three children are without a mother. A grandmother is left explaining to these children where their mother is. Words cannot describe the extent of the neglect here,” he said.

It’s also indicative of Canada’s failure to act in the best interests of Indigenous Peoples, he said.

Alongside this matter, the lawyer is also legal counsel to a coalition of several First Nations and tribal councils, led by Wunnumin Lake First Nation, Matawa Chiefs Council, and Windigo First Nations Council, which filed a human rights complaint against ISC on Oct. 1.

“The complaint alleges widespread neglect and systemic discrimination by the NIHB, whose routine administrative failures effectively deny life-sustaining healthcare to remote, fly-in communities,” stated a release on the Falconers legal practice’s website.

The coalition is seeking “sweeping structural overhauls,” as well as $20,000 in damages …

content:

Erkekler EuroLeague'de 9. hafta maçında Beşiktaş, Virtus Bologna'yı deplasmanda bitime 0,1 saniye kala Conor Morgan'ın kaydettiği üçlükle 103-101 yendi.

İlk yarıyı 54-47, üçüncü periyodu 74-70 geride tamamlayan Beşiktaş, son bölümde unutulmaz bir geri dönüşe imza attı. Lonnie Walker IV 30 sayıyla sahanın en skorer ismi olurken Scottie Wilbekin 16, maç kazandıran üçlüğü sokan Morgan 10 sayı attı.

Virtus Bologna'da ise Derrick Aiston Jr. 19 sayıyla takımının en skorer ismiydi.

Beşiktaş böylece 4. galibiyetini alarak haftayı 11. sırada tamamladı. Aynı galibiyet sayısındaki Virtus Bologna ise 13. sırada yer alıyor.

title: Διεθνής απεργιακή ημέρα δράσης σε 110 λιμάνια σ’ όλο τον κόσμο: Δεν δουλεύουμε για τον πόλεμό τους!
content:
Σε όλες τις ηπείρους και πάνω από 110 λιμάνια ανά τον κόσμο κινητοποιήθηκαν στην απεργία των λιμενεργατών και τη διεθνή ημέρα αντιπολεμικής δράσης φωνάζοντας ότι δεν δουλεύουν για τη μεταφορά όπλων. Λιμάνια των λαών και της ειρήνης και όχι ορμητήρια των ιμπεριαλιστών. Στη Γαλλία 90% ακινητοποίηση, στην Ιταλία πάνω από ένα εκατομμύριο στους δρόμους 70 πόλεων. Στην ελληνική γεωγραφία, μεγάλη παμπειραϊκή απεργία και συμμετοχή, στη Θεσσαλονίκη μπλοκαρίστηκαν εμπρευματοκιβώτια και φορτηγά, κινητοποιήσεις σε πολλές πόλεις και λιμάνια.


Χαρακτηριστικά του έντονου αντιπολεμικού και αντιϊμπεριαλιστικού παλμού των διαδηλώσεων είναι και τα συνθήματα στα πανό: Καμιά θυσία για τα κέρδη και τους πολέμους τους. Καμιά συμμετοχή στα ιμπεριαλιστικά σχέδια ΗΠΑ, ΝΑΤΟ, ΕΕ, Ισραήλ. Δώστε λεφτά για μισθούς, υγεία και παιδεία και όχι στου πολέμου τα σφαγεία. Κρίση, πόλεμος, ξερηζωμός, αυτός είναι ο καπιταλισμός. Κανένας ναυτεργάτης στις εμπόλεμες θάλασσες, καμία θυσία για τα κέρδη των εφοπλιστών. Κάτω η κυβέρνηση του πολέμου. Λευτεριά στην Παλαιστίνη. Έρευνα για τις κοινωνικές ανάγκες κι όχι για τον πόλεμο. Καμιά εμπλοκή των πανεπιστημίων στην πολεμική προετοιμασία. Μπλόκο στην πολεμική μηχανή.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Family searches for missing Inuk teen in Ottawa
content:
The mother of a missing 14-year-old Inuk girl is hoping her daughter will find her way home as Ottawa police and community members continue searching for her.


“I just want her home,” Julian Oyukuluk said in an interview Friday about her daughter, Lydia.


Lydia Oyukuluk was last seen Wednesday, Oct. 28, between 5:45 and 6 p.m. in the 1000 block of Gladstone Avenue, where she lives with her family, her mother said. It’s a bit south of the Hintonburg neighbourhood and a few blocks west of Preston Street’s Little Italy area.


Julian said she expected Lydia to return home that night. Lydia left without her cellphone, which is now with investigators, her mother said.


Family members, friends and members of Ottawa’s Inuit community have joined the search, Julian said. So far, they have looked in Major’s Hill Park near the Parliament Buildings and along the Rideau Canal.


“She’s very easy to approach,” Julian said of her daughter. “She’s friendly and she’s sensitive.”


The family is originally from Arctic Bay and has lived in Ottawa for more than a year, Julian said.


On Friday, Ottawa police asked residents in the 1000 block of Gladstone Avenue, including along Spadina Avenue and surrounding streets, to check their backyards, sheds, garages and other places where Lydia might have sought shelter.


Police are also asking residents to review doorbell camera and surveillance footage from Wednesday evening onward for possible sightings.


And police released a second picture of Lydia in which she’s wearing a prominent cross necklace. But police weren’t able to say whether she was wearing it when she went missing.


Lydia is described as four-foot-nine with a petite build and long black hair partially dyed red at the back.


She was last seen wearing baggy black sweatpants, a black camouflage hoodie and socks. She was not wearing shoes.


Ottawa police have also released an additional photo of Lydia taken before she went missing. The image is the most recent one available to police showing her appearance and build, said Ottawa Police media spokesperson Const.

Fern

 John-Simon.


Anyone who sees Lydia Oyukuluk is asked to call 911 so she can receive immediate assistance, an updated release said. Anyone with information about her whereabouts can contact Ottawa police at 613-236-1222.

author: labor4pal
title: Canada’s central labour union says workers will not handle military cargo going to Israel (Middle East Eye)
content:
The Canadian Labour Congress says it voted for ‘solidarity with Palestinian workers and their families’

Shipping containers are seen in the Port of Montreal in Montreal, Quebec, on 23 August 2026 (Andrej Ivanov/AFP)

Published date: 30 October 2026 20:30 GMT|Last update:3 days 17 mins ago

After a landmark vote on Thursday, Canada’s central labour union, representing some 3 million workers across the country, has announced that it will “refuse to handle weapons and military equipment destined for Israel”.

The Canadian Labour Congress (CLC) said in a statement that it supported the resolution “in solidarity with Palestinian workers and their families, and with all those calling for peace, justice and respect for international law”.

It demanded the government of Canada do the same and “end all direct and indirect transfers of arms and military equipment to Israel”.

Last year, Middle East Eye reported that the Canadian government misled the public when it said it was pausing all new weapons export permits to Israel.

Commercially available data showed shipments not only continued but were actually fast-tracked – and sometimes via indirect routes such as through the United States, according to findings compiled by an all-volunteer team from the Palestinian Youth Movement (PYM) and the groups World Beyond War and Arms Embargo Now.

Ottawa, the groups said, wanted to placate an electorate that has expressed growing dissatisfaction with how the Liberal Party has responded to Israel’s war on Gaza – but without actually reversing its policy of unconditional support for Israel, as it publicly pledged.

The 58-page document, entitled “Exposing Canadian Military Exports to Israel”, cites more than 390 shipments from 21 Canadian manufacturers in six cities that included more than 420,000 bullets, 735 cartridge parts (ammunition sets for firearms), F-35 jet parts, such as navigation sensors, radar systems and dual-use items like GPS antennas.

“Canada has a responsibility to ensure that weapons and military equipment produced here are not used to harm Palestinian civilians or contribute to violations of international humanitarian law,” the CLC said in its statement.

“Canada must uphold international law, protect civilian lives and support a just and lasting peace for Palestinians and Israelis,” it added.

“The labour movement has always stood for the rights, safety and dignity of working people everywhere. We reject all forms of hatred and discrimination, including antisemitism, anti-Palestinian racism and Islamophobia.”

The CLC has decades-long ties with the Israeli trade union, known as the Histradut.

Those ties slowly began to fray after the First Intifada, a 2014 study in the Journal of Labor and Society showed.

In May of this year, the CLC voted to cut ties with the Histadrut, though debate was blocked on a resolution to declare all Israeli goods, services and institutional relationships “Hot Cargo”.

Labour for Palestine – Canada, which has been at the forefront of the movement to ban the handling of military shipments to Israel, said Canadian workers “helped end apartheid in South Africa”.

“We supported East Timorese liberation. We took a stand against war in Iraq. Now is the time to take a stand for Palestine,” the group said.

The advocacy group Canadians for Justice and Peace in the Middle East hailed Thursday’s vote in a post on X, calling it “an important way that workers can prevent Canadian weapons from facilitating genocide”.

The activist group Independent Jewish Voices said the move “is a clear message”.

“Canadian labourers refuse to be complicit in Israel’s genocide in Gaza and the expansion of illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank.”

Global Affairs Canada, the country’s foreign ministry, said it has exported more than $44m in “military goods” to Israel between 2023 and 2025.

author: Λουκάς Σταμέλλος
title: Δίκη για τον βασανισμό Μάγγου: Ψεκ αγορεύσεις με χυδαία προσβολή θύματος και γονιών
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Δίκη για τον βασανισμό Μάγγου: Ψεκ αγορεύσεις με χυδαία προσβολή θύματος και γονιών


Φανταστείτε λίγο τα παρακάτω:


***


Ο Βόλος έχει μακρά ιστορία παρουσίας σκληρών αναρχικών. Εκεί, οπαδοί του Κροπότκιν, του Μπακούνιν και του Νετσάγιεφ (μαζί), σε συνεργασία με πράκτορες της Στάζι που μετεγκαταστάθηκαν στη Μαγνησία από τη δεκαετία του ‘90, διατηρούσαν στον νομό δύο γιάφκες της Συνωμοσίας των Πυρήνων της Φωτιάς και έφτιαξαν μια συλλογικότητα που ονομαζόταν «Συντονισμός Συλλογικοτήτων Βόλου Ενάντια στην Καύση Σκουπιδιών», με επικεφαλής και ιδεολογικούς καθοδηγητές – ινστρούκτορες καθηγητές Πανεπιστημίου.


Τη νύχτα της 13ης Ιουνίου 2020, αφού είχαν στείλει υψηλόβαθμους αξιωματικούς στο νοσοκομείο με μπροστάρη τον Βασίλειο Μάγγο, αποπειράθηκαν να καταλάβουν το κτίριο της Διεύθυνσης Αστυνομίας Βόλου αλλά τελικά απωθήθηκαν χάρη στην ηρωϊκή αντίσταση των – εξαντλημένων από τις υπερωρίες και την ανίκανη επιχειρησιακή ηγεσία τους – αστυνομικών.


Το ασήμαντο περιστατικό με το σπάσιμο των πλευρών του Βασίλειου Μάγγου (που δεν ήξεραν ποιος είναι) έξω από τα δικαστήρια, στις 14 Ιουνίου 2020, έτυχε να καταγραφεί σε βίντεο, το οποίο μπορεί να αποκτήσει όσο αντίκτυπο θέλει αυτός που το διακινεί, ασχέτως του τι δείχνει. Για κακή τύχη της Ελληνικής Αστυνομίας, της Δημοκρατίας και της Δικαιοσύνης και προς μεγάλη ικανοποίηση των ηγετών αυτής της συλλογικότητας σκληρών αναρχικών, η οποία ελέγχει και τους δημοσιογράφους στην ΕΡΤ, στο The Press Project και στο OmniaTV, ένα νέο καταχθόνιο σχέδιο αυτών των ολετήρων της Τάξεως τέθηκε σε εφαρμογή.


Κάποιος δημοσίευσε ένα κείμενο καταγγελίας, το οποίο θα ήταν απολύτως αδύνατον να έχει δημοσιεύσει ο ίδιος ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος, επειδή περιείχε πολιτική τοποθέτηση. Οπότε το κείμενο είναι πλαστό εντελώς, αλλά ταυτόχρονα αποτελεί και απόδειξη ότι οι μάρτυρες που κατέθεσαν στη δίκη χάρη στις μηχανορραφίες του Συνηγόρου του Πολίτη (ο οποίος δεν έχει κανένα ρόλο εκτός από το να εξυπηρετεί σκοπιμότητες, είκοσι χρόνια ο ίδιος) δεν είναι πραγματικοί μάρτυρες, επειδή δεν αναφέρει τα ονόματά τους η καταγγελία. Είναι κομάντο της συλλογικότητας αυτής που προαναφέρθηκε: οι καθηγητές πανεπιστημίου τους επέλεξαν ως μέλη του σκληρού πυρήνα και τους καθοδήγησαν τι να πουν στο δικαστήριο. Ούτε είχαν δει τον Μάγγο ούτε τίποτα. Αλλά δεν είχαν προλάβει να προετοιμάσουν καλά την πρώτη μάρτυρα (έξι χρόνια μετά) και κάτι της ξέφυγε. Αλλά τελικά δεν είπε και κανείς από αυτούς τίποτα στο δικαστήριο.


Επίσης, την καταγγελία την έγραψε ο ίδιος ο Μάγγος για να γίνει αποδεκτός από αυτή την ενιαία και συμπαγή συλλογικότητα σκληρών αναρχικών. Το κείμενο της καταγγελίας έχει επίσης την ίδια γραμματοσειρά με τα υπομνήματα που κατατέθηκαν από μάρτυρες, επομένως όλοι καταλαβαίνουμε τι μας κρύβουν.


Η δίωξη των αστυνομικών για βασανιστήρια στον Βασίλειο Μάγγο, είναι μέρος του ίδιου σχεδίου με τον θανατηφόρο τραυματισμό του αστυνομικού της ΥΑΤ, Λυγγερίδη και με την προφυλάκιση δύο αθώων αστυνομικών στο Άργος από τους οποίους, ενώ καταδίωκαν κάποιον που κρατούσε πιστόλι – δεν ήξεραν ότι ήταν ρέπλικα, πού να το ξέρουν; – «έφυγε» μία σφαίρα και εποστρακίστηκε και έτυχε να βρει τον καταδιωκόμενο. Το σχέδιο αυτό (αφού απέτυχε η κατάληψη της Διεύθυνσης Αστυνομίας Βόλου το 2020; έμεινε αδιευκρίνιστο) είναι να αποθαρρυνθούν οι Έλληνες Αστυνομικοί από το να κάνουν τη δουλειά τους. Θα λέτε «χρειάζομαι αστυνομία» κι εκείνοι θα λένε «χρειάζομαι την οικογένειά μου» γιατί θα κινδυνεύουν με φυλάκιση. Αυτή την αστυνομία θέλουμε; Παλιά η τηλεόραση έδειχνε ωραίες εκπομπές με μότο «Σύμβολον θυσίας υπέρ του έθνους ο Έλλην Χωροφύλαξ». Αλλά όχι πια, οπότε μη ξεχνάτε ότι κινδυνεύει η Δημοκρατία, η Δικαιοσύνη, η Κοινωνία, η Ειρήνη και το Έθνος.


Ταυτόχρονα, ο πατέρας και η μητέρα του θύματος, χρησιμοποιώντας τον Συνήγορο του Πολίτη και μια σειρά από εισαγγελείς – οι οποίοι, να σημειωθεί, είναι είτε ανίκανοι είτε υπηρετούν σκοπιμότητες – τα έστησαν όλα αυτά μόνοι τους, για να κάνουν αγωγή στο Δημόσιο και να πάρουν λεφτά. Αν θέλουν να αποδείξουν ότι όντως πιστεύουν ότι φταίνε οι αστυνομικοί για κάτι, ας παραιτηθούν από τα δικαιώματά τους για να μας πείσουν. Αλλιώς έρχονται μαύρες μέρες για το έθνος μας.


***


Αυτή είναι η εικόνα των ισχυρισμών που προέβαλαν οι τέσσερις συνήγοροι αστυνομικών που αγόρευσαν την Πέμπτη 29 και την Παρασκευή 30 Οκτωβρίου 2026, στη δίκη για τον βασανισμό του Βασίλειου Μάγγου, ως εναλλακτική/-ές θεωρία/-ες που εξηγεί, κατά την άποψή τους, το γιατί οι πελάτες τους πρέπει να κηρυχθούν αθώοι.


Για του …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: ‘We take care of each other’: Voices from Montreal’s Cabot Square
content:
In Montreal’s Cabot Square, where homeless Indigenous people have gathered for decades, news that a member of the city’s police services (SPVM) had been suspended for urinating on homeless Montrealers was greeted largely without shock.


Regular visitors, as well as outreach workers from the various organizations serving unhoused populations in the west of downtown, describe relations between homeless people and police in and around Cabot Square as marked by distrust and fear.


People APTN News spoke with in Cabot Square over the last two weeks reported accumulating tickets, amounting to hundreds of dollars in fines, for fare evasion on the city’s transit system or jaywalking on Ste. Catherine Street. People who drink alcohol in the Square also said they’d received tickets for open containers.

Few make any attempt to pay the tickets. For them, getting another ticket is simply a fact of life in Cabot Square, though one that may give police a reason to eventually arrest them.


Cabot Square


Measuring one block by one block, Cabot Square is the only significant piece of greenspace in the western end of downtown Montreal. Located on Ste. Catherine St. at the corner of Atwater Ave., the Square is directly across from the former Montreal Forum.

 


For decades, the space has attracted homeless Indigenous people, thanks in part to a years-long provincial policy of housing Inuit from Nunavik, flown south for medical care, in the nearby YMCA. 


Though medical patients from Nunavik have been sent to the Ullivik residence in Montreal’s western suburbs since 2016, Cabot Square maintains a community of unhoused people with a strong Indigenous presence.

 


During the golden years of Montreal hockey, crowds used to gather in Cabot Square ahead of the Montreal Canadiens’ many victory parades. The 1955 Rocket Richard Riot kicked off there when enraged French supporters of Canadiens’ great Maurice (Rocket) Richard gathered to protest his suspension by an Anglophone NHL president, which they believed to be ethnically motivated.

 


Northeast view of Cabot Square from the corner of Ste. Catherine and Lambert-Closse. The former Montreal Forum is on the right, just out of frame. Photo: Jesse Staniforth/APTN


Since the Forum closed in 1996, a

city document about revitalizing the neighbourhood

 notes that “The disappearance of this important generator of traffic caused a marked deterioration of rue Sainte Catherine Ouest.” 


In practice, this has meant Cabot Square has largely been the domain of unhoused people.

 


In 2013, the city redeveloped the Square, but by that point the homeless population was so stable that developers expected they would return. Designers maintained benches and low walls that denizens of the Square routinely sleep on, and the city renovated the small building known as the “Round House” that has become a café and office for outreach workers working with the square’s unhoused occupants.

 


A small geography

 


A mediator from the Cabot Square Project, an initiative started in 2014 by the Native Women’s Shelter of Montreal in collaboration with the local borough and the YMCA Homelessness Assistance Program, told APTN the Square tends to separate along linguistic and ethnic lines. In the eastern part of the park, there are more white people and more francophones.

 


In the west of the Square, near the Round House, mostly Indigenous people gather, mixing with Black people, all speaking English. The seating space around the statue of Giovanni Caboto (John Cabot) in the centre of the park is shared by everyone, while the alley due east of the Square is where people go to smoke crack.

 


On rainy days, Cabot Square empties, as regular visitors head to the Resilience day centre a few blocks down the hill on Atwater Ave., as well as nearby libraries and shopping centres. 


They used to go into the Metro, Montreal’s transit system, particularly the entrance to the Atwater Metro station adjacent to the Round House in the west end of the park. But in November 2024, Montreal’s public transit authority the Société de transport de Montréal (STM) sealed access to the station from the Square. 

 


The west side of Cabot Square, featuring the Round House (renovated in 2013) on the right, which has a small café and outreach office. On the left is the sealed entrance to Atwater Metro station, bearing the notice (in French), “Access closed to improve security at your station.” Photo: Jesse Staniforth/APTN News …

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Professional women hockey players to lead training camp in Iqaluit
content:
A team of professional women hockey players is coming to Iqaluit this weekend to lead a hockey camp for girls.


The Nunavut Ukpiit Hockey Association has brought in three players from the Toronto Sceptres, who compete in the Professional Women’s Hockey League, to take part in strength and conditioning courses led by Sceptres training coach Kate Germain, according to an update on the association’s Facebook page.


Events are scheduled to start Friday at 4:30 p.m. and continue through Sunday. Girls registered with the Iqaluit Amateur Hockey Association are invited to take part.


Regularly scheduled events hosted at Arctic Winter Games Arena, such as public skating and other practices, have been cancelled to allow for the hockey camp programming.


According to the association’s website, the goal of this camp is to empower women’s hockey players across the territory, both in hockey and in life.

author: labor4pal
title: With ‘Largest Coordinated Port Action Ever,’ Dockworkers in 22 Countries Strike Against Gaza Genocide (Common Dreams)
content:
Seafarers and dockworkers chant slogans as they take part in a march from the port of Piraeus, near Athens, towards Greece’s Ministry of Maritime Affairs on October 30, 2026.

(Photo by Aris Messinis/AFP via Getty Images)

Dockworkers in more than 20 countries—from France to India to Greece—are withholding their labor on Friday to demand an end to Israel’s genocidal assault on Gaza and highlight the role that commercial ports play in fueling deadly militarism worldwide.

Organizers said the work stoppages, led by dockworkers’ unions at 113 ports across 22 countries, would be the “largest coordinated port action ever,” easily surpassing the international day of action held in February. No Harbour for Genocide, a collective of trade unions and others supporting the day of action, said $2.8 billion worth of cargo will be halted at Mediterranean ports, where workers are planning to strike for 24 hours.

“A cargo refused in one port sails on to the next,” said No Harbour for Genocide. “Refused in every port, it stops, and the workers have enforced the embargo that governments announced and did not.”

In a joint statement last month announcing the day of action, dockworkers’ unions from Türkiye, Morocco, Italy, France, Greece, Italy, and Basque Country laid out their demands:

An immediate end to the genocide of the Palestinian people and the opening of safe corridor for humanitarian aid.. An end of colonization, occupation and apartheid imposed to Palestinian People and the recognition of an independent Palestinian state recognized by the international community on the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

An end to the war in the Middle East. No support, no facilitation, no participation in the US-Israeli war against Iran, Lebanon or any other imperialist intervention. Military fleets and bases out of the region. We express our full solidarity to the people of Cuba and Venezuela and Sudan menaced by US imperialism and we call for defend people’s sovereignty, resources, territorial integrity, peace with justice, and the right for resistance for self-determination.

Ports must not be used for the transport of weapons, ammunition, military equipment and troops. We call on unions to strengthen vigilance, to inform workers, to expose the cargoes of war, and to organize mass collective resistance with all our rightful available means and our struggle.

An end to the militarization of ports and critical infrastructure. Ports belong to the peoples and the workers. They are not bases for NATO, the USA or the EU, nor tools of shipowners and monopoly groups.

No to the war economy and armaments. The money must go to wages, collective agreements, health, education, social needs, and the protection of life and safety at work.

Health and safety measures in the workplaces. Not one worker dead for profits. An end to intensification, subcontracting, dangerous conditions, and employer arbitrariness.

Collective agreements with real wage increases, stable jobs with rights, a retirement policy with better pensions, and a reduction of working time. Technological developments, mechanization, automation, the use of AI and the development of ports must serve the needs of workers, and not lead to the intensification of work or the disappearance of their jobs.

“Our strength lies in organization. It lies in our unions, in general assemblies, in collective decisions, in solidarity among workers from different countries,” the unions said. “We, the workers in the ports, know very well that without us nothing moves. Without our hands, containers remain still, ships are not loaded, the war machines are blocked.”

Al Jazeera noted that of the ports participating in Friday’s actions, “Genoa, Livorno, and Gioia Tauro in Italy, Marseille in France, Piraeus in Greece, and Tangier in Morocco all have proven links to weapons shipments to Israel.”

The strikes come as Israel’s genocide in Gaza continues despite a ceasefire agreement that putatively took effect last October. A United Nations report published earlier this week noted that “Israeli authorities and forces continue to commit genocidal acts” in Gaza “even after the so-called ceasefire agreement, with the intent to destroy the Palestinian people, in whole or in part.”

The report found that Israel—which is armed and supported diplomatically by Western governments, principally the United States—has “committed war crimes and the crimes against humanity of extermination, persecution …

author: Solange Guimarães
title: Fuga de Flávio abre caminho para bolsonarismo abraçar políticos para além do sobrenome
content:
A derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) para Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) nas eleições presidenciais e sua fuga para os Estados Unidos abriram uma disputa pela liderança da extrema direita brasileira que pode resultar em um bolsonarismo cada vez menos dependente dos membros da família do ex-presidente.


Para três pesquisadores que estudam a extrema direita, ouvidos pela

Agência Pública

, o episódio pode representar o início de uma mudança mais profunda: a separação entre o capital político acumulado pelo bolsonarismo na última década e a família que deu nome ao movimento. A crise dos herdeiros de Jair Bolsonaro, entretanto, não significa necessariamente uma perda de influência da extrema direita, que poderá manter sua agenda política, sua capacidade de mobilização e sua atuação nas instituições mesmo sob novas lideranças.


Michelle Bolsonaro, o governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), e o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) estão entre os nomes citados pelos acadêmicos que podem ganhar espaço na reorganização do movimento, que perdeu a disputa pelo Palácio do Planalto, mas ampliou sua presença no Congresso Nacional.


“Acho que todo mundo, de uma certa forma, respira aliviado com a fuga do Flávio. Porque isso significa que há espaço dentro do bolsonarismo para além da família Bolsonaro”, afirma a antropóloga Isabela Kalil, pesquisadora especializada na extrema direita brasileira. Segundo ela, o senador não dispõe de capital político próprio suficiente para exercer, a partir do exterior, a liderança que seu pai construiu no país.


Pesquisadora da extrema direita no Brasil, Isabela Kalil enxergar espaço no bolsonarismo sem os Bolsonaros


A avaliação é compartilhada pelo filósofo Rodrigo Nunes, professor da PUC-Rio e professor visitante da University of Essex, no Reino Unido. Para ele, a disputa pela sucessão já alcança o interior da própria família. “Parece que a briga pela sucessão está se abrindo dentro da própria família Bolsonaro, porque todo mundo percebe que o grande nome dentro da família agora é claramente a Michelle.”


A historiadora e cientista política Tatiana Vargas-Maia, professora de Relações Internacionais da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS), aponta uma transformação ainda mais ampla. “Talvez a gente veja a morte do bolsonarismo como identidade, mas uma manutenção dele como estratégia”, afirma. Na avaliação da pesquisadora, o movimento pode abandonar gradualmente a dependência da figura de Jair Bolsonaro sem abrir mão das práticas políticas, eleitorais e de mobilização desenvolvidas nos últimos dez anos.


A reorganização foi necessária após a vitória do presidente Lula no segundo turno, com 51,79% dos votos válidos, contra 48,21% de Flávio Bolsonaro. O senador recebeu quase 60 milhões de votos, mas deixou o país dois dias depois, apesar de uma determinação do ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) Alexandre de Moraes, para que entregasse seus passaportes à Polícia Federal.


Flávio chegou a Miami na quarta-feira (28), acompanhado da mulher e das duas filhas, após passar pela Argentina onde pegou um vôo particular com escala no Equador. Já nos Estados Unidos, divulgou uma carta em que se apresentou inicialmente como o verdadeiro presidente do Brasil, apesar da derrota nas urnas. Posteriormente, alterou o documento para se autodeclarar líder do país, mantendo acusações de fraude eleitoral sem apresentar provas.


Entre aliados, as decisões de Flávio provocaram reações que evidenciaram o seu isolamento. desde Tarcísio de Freitas defendeu o reconhecimento do resultado das urnas, enquanto Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), coordenador da campanha presidencial do PL, afirmou que não havia elementos para sustentar as acusações de fraude. O distanciamento reforça as dificuldades de Flávio para se apresentar como líder da oposição a partir do exterior.


Michelle e Tarcísio despontam na disputa pela sucessão


Como senadora, Michelle Bolsonaro pode consolidar a sua liderança no bolsonarismo


Lideranças do campo conversador não demoraram a enxergar o espaço construído pela fuga de Flávio Bolsonaro. Para os pesquisadores, Michelle Bolsonaro e Tarcísio de Freitas são os nomes com maior destaque nessa reorganização até o momento, embora a disputa também envolva políticos mais jovens e movimentos que não se identificam integralmente com o bolsonarismo.

author: Cierra Bettens
title: InFocus: What’s at stake for Indigenous Peoples in the U.S. as midterm elections draw near?
content:
On Tuesday, U.S. voters will cast their ballots in the country’s midterm elections. The elections come halfway through a president’s four year term.

A record-breaking number of Indigenous candidates–at least 355–are running in this year’s race.

This week on InFocus, Pawnee/Ponca lawyer Brett Chapman tells us about the candidates he’s following and how Native Americans are feeling the impact of Trump’s second term.

A recent study by the Brookings Institution reported that the Trump administration slashed $469 million in grants and contracts to tribal communities.

“I think a big problem with the administration, the second go around, is that because of the focus by them on DEI [Diversity, Equity and Inclusion], things of that nature, they have really tried to reduce Native American issues to [being] race-based,” Chapman said.

“What defines being Native American in the United States is not being a member of a race. It’s political sovereignty in the history of over 500 tribes having treaties with the government, and they’re having their own governments. And so you’re having a government-to-government relationship.

“You’re really seeing a weakening of that when it should be stronger.”

Covering elections is nothing new for Mark Trahant, a founding editor of Indian Country Today, now called ICT. The Shoshone-Bannock journalist has been in the industry for over 50 years.

However, with the Trump administration’s threats to press freedom, it’s a slightly different terrain.

“One thing I’ve been writing a lot about is how do we plan for life after Trump and start to build institutions again? And I think media is a big part of that,” Trahant said on InFocus.

“One that I would advocate for…is starting to think about government funding of media. You look at, particularly in Indian Country, how much people have to do with so little resources. Whereas, in other countries in the world, they have a steady stream of revenue that allows them to expand, and report, and do things that you would normally do in a media environment that’s healthy.”

Listen to this week’s episode for a closer look at how the U.S. midterm outcomes could impact Indigenous communities.

Cierra is the host and co-producer of the of the weekly APTN News InFocus podcast. She joined APTN in 2024 as a reporter-correspondent in Winnipeg after working in campus and city news. She’s currently completing her Master of Arts in Media Studies at Concordia University in Montréal. Cierra has mixed settler and Red River Métis roots and is a member of the Manitoba Métis Federation.
